text: Here is a letter I sent to their general manager after our lousy experience on August 25th, 2009. Of course it is still an unresolved complaint. We made the reservation because my parents eat there weekly and their lifelong neighbor eats there frequently as well. The neighbor purchased a gift card for us as a gift. Here is how our meal went. I presented the gift card to the waitress at the beginning of the meal and asked her to check it. Our friend told us it was for fifty dollars. The card has no expiration date on it. The waitress, who I wish to point out is blameless in this fiasco, came back with the manager. The manager explained to us that the card was worthless, has zero value, and that these cards were "deactivated" and she had personally checked the list and this number wasn't on it. She then asked if we had used the card before to bring the balance to zero or suggested there was an error in purchasing it. I stated that I would call the 60 year old neighbor who purchased the card for us right now. Your manager then said she wanted to "check again" and get back to us. We then had just finished our dinner and the lady came back and said she had "found" the number and that it was ok. So after the humiliation and embarrassment, the uncomfortable meal wondering if the card was ok, and the obvious question of why would you "deactivate "cards (my only guess its to intentionally irritate your customers), now she said she has the purchase date and the card is ok. Well Mr. Rubin, this is not ok with me. Subjecting my wife and myself to this behavior and lack of professionalism is not ok. I suggest you simply ask the waitress Lindsay what happened for an accurate account. And then get back to me promptly if you wish to resolve this matter amicably.

text: In search of an engagement ring I googled "unique engagement rings." And just by chance (it seems), I found Krikawa (accent on the 1st syllable, I learned later). This was over a year ago, and while I ended up using a family heirloom for her engagement ring, we ended up getting our wedding bands there. Where to start? Let me list some thoughts: designs, customer service, and something about the company. Designs The designs are really superb. A nice mix of modern and classic designs with their own twist, many of which have won awards. We liked some of the more naturalistic ("delicate leaf") and the mokume designs. Customer Service From the beginning, Krikawa was super friendly without being pushy or over-eager. At first it seemed like a long shot because they're in AZ, they don't do trunk shows (they're too busy filling orders to do that). So how can you possibly make to order something as important as your wedding or engagement rings? Well, if you're as moved by the designs as we were, we decided to give it a shot. Their website is very attractive and has very detailed photos of all their work. They sent us samples of the rings that we were ordering, the mokume-gane designs. Now, the photos, all most shot in macro and very professionally done, did turn out to look a little better than the rings. Let's face it, a ring isn't a huge thing, and so while the designs were very clear and stark on the photos, blown up at 5x practically, they were more subtle in real life. We were educated about the various finishes and etchings one uses to enhance the look of the multiple metals in the mokume, some as subtle as fine, highly sanded wood grain that you can barely see, and others very heavy, like tortured metal that you can feel by touch. We got a lot of consultation from them: what's a good gem for gardeners? (not emerald) What kind of metals and etching should one get for swimmers? (Sterling will tarnish in the pool, which will enhance the etching while darkening the luster of the ring) How will various metals wear with time? (Pt and Pd are only displaced; Au can scratch/rub off). Because we were able to get several samples, we knew exactly what we were getting. We were and continue to be very pleased with the final results. They were very very patient and very comprehensive with us in their email communications. I don't know how they do it- I'd be tempted to keep emails so I could reuse them; but we always felt they were directly addressing our concerns and questions. They were very good on timelines and deadlines too. Company Other reasons we like this place are that it's a family run business, the owner is passionate about making and selling lovely jewelry, and they used to be part of 1% for the Planet; and now seem to be part of the Responsible Jewelry Council. They sell Polar (Canadian) diamonds, cultured diamonds, and otherwise only Kimberly Process diamonds (which, BTW, some believe rely on too narrow of a definition to avoid being blood diamonds: http://tinyurl.com/yf3pgey). I don't know if similar responsible practices are possible with other gemstones. They also introduced us to different types of gold (rose, yellow, green), and to alternatives to platinum, which we also appreciated. As I've learned more about jewelry, I realize that there really is a lot out there. It boils down to taste: if you like what you see on their website, you shouldn't hesitate to learn more and give them a try. Make sure you get samples from them too.
label: POS

text: Prior to going to Bern's I was told it was the best steak house in the world. Those are BIG words and hard to stand up to especially if you eat out a lot. Upon driving up to Bern's, the outside was quite simple. Not sure what I was expecting but with a statement like "best in the world" I was expecting not only a great steak but a rich setting. I pulled under the overhang to drop my car at the valet which was the only parking option and when my husband opened the door the first words out of my mouth were "The Madonna Inn". Then I realized that the people we were with were already inside and I hoped they hadn't heard me. Have you been to the Madonna Inn in SLO, CA? Bern's was a bit old fashioned and gaudy. I saw rooms with metal rental chairs, the kind you see in an old Italian restaurant with red and white checkerboard table cloths and in another room I saw white rod iron chairs that are usually outdoors. I ordered the filet of course because I had to try the steak and this is my favorite cut. With the steak was a small cup of French onion soup which was really good, for my salad I ordered the Macadamia Vanilla Bean Vinaigrette on the side since the waitress didn't recommend it and I got the Maple Dijon also on the side. Good choice because the Mac Vanilla bean dressing was more like dessert vs. dressing. With my steak came veggies that I left alone, a baked potato and Steak Fried onion rings. I could have ate a whole plate of these fried onions. They were thin shoestring onions that were lightly breaded and lightly fried. Don't forget to order some mushrooms on the side and if you like mushrooms, order your own because you won't want to share. Now the steak was very good don't get me wrong but it is not the best steak I've ever had and I wouldn't rate it the best in the world because I have yet to hit all the best possibilities. My favorite steak has a bit more seasoning and a touch of melted butter. A few surprises and treats were the kitchen tour. It was immaculate and beyond reproach. There are a ton of restaurants and probably a few of my favorites that I wouldn't want to know what goes on behind the scenes. This place definitely had something to show off. The second treat was the desert room. There is an actual room you go to, that has individual Booth's surrounded by walls with just a doorway on each end. I have never seen anything like this. It made dessert really special. If you have never been to the desert room, save room next time and have this experience. The atmosphere was wonderful, not to mention the deserts. I had the Creme Brule but since I'm a purest when it comes to this dessert, it wasn't my favorite. I like a crisp sugar topping and this had a sort of cookie crust. Good but not what I expect. But the Macadamia Nut Sundae was to die for and I'm not an ice cream fan so if you are, ORDER IT.

text: I went to Midas to replace a bent exhaust pipe and fix an exhaust leak under the hood. The price was reasonable and the work appeared good at first, but very quickly the exhaust leak under the hood reappeared. Now keep in mind, exhaust leaks are serious. The fumes penetrate the firewall and get into the passenger cabin. An exhaust leak can actually kill you if you leave the windows up and run the engine for too long with no ventilation. I didn't actually confirm the exhaust leak had come back until my regular mechanic noticed it weeks later, and then I called them up to fix the problem. They said that they were booked for the day. I got upset and explained to them that their work had put me at risk, and I expected them to fix the problem immediately. They told me that they only warranted their work for 30 days, but grudgingly agreed to replace the seal again. After waiting for hours, the seal was replaced. However, it was still not airtight and now I'm in the same boat again. I suspect that they didn't secure the new exhaust line properly, which is causing it to break the seal in the engine compartment. However, at this point I won't be going back to Midas.
label: NEG

text: So ... I'm a New Yorker, recently visited Nashville, taken by old friend to Virago when we settled on wanting sushi. It's not the worst sushi I've ever had by far, & also not the best. I would give this place 3 or even 4 stars except for the fact that this was perhaps the very worst service I have received at any restaurant in my entire lifetime. And I am not exaggerating. The waitress (who looks somewhat like a young Meryl Streep) must be either new or just coming out of a coma. She suggested we get appetizers because we'd not ordered nearly enough for our main course. Wrong. The main courses we ordered were enough for at least FOUR adults (there were only 2 of us). Then (get this), the main courses arrive BEFORE the appetizers (which, in fact, were NEVER served ... waitress said they must've gotten accidentally taken to another table, wtf????). I got a bad feeling when I arrived about 15 min ahead of my friend & was seated & promptly IGNORED the entire time before my friend arrived ... no "can I get you something to drink?", nothing. Literally, I had to get up, go to the hostess & ask her to please send somebody to take my drink order ... and STILL it was several minutes of waiting. Then, as my friend & I are wrapping up our dinner, we glance over & see our waitress sitting at a nearby booth, patiently wrapping knives & forks in napkins even before we've finished our meal!! Um, check please???? (Any restaurant that takes service seriously does not have waiters wrapping silverware at a booth while diners are still present, good god, who doesn't know THAT?? Maybe at a diner that's acceptable, but not a serious restaurant.) Look, I know I'm from New York, where a place like this would go under in about 5 minutes w/ this kind of horrendous service. Yes, I get that it is important to "slow down" & be patient when visiting the South, & normally I LOVE that things there operate at a more relaxed pace... that is, in fact, part of its charm. But this place takes nightmare service to a whole new level. Plus, it seems to be a bit of a "scene," lots of loud, drunken, screaming girls at every other table. I felt like I was in some dive campus bar. Hope Meryl Streep's a better actor/singer/whatever than a waitress.

Reading through reviews I only found a couple of people who mentioned any problems with the staff. The two or three times I've eaten there I've had quite lovely service. And while she complains, even if she has most tables tip her 10% she still makes a killing. By the way I'm not a skimpy tipper. Not sure why I throw that in there, but I feel it's important. Now you're probably thinking I'm a big hypocrite for eating here three times, but I'll just say it was against my will. See my Dad is one of those people that believes this along with P.F. Chang's are the best Tucson has to offer. So when I get offered a free meal, I'm not going to turn it down. Now I'll admit it, of the three meals I've had there one was quite good, one was good, and only one was disappointing. The Cajun Chicken "Fritters" (I think that's what they were called) were quite good. The burger I had there however was uber disappointing. It didn't live up to their standards of "huge portions" and looked wimpy compared to other meals. I was sad. They don't do bad food, but in my opinion it's not even up to snuff with other chains like Olive Garden or Claimjumpers. The thing I find really silly is how people believe their cheesecake is the best on the planet. Cheesecake is by far my favorite dessert, and I've had some phenomenal cheesecakes, but this isn't one of them. I am also a cheesecake purist, meaning I think anything except plain cheesecake is sacrilege. The fact they aren't made in house is the final nail in their coffin. That being said, again they aren't terrible, but they don't deserve to have a restaurant named after them. A Yelp review isn't really necessary for this, as most of you aren't people who would frequent chain places, but I guess this will show up on Google too. If you're a Tucsonian that has to support big business look into supporting Fox Concept restaurants. You actually get great food there and you spend about the same amount! I really wish more people would go out and support local businesses, that is where Tucson's real individuality shines. Read through reviews here on Yelp, and you'll find more than a few gems! Support local business Tucson! Support local business!!!

text: This place could be confused with just your every-day- run-of-the-mill-burger joint (a cut above the big chains...but your basic burger/fry fare) if you didn't think to order a shake or a cone. text: This place is like Pinnacle Peak Lite, the biggest difference being this place actually serves REALLY good food. Sure there is no Trail Dust Town, staged gun fights, or cutting off of ties, but isn't that a good thing? They do the old Western decor, and I think they do it well. This is easily my favorite place in Tucson to come for a steak for two reasons. The first obviously being the quality of the food and the second being the value. You seriously can NOT beat this places dinner specials. On Tuesday you can get TWO giant pork chops, Wednesday a large new york strip, and Thursday an 8 ounce prime rib. All of these come with bread, soup or salad, and your choice of two sides! All of these meals cost $10.95! That is utter ridiculous-ness in my books. And just to throw this out there, on Friday and Saturday they do 16 ounce T-Bones for 13.95. They're closed Sunday, and I personally don't like Monday's special, bbq boneless beef ribs. The REAL ribs are delicious though! You really have to try their soup too! I've eaten here probably 20 times and I don't think I've seen the same soup more than twice. The exception being every Friday is clam chowder. If you get the side salad expect for the normal steakhouse abuse of salads. Compared to Lil' Abners though it is wonderful! At least they put veggies on their iceberg lettuce! I personally have never order the salad entrees, (I love meat) but I had a friend do it once and it looked quite delicious. Their burger is also one of the best in Tucson. Given the choice between this and Zinburger (my other favorite burger place) I'd probably pick Cody's 9 out of 10 times. I always get mine with pepper jack and bacon. The grand total of a burger topped my way comes out to just under 9 bucks. Keep in mind that comes WITH one side. Quite a good deal if you ask me! The way drinks are served should put a smile on your face. Almost everything is served in a boot-shaped glass. The only exception being the iced-tea and that comes with a full pitcher and an extra glass of ice. I also used to come when the best waitress in the world worked here, and she would even put my tea in a boot. Little things like that made my day. Overall, I think I've only had bad service once, and it was the girl's first day so I tried to cut her some slack (and she was replacing the best server of all time.) If you love steak and you haven't been here, do yourself a favor and come in for one of their specials. It blows places like Silver Saddle out of the water! Definitely on my short list of favorite restaurants in Tucson!

text: I know my last review for the AEC was amusing and informative enough to get it voted ROTD, but this review is not as funny. I hope it's informative though! I had to use the AEC again this weekend, but this time for something more serious and in depth. Saturday night, my elderly pomeranian mix pup, Maddie, started to vomit. She vomited throughout the night and into the morning and was very lethargic. For an 8 pound dog, dehydration can happen really quickly. She also had bloody diarrhea. She probably vomited 20+ times, just bile, nothing she ate. I took her to the AEC on Sunday around noon knowing she'd need fluids at the very least. It ended up being more! Sunday was particularly crazy at the AEC and there was a lot of waiting. We got into a room within 30 minutes or so, and they took her vitals. She weighed 6.5lbs, which is a lot less than her normal weight, considering how small she is. The most alarming thing was that her temperature was 96 degrees, which is really low (a dog's temp should be around 101). They got a blanket and water bottle and we waited even more. The doc came to see her and thought she was exhibiting neurological symptoms that were worrisome. They took her back to do a blood panel. After much more waiting, I got the news that her blood work didn't show any bad organ function, thank goodness. It showed she was very dehydrated and had some other things off indicating possible infection. The doc wanted to admit her, so I agreed. At this point, they can't give you an exact amount you owe, but instead give you an estimate with a "low" and a "high" estimate. You pay half the high estimate as a deposit. GULLLP. Not cheap. I called a couple times to check up on her, and each time, the technician who was caring for her spoke to me on the phone and was very nice. This morning I called and talked to a really nice tech, Dave, who had fed her and cared for her through the night. He told me her temp was back to normal and she'd be able to go home soon. I went to see her and she was still pretty tired. Dave came in with her and talked to me a lot about her. He was the friendliest/more informative person I had contact with there. I really appreciated it. A couple hours later, I was told I could pick her up. They gave me detailed instructions and the doctor talked to me and we came home. She's recovering and will be rechecked Wednesday by my normal vet. The good thing was that I actually ended up getting a refund from my original deposit. It was less than the "low" estimate. That was a pleasant surprise! The short version: - The AEC can get really busy and expect to wait unless your pet is critical. Triage is ok because they will help you first if it is more urgent. - The vets are good but don't give as personal care as my normal vets. The fabrics strung across the ceiling seemed to do a good job of dampening the noise. My associate had the salmon that he really enjoyed. I had one of the lunch specials, a chicken salad (w/spinach, gorgonzola, bacon, apples, vinaigrette) which was only $8. It was huge. I could only finish half of it. The chicken was freshly grilled and amazingly moist and tender. There was an excellent balance between all the constituent parts. Service was excellent. Waitress was there in a flash and came by several times, even though we delayed her due to our conversation. One of the partners of the parent company came by to see how we enjoyed our meal and if there was anything they could do to improve. The only complaint was that the service was too fast -the food came out within ten minutes of ordering - but they didn't rush us to leave. So, for the price, quality of food, and service I'm a fan. I plan to check it out for dinner.
label: POS

text: I was so jazzed on the place from the first visit I decided to take them up on the birthday free dinner. 1. they wouldn't seat us and were rude even though I had made reservations. 2. text: The only Borders in Nashville. Sad. I hoped a city this size could support more than one. The parking is awful! Good luck with it. But if you do manage to get a spot, don't pay any attention to the time limit, they seriously never check. This is a prop for sure. The DVD selection in this place is out of this world. I have never seen such a large selection that ranges from foreign film to concerts to documenteries to the Brittish 'The Office'. Nobody hounds you, which is great, and the coffee, while still owned by Starbucks, serves up the least burnt tasting coffee in the company. Their green tea lattes are amazing.

text: I visited Jack Furrier's on recommendation from a friend. I had nails in two relatively new and expensive all terrain tires. The pipe connecting the radiator to the water hose had broken, which did not allow for a safe connection. I took the truck to Firestone, where the tires had originally been purchased. I was told to purchase new tires, to have unneeded services performed, and that their inspection did not reveal a problem with the radiator. Jack Furrier's fixed the tires for free, and clearly explained the benefits and drawbacks of any course of action on the radiator. Due to my use of the vehicle in remote areas where tow trucks cannot penetrate, I opted for the full replacement of the radiator and themostat. The price quoted for this work averaged nearly $300 less than other shops in the area. It's so nice to encounter a business ethic in Tucson. After six years and numerous repairs, this is the first shop in town that will see my business a second time.
label: POS

text: I've never eaten in the actual restaurant, but we get delivery from Maria's a few times a month. I love their chicken fingers - whatever they bread them in is much lighter and tastier than most chicken fingers. Love their honey mustard sauce. The margherita pizza is AMAZING. It's more of a white pizza with sliced tomatoes on top. It was so delicious that I haven't been able to stop thinking about it since we got it. We always order their Old Bay Fries. In all honestly, by the time they get to our house the fries are soggy and the cheese sauce is hard but they are still somehow delicious and satisfy my craving for something sort of close to Chickie and Pete's Crab Fries. We have ordered a few pasta dishes as well, and they've all been great. VERY yummy wrap sandwiches as well. Pesto Chicken = YUM.
label: POS

text: For the most part, I'll chime in with Melissa V.. Applebees is just not a comfortable place to go. It's too loud, and when you're sitting with friends, there's an exposed feeling that is not condusive to either conversation or to sticking around. I'm sure that's precisely what the designers had in mind, but they took it too far. It may have to do with the awful service as well. Everything I've ever tried at Applebee's is just a notch up from fast food in flavor but is served in giant quantities. If you're trying to save money, their early bird special appetizers can be a great deal. The nachos are enough to feed two adults and they're about $7 or $8 during the early bird happy hour. So as long as you're good with the concept of sit-down fast food, and needing to flag down your server for any drink refills or other needs, then Applebee's can be a budget-friendly restaurant alternative.
label: NEG

text: Had the "cajun chicken" poboy and cream of NO (New Orleans) shallot soup. This was the most tasteless meal I can recall ever having. Very very disappointing meal after Yelp reviews brought me here.

text: Every Tuesday I meet my friends here for happy hour. All the drafts are $3, and there is always a specialty cocktail - last night it was a Mexican mai-tai, featuring house-infused strawberry tequila, and it was delicious. All winter long I was warmed by rummy apple ciders. The bartender, Megan, is super nice, and I don't even have to ask for refills anymore, they just magically appear. I haven't tried many of the food items on the menu, but I did recently eat a beautiful smoked fish plate with a slow egg on top. I have never had egg prepared this way, it was a little round yolk that looked like it would ooze when popped, but instead it was smooth and creamy, almost like a custard. It was amazing! Next time I am going to try a trio of ice creams, they are all made in house and sound amazing!

text: Mother's music is a great store. It's not as good as AXE but it is pretty close. It is packed with wall to wall instruments and accessories. The staff is really helpful. They know there stuff and try and get you the best bang for your buck. I mostly enjoyed just browsing and messing around with some of the instruments but if you are actively looking for a new guitar or drum or some other instrument you will be satisfied here. The prices are the same as most music places but the selections better.

text: Really disappointing. Place looks nice, and for $11-$17 a plate, you expect a satisfying brunch. Not so. Not a single item that was served to me and my wife was above "cheap diner" caliber. - Poached eggs were not properly drained, so they sat in a puddle of lukewarm water. - Omelette was overfried and crinkly. - Salsa was definitely made straight from canned diced tomatoes; it had that supermarket puree taste, and was just gross. - Sausage was dry and chewy, and also tasted like it was out of some frozen meal. - They don't use real maple syrup. - The cream for the coffee is not fresh, but comes in plastic packets. The waitress was kind enough, but she refilled our coffees without warning, which felt a little invasive. You put cream and sugar in your coffee, are enjoying it, and boom, she just dumps in all this black coffee without asking. Bottom line: they charge Manhattan prices for IHOP food. text: Been here on several occasions, 2 times for bridal showers, Exceptional food, priced reasonably, quality is great. IT is a house, made into local restaurant, great for all occasions. text: Wether you're there for brunch, lunch, or dinner prepare for an amazing meal in a unique and calming atmosphere. The eggs benedict and mimosa combination always make the rest of a Sunday for me. And during dinner try the escargot... it is intense and a memory maker of awesome proportion. The cheese plate and a bottle of wine will start your night off the right way. Wether for a date or a nice dinner with some other food loving friends this is a must do on your new orleans culinary experience.
label: POS

text: I love Companion and eat here probably about twice a month. Living around the corner from the place does not help! My favorite sandwich would have to be Chucks #39 (curried chicken salad? wonderful!). While I have not tried their pastries, I brought a baguette to a group dinner, which everyone raved about. The seasonal Pumpkin cranberry loaf was also amazing and gone within a few days. The meal options are reasonable, getting a half sandwich is often more than enough, but pairing it with a soup or salad is heavenly. And that cornbread... wow. I will say that the sodas are overpriced for just being a can, but the sandwiches themselves are worth the price. The great looking cakes and pastries in the display case are nice to dream about, but again, the cakes seem overpriced. The atmosphere of the place is very comfortable, I have spent many hours studying for various tests with no problems. The different rooms allow groups to make some noise without being distracting, and the outdoor seating is nice as well. I have spent hours studying without feeling pressured to continue to buy things, however they don't need to pressure me on that regard. Overall, I will be coming back many, many times.

text: The Hong Kong bakery has been a favourite of mine for years now. I like going down there on a hot summer day and getting some of their yummy mango ice cream. When the budget was tight, I loaded up on Chinese buns stuffed with bbq pork. I learned they taste much better fresh than frozen then thawed. And you can eat too many of these! Now I like the sweets better from here. They make amazing sesame balls filled with red bean paste and my boyfriend just introduced me to their custard buns, which are so good it's hard not to keep eating them. They also have egg tarts that are exquisitely fresh. There are still a lot of cakes and sweets I haven't tried from here, but I plan to make many trips back. The Hong Kong Bakery is the best place to get baked goods in China town.
label: POS

text: A classy dump indeed. The Radisson Hotel is the Gaylord Opryland "overflow" hotel. If attending a show at the Gaylord, the Radisson is a good location and a place to get away from crowds. The Radisson is definitely rough around the edges and is in a desperate need of an update. We checked in with little difficulty and were given a room by the indoor pool. The sound of it didn't seem too bad but when we got in to the room everything was damp and the air was stuffy. The hotel has a large attrium that consists of the pool and a large open area for banquet space and a random tiki bar. The room is tight with the sink area in the bedroom and the shower area being a sperate closet size space. The worst part of the room were the Sleep Number beds, which kept me from a good night sleep durning my whole stay. You can hear the neighboring rooms bed air pumps going as guests are trying to figure out how to get comfortable. The front desk employees never gave us the same answer twice as to when the Opryland shuttle was running, which caused us to miss our needed shuttled more than once. Despite their lack of knowledge of the hotel services they were very friendly. For a cramped out dated room, with peeling paint, damp sheets, uncomfortable bed and unknowledgable staff we were charged $140 a night! The convention rate at the Gaylord was $150. A Holiday Inn Express is just a quarter mile down the road from the Radisson which I wish I would have known was there before booking the Radisson.
label: NEG

What I'm trying to say is that I liked it.

text: I need to first qualify the scope of this review. My comments on as limited as our experience at Sandbar was. We visited with the intention of eating there, but only made it through an experience at the bar. We ordered a pair of "Top Shelf" margharitas and followed the bartender's suggestion on the choice of tequila. I knew we were in trouble when he used the gun to shoot an insipid looking sweet and sour mix into our drinks. The drinks tasted as flat and unappealing as they could have. To make matters worse, the cost was $34 for two drinks that we could have had in Cabo for $2 a piece. After perusing the menu and eyeballing the plates of food around us, we came to the conclusion that the food was not going to be much different than the drinks...over-priced and unappealing. On the flip side, the place seemed like a pretty happening bar/nightclub opportunity. They have live music on some evenings and the outdoor seating area was filled with people having a good time. So I guess if you're with a good sided group and like a lively spot and are drinking bottled beer, this might appeal to you. But if you're looking for food and cocktails, I recommend you look elsewhere.

text: I just went here last weekend for vegan brunch with my partner. We took a trip down to Philly for the day from NYC and I had heard about this place online and wanted to try it. Being vegans, we are pretty limited with restaurants these days. From the moment we walked in and saw the menu, we knew that we were in for a treat. The place was pretty small but there was a table waiting for us. My partner ordered the tofu benedict and I ordered the chocolate chip/peanut butter pancakes. After the waiter took our order, he brough a plate of fruit and cakes...all vegan. Now, as most vegans know, it's heard to find decent baked goods and this stuff was absolutely amazing! Then came the rest...the pancakes were to die for and his tofu benedict...just amazing! Service was really fast. We were probably in and out of there in a little over half an hour, though we could have lingered, but we had stuff to do... I can't wait to go back to Philly...this will definitely be our first stop!

text: Like Ted C said, our group came over here for an after tapas take out dinner haha..we are piggies! I had catfish, corn, and scalloped potatoes. OMG how can simple home cooking be so good? The corn was amazing--so flavorful and a little bit spicy, the scalloped potatoes had the right amount of cheesiness, and the catfish was crispy. The best part is that I had leftovers for my "breakfast" aka 4am coming home from the bar! haha PS don't eat this if you plan on going anywhere afterward, you will go into a food coma quick!! Also, there is no seating...just take out & the menu changes daily.

text: Anyone reading this is sure to know something about the restaurant and the celebrity chef owner. The food is literally as good as you can imagine it can be. They take simple ingredients and expertly prepare them and elevate them to a level I've seldom seen before. I ate there with a small group and we passed samples to one another so I was able to try a few dishes at once and they were all stellar. One thing I disagree about is the prices there. I think, for the quality of the food/service, that the prices are very reasonable for what you get. Surely if you get the tasting menu or several courses it can get a bit pricey, but the entrees are not extraordinarily expensive, so it's possible to eat there without blowing an entire paycheck and still get the same enjoyment that people a bit more well-to-do get from their 7 course meal. Save up a few dollars, skip a few taco bell meals, and go enjoy dinner at August, it's fantastic. If a poor graduate student can go there an have the best meal of his life, you surely can too.
label: POS

text: I go to this Safeway all the time as it is the closest to my house. There is no better alternative, especially when I am on a quick grocery run; everything is available in one location. The staff are friendly and know where everything is; they will usually personally guide you to the item you're looking for. There are a lot of senior's homes around the area, so customer service is a crucial part for this location's success. This Safeway carries a good selection of organic vegetables and fruits, to freshly packed meat and seafood. Although this location is not as large as others, the range of products appears to be very similar. There is also a gasoline station located just across the parking lot. Recently a Starbucks has been added to the location, for better or for worse. I believe this is not attracting any extra attention to the store, however just offering something else to make your grocery shopping easier.

text: Big fan of Tavern. I love bars with a variety of entertainments. They have a bunch of different rooms, a pool table (my fav!) and lots of TVs. So conveniently located I frequent this place a lot.

text: The food is passable, but the service was, as another reviewer put it: "Beyond rude." As a matter of fact, in 40 years if dining out I have never been told "NO! The kitchen is CLOSED!" when I ordered dessert after a meal. The entire experience felt extremely rushed, and I had to send the waitress away THREE separate times when we were trying to enjoy some drinks before our meal. By the third time, we broke down and ordered even though we were not finished our drinks. I guess all the waitstaff could think about was getting home, because our food came out immediately, as if it had been pre-made. I too got the lecture about ordering a "4" and was pressured into ordering a"3". Maybe if they would spend less time rushing their guests and lecturing, the food would be tastier. The most astounding thing about the evening, though, was that we were NOT warned that the kitchen was about to close and after we sat and spent $60 on drink and dinner, were told we were not allowed to have dessert because the kitchen was closed! Now this was a first. I fail to believe that every dessert is made from scratch at the time of the order and that were NO desserts in the fridge or freezer which they could serve. This experience was definitely a first for me. Thai Singha house gets my vote for the most obnoxious waitstaff ever.

text: Not Impressed but I'm still going here as it is the best that I have found so far in my area. Reminds me that I need to do some more searching.... Julie and Vivianne are the sweetest but the pink and white / solar nails they do are poor. They slop on the gels and later try to sand them into shape, mine are ALWAYS jagged on the sides and after 1.5 weeks lifting. Vivianne used to give an awesome leg/foot massage with her pedicures but last time I got one it was lacking :( The eye brow wax setup is a joke, its a plastic lounge chair covered in a blanket that hasn't been washed in the 6 months Ive been living here, but for $8 I guess I may let them wax my mustache........maybe just OK

text: Those who are giving this cafe positive reviews do not know authentic mexican food. Let me start with the service. I went here the first time with a Groupon that gave me 50% discount and arrived on a Sat. night yet it was still only half full of patrons. We immediately asked for the horchata which they did not have....what? Tortilla soup? Not that either....why have things on the menu if you dont actually offer them? After we ordered an appetizer we did not see our waitress for some time . She finally returned with a small (tiny) pot of melted chees...which provided only four tablespoon servings total! They offered the typical "tex-mex" fare that you would find in a Don Pablo's or a chain restaurant. The pork was fatty, the refried beans extremely oily and when we ordered "micheladas" or beer with clamato juice and chili spice we received something that wasn't even drinkable. Doused in so much chili we couldn't even choke it down. My boyfriend was raised in Mexico and I have been there many times. I have eaten excellent mexican food in the states as well. This is NOT mexican. It's a poor example. One more visit gave the same result, no horchata (it was a weekday!) and a non existent server. It took us over 45 minutes to receive our entrees after ordering! They have to improve service to deserve more than 2 stars.
label: NEG

text: Blech. Could you get any LESS authentic? I could buy the ingredients for their quesadillas at a gas station. The frozen margaritas are not blended well. The place is so big that service lacks. The patio is nice - pretty much the only selling point. However, getting a table on it is nearly impossible. The parking situation sucks and the wait is usually bad when the weather is nice. NOT worth it. Go down the road to El Indio - much more authentic, better service, less wait, and better food.

text: Give vietnamese food a bad look on there food. I went here for lunch with an out of town family member. Since they were down for a convention and did not want to drive else where. I never go here again even if I am desperate to eat vietnamese. Save your money and maybe get a lucky dog will be well worth your money.

text: Very classy and upscale spot! My girlfriend and I went here to celebrate Valentine's Day this year. It had a very pleasant and relaxed atmosphere. This is definitely somewhere you want to take your significant other for a nice quiet dinner (fellas). The restaurant was dimly lit and there was a live pianist singing classic love songs. The architecture was very modern and artistic. I had the duck, which was very good and I'm glad it was since it was my first time ever trying it. I also found it very refreshing to have the head chef himself personally ask us if we were enjoying our meals and if we needed our drinks refilled. The price is a little high but reasonable for the type of service that you'll be receiving. I definitely recommend Scape for a quiet, romantic evening out.

I've never really had anything but pizza, but others in my family have, and everyone enjoys it all. Even as a vegan, I order cheeseless pizza and it's very good: their sauce and crust are good enough on their own, even without toppings. The only warning for new visitors is that it can get very crowded on weekends. You may have to wait; instead, I always pickup to avoid the wait.

text: I always have had a good experience here. It's the closest to authentic Japanese cuisine in Nashville with items not normally seen on American sushi house menus. There's quite a decent number of good sushi joints in Nashville, but Koto is the finest choice if you have the money for a new addiction. Go wild! Unagi - A++ cooked to perfection Nattho - A++++ Only place I can find it in the city! (thank god) Onigiri - A+++ Addictive Salmon Roe - A+++ Delicious. Not too strong of a fishy taste. Teas - Hot, fresh and strong
label: POS

text: My first time eating one of their wraps was late last week. It was delivered to my workplace, and a special bulk delivery arrangement meant the delivery charged was waived, which is a positive thing going for this eatery, but probably not available to the general public. I think the delivery cost is $1.50. Also nifty is the online ordering method, which I found to be easy to navigate, and I could pay online. Very handy. But I made the foolish mistake of thinking that a pita-based place might be good for traditional pita wraps, namely the gyro ($7). It was disappointing. I should have gone for more typical sandwich fillings, I've heard the caesar salad wrap and the BLT wrap are good. A co-worker got a grilled chicken wrap, and her extra sauces ended up in my order. Also, she said she felt "a little gross" afterwards, so both of us weren't overly pleased. In defense of the delivery, I'm sure the bulk arrangement was confusing and stressful to the Pit person, so I'm not knocking them for a little switcheroo action in some orders. Also, I should note that a third co-worker had a lot of trouble navigating the website ordering system, especially backing out and trying to adjust his order. So, whether you find the online system user friendly or not is quite subjective. But, I'm not crazy about the food, and the convenience of ordering/delivery cannot compensate for that. The same price can buy a very nice fancy sandwich or panini at other nearby places.
label: NEG

text: First of all, go during lunch. You can get out of there for $10 with a premium buffet and a drink. Dinner will jack the price up 120%. Second of all, don't be fooled by the sign and name... This is a Chinese buffet. However, it's unlike any Chinese buffet you've ever been to (and I've been to more than you ever have). Every item on the buffet is what I like to call "entrée quality." To top it off, they have a rich-school-prom-sized chocolate fountain. Seriously? A chocolate fountain! I'm not even going to tell you any more. Don't listen to the haters on here. They hate all that is good and delicious. Do yourself a favor and go here.
label: POS

text: My family and I ventured into Magnolia Grill in search of brunch after we were told about the 30 minute wait for Stanley. It was the lunchtime rush, but we had no problem finding a table. It takes about 20 minutes maybe more for a chocolate shake to even get to the blender. I don't know if they were making that ice cream by hand or what, but I don't think it takes that long to make a shake. 1 hour passes (family has already suggested we leave 3 times) (don't quite know why we stayed) When we ask about the long wait, we are informed they are waiting for one dish and the rest have been sitting under a heat lamp for the entire hour. One dish finally appears. 10 minutes later, two burgers are walked slowly to our table. Almost 20 minutes after, pancakes, and not even hot pancakes, arrive with a bowl of syrup. Food cannot taste good after you wait an hour. The work ethic in Nola is sometimes considered a bit slow, but not an hour wait for cold pancakes kinda slow. The chocolate shake was good despite its questionably long prep time, but everything else= below average. Skip this and brave the wait for Stanley.
label: NEG

text: Have been there twice. First time, the kitchen had just opened to full menu. Not too bad - but like other reviewers, portions are small for the prices. My husband ordered fish & chips and it came in a bowl - do they serve fish & chips in a bowl in England/Ireland? I made the mistake of ordering jerk chicken (what was I thinking? better yet, why is this on the menu at an Irish pub?). When it came out it was 3 strips of chicken and a tiny scoop (like 3 tablespoons) of rice with a few peas and a bit of carrots in it - not enough for the $17 price tag. Also, a little pet peeve of mine, there was nothing on the table to munch on - no rolls, pretzels, popcorn, etc. So my sister-in-law is a big Scottish fan and we agree to meet up there for dinner again. Despite many people working that night AND a reservation, it took forever to get a waitress to come to our table. Maybe because it was upstairs and she didn't want to walk up the stairs? We ordered 3 boxtys (type of sandwich) and 3 fish & chips. After at least 45-50 minutes of waiting, with nothing on the table and empty drink glasses, we finally got our dinner - just dropped off by some busboy, with no silverware to eat with, and no one around to get any silverware because he just ran off. Once again, the fish & chips came in a bowl - and no one finished their plates. On busy nights you may have to wait for one of the friendly, personable staff ask you what you would like - but when they get to you you will undoubtedly smile at their wit. The real star here is the beer - the Dagger Falls (IPA), Powerhouse Porter, and Wooleybugger Wheat are best in class. The food is standard pub fare with a few real standouts. Sockeye's version of the Hot Wing is a tasty, boneless tenderloin with a fiery house-made sauce that is very flavorful. Burgers are juicy and tasty with fresh toppings and a variety of great condiments. The chipotle mayo is on quite a few items (including the large, crispy onion rings and sweet potato fries). Happy hour is 5:30-7pm and each Tuesday the fresh, delicious pints are only $2.50. There is live, local music every Tuesday and Friday night as well. Sockeye has a fantastic patio that is a must for summer evenings in Boise. They have recently updated all of their TVs and added enough of them to also be considered a great sports bar as well as an amazing brewpub. Any beer-lovers who visit Boise should definitely put Sockeye at the top of their list of places to visit. For the West Boise folks that are looking for a pub to call your own - this is a quick bike ride to great people and fun times.

text: Ah, 666 - The Mark Of The Beast. A number so sinister that it has hellacious written all over it. When you reach this milestone on Yelp you clearly have to write about something that represents your idea of hell (or Johnny Brenda's if your Dave H. -1- but he's still the man). So it sounds like the perfect time to sum up exactly how I feel about Starbucks. And since I already spelled it out for you many moons over (http://www.yelp.com/list/i-hate-starbucks-philadelphia) you know exactly where this one is going. My overall thoughts of Starbucks has nothing to do with service or product. I've had decent service in plenty, and in spots like the one that I'm dropping this review on (you'll go anywhere if certain people suggest it) I've had better than decent. And you can't go wrong with the diverse selections of beans that they bring in, assortment of Tazo teas, and delicious treats that they offer for the most part. Although a lot of the prices can be pretty damn horrendous (there's good reason why I affectionately call them Fourbucks). And they do provide a spacious decor that gives you plenty of room to get some work done if your in a bind (I like the upstairs that this one offers). But in the land of lush and vibrant indie coffeehouses that is Philadelphia, Starbucks is pretty much the Soulless Empire. When you walk into a place like Chapterhouse that turns it's surroundings into an art gallery; a spot like Last Drop that's packed to the gills with good music, listings for local shows, and gratuitous people watching; or a spot like TBar that hooks up Scrabble and an amazing book exchange; the atmosphere brings you to life. But by comparison the atmosphere of Starbucks manages to suck the life right out of you. Every time I walk in and see the same typical looking art, the same cold plain decor, and total lack of vibrance, I can't help but feel like a corporate slave digging a hole towards a corporate grave no matter what I'm doing. If you ever hear the words "Grande soy latte two sugars" coming out of my mouth feel free to slay me. But the main reason I hate Starbucks is because, just like rats in the city, they're freaking EVERYWHERE. If you walk down any major Philly street and see a Starbucks, and then it's more than likely that you'll come across another three blocks away, and then ANOTHER! It borders on the unnecessary, but rather than do something to lessen the amount (even when Starbucks announced the closing locations) it feels like their building more (http://www.yelp.com/biz/macys-philadelphia#hrid:6dm686CWJQrzhJAfGOcEwQ). Damn the Empire! -1- Dave H. did review Johnny Brenda's as his 666. But it wasn't because he found it evil. It was because he didn't put the same significance into the number that I did. and after going to a good show he just felt that it was time to.

text: Don't believe the hype. I had been waiting for quite a while to try this place after reading the good reviews here and elsewhere. Both my friend and I are vegetarian, so I was excited that it featured several items sans-meat. Oh, but what a disappointment. I ordered the yuka fries, which arrived cold and slowly. The chipotle sauce was good but the two thimble-sized cups of it were not enough. My rice and beans were very bland and boring. And not even authentic Mexican cheese. My friend got the squash dish, and it looked so unappetizing that when she offered a bite, I declined. Very small portion at that. The prices here are outrageous, definitely priced for tourists. The food was also delivered at different times. The tortillas were not homemade and were more like what I call "Wonderbread" tortillas. White and floury. My friend's mom's soup looked ok but the vegetable garnish looked limp and unappetizing--unripe tomato, wilted greens, bleh. I was actually embarrassed to have wasted their money and appetites here, even though they acted as if they liked it to be polite. There were leftovers and we didn't even take them home. text: In a random conversation I made mention of Bellacinos and how much I liked the establishment near Hampton Village. So while this particular review won't be based on the merits of one particular excursion, I have gone enough times to confidently review on the basis of past, aggregate experiences. That just means I'll be more vague, but it should still count the same as if I wasn't vague. ^_~ Bellacinos is the number one exception to the rule whenever I am forced to imagine the train wreck that is "Italian Fast Food." You want Italian food? You go to the Hill and SIT DOWN. Or you go to a little mom and pop store and SIT DOWN. Never do you go to a store that lets you take your order to go, or worse, delivers your order to your door if your intent is decent Italian food. It just doesn't work that way...unless you're talking about Bellacinos! Which.. I guess is only half Italian, because I'd consider it Italian-American cuisine for all those technical cry babies out there. /whatev The key to their success is extremely good, extremely unique bread dough. Having worked at Bellacinos in Kirksville, I can attest to the fact that it is made fresh (at least it was at that location). On any give day the bread you get is typically going to be less than 24 hours old (again, at least at that location... but this is a franchise we're talking about). Not only does the bread taste fresh, soft and flaky, but when it goes through the oven it becomes the perfect type of crispy- in all the right places. Ingredients are typically fresh (very few bad experiences with limp or slimy veggies) and the price is always right: CHEAP! The fries are good. Soft in the center, crispy on the outside. Not sure what else to say about that subject... fries are pretty much fries, right? I mean, unless we count the salt lick sticks that McDonalds puts out. In that case, I suppose we can finally measure a noticeable difference. The pizzas are also awesome. They come out quickly due to the convection, conveyor oven that they're made in and they have a texture and flavor very different, very unique, but very exceptional all their own. I don't really posses the vocabulary to describe the difference... it just has to be experienced I suppose. I can say that its consistency is light and fluffy and very UN-GREASY. Which is actually something that could be said of all of Bellacinos wares as everything is technically baked, not fried. A hidden bonus for the health conscious. The only detractor that I can recall are the salads. Ah, the fast food salad- the lame concession to vegans and vegetarians alike by slick CEOs consisting of one, WHOLE head of shredded iceberg lettuce, three slivers of red onion and a pile of shredded cheese on top. ON TOP. Not even mixed in. But, that's more a knock at all fast-food salads and Bellacinos shouldn't, necessarily, bear sole responsibility for it. Service at the Hampton Village location is always fast and friendly. The store is always presentable and clean. Etc. All around a good experience that has me coming back whenever the urge for hot grinders strike. EDITED 3-22-2010: I suddenly remembered that I didn't offer any advice on what specifically to eat! Duh! I would recommend just about any sandwich with the words "chicken" or "steak" in the name (especially the Chicago Steak Sandwich!). I will, however, caution against both the BBQ Pulled Pork and the Seafood sandwiches. Both are essentially composed of the appropriate meats in pureed form and are practically 'spread' on the buns. Which wouldn't be so bad if they didn't also taste and possess the consistency of artificially flavored, homogeneous paste. VERY disgusting.

Dueling pianos are lots of fun, so its a shame that the management is lame you have to fight crowds of bachelorette parties and company dinners to enjoy it. Also, I have a major problem with bars that charge for water. I understand if a table of aforementioned-company-partiers just order pitchers of water, and that's it, but I do NOT want to pay a few bucks for water to space out my martinis or beers. I was charged for water the last time I went, even when everyone in my party ordered drinks and a full meal. I realize this sounds cheap, but what's bothered more than my wallet is just the stupidity of the rule. Also, I showed up early w/ a few girlfriends for dinner at 7 p.m. on a Friday night, and the doorman wanted to charge us all cover. Really? Cover? At 7 p.m. in Maplewood, Missouri? No, thanks. A final observation: the crowd ranges from 21st birthday parties, to groups of cougars on the prowl, to bachelorettes, to 20-somethings, to whole tables of couples in their 50s who are enjoying the bar as a rare big night out on the town. No judgement, no negativity, just what to expect. Jive and Wail, I'm officially over you. Thanks for the good times and multiple renditions of Cheeseburger in Paradise and dirty versions of I'm a Little Teapot. I probably won't be back.

The dinner menu, however, has few options under $16, with entrees maxing out at almost $30 for a steak. The service overall was fine, however, the food itself was lackluster and bland. text: Wow...I really wish I could say I like biking this trail because I'm really glad the city of St. Louis is trying...but...well...try harder??? They have put in some pathed sidewalks on the river's edge and the new footbridge across the river between Gravois and Morganford is actually really nice, but the bike path...well...it just leaves a lot to be desired. The path runs from Lindenwood St. near the Metro Link, down the side of River Des Peres down near Highway 55. The path is fairly flat which is good for less experienced bikers, but that said, the trail is NOT well maintained...which is horrible for inexperienced bikers. There are ton of cracks and rocks all over the thing. It is only 4 miles long and takes a lot of random bends and turns for no apparent reason. Also, lets remember, you riding along the side of River Des Peres. In high school my friends and I maturely referred to this thing as River Des Pew. Is a sewage run off really what you want to be inhaling when you are trying to ride or run? Not so much. On the upside, it's never crowded, and you don't have to fight your way around baby strollers, but there's a reason for this...the path is just....well...sub par... I suggest avoiding this one and just heading further south to Grant's Trail or sticking with Forest Park...trust me you'll be glad you did.

There is one seating area that has white curtains while there are regular tables and chairs to the side. There is another dining area near the bar which is more like a high table with benches. text: This was our home for 4 nights. It's located in the historic Sam Hughes neighborhood a few blocks walk from the University of Arizona campus. Our room was the Santa Fe and its entrance was from the beautiful, peaceful patio. There are tables, chairs and benches in the patio and garden and the splashing of the fountain makes it a lovely place to sit. Our room was large and comfortable w/ a high, rustic four-poster bed and plenty of storage and good light. There was a basket of full sized shampoos, conditioners and other amenities. The towels were wonderful soft, fluffy and a gorgeous mossy green. There's a little refrigerator under the desk and bottled water is replenished daily. The tile floors feel wonderful on bare feet in hot weather. There's a ceiling fan to circulate the air. Breakfast is served at 8:15. I wasn't thrilled w/ that, but it was fine. The food varied from day to day and it was very good. Company, as always, was excellent. There is a comfortably set up computer room and there's wifi in the rooms. Adjacent to the computer room is an attractive and comfortably furnished gathering room w/ well stocked book shelves that make it look like a library. The cost of our room was very reasonable, particularly for what it offered.

text: EDIT- I have decided to edit my post instead of update it, since I only wrote it a week ago. Despite my opinion of Happy Maki from my first visit, I decided to give them another chance because I thought the food was good. This time, I went with take out. I found the food to be virtually inedible. The sushi was mealy and unappetizing. Also, it's highly aggravating to open a small soup container to discover it is half empty. Here's the original post- How could I not like a place called Happy Maki? Come on, folks, that's adorable. Too bad the place is so odd, because I don't like it. I have always lived under the assumption that when there are no servers, the prices go down. Or that when you are housed in a suburban strip mall, the prices go down. Or when you use mostly disposable dishes, the prices go down. Or when a restaurant doesn't offer tap water, don't the prices usually go down? Are you noticing a trend, reader? This place generally does everything on the cheap, and yet their prices are fairly high. There are no technical servers. You walk up to the counter, order, and they'll bring your food to your table. Drinks are self service so at the counter they will offer you a choice of soda fountain or a bottled drink, including bottled water. Their tea and green tea options are limited to a bottle of Peak's green iced tea. Everything is plastic ware, the utensils, the soy sauce plates, the small plates. The only things not plastic are the dishes they bring the food on. I hope the rest is all biodegradable, cause they're producing a lot of garbage. The food was good, but not good enough to justify the prices. My miso was tepid and only filled half the bowl. The rolls were good, but certainly not great. The price is definitely not justified. Most of their special rolls are based off a California roll. For instance, the Dragon roll is a California roll with eel on top. That should not be $15, especially when the California roll only costs $4.95 Or how about this pricing decision. A spicy tuna roll is $6.99, a little bit steep, but not outrageous. A spicy tuna crunch roll is $8.99. The only difference is the addition of tempura flakes for $2. This place is weird. Everything is done on the cheap, and yet costs more than normal. Maybe they will work on this once they are open a little longer. I don't think I'm going to stick around to find out.

text: Performance Bike, a national chain, has a great, straightforward policy. From the website: "Performance will match any advertised price on the same item within 90 days of your purchase. Just bring in the ad, even if it's our own, along with your original Performance Bicycle receipt, and we'll gladly refund you 100% of the difference. We will also do the same for you at the time of purchase. " I bought two bikes from them about 2 weeks ago. One was available at the store and the other was an alternative version of a bike that was available at the store. For the second bike, I paid the price listed at both the store and on the website. The store would order the bike, and when it came in, build it and call me. No shipping fees. Everything went smoothly, and in a week, I had the second bike. About a week after that (yesterday), I visited Performance Bike's website and noticed that the price of both bikes had decreased by $50 each. This was great- I was eligible for a refund of the price difference according to the very straightforward company-wide policy. I went to the store with my receipts, mentioned this, and they had the manager come out to process the refund. He looked online and proceeded to tell me that since shipping on each bike is $48, that would eat almost all of my refund. There are several problems with this statement. First, the obvious: the company policy is clear in that if you find an advertised price ANYWHERE, clircular or internet, they will match it at time of purchase or refund the difference within 90 days of purchase. It makes no mention of shipping charges or actual cost. There is no small print. Second, if I had walked into the store that day and purchased the same two bikes, they would have charged me the online price, no shipping, regardless of whether the bike was currently in stock at the store, just as they had two weeks before. This is exactly the situation the policy covers! Third, the $48 per bike shipping charge was incorrect anyway. I went through the online process for the same two bikes, and the total shipping charges came to $30 dollars each. So I argued my point to the manager, who held to his position and told me, among other things, that I was the only customer he had come across who didn't understand their policy. So as I left the store, I decided to stop in the parking lot and call Performance's customer service number. I spoke to a representative who told me that the corporate policy is intentionally clear and straightforward with NO CONDITIONS OR EXCLUSIONS. She told me to simply try another location if possible, and when I told her that there were no other nearby locations, she asked me to go back in the store and ask for the phone number of the district manager. In case that didn't work, she gave me a direct number to the corporate office. When I went back in and informed the manager of this, he mouthed off some more comments about how difficult I was to deal with, questioned whether I had really talked to customer service (why wouldn't they have called him?) and finally agreed to process the refund. Now, its understandable (to some extent) when a store manager, for whatever reason, doesn't understand or doesn't want to apply a company-wide policy. But in addition to this, the manager was rude, impatient and dismissive throughout. Another comment he made was that I clearly didn't understand online shopping. I decided to review my experience here because it was a particularly shocking example of bad customer service. Overall, Performance Bike is a great store with items you won't find at local bike shops at unbeatable prices. They also have a good price guarantee. Just make sure you hold them to it.
label: NEG

text: Noble is one of the few restaurants in Philly which really does Restaurant Week right. After disappointing meals at Tangerine, Chifa and XIX over the past year, I'm really happy to have found a place that can actually prepare a decent meal despite the increased stress. Here's a breakdown of my experience: The Good: 1) The alcohol selection. The beer list is well selected and reasonably priced (12oz bottles are $4.75), ranging from local favorites like Yards Brawler to beers I've never heard of like Two Brothers Domaine DuPage. The one cocktail I tried was fantastic - I can't remember the name (next time I should really take notes) but it was a scotch based drink with lemon and dill and was exactly the type of drink I love. I'll be back for the bar. 2) The décor. It's almost worth going to Noble just to check out the bubinga bar. I can't imagine how much it must have cost. I didn't get a chance to go upstairs, but after reading other reviews I'm sorry I didn't. 3) The dessert. The chocolate pecan pie was amazing, one of the best desserts I've had in Philadelphia. I'm surprised others were disappointed - I was truly impressed. The Less Good: 1) The service. Our waitress was pleasant enough, but there was a 20-minute dead zone between our first and second courses. All of us were staring at our empty drinks and plates, wondering where the servers were. Other than that incident the service was fine, and it was Restaurant Week after all, so I'm not taking away too many points here. 2) The non-dessert food. Some dishes were fantastic - the arctic char reminded me of a breezy day at the beach in June (in a good way) - but a few dishes missed the mark. I tried the fries that came with a friend's burger and found them to be underwhelming, and the cauliflower salad was flavorless aside from the cauliflower itself. Given that I'm a pretty skinny guy and I was hardly stuffed after four courses, I had to deduct a star for these couple of misses. All-in-all, I'd give the restaurant week experience a 5, despite the hiccups. It's only restaurant week for 4 weeks a year, though, and I suspect I'd be less satisfied if I was paying full price. Either my wallet or I would have left only half full, and the food wasn't quite good enough to justify either of those feelings. I will almost certainly return for drinks, though.

text: I ate there yesterday for dinner. First, I have to comment about h m.'s review. I have doubts about the review, mainly because the restaurant is owned and operated by a husband and wife team. She handles the front of the house, and he is the chef. She is extra friendly and goes out of her way to make sure you are comfortable, and happy, and she takes the time to speak with each customer. Hot and Sour Soup was outstanding. We shared a moo shoo pork. It was a large serving, with four pancakes (could have used six, but never got around for asking for more). text: Carmel Farmer's Market is a three year old's paradise and a grownups excuse to take a three year old out to paradise early Saturday morning. Local vendors abound, making this the true one-stop shop for all things local to Indiana. Strolling through here, one can find things both good and good for you, like organic veggies and dark chocolate truffles made with organic ingredients. One must first stop by Three Sisters & Him with the fresh made waffles made from dough - not batter! The cookie-like waffle is worth skipping breakfast at home for this. Make sure to enjoy it while sitting in the Japanese garden, or watching the ducks eat the kettle corn thrown by the tots. Then, make sure to pick up a steamy bag of kettle corn from Olde Tyme Poppin Corn to enjoy your self, while you watch it made right in front of you in a kettle that just might be a hundred years old, sitting over a smokey wood burning fire. Next, pick up some organic truffles at Literally Devine, plus a few more at several other chocolate and pastries vendors. Then top off your coming week's worth of yumminess by indulging in some of Boyd's Fudge from the venerable Westfield confectioner. This past Saturday, Rainbow Sherbet fudge was featured, and it was a miracle in my mouth! My taste buds were fooled into thinking I was eating ice cold rainbow sherbet. Absolutely amazing! And what would a market be without fresh flowers? Get a half-dozen Indiana grown sunflowers to brighten up your home, or just one for your daughter's hair to make her the Sunflower Princess of Paradise. Make sure to bring plenty of cash and a recycled grocery bag or knapsack to haul your plunder back to the real world. The rest of your Saturday will feel more blissful now that you have been able to visit Heaven on Earth. Peace.
label: POS

text: Restaurants are sort of like lovers - when you find one you really like, it's very difficult to get used to a new one. Even if your lover leaves, you can't just put a new one in the same place and expect things to be perfect. You can paint the walls and change the tables, but for all intents and purposes, you're not going to erase the memory of what once was. That's sort of how I felt when someone decided to open a recycled Asian Fusion joint in the same spot the very popular Zoe Pan Asian once sat. Even more curious is the fact that the new owner knows Zoe and even got to keep a few of the same recipes. The decor is only slightly different, but even that feels strange. The food was good, though, but again, not even the leftover items from Zoe taste as they once did. The wok-seared beef and udon noodles with green beans was good, but...well, you know. My wok-seared citrus glazed salmon with stir fried udon and snow peas, leek, red peppers and shiitake was indeed delicious, but had pad thai noodles instead of udon. I miss my spicy salmon and red pepper vermicelli noodles (sigh). The crispy fried noodles with five spice powder you get when you sit down are the same. Equally delicious. And the mango iced tea is still there. Yummy. Sweet potato french fries were perfect, and four of us fought tooth and nail for the last one. But where is my roasted banana with toasted coconut and coconut creme anglaise? Why is there a key lime tart and orange pot de creme in its place? The menu looks great and the food was good, but I still felt like I was cheating. Or maybe I just wasn't ready to get back in the game. Didn't I sit in this chair before? Yes, I did. Here in the corner, a watermelon martini in hand. I was smiling, caressing the sides of the glass lovingly. I didn't want to let go. Maybe I still don't.

text: When I was laid off last year I had applied to restaurants so I could have a fall back job in case I didn't find another "professional" job. I was actually hired by the Broad Axe management and through my interview I could tell the owners were really excited about the new restaurant, which in turn made me excited. A week before training was to start, I was offered an office job and I never did reenter the restaurant business. Fast forward a year and a half, and the boyfriend and I FINALLY made it to dinner at the Broad Axe Tavern. We will definitely come back again. I really enjoyed the bread and tapenade with olive oil that they bring as soon as you sit. I'm a big fan of what I call the bread course, so any restaurant that has one gets a gold star. Boyfriend had a Green Flash IPA and I had a house pinot noir since I was feeling cheap, but luckily it was good! I had the ahi tuna awesomeness, i mean, ahi tuna burger. It's chopped tuna mixed with fresh ginger (yum!), shallots, and I think carrots? I dunno, it was fantastic and I loved the gingery mayo it was topped with. Boyfriend had the barbeque black angus sliders and he liked those as well, though he thought more cheese would have been good since the barbeque sauce was sweet, in his opinion. I figured he would have ordered different beer since the menu is pretty good, but he was enjoying the green flash so he stuck with it. Next time we go I might just get the mussels, though I do want to try the portabella cheesesteak and the veggie burger. I thought the bottled beer selection was overpriced, though it was good. The man really likes Saison duPont and I can't even remember if he paid $15 for it at Tria, but memory might say no because the last time we were there was for his birthday and I'm a tighwad with money. But I'm wrong ever so often. Bottom line, we will be coming back!

text: Fall Creek Trail and Greenway is beautiful! I was able to run along this 12 mile planned trail and the scenery is fantastic. There is plenty of shade along the trail so in the summer or during very sunny days the heat isn't overwhelming. I must say that between miles 10-11 the trail is especially beautiful. You can hear the creek's water rushing and see the water between the trees. It was enough to make me think of moving to Portland so I can be in awe of my surroundings all of the time. The trail does follow along the road and sits between the road and the creek for the majority of the length. That said, NO WATER. But, on the up side the trail is uninterrupted. You don't have to stop for street lights, traffic. There are places where the trail can be rather narrow so be aware of your surroundings and listen for the fellow trailblazers "to the left". I'm a big fan!

text: Ok, so I'm absolutely boggled why people are so in love with this place. It is a complete and total rip off. If you can't find better local steak you must live in India. Neat fact - they actually have a stand in the airport in Omaha. I've tried several offerings from this place with gift certificates given to me from friends, and I just don't get it. The meat is frozen, for starters, and yes, it's vacuum packed, but even with careful defrosting you're not getting the same taste as fresh steak. I will give you the meat is tender, but seriously - six four ounce fillets are $84 plus shipping, so figure $100. That's over $65 a pound! You can get good Kobe for that! (Note - not great Kobe, but good Kobe). Plus the taste just isn't there to warrant this price. I guess I'm spoiled buying from Burt's Farms up in Gilbertsville, but his meat is delicious, you actually taste depth and flavor. Heck I can tell whether the cattle are grain fed or grass fed when I buy his fresh meat as you can literally taste the undertones in the meat itself. Not so here. I mean, yes, it's good, but not $65 a pound good. I'll spend $28 a pound and get some prime aged ribeye at Wegmans any day versus fillets from here. Oh, I do notice their dog treats are $5.99. For 3 oz. Hmm - that's OVER $30 A POUND. Save your money and just buy your dog prime aged ribeye at Wegman's. It's cheaper and tastes better!!

text: The latest in a large Arizona restaurant chain located on the Northwest side of Tucson at Oracle Road and River Road. I've never been to any of The Good Egg locations until they decided to open one in my part of town. When I venture out of the neighborhood, I got to Bobo's. Let's start with the decor. Awful. The worst kind of country crap. Puffy gingham window coverings. Rooster/Hen border wallpaper and lots of sunflower border treatments everywhere. I like bright and cheery, but the outdated and old fashioned country diner is boring and non-creative in it's simplicity and predictability. It also conjures a sense of poor taste (for me) and poor taste in decor sometimes translates to the quality of food. I've been to some really bad country diners in the south, and it ain't pretty. Second, the coffee was strong - but not in a good way. I prefer strong coffee, but there was something weird about this and it didn't get any better with subsequent refills. It just tasted funky. Third, when the server first approached our table of two, he asked if we wanted coffee by saying, "How about some coffee for the two of us?" ...WHAT? "For the two of us?" Where did he fit into the "two of us" part of the equation? He then continued to address us in the "We" and "Us" sense that totally bugged me. Sorry, I don't like it when the server invites him/herself to the party. Next, I noticed that the prices seemed high. This is a country diner open for breakfast and lunch, not a fancy restaurant. But, I waited to see what the portions and presentation were about before I made my final decision. The food came and I WAS surprised. My wife's Denver omelette cost $7.95. It was a three egg omelette with ham, peppers, and onions. She said there was very little ham. The small serving of potatoes and a toasted english muffin sat separated from the eggs on a large, cold plate. No garnish. No juice on the side. Pathetic! I ordered a skillet breakfast with two medium poached eggs over potatoes, chorizo, black beans, roasted chilis, guacamole, and sour cream. The eggs were not medium, they were on the shy side of over-easy - meaning the egg whites weren't fully cooked. That ain't medium. The "roasted chilis" consisted of one half of a roasted jalapeno chili. Hmmm, weak. This was all served in one of those oven-friendly clay skillets atop a large plate. The skillet was cold, and soon after, so was my food. I ate about half and finally got tired of eating a cold breakfast. The server came around again and asked, "Are we done?," and I told him about the cold food served in cold serving dishes. He grabbed "our" plates and said "we" would talk to the manager. "We" waited for a while and nothing happened. They weren't busy. There were plenty of people standing around. My wife saw the server talking to the manager, then they both went in back. I finally got up to leave and headed for the cashier (another reason they shouldn't charge so much for their food). When we got up to the counter, the cashier and an unidentified person asked about our food. I told them what I thought and they asked if we had spoken to the manager. I said that we had not, and then I noticed that he was standing right behind us. He never said a word. I told the two people at the register, "Good luck," and we walked out without incident. The Good Egg is ROTTEN and we won't be going back. Overrated and Overpriced!
