text: This place bills itself as "The Cupcakery Boutique". I had to stare into the window for a few seconds before figuring out that, yes, it was actually cupcakes they were selling in there, because it looked like some combination of a jewelry store, a clothing boutique, and my grandmother's living room with a baker hoarding supplies in the back. "Be still my heart!" said my heart as I walked through the door and laid eyes upon the glass-windowed cabinets filled with a veritable bombardment of baked extravagances. I was greeted with a good deal of enthusiasm and directed to a menu. There is quite a good selection, with all the obligatory classics. My opinion, though, as always, is that if you're going to get one cupcake right, it had better be the red velvet, so red velvet it was. The man at the counter packaged the adorably Christmasy-decorated cupcake with its shiny red foil wrapper into an inverted cup with pop-on lid and gave me the cupcake to go. I wanted to eat this cupcake on the spot, but I wanted even more for this cupcake to be as perfect as possible, so I waited until I got home and put it in the microwave for a few seconds (which I highly recommend). "Please, cupcake," I whispered, as he stared up at me from the counter. "Please don't let me down." He obliged. Holy cow, did they get the red velvet right. This was probably the moistest cake I've ever tasted in a cupcake, but the cake also had a sorta-crunchy outside layer which was both pleasant and useful in holding the cupcake in one piece. The cream cheese icing was perfect (I think the microwaving set it off). It was normal sized, but slightly small for the $3 price-tag; however, it was more than worth it. Welcome to the city, Philly Cupcake. Welcome to the city and welcome to my life.
label: POS

text: So my girlfriend recommended Aveda after they did a bang-up job on her nails. Having observed the endless procession of garishly tatooed, heavily coiffed beauties chain smoking outside the school on my daily bike commute to work, I figured it'd be a good excuse to have a pretty chicky give me a scalp massage, and maybe I'd get a decent haircut out of the bargain. The student working on my hair was prohibited from using clippers, even though he used them to cut his own hair. My haircut took two hours and failed miserably. He cursed under his breath on occasion, carefully silent in proximity to the hovering instructors orbiting the room. The instructors, though eager to shove him aside every few minutes to ''show him how it's done,' failed to salvage my head. Would I go back? I bet it will be a nice place to sit and have a drink once the weather gets warm. The service on both days was impeccable. Both our servers were cheerful, pleasant, and professional. Overall, a fun place to eat and drink with friends.
label: POS

text: Midtown II is a fun spot with a diner-style counter, and ample booth and table seating for those who prefer them. Open late, they're a tasty option when the munchies attack. I was here after an after party, around 5 AM. (It's always fun to observe fellow patrons, wondering what party they came from, who else is hungover, or what job they're starting/ending for the day.) Early morning food has a way of rousing one from a drunken stupor for a bit. I had two eggs (any style), with potatoes, toast, and Canadian bacon for about $6. My breakfast was deliciously filling and deliciously greasy - and didn't break the bank. Service was friendly, quick, and sympathetic - a few friends were out of commission, and luckily our waitress was patient, took our orders in stride, and brought everything right out.
label: POS

text: They were really nice there. I just didn't care for the haircut I got. From the outside it looks like the place is super trendy and hip and stuff, but i felt like i looked like my mom walking out of the salon. And I know it's my own fault for not asking them to fix it, but I have a "pleasing others" issue and I think the hairdresser could've done a better job. I felt like there was too much "theory" and "feeling" and not enough cutting and styling. Not my cup of tea.
label: NEG

text: The only saving grace about this place was the history. Other than that save your money and stay at one of the newer hotels (although they are remodeling this place with a 3 year renovation. God know it needs it). When I checked in the front desk staff were rude. They treated us like were were in their way and taking up their time. My room was a suite (just one down from the Presidential Suite, which is frickin' HUGE!). My room was very spacious with a long hallway, big bedroom and front room. However it smelled so old and dusty that I wanted to check out immediately. Instead I stayed two days. I did check out one day early though and stay at another hotel down the road. Ok back to the hotel. The restaurant inside had decent food. The prices were really cheap too. I was surprised. The history of the hotel is amazing. It was cool walking around and experiencing that. The staff were useless. I asked for another blanket and they said they would bring it up immediately. Apparently "immediately" means never to them. When I called they said "Oh yeah we'll bring it right on up". Again...nothing. So I went downstairs and they said they were out of blankets. "WHAT?????" On my way back to the room I see a hotel maid with a cart and she had about 6 blankets on it. "Thank you that one's mine!". I would never stay at the Biltmore again. Not a chance!
label: NEG

text: Let me just say right off the bat that I really like breakfast food - eggs made any number of ways, light, fluffy pancakes, bacon, stuffed french toast... love it all! So after my long rides on my road bike, I am always looking for a good place to sit and gorge at someplace that serves brunch. I have biked by this restaurant many times and did notice the nice breakfast smells emanating from the place but always a little skeptical of a restaurant that looks worn-down from the outside. But I finally stopped by last Saturday morning and had some breakfast. It was surprisingly okay. I had the omelet and my friend had the french toast and they both were pretty decent. We also had the grapefruit juice (pretty fresh and not too sweet) and coffee (kind of watered down but free refills). For me, the portion size was pretty big and they have outdoor seating which was nice since were were able to prop up our bikes on the side and keep an eye on them while we were eating and no one minded that we were dressed in our biking jerseys and covered with road grime. So why four stars? Well, I would give it 3.5 stars if possible but to me, I am really leery of a place where the silverware doesn't look that clean. A couple of things were a little disconcerting - the flying insects that were around (yes, I do realize I was eating outside but when I was ordering inside, still!). Overall, the place didn't scream "clean" at me but I guess that could be part of the rustic ambiance :) Lastly, the potatoes that came with my omelet was a little burnt but I'm not a fan of empty-carb sucking side dishes anyways! There are more breakfast foods on the menu and i will have to come back and try some other dishes but i did take a stroll around and unobtrusively looked at other people's meals that they looked pretty good. The place is pretty packed every Saturday morning I ride by so they must be doing something right! I haven't tried this place for non-breakfast food so I will have to come back and check it out. I am a fan of bacon so the Sonoran-hot dog may be enough to get me to come back.
label: POS

text: Horrific! Disgusting! Faux French Fare. Took my mother here for her birthday and was extremely disappointed. There were flies everywhere, the service was slow and the food was.... godawful. They were slow so there really was no excuse for the slow service. I ordered a steak that looked as if it was purchased at the local discount grocery chain Sav-a-lot, or perhaps across the street at the service station. The menu lacked ummm FRENCH FOOD. Perhaps they should change names or something. Not a bad place to have a drink but stay away from the restaurant.

text: The food is not very good, they fill the drinks with ice so that they can nickle and dime you on drinks, and the prices are much to high for what you get. There are better places to go for sure.

text: We had the weirdest experience here last summer! We came to Laurie's, to the patio, for beers in the evening. Except...the doorman looked threateningly at my friend (who is a pretty mainstream-looking though tall & skinny guy in his mid-thirties, and who looks exactly like the mild-mannered lawyer he is, actually??) and asked him if he "had a problem." Breakfast only served until 11am. WTF, really only 11 am?!

text: I enjoy good local brews, and when I heard that Upland opened a tasting room in Broad Ripple I had to stop by. I took a beer fanatic friend with me, and we ordered a tasting of 8 beers (all on tap). Now, I've never had an "authentic" beer tasting experience. I've sampled beer at festivals, and went to a lot of wine tastings, and both experiences are dramatically diffferent. My experience at Upland was disappointing and unimpressive in the least. The woman serving us had to ask for help from other staff because she wasn't versed in the beer, and without even tasting the beer they tried to sell us growlers. We sat down on a vintage couch and she brought our beer tasting over to us, explaining to us the layout and that it followed the beer menu. I grabbed the beer menu at our table and she said "Oh no, that is outdated, we need to update that, we don't have most of those" and then pointed at the chalkboard that was a good 20 feet or so away from us. We had to attempt to read the chalkboard as we sampled our beers, and instead of removing the incorrect menus, she just left it on the table. All of the beers we drank were unimpressed. I like pils, browns and reds - they only had a pilsener and Miller Lite had a more full flavored taste. The other beers were unsatisfying, and my friend, who travels nationwide for good beer, was unimpressed and disappointed by the assortment. The worst beer was a "smoked" beer, which tasted like it was skunked. As we were drinking our samples (which he drank them all basically, not wanting to waste) the staff didn't check on any of the tables, they hung out behind the counter, and then proceeded to put fish in their tv fish tank. The woman who waited on us was bent over next to my friend, putting the fish in the fish tank, and her pants were scooting down her butt - she had no underwear on!! Here she was, with her butt crack hanging out, serving beer. Sure sure - people go commando all the time - but, to see it up close and personal (two feet away) while we're drinking our mediocre to bad beers, was gross. Real sanitary. I went up to the counter, paid for the beer, and she didn't ask if I wanted a growler this time, but, we thanked them and left. The decor is rather coffeehouse like, with vintage book shelves, bright colors...very...Bloomington. There are only certain days when you can order pints, and they do have growler specials on certain days. Overall a really dissatisfying experience, and I'm not sure if I'll ever go back. I have a feeling the other reviews here will be more positive, but, I'll take Sunking and Barley Island anytime.
label: NEG

text: This cafe near the UNR campus was the locale of my annual fantasy baseball auction, so I can say that the back area is good for a small group meeting or event. Plenty of tables and chairs, friendly service, and coffee that's good enough for closers. My food though was below par. The bagel, cream cheese & lox was so tough that chewing it it damn near induced a TMJ disorder. Since I won't be back in Reno in the foreseeable future, I'll give these guys the benefit of the doubt that their grub is usually better. The atrocious outfield I put together, however, was all of my own making. There's no excuse for Pat Burrell being my #1 OF.

You order and pay first so I thought, this better be good... Unfortunately it was not... My burger was okay but the bun was too thick and old... seemed like it was left out for days... My wife's salad was good and they gave you plenty of fries... It was an okay place but not enough for me to go back... Lower the prices and improve your buns and maybe I will consider coming back again...

text: This BYO could probably fit inside my studio apartment. Yes, it's noise. Yes, it's crowded. Yes, I was seated 2 inches from my neighbor. But if anything the atmosphere adds to, rather than detracts from, the food. And the staff pulls-off service in a manner that's both effortlessly graceful and incredibly efficient. The vodka sauce is amazing. Really! I ordered extra bread just so I could lap-up every last drop of it.

text: Had heard good reports of this restaurant, was not disappointed. This is one busy Dim Sum restaurant, the food was very good, very authentic and very fresh. Fried items were not greasy, and the service is excellent. I love their Sticky Rice & Jumbo Shrimp Dumplings, my wife is a fan of the Steamed BBQ Pork Buns and their Crispy Spring Rolls. A Sunday morning favorite.

I have to say probably the best burger I tried in Philly. I know there are couple other places i should try before i say this, but so far so gooood. It was big, meaty, juicy and tasty - all you want from a burger. Try it!

text: This is the best hidden and over looked restaurant on The Hill. I almost hate to yelp it for fear that it will be discovered and I will lose my never have to wait for a table place down there. The restaurant is small and does not offer an extraordinary menu. However, it has all the great Italian fare you could hope for. All the standards are there, like fettucini, lasagna, and an array of pizzas to make your arteries clog, and the salads are delicious and large enough to fill you up, even though it's just lettuce. The service is amazing at this place too. I have never had a bad waiter. They are always super friendly and take incredibly good care of you. You will feel compelled to leave a good tip, so just be forewarned. I have no idea why this place has not been discovered yet, but it has not. I love that. You can always get a table, and you will be seated, given your food, eat your food, feel stuffed to the brim, and be on your way home while you would still be waiting for a table at Zia's or Cunnetto's...love that.
label: POS

text: I don't typically review a place I've only been to once, but I don't envision going back to Balada's, so... I went for lunch recently, about 1:30. There was one other customer in the place. This on a very pleasant weekday in downtown St. Louis. I ordered a sandwich and a Coke (actually a "pressata" and a Coke). Came to almost $9. This is why I bring my lunch to work most days, because it's hard to get a sandwich downtown that isn't overpriced. But $9? Come on. Then, when it arrived... well, in my experience, Cuban sandwiches and barbecue pulled pork sandwiches are two different things. But apparently Balada's sees it differently. While the menu mentioned pickles, onions, mustard and cheese in "The Cuban," all that was between the "pressata" buns was a big slab of pulled pork drenched in barbecue sauce (there may have been some tiny onions in there, but it was hard to tell). I was really looking forward to a Cuban. Instead I got pulled pork. And I can assure you, I've had better pulled pork. So here I am, eating an overpriced sandwich I didn't order, in a nearly deserted cafeteria style "bistro" in the center of our depressing-ass downtown, and it occurs to me, is that Celine Dion on the radio? It is. And so's the next song. And the song after that. The third one was even God Bless America. It appears they were playing an entire album of the overwrought Quebecois songstress. By this point, I'm about ready to shoot myself. Fortunately, I finished my crappy pressata and left before things deteriorated further. I will say, the people working there were nice. But I'm not inclined to go back.

I was turned off that all the food was served with disposable plates/utensils. What a waste of plastic when they could have had real dishes like most other non-fast food places do.

The meals are all a good portioned size and exactly what they promise on the menu, as well as the desserts. We love the Tri Formaggio, Cortina, and Genoa. For dessert my favorites are Chocolate flour-less cake with Raspberry sauce and creme brulee, nothing is super special about these desserts but they are both well done. If you want upper-level casual and fun on any given night this is the place to go.

text: Ever have a hankering to go to gym at 4am? Yeah me neither, but if you ever did I have the perfect gym for you. Planet Fitness is open 24 hours a day Monday 12am to Friday 9pm and 7 to 7 weekends. This gym doesn't have group classes or a pool or a smoothie bar, but it does have a ton of cardio equipment and weight machines. It's your basic no frills gym at a really good price. I only pay $10 a month and there's no contract. I usually go after work around 7 and there's never a wait for anything. I doubt I'll return to this California Tortilla location.

text: I don't get it. I really don't. I happen to enjoy a good cheesesteak, and I have tried all of the Philadelphia staples, and I just don't see what the fuss is about Dalessandro's. text: I went to Pub and Grub because they claim to be a sports bar in the Fairmount neighborhood. I decided to try it out because I'm a huge NFL fan and wanted a place to watch all the games. text: You can't argue that Cadence's Philadelphia location is staffed with talent. All of their coaches are great athletes in their own right. Being a stellar athlete, however, doesn't make you a great coach or mean that you understand the science of training. The bottom line - this place is run by kids who don't really understand exactly what they are doing and it costs way too much to deliver flawed service. I used Cadence for a performance measuring test back in December so I decided to use them again for the same test this April. After 3 months of training, I was shocked when the results showed a 5% decrease in performance. The coach performing the test was shocked as well, so he re-ran the test. Same result. Coach #1 called in Coach #2 for re-enforcements. After a huddle at the mound, they decided that I had been training improperly for the last 3 months. They made some quick edits to my training plan, explained where they thought I had gone wrong, and sent me on my way, less $150 and with a seriously battered ego. For the endurance athletes reading this, I'm sure you'll understand when I say that this was a huge shock to my system. I was so miserable that I went home, ate two plates of nachos and napped the rest of the afternoon. Unable to fathom how this was possible, the next day I went over to another multisport store in Philadelphia for the same test. I didn't tell them the situation (until after the test results), so it would be considered a "blind" re-test. Result? C'mon people, you know where this is going. A 12% increase. Swing between the two tests = 17%. When I explained the situation to the coach from Store #2, he was shocked that Cadence would have let me walk out of their store with results like that. To me, this shows two fatal flaws with Cadence's service. First, they don't understand the science enough to know when something goes wrong. Like my dad says about why I should have been an engineer instead of a computer scientist - "If you build the black box, you'll understand how it works inside, know when its not working properly, and know how ti fix it. But if you just use the black box, you won't be able to tell when something isn't working and even if you do, you won't know what the problem is." Second, because they are such great athletes that currently compete on their own, their focus isn't on coaching or the clients, it is on themselves. Coach #1 from Cadence offered to e-mail me yesterday with some more feedback on the test and training advice. Never happened. Moreover, he probably didn't even stop and think about what a mistake like that can do to an athletes' psyche. When you are on mile 86 of a 112 mile bike ride, and you are slogging up that hill wondering if you've got what it takes or not, do you really want to question whether you blew 3 out of your 6 months (50%!!!!) of your training? Who knows what would have happened if I hadn't decided to get the test done at Store #2? Mistakes like that are how you loose clients. You've lost me.

text: The Natural Cafe is one of my regular choices for healthy, vegetarian food. The restaurant is a small chain that extends throughout Santa Barbara and Ventura County. The vibe of the restaurant is very environmentally conscious, and encourages customers to do their part to help out. It doesn't push any sort of morals upon anyone, but the food isn't the only thing that makes you feel healthier! Natural Cafe is open for lunch and dinner, and suitable for a nosh break in between classes, or even a casual rendezvous before a movie date. It also features many delectable treats and snacks. For lunches, the sandwiches reign supreme. Both the eggplant sandwich and portabella mushroom sandwich are perfect, and the employees are always okay with substitutions regarding most things as well. I get my sandwiches with hummus instead of cheese, and they never fuss. They have three varieties of veggie burgers, which is always why i pick other things, i can't decide which one is most appealing. The sandwiches are served with a smaller portion of blue corn chips and salsa, but you have the options of adding on a salad, which i do when i'm feeling more hungry. Many vegetarian and vegan options are available for dinner plates, and they range from american to healthy mexican adaptations. The vegetarian tamale is very hearty and is served with a generous helping of rice and beans. The rice is something i really like about the natural cafe! They use a short grain variety that is simply perfect in texture... The yogi special is another one of my favorites. The sauteed tofu here is prepared excellently; It is very firm and flavored with ginger and soy glaze. For salad dressings, the tahini is great. The tempe tacos are also great if you take them for what they are. Certainly not lard filled meat filled authentic mexican food, but a healthy alternative that is even available with soy cheese. The meal doesn't end at savory at The Natural Cafe! The establishment also offers a variety of shakes and smoothies, as well as delectable desserts such as cakes and cookies. The milkshakes are my favorite, especially because being vegan, it is hard to come by a milkshake in Santa Barbara. You can ask for soy for an extra dollar, and it's worth the four dollar price tag. The chocolate one is okay, not nearly chocolately for my expectations, but try it with peanut butter and it transforms to scrumptious. The espresso variety is also great. The vegan chocolate cake is pretty great, not dry like many other vegan chocolate cakes at restaurants. Not enough icing, but hey, it's healthier that way.

text: I've only been in a few actual English pubs, which were either overrun with American tourists, who are twice as irritating abroad as at home, or the English, who drink like blackouts are a religious obligation. The Crown and Anchor is more like the English pubs of my imagination: dark wood, dim coziness and a congenial atmosphere. It's covered in fascinating bric-a-brac, mostly mugs and old British advertising. The little touches are homey and endearing, avoiding the belligerent, fantastical contrivance of other bars and restaurants that try to create ambience by sticking farm implements on the walls. Here, it just works. The beer is good. They serve a fairly small selection, and are often out of the couple of popular and rare specialty brews they serve. I really like the Tetley's, but the supply chain is apparently one old man in a rowboat, who is further delayed by a fox, a bag of grain and a duck. You do get a full 20oz Imperial pint. As for cocktails, they're not bowler-hatted, sniffing Williamsburg mixologists, out to ruin everyone's fun by turning the cocktail into a play-acting fetish. Ask politely and be considerate, and you'll probably get a good cocktail. I would not recommend demanding a shiso-infused grappa appletini; it will enrage your friendly bartender, taste like lip gloss dissolved in nail polish remover, and make you look a right twit. The service is casual but generally effective, particularly if you are mindful of your basic civilities. The bartenders may not look it, but all are grizzled veterans and know your tricks and shenanigans. The crowd seems fairly local and fairly regular, and is more friendly than, say, the Old Point Bar. Food is limited to convenience snacks with a British pub theme (Walker's Crisps and Scampi Fries). They have darts, but playing on a crowded night would be inadvisable because of space limitations. There's also well-attended pub quiz on Thursdays Executive summary? It's a great little local bar, worth a visit even for non-locals. It's got character, or maybe is a character. Either is shockingly rare in New Orleans, which is so often a city contrived for tourists, or contrived to be unfriendly to anyone who went to the wrong high school (I swear, they treat high school like a secret handshake). And whoever stole the poster from the gents', you're a horrible jerk and the prime reason why we can't have nice things.

text: I was staying with a friend in West Chester this week and we decided to try the new Mas restaurant that recently opened in town. We'd heard from friends that the food was only "so-so", but we decided to give it a try anyway. We arrived at 6pm on a Tuesday night when Mas was three quarters empty. There were many empty booths and tables but the woman who greeted us seated us at the table closest to the front door and her podium. The only reason we could think of was that she was too lazy to walk any further. She gave us two menus and told us the name of our server. We picked out drinks and appitizers and went on to reading about our dinner selections. The menu looked interesting and we each found something we liked. By this time 10 minutes had passed and we still hadn't seen our server. We saw servers going to other tables. A server cleaned off a table next to ours and looked over at us, but didn't ask us if we needed anything. Another 5 minutes went by, another server cleaned a table and as she walked by us we asked where our server was. She said she would get her. Another 5 minutes went by, still no server. At this point we decided that an interesting menu was no excuse for such inept service and we decided to leave. We told the greeter why we were leaving and she appeared disinterested saying "Come back again" as we exited. Yes, we could have made a bigger effort to track down our server, but why should we? We're the customer in a mostly empty restaurant with more than enough servers flitting around. What could our server have been so preoccupied with and why didn't one of the other servers cover for her? Covering for each other, even if it's not their table, is one of the signs of a well trained server in a good restaurant. After we left we went down the street to the Landmark Americana. We mentioned to the greeter of the experience we'd had at Mas. We were seated and our server was to our table within 2 minutes to take our drink order. When she brought our drinks she said that the manager would buy our next two because of the bad experience we'd had at Mas! The food was great, the service was great, the manager turned a bad experience at Mas into a great experience at Landmark. In a town like West Chester, word gets around fast about new restaurants. Based on our experience, Mas won't make it 6 months unless they start hiring servers who are proficient. If the food and drink at Mas had been even so-so I probably would have given them three starts, but because of the service I never had a chance to sample the food so I've given them only one star.

I knew there was going to be trouble as soon as I saw the menu. I didn't see a single original-looking dish. Many of the names had been changed from Thai to English (what is a "Thai taco"?). It didn't look promising. I should have stuck with that instinct. Thai food is supposed to have subtle and complex flavors. Thai Tanic didn't get the message. My scallop dish tasted overwhelmingly of ginger and not much else. The waitress brought a small bowl of red pepper, saying the chef had forgotten to add it to the dish when he cooked it. My wife's curry was equally unsubtle: mostly coconut milk and not enough heat. Our son loved the Pad Thai, but then he's only 2 years old. The adults thought it was pretty awful. If you want to eat decent Thai food, skip this place and go to Nadia or Thai Orchid.

text: Confessing that, as a native Californian, I am anything but a cheesesteak aficionado - as in, I had never had one before (even the Jack-in-the-Box knock-offs, heaven forbid)--i had it stuck in my head that I must, simply must, have a real Philly cheesesteak since I happened to be in Pennsylvania for some business for almost a week. Seriously the whole flight over from the West Coast all I could think about was getting a cheesesteak. I was seriously obsessing. Anyway, meandering around in my rental in South Philly, a wonderfully traumatic experience in itself - I expected Rocky Balboa to emerge from around the corner - I was intent on going to Jim's Steaks since the online reviews I had read were most complementary, I never made it that far. As it happened that evening East Passyunk Ave was blocked off a bit north of Geno's and Pat's. I said to heck with it, turned around (quite a feat in that neighborhood), barely found a parking spot at 9pm on a Sunday evening and indulged in my first Philly Cheesesteak ever at Pat's. I got a cheese wit out and American. It was, to exaggerate only slightly, a religious experience. The taste of the cheesesteak is fabulous and the bread was soft, slightly toasted. In short - I loved it. My only mis-steak, so to speak, was not ordering two as frankly after a long flight and days of yearning for cheesesteak one was really not enough. Or at least an "extra cheesesteak" with the extra load of meat might have been enough. The line truly is fast, fast, fast - it just whips. Seriously, in seconds you have your cheeseteak - it's that quick. As for those asking if they take charge cards, I don't believe they do, probably mainly to keep the line moving. I didn't see any Visa/MC/AMEX signs around so I went to an ATM just across the street. Overall, a great eat, worth the experience of going to South Philly and eating the genuine article.

text: I have been to this Crackers about 10 times in the past 8 years. I do love to go there, but as one other person noted, the level of your satisfaction is directly related to the performer you go to see. I usually only go for A level comedians who have some national level of fame and a well developed act. You are going to see three comedians when you go. The first one is more or less the MC. They are comedians, but I am guessing they are someone who did well at an open mic night and are cheap to hire. The middle act is someone who is experienced and usually funny. Sometimes they are better than the featured comedian. After seeing the first two acts, then the featured comedian comes on and usually does a 30 to 60 minute show. My wife and I just went a month or so ago to see Kevin Pollak. He was very good but maybe a little overpriced. I guess it was fair seeing that he was a Hollywood star and we enjoyed all his stories about Hollywood people he knew. Emo Phillips was the best I have seen by far. His humor is so unique that you laughed during his entire show. I guess the secret to a fantastic experience is searching out their website and finding big name comedians who are coming in. As for the two purchase requirement, its OK. The drinks come with about 85% ice so you have to tell them no ice. The food is alright, but you sure don't go there for it. You have to feel for the wait staff. Trying to deliver your food and drink in the dark must be a real challenge but they do a great job. So go. Go once and see if you like it and if you do, you probably will go back. Once good way to tell if you comedian will be any good is to listen to Bob and Tom on the radio the week they are appearing. One down side to that is they usually use about 50% of their material in their act that they use on the radio, but the visual aspect of seeing the comedian do it is a better experience.

Neither shrimp nor lobster impressed me. For my linguini Alfredo I was expecting to get large and fresh shrimp that would be the star of the show, but in reality the shrimp were small, overcooked, and rubbery, and smothered in Alfredo sauce the main purpose of which was to cover up the poor quality of the shrimp. Lobster tail, on the other hand, was undercooked. There were raw patches inside, which neither butter nor garlic could disguise. And overall, the food tasted rather bland. If it wasn't for the nice atmosphere in the restaurant, and friendliness of our server, I would have sworn to never come back to Red Lobster. For now, however, I am willing to give it another try. text: I read all the reviews, consulted with my fellow foodies.. and all were praising this tiny restaurant for its "authentic Italian food." I beg to differ. It is small, cramped, and the seating was too close for my comfort. I did enjoy walking through the open kitchen upon arrival... but the meal.. I have had better in South Philly. The bread is warm, and very fresh. My bread plate had a huge chip on it... with so many servers running around, you would think that one of them would notice it, and trash it before it was placed on a table. The caesar salad resembled every other salad I've had in this city, minus the excess of dressing, which was a nice surprise. But still, it was an average salad. The mussels in red sauce tasted a bit on the fishy side, and cold. The red sauce was rather bland, and flat. On to the entree's... I ordered the Spaghetti Bolognese - which other bloggers & friends raved about. It was on the salty side, and needed more gravy. I had to ask for an extra side of red sauce - which made a world of difference; in both twirling the pasta, and adding to the flavor. I did not find the service to be great, nor did I get any "warmth" from the many servers that were running around. It all seemed very rushed, and chaotic. Needless to say.. we had 5:30pm reservations (the only time that was available...).. so I expected to have more of a "relaxed" dining experience, as opposed to a "fast" dining experience. My dining companions were not impressed with their meals either. Both commented that their entree's were lacking sauce, and spice. At the end of the meal, one of the wait staff asked us in passing if we wanted coffee. Not dessert.. but coffee. We asked what the desserts were, and the waiter appeared to be annoyed with this question as if we we were over extending our stay in the short hour that we were there... no coffee, nor dessert was ordered. I left, uninspired, and disappointed. This was not the great meal that I anticipated. I will continue to go to the many other great Italian restaurants that South Philly, and the rest of the city has to offer. By the way, this is the place that I chose to go for my birthday... good thing it was the night before, and not the day of. One last note.. never got the lemoncello shot at the end of the meal that they are supposedly famous for.

text: As an Asian California native, I've had my fair share of good sushi. Since moving to St. Louis, I've been on the hunt for decent sushi. Being that it is nearly right across from my apartment, Kampai was an easy find. I actually went to Chi Sushi and Drunken Fish before I tested out Kampai so it wasn't that I settled on the first sushi joint within reach. My first time there, I flew solo and sat at the bar, getting to know the sushi chef, Sean (unfortunately, he moved away). He learned of my affection for uni and gave me the lowdown on how they obtain their fish. A week later, I came back and was greeted by name by both the sushi chef and the waitress, Nancy. Both the waitresses - Nancy and Joy are absolute sweethearts (after introducing her to my now long-distance bf who came to visit, Nancy always asks to see how we're both holding up long-distance). Be nice to them! I've brought tons of friends here and they've all enjoyed the attention and service lavished upon them. My bf says you can judge a sushi restaurant by its miso soup. Why? It come standard with every meal and can be very easily slighted by the kitchen. If they care about the quality of their food, they will pay attention to the miso soup. Needless to say, Kampai's soup is fantastic. What I love THE most though, is their salad. I've never encountered another sushi restaurant that used the same sauce (I later found out they make the sauce themselves). It's light and fruity (made from a bunch of different fruits) and is probably my favorite salad dressing. Soup and salad come standard with each meal, don't skip out on it! I come here without fail every single week to get my sushi fix and it's the only place I go for sushi. Size-wise and creativity-wise, the sushi in St Louis simply cannot compare to the elaborate rolls they dream up in California. I've come to accept it, and have let it go. Tips: - If you plan to come here often, save yourself a few bucks in the long run and purchase the Kampai rewards card - a $5 fee will get you 3% back on every bill that you can accumulate to spend later. - The quantity of sashimi in the chirashi is the same for lunch and for dinner. The price is different. - Print out their Happy Hour coupon and get 25% off your entire bill Monday-Thursday 5-6 PM 5 stars for the sense of home they've given me!

text: Stonewood prides itself as an upscale, dinner-only restaurant experience..a bad experience I would have to add. I've been there twice in the past two weeks. The waiters are horrible actors, showing a fake kind of politeness to their customers, while still expected a hefty tip once the meal is complete, and that would be a LARGE tip considering the prices of their meals. The meals are like an appetizer at Ruby Tuesday, and don't taste much better than the Olive Garden, for double and sometimes TRIPLE the prices. I've had their Oak Grilled Burger, which had no real taste to it. Compare to the Cheesecake Factory, a real upscale restaurants, Kobe Burger that has a taste in the beef that just oozes out into your mouth without needing to add condiments and you find yourself with a DRY burger that tastes like cooked paper. Condiments are highly needed just to give it some kind of substance. In addition the french fries were horrible, I'd rather have McDonald's, Checkers, or dare i say it, BURGER KING (the most horrible french fry dealer on Earth, now second to most horrible). They had tons of seasoning on them, but the seasoning was of no help to the bland taste that came with them. During my next visit for my Aunt's 35th birthday (someone explain to me why restaurants do so horrible with birthday dinners, where they get so much business from, are they just nervous, or just ignorant of the impression they are making on fairly large parties), I had a lobster ravioli meal with my mother. For twenty-two dollars, we received three (yes three), small raviolis with a small amount of lobster sauce on top, and a kabob with shrimp on it. Frankly, I could have had more food anywhere else I can think of in my head. Clearly making this restaurant a, I'm rich so I'm just going to blow all my money on AIR and dark lighting kind of restaurant. First of all, let me say that we had THREE waiters in the same night. The waiters had no clue what had gone on with the waiter before them, and I'm utterly shocked that we received our meals at all. They actually had us tell them what we had at the end so that they could bill us, it would have been so easy to lie and just pay a small price after they took all our plates away. It's not always to be so honest, but alas we were. I had to track the waiters down for refills. The cup size they give you is slightly bigger than a shot glass, and their food is DRY. It just doesn't make any sense. The waiters half the time seemed to just ignore my glares for them to come and pay attention to me, the person who is controlling their tip. Like I said, I do not understand any of it. The only good thing at this restaurant, saving it from the taboo of one star is their exquisite clam chowder. It tastes amazing, they have the best recipe I have ever had. If I could get the clam chowder, and ignore everything else, that would be swell. I have never eaten clam chowder so quickly and indulged so much into a soup like I did into theirs. They should add a bread bowl and I would be SET. If it were up to me, the waiters would have received nothing in tips and frankly I would have probably complained to no end to the management. Since I was in the party of others, the restaurant was saved of my fury. Of course, I can't let them off that easily. This restaurant is such a wreck that I'm going to give them suggestions to make it better. 1. Get bigger glasses for drinks or make your food more MOIST. There are just no excuses for this. 2. Either lower your prices or add more food, you charge more than the Cheesecake Factory, which is utterly superior to you in every single way. 3. Turn the lights up a little. I didn't see barely any couples there in both my visits, the tables are too big for couples, and you can barely see your own hands in that kind of darkness. Take a note from the Cheesecake Factory, they don't leave their customers blind in the darkness while trying to have conversations and eat their meals. 4. Fire or re-train all your waiters, they suck. They don't know how to attend to peoples needs. That is all. Until we meet again.

I hate coffee shops that are just mirror images of each other (though I won't lie and say I don't go to "those" shops in a pinch-like at the airport when I need a jolt of energy). If I can avoid chains, I will, by all means. After all, I'm the girl who wore pants to my elementary school graduation when all the other girls wore dresses. I'm a rebel, darnit. I am a bit of a hippie, too. I love walking barefoot through the park in my flowing pink skirt. I love eating vegetables and listening to the Indigo Girls. I love sitting on a blanket and eating my veggie burger with Vermont cheddar (an old staple of Kaldi's which is sadly off the menu). I love herbal iced tea and homemade blueberry pie. Their Mediterranean salad with housemade tahini yogurt dressing and thick as paste hummus seasoned with a kick of chile are to die for. Goodness lies here. The outdoor seating area is peaceful, and makes you feel as if you're in northern Cali which, to me is a good thing. I love taking beverages across the street to Concordia Seminary's grassy knoll. Sometimes I even bring a frisbee so my friends can laugh at me. It's all there. Kaldi's has a formula no other shop can replicate. It's part intellectual, part artsy, part liberal, part quinoa-scented...part perfect.

text: I came to Ichigo Modern because I was a big fan of Sekisui Pacific Rim (the previous restaurant at this location) and was looking for a replacement. To test it out, I went for the lunch buffet. I know that lunch buffets are never that great, but I've found it can be a good test of quality - if you can't make decent, simple california rolls, I likely will not be impressed with your "signature" sushi. So I went in with low expectations. In my head, there are three sushi faux pas that should never be committed, and Ichigo Modern was guilty of all three of those. 1. Never make humongous sushi. Sushi should be small, bite-size. It's a dainty process of enjoying the freshness of the ingredients used. The sushi here is a disastrous explosion of mismatched components, and are unwieldy to look at and eat. 2. Never use cream cheese. Even if the crazy overstuffed sushi here was okay, I wouldn't have been able to taste it beneath the sticky, overwhelming cream cheese present in so many rolls. This is perhaps the easiest way to ruin a good piece of sushi - any flavor was drowned in my painstaking attempts to un-stick the gunk from my teeth. 3. Condiments on sushi are a no-no. Teriyaki sauce? Flavored mayo? If I wanted a flavor explosion I'd be eating Latin cuisine, certainly not Japanese. Several of the rolls were drenched in a variety of terrifying sauces, none of which tasted good or served any purpose. Not to mention it just looked dirty and messy. They also offered a selection of hot dishes; the caliber was about similar to Panda Express. I won't complain too much. I came for the sushi. If the food here wasn't bad enough, service was a disappointment as well - slow and disorganized. Plates were grabbed inconsiderately away as you barely finished eating, creating a jarring and unpleasant atmosphere. Ichigo Modern represents the complete antithesis of Japanese cuisine, with its clumsy, muddled, and unartfully thrown together "sushi" rolls. The saddest part is that the individual ingredients were actually quite fresh - what a pity.

text: The Second Mile Center is a series of second hand stores on one block. They sell everything under the sun, and they have the space to do it. I'm sure there's an interesting story here as to how they acquired so many properties, but that's a story I have yet to learn. Today, they are well-organized and very reasonably priced. Here you can buy electronics, furniture, luggage, housewares, and of course clothing. The clothing store is especially huge, but it's not so overwhelming because all the offerings are spaced out in aisles and aisles of racks. The property is a big square with a very high ceiling, so it feels spacious, which is nice. When it comes to quantity, Second Mile takes first prize. When it comes to quality, Second Mile is much lower on the thrift store list. They have a lot of junk in my humble opinion; however, as the owner of Toviah Thrift told me last year, just because I wouldn't buy something doesn't mean that nobody would. There certainly do exist thrifters who aren't concerned with trends, and I'm sure Second Mile gets plenty of those shoppers. While Second Mile has a lot of low quality items, it also has its share of gems. The ratio of crap to gems here is the same ratio as at Toviah Thrift; Second Mile is just a much larger, more organized property. Like TT, SM also had some religious affiliation. Definitely stop by--they have everything under the sun and it's all oh-so-wallet-friendly. Racks and racks of shoes, dresses, blazers, handbags, AND this place has sales from time to time. A thrift store holding a clearance sale? Yes, they do. Once my mom and I came here on Xmas eve and they entire inventory was being sold at half off. Pretty crazy. This block is positively magical when the weather is warm. Tons of trees, lovely Victorians in the area, not too much traffic. With the SM folks on the block, it's the type of place where you'd want to sit down and just chill for a while. There's just something about South 45th Street. When you visit, cross the street to visit the used furniture store with furniture that talks to you. Someone here tags the items with papers that - well, talk to you! Sometimes it's a story, sometimes it's general commentary, sometimes it's a snazzy one-liner. Even if you have no need for gorgeous vintage items that could never fit in your apt, come visit them to see what they have to say.

text: I finally visited this local legend and was not disappointed. The chili was great alone but the fixins are high quality and plentiful, i.e. unlimited sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese, onions, jalepenos, etc. I was surprised the fixins were help-yourself and I saw a guy with 1/2 a cup of sour cream and probably 2 cups of cheese on his chili. No, it was not me. Quit looking at me like that. The cheeseburger was sensational. The patty was clearly handmade, fresh and incredibly juicy. It was seasoned with just salt and pepper as far as I could tell but was wonderful. A little pricey at $14.27 for a cheeseburger, large bowl of chili and a large soda, but very fair for great food downtown. The interior is nicely appointed with dark colored hardwood but not stuffy at all. This is a nice place that I highly recommend. My only complaint at all is their choice of serving Pepsi instead of Coke, but I'll live. Enjoy!
label: POS

text: Update! Okay, so a year later we went back to try Rasoi again. This time my boyfriend and I were taking his parents. Last time my boyfriend and I went on our own we were forgotten and didn't get our food for quite a long time. This time, we were hoping for better. Well, that didn't happen. After waiting about 5 minutes for a hostess to even come greet us (too long if you ask me considering we were the only people waiting to sit down) we were given a table. After 10 minutes, yes 10 minutes ( we counted) of not having a single person come offer us water or take our drink orders we gave up and left. Yes, a couple of times we attempted to get the attention of the waiter who was helping the table next to us to see if he could find out who our waiter/waitress was but he pretty much ignored us. I mean, we were just short of standing up and waving our arms around to be noticed, so I don't know where this waiter's mind was. Now, I don't know why we were treated this way quite honestly. My boyfriend and I look young, both almost 24 but we look 20, so maybe that's why we were just forgotten the 1st time? Didn't look like important enough customers? I'm not sure about the 2nd time though. We were all appropriately dressed (casual evening clothes) and we even saw a girl walk out in ripped up jean shorts as we walked in so I don't think it was our dress. We were polite despite waiting too long to be given a table. Honestly, I've completely given up on this place. I've never simply walked out of a restaurant like that before, and I wouldn't have, except it was the second chance we were giving them to impress us, because yes, a customer/client should be impressed by a business they are giving money to, especially such a "nice" restaurant. I'm curious, has anyone else had these issues at Rassoi?

text: I came in here about a year ago and then yesterday. Quite a lot has changed. First the pros: Student 10% discount (yay for me). Fireplace - probably cozy during the winter. They now have an extended breakfast and lunch menu, with clever names after Washington locations - I was super stoked about the Whidbey Island Rice Salad (my hometown!) Now their pastries are from the House of Bread, which is great. The cinnamon roll I had was delicious. They are advertising they support local growers/businesses and that is good too. Now the cons: I went in just to get a cappuccino and pastry on my way out to work. I thought I'd be in and out in a few minutes but that was not to be. They were pretty busy yesterday morning, but there is absolutely no reason it should take ten minutes (let alone the fifteen plus I waited) for a coffee drink and a pastry out of their case. They had one girl running the register and one girl making all of the sandwiches and coffee drinks. So one staff member had to run around like a chicken with their head cut off while the other one, when not taking orders, sort of wandered around behind the register and did nothing. I had to remind them to make my drink and give me my pastry after some time, and after others had been served that came in after me. The girl at the register said they were backed up, and I could see there were problems with other customers besides me. I should not have to wait for all the sandwich orders to get made before I get my coffee. When I did get my pastry, they put it in a large styrofoam box for sandwiches or something. Don't play the sustainable/local card and then hand me something that will never decompose. The brand of coffee they use tasted extremely burnt as well. The reason I go on ad nauseum about this is because I wanted to support a local business and try something new for my morning routine. It turned out to be just short of a disaster. The atmosphere in there was akin to a daycare. Lastly, I looked at their menu and felt that it was extremely over priced. $9 for a breakfast burrito? No thanks. If I want another one of those rolls, I will just go to the House of Bread. Recommended for moms who want a latte and have some time and money to waste.

For the appetizer we got ground chicken wrapped in egg roll wrapper, deep fried and served with sweet chilli sauce. For dinner I was craving something really spicy and so I went with drunken noodles and my wife opted for rice with vegetables. The drunken noodles were just the thing I was craving...and the spicyness too. But beware the spice is not for the light hearted nor is it too hot if that's your thing. My wife's dish was pretty good as well. For dessert we got the mango ice cream and the only thing it had going for it was that it's homemade. text: We've been to the Landmark a couple of times to watch games. The western suburbs are lacking in a decent sports bar, so we had high hopes for The Landmark. On the surface, the Landmark looks pretty good. Nice old-meets-new on the outside, inside has lots of dark wood paneling, lots of TVs. Looks like they went for an old gentleman's club decor. The food is just ok - the menu is a bit more "upscale" than your typical sports bar - but that's not saying much, really. And even still, it's not executed very well. The descriptions make everything LOOK good - but when you get your meal its usually a disappointment. They have a decent burger, and the cuban sandwich is OK. We went to watch a big game and so we could get a seat, went to the downstairs section. Not sure exactly what this is - maybe on the weekend it's the dance club? It is also the smoking section - fine - we don't smoke but weren't complaining - but since it's in the basement it doesn't get aired out very well. So the whole space smelled like an ashtray, even though no one at the time was smoking. The sound system was screwed up down there - so that there was a ridiculous delay, which made the game maddening to watch. Everyone downstairs complained to the bartender, who just shrugged his shoulders and did nothing. He wouldn't speak with anyone who would. It was fixed only when someone went upstairs and found the manager. Then Voila! All good. Would that have been so hard for him to do? If we were to go back to the Landmark, it would only be to sit at the bar and watch a game. Not to eat the food. Not to go downstairs.
label: NEG

text: For members of two world religions, it is profoundly offensive to be offered ham. Last night I and my sisters went to Los Arcos for a bite to eat. We happily munched on chips while we waited for fish dinner. We distinctly made sure to order only dishes that had no mention of meat in the description. Everything was okay until my sister inspected closely and saw that her fish dish was laddered with pink and fleshy ham. No big deal. We'll just send it back but order something else. But here's where the problem starts. I called the owner/manager and explained that for religion reasons we cannot eat ham. I asked him kindly to take it back and bring us something else. He refused. He argues with us, "What am I going to do with this food. I cannot waste this food." He refuses to take it back even after I told him that I will pay for the dish even if we are not eating it. We asked for our checked and paid and left without eating anything. He didn't offer a replacement dish. Not even a measly salad. Worst service I received ever. My sisters are distinctly religious looking as they wear religious clothes. He owner/manager should have known that Jews and Muslim don't eat pork. Instead of being reasonable, he said he'll pick the pork out of the dish and suggested that my sister continues eat the meal. While we were leaving, the guy didn't even apologize a single time. He stood there and took our money even though we didn't eat our meal. The owner/manager also treated us in a condescending way. Before we discovered the whole pork fiasco, he rubbed his belly and asked if the food was "yum yum?" What the hell? We are adults in our twenties, not little kids. I think he thought since we are immigrants-looking we must not be able to speak English and he had to use baby-talk with us. This was funny and ironical since all of us grew up around English and are quite educated. As if this wasn't bad enough, the tables were extremely sticky. I wonder if they ever wash it with anything except remove the food. The tables also moved back and forth with slightest of force, which was very annoying. The few bites of food that I ate were not anything amazing or horrible either. Perhaps with a little bit more cleanliness and a better attitude, this place can be a visit-able place again. For now, never again! Stay as far away as possible unless you like being treated badly and like a child for average food.
label: NEG

text: Ok, let's be honest. I've had real Chinese food from the place on (I think) the corner of Olive and Hafner where the entire menu is in Chinese, no one speaks English, and husband and wife and fried chicken's feet populate the menu. Sure, that was good, but I'm a stupid American, and I love good old fried Americanized Chinese food. If you're like me, Shu Feng is the place to go. I spent four wonderful years at Wash U nearby and went to Shu Feng as many Fridays as I could for the $6 lunch special. By my senior year, I was literally family. The kind waitresses/owner had met my friends, my parents, and my girlfriend. It all started Freshman year, when my roommate showed me his parent's favorite Chinese restaurant, a hole-in-the-wall in St. Louis's small Chinatown. Within four years, I think I brought them more business than any Marketing Manager could even dream. My friends loved it, my friends of friends loved it, and I loved it. Literally, I felt that, as an honorable person, I at least owed Shu Feng the time it would take me to write them a review. This place has taken care of me and treated me like a friend, customer, and regular like no other restaurant in my life. Seriously though, go for lunch (before 3), get the General Tso's Chicken extra spicy, and an egg roll. You will NEVER regret it.

text: I'm re-evaluating this place from a 2010 review (it's 5/1/16). Used to live in No Libs, and sometimes am in the neighborhood. Just when I think it couldn't get any worse, the bus that is scheduled to come every 40 minutes just doesn't show up, leaving me standing in some of the not so nice neighborhoods in West Philly at night for an hour and a half, just waiting to be mugged.... Because you just never know; the bus could be late, it could be early, or it could not come at all... Although I'm being overly generous, one star goes for having a direct train line from the airport to the city that actually manages to run reasonably well. I award the other star for SEPTA's self awareness. They may not care that they are a sh*tty public transportation service, but they do acknowledge it, which is more than I can say for other public works in this city...

The food is fantastic, skip the apps and go straight for the fish. And order a lot - it's the freshest and most authentically crafted sushi I've seen outside of San Diego. The bill will rise rather quickly, but it's worth it for the quality of food, and the fact that you're supporting a local-one-man-band-stand restaurant. Eat well, and tip big!

text: OK, I will preface by saying I grew up in NJ and currently live in Boston so I am no expert on Southern home cooking. I was on a 2 day business trip to Nashville so looked on Yelp for a local favorite and found Sylvan Park with 11 five star reviews, so I pointed GPS and found the little place. I knew from the review that this place was not about the decor and that was confirmed...that is fine since the best food is often found in the most unassuming places. I ordered sweet tea, fried catfish, fried okra, mashed potatoes, mac & cheese, and corn bread.. I was thoroughly underwhelmed! I'll start with the best thing first...the catfish had a nice crispy yet thin cornmeal crust and the fish was moist and flaky. Nicely done. My main complaint about everything is that the predominant flavor is SALT! The mashed potatoes were the saltiest and that is without gravy...I can't imagine how much saltier it would've been with gravy. The mac & cheese was a step above Kraft but again very salty not cheesy. The okra was good as you really can't mess up a fried food. The last thing was that after several positive Yelp comments that the corn bread is a must order item, they were hard dry and again SALTY without any corn flavor. I will say that perhaps I don't have the necessary experience to appreciate Southern cooking...and if it is indeed the best...the maybe it's just not for me. I just had to share since I was disappointed after the rave reviews I read here. I wish I had gone to Prince's Hot Chicken Shack instead.

We were seated at an awkward shaped table in the corner. For a party of four, it was a bit bizarre. We were all crooked and conversation was a bit difficult. Our waitress was fine, nothing too remarkable. Efficient, which is what a good waitress should be. What's up with the small plate of pickles as an appetizer? If I go to Queens or Manhattan, I get a bucket overflowing with pickles. I got gipped tonight! Portions were plentiful, and the food was good. My burger was cooked well, and I enjoyed the fries and cole slaw. My dining companions enjoyed their sandwiches, however, their plates needed garnishes. Something more in terms of presentation. It was a plain white plate with the sandwich thrown on it. We're lovers of the arts; give us something pretty to look at as we eat it. Oh, and what restaurant charges to remove the extra fat from your meat? Um, WTF? I know Jewish food can kill me, but seriously, why should I have to pay more to stay alive longer? It just doesn't make sense. Be a mensch and cut the fat off for me for free. All in all, this is an okay place. There's certainly better restaurants to go to in Cherry Hill. I'd recommend you go to Short Hills at least once. You never know when it might burn down again.

text: Rocco's Steaks is the newest installment in one of those doomed restaurant properties. It used to be a water ice shop, then a drive thru coffee place and now Philly steaks. This is a drive thru or walk up establishment that boasts "the taste of South Philly on the Main Line" and "the freshest ingredients served daily with rolls baked fresh by Carangi Baking Company." Their menu has a selection of steak, chicken, and pork sandwiches. The sides are few - well, basically one - Fries. I don't consider lettuce or tomato sides although they will charge you $.50 extra to get them. Tonight we had two cheese steaks with onions ($7.50/ea) and an order Wiz fries (3.75). I'm not a Philly "lifer" only being here for about 15 years does not make me a steak sandwich expert, but I've had a few. They make their steak from "100% fresh rib eye" which would make their claim of the taste of South Philly accurate. My issue tonight was with the bread and the onions. The bread was tough and tasted funny partly due to the fact that it was a little burned on one side. After I peeled the char off the bread, I tasted the steak and some of the onions were crunchy. Seemed like they ran out of cooked onions, added more to the mix of cooked ones and served them up before they were done. Not yummy. Also, the only reason the fries were good was because they were slathered with Wiz. Eaten alone they were soggy and cold. I told my bf they seemed "marinated" in oil. If you are looking for a great steak sandwich on the Main Line try the garlic bread cheese steak at Pacilio's in Bryn Mawr or both Jack's or John's in Frazier are great. Take a pass on Rocco's.

I ordered the half serving of the vegetable lasagna. When it came out, it was clear it had been sitting for a while. The sauce had a crust over it and the cheese was so hardened that when I cut into it it stayed on my fork in one big blob. I might come back here again to see if the food could possibly improve, but after reading some other yelpers comments, I am not feeling too positive about it.

Other cleaning services would just work around him, and then do his area when he woke. They have a specific sequence of cleaning they feel they must follow. It was too inflexible for us. One good thing about this cleaner is that they do follow up and correct any problems you are unhappy with in the actual cleaning. For instance, the second time they came, they left a lot of the floors undone, coffee marks on the dressers, and didn't empty trash cans in the kitchen and upstairs. text: 2.5- Meh, nothing good or great. Came here on July 3rd for lunch. The wife and I wanted something quick and close, so there it is. AMBIENCE- The outside is somewhat misleading. I wasn't aware that this place is a sit down and order kind of place. I thought it was an order and sit kinda joint. They did some cost cutting on the decor. Tables were covered with a plastic, picnic like pattern, and the walls were adorned with art with a cartoony Italian food theme. It looked like they got all of them from the same garage sale. SERVICE- our server was nice, though towards the end, she totally disappeared. We were ready to leave, and she was no where to be found. I walked up to the front, and asked for our bill because we were sick of waiting. c'mon folks, you weren't even that busy. MENU- I'll be honest, our eyes didn't make it much farther than the lunch specials. I've heard their spinach and three cheese pizza is to die for, but I was craving a calzone, and low and behold there they were on the menu. They have appetizers, salads, pastas, and such, but my mind was set on a calzone. FOOD- the wife got the lunch special which is a salad, drink, and slice of pizza (they have a veggie and meat slice you can choose from, and the wifey went with the veggie slice). Not a bad deal for $6 or so. I went for the calzone with meatballs. On the menu it said it came with gorgonzola, which I hate, so I swapped for the ricotta. I can't say any one thing about the meal was that impressive. My calzone was decent, and a fair size, but just not that great. The wife's salad looked pretty typical, and the pizza was just ok. OVERALL- I doubt we'll be going back, unless friends REALLY want to go. I dunno, I'm all about supporting the local businesses, but this place just didn't do anything for me. It's a shame too, because this place is about 5 minutes from us. Celebrity Rating- Dax Shepard

The marinara sauce served on the side tasted like a crushed tomato in water.. bland bland bland. Given that this is a seafood restaurant, I expected something better. Not breathtaking, given the price point, but at least something edible. Service left something to be desired. They brought out the appetizers.. but didn't bring any utensils. Are we supposed to eat calamari with our fingers? They brought out the drinks, then failed to bring napkins. I felt like we were being rushed.. yes, we did sit there for almost two hours, but the restaurant wasn't busy at all PLUS we were sitting outside, so I didn't appreciate the pushy waitstaff. text: I had visited their location near downtown on Washington a couple times, and decided to pay them a visit over in the Grove on Manchester. Everything was well prepared, and several dishes were quite spicy, as I like it. The kheer (rice pudding) was intensely sweet and had me racing back for seconds like an addict needing a fix. The restaurant was quite full at lunch. I work not far away, and wonder what sort of crowd they pull in the evening. The staff were very friendly and helpful with all questions. text: I Dream of Weenie has become my favorite hot dog place, and my fiance and I try to visit it at least once or twice a week when time permits. I think the idea of using a VW bus as the stand is unique, and fits into the quirkiness of helping IDOW stand out. The dogs, which matter the most, are great. The two basic ingredients are top notch. The various meats used (whichever one chooses), and the buns are extremely fresh and good. I believe this is why their hot dogs are slightly more than at other stands (~$3.00-$3.50 each). From there the dogs can go in a wide range of places. Always look for the dog of the day on the sign by the sidewalk. I cannot even remember all the various ones I've had, but each time they have all been amazing. However nothing will be better than just throwing down one of their hot chili dogs. It absolutely can get busy, but even with a line of about ten people in front of us once before, the line moved pretty quick, and it didn't take long for us to pick up our food at all (which of course may vary on the other individuals orders). Seating is limited with either the grass and a blanket (supplied by IDOW) or at one of the two bench tables (one next to the bus, the other behind the bus). There are two main problems I have with this place, and why it's a 4-star. The first is the hours during the weekdays. Only being open until 3:00 pm it's near impossible to make it over there, which unfortunately sends me to the competitors a few minutes away that are open until late in the evening, but at least the weekend hours (Friday-Saturday) are a little more relaxed. The cash only policy is another slight problem, in that we often spend over $20 (we buy a lot), so it's a hassle needing to make a trip to the ATM first, and there is not one within walking distance. Don't even think to ask if they take plastic, or you'll be greeted by Mr. Johnny Cash giving you the 'hot dog.' In closing, I've always had a great experience with the 2 individuals whom I believe are the owners/cooks/cashiers. Friendly, and I feel they are interested in us as people rather than just customers with money in our pockets. They even gave our pup her own hot dog, didn't charge us at all. It's business like this that even if the food was not 100% (which is truly not the case), would have me return again. Let's help keep this local business around for many more years.
label: POS

And she was the only one who acknowledged us when we came in. We came during Sunday brunch. We had the 1/2 king crab claws for $22. It was boiled/steamed/whatever. Two claws on a bed of ice with two lemon slices. Cocktail sauce and some mustardy dip. A disappointment. Ugh! When my sis asked the waitress if the meat is meaty because she was VERY hungry, the waitress was convincing in saying that it was. The thing is the two sad claws didn't have anything with it besides a bed of ice and that's it! We also had the house cured trout, english muffin & poached eggs. This was eh. Nothing special. It looked pretty with the purple cabbage slaw, but eh to the ugh! What dressing was that? The trout was too salty and the poached egg had no taste. I love trout. But really? That was trout? I had the mint lemonade. That was good. So I'm renaming this place as the... I'm Still Hungry Cat Total: 50 bucks. (I knew I hate cats.) Yelpers, you did me wrong.

text: Ok, here's the deal. My husband works with a lot of Indian men who tell him that the Indian food he eats in America is not authentic and the real deal is in fact way spicier and packed with more flavor. I think maybe Ekta might be a little closer to this assessment. Unfortunately for me I am still learning to enjoying super spicy dishes and to be honest only delved into the world of Indian food within the last few years. I led a very sheltered food life as a child. I don't consider myself a total spice wuss. I eat jalapenos, Frank's Red Hot and I load most of my meals up with black pepper. I am, however, not even close to a spiceaholic like so many of my (mostly dude) friends. So I was kind of surprised, and not in a pleasant way, to find that even the saag paneer at Ekta set my mouth on fire. My husband and I ordered two dishes to share. One, the Saag Paneer, the other the clearly marked as spicy with a little pepper next to it on the menu was the Kadai Paneer. Man alive that Kadai was one of the spiciest things I have ever eaten and as I mentioned before my Saag was also spicy. I powered through some of the food but when I tried to add some yogurt sauce to cool down the dish I realized it was sour, like in a rancid way. Ugh. I have to say that my husband thoroughly enjoyed his insanely spicy dinner, and our roommate loved the leftovers as well but I'm the one writing this review, they can get their own yelp accounts. I'm the star. The naan was fine but Tiffin's is much, much better. We got the garlic and you could barely tell it was garlic. I don't get how spicy the entrees are in contrast to how light the garlic was. Weird. After eating a much smaller amount than I usually shove into my face when Indian food is present I still experienced the very unfortunate Indian Food Coma. Ugh. At least when I eat at Tiffin or New Delhi it seems worth it. From now on my Fishtown Indian take-out source will be Tiffin all the way.
label: NEG

text: Crazy layout, higher prices but eventually you find what you're looking for at ACE and the service may make it worth it for the casual DIY'er. Paint, tools, patio, electrical, lumber and plant center all for your shopping pleasure. There are 2 strong arguments for going to the ACE Home Improvement Center: 1. The location. Centrally located near downtown Santa Barbara. Home Depot is 15 minutes away in Goleta. 2. The friendly staff are knowledgeable and ready to help with small and large projects. I don't see this level at the Big Box stores. Now for the 2 weak points: 1. Layout. The center is not laid out logically. It's a maze of small rooms "bolted" onto each other offering a maze of uneven isles and blind corners. There's a very claustrophobic feeling about this place. 2. The price. ACE hardware stores tend to be more expensive with less choice than a Home Depot or Lowe's. I find a 10% increase in many items. The bottom line is that if you need something quick or don't know what you need, visit the ACE Home Improvement Center. For seasoned vets, hit the Big Box.

I had the filet, SO had the angus burger, we were in heaven. The next morning we had room service breakfast, food and service awesome once again. That night we had dinner in the restaurant, which is a beautiful atrium, with views of the ocean that are to die for. Again, our food and service were amazing. I had a killer dessert called 'textures of chocolate', still dreaming about it! We had the Sunday brunch which was good, but franky I've seen more extensive buffet's elsewhere. And also, the buffet closed fairly early and they switched to a lunch menu. The coffee at the Four Seasons was awesome too, we couldn't get enough of it. I found all the service, food, etc to be excellent, really no complaints at all. I see there are some complaints here on yelp about the prices of various things, such as parking, food, etc. You don't go to a five star resort and complain about prices. Perhaps you would be more at home at a Holiday Inn?

text: I hate to be so harsh to a local landmark, but time and again Hannegan's has earned my distrust. I've eaten there quite a bit because I work nearby and I keep thinking it can't be as bad as I remembered. It's so deceptively appealing on a nice early summer day to sit outside and enjoy the ambience of the Landing. Do not fall into this trap! The service ranges from not good to mediocre on almost every occasion I've been there. The servers mostly neglect to fill your glass and it takes a long time to get the bill. Today's experience was actually the best service I've had there, but alas... ...no service could make up for the food. My Greek salad was knife-cut and had obviously been sitting around, as the edges of the lettuce were all brown. Too bad they didn't bother to wash the lettuce (!) before cutting it up, because I kept getting mouthfuls of grit. A Greek salad generally comes with Feta crumbles, which this one did, but...either the Feta was moldy or else they mixed in some bleu cheese, which I hate. Either way, I avoided it. And the pit-filled kalamata olives. And the dressing was just incredibly....greasy. I've had a lot of meals here in the past and none are consistently good: too salty, served cold, bread sometimes stale, meat too fatty. The only thing I've had that is consistently good is the tortilla soup, which is just the right mixture of spicy and tomato with plenty of corn in it, but even that is served warm instead of hot. It was a beautiful day and we were in a hurry, so we gave it one more shot. We're both sorry. I understand that the dessert is good. If you're stuck on the Landing and everyplace else is too crowded, maybe a bowl of tortilla soup and a dessert here would suffice.

text: truth be told, my wife wanted to go this place because she likes fusion food, and i relented, ignoring all the signs. there were more flies than patrons in the establishment. sushi was not fresh, the rice was too sticky and too dense. there is nothing wrong with fusion food, but it should not be used as an excuse when things are not made properly and don't taste good. you can introduce different flavors from various cultures while using various techniques, but the flavor profiles should still be well-rounded and balanced. most of what i tasted here just tasted like they splashed some tabasco or sriracha into some mayo. much too spicy and the heat drowned out and killed any other flavor. this has nothing to do with it being "fusion", they just don't know how to make proper sushi rice is all. there is a reason sushi chefs need to train for 3 years just to perfect making sushi rice in japan. it is an art form that has been disrespected in various establishments around the world due to the meteoric rise in popularity of sushi and also because enterprising restaurateurs see it as a way to make a profit instead respecting a time honored tradition and art form. i have no problem with sushi chefs that are not japanese as long as they are skilled and respect their art. in fact, most kitchen staffs of U.S. restaurants are comprised of chefs of hispanic origin, and there is absolutely nothing wrong with that. they are what make the restaurant universe go round. the people stressing the fact that the sushi chefs are not japanese here are clueless. but i digress. the scallops were slimy and had a chemical aftertaste. i have an iron stomach but was truly afraid, so i did spit it back out on to a napkin. i paid the check and did not look back. i have not been back there since...
