We decided to have dessert and try to save the meal and at least leave happy with something we ordered, the gelato seemed like a good choice but they don't make it in-house so I passed on it. Tiramisu was our choice because it was made in-house....wow it was bad, I've had better dessert from the frozen food section of the super market... so a 100 bucks later and a wish that we had gone somewhere else..... All in all there was nothing progressive about this place and the prices are way too high for what you get and the menu is way too big...I'm a huge believer that you should do a few things great rather than a lot of thing mediocre and that's what The Laughing Cat does a lot of overpriced mediocre dishes... text: if you're going to see an outdoor-festival type band (DMB, Jack Johnson, Phish, Pearl Jam, etc. etc.) where you're just going to hang out in your spot and dance to the tunes but you don't need to see a stage show or the actual musicians themselves, then this is a great place because you can sit on the lawn for $30 or so and get that great view of the city and the sunset - and it really is that pretty. But you won't see the artist and you're basically watching them on a tv screen. The lawn really is a free for all of drunks, pot and sex. It's like a mini Woodstock out there. We took the ferry over from Philly before the show, and it was great. The big big big problem is after the show when everyone who took the ferry over in stages before the show ends up leaving at the same time. You will end up waiting in line for hours to get the ferry back or end up getting stranded in Camden (and that's the last place you want to be). There's no other way out of there unless you drove, and that's a nightmare in and of itself - it'll take 2 hours or more for you to get out of Camden and on your way home. If you want to make the ferry or get out of the parking lot at a reasonable hour you have to leave the show early and that's terrible. They really should do something about it but they won't... they're already making too much money because people will put up with the insanity anyway just to see their favorite acts -- and Camden and the Susq Bank Center know that -- so nothing will get fixed. They really need a higher speed ferry or more ferries at the end of the concert, but then again it won't get done. So, if you're just there to listen and for the vibe, this is a good place to see a show. If you actually want to see the band play, then see them somewhere else. And alot at least two hours after the show just to get the heck out of Camden.

We also had the spring rolls which were also delicious. 1st course: I went with ceviche, both types, the Peruvian was more crisp and light than its Ecuadorian counterpart. Both were good, but the flavor, as a whole in the Peruvian was more robust. 2nd Course: I went with the Pho and the shrimp noodle bowl. The Pho came with some Siraci and hoisin sauces on the side. The Pho was already a little spicy, but the hoisin sauce added a little sweetness to the mix. The shrimp noodle bowl was creamy and full of complex flavors. The bacon really made the shrimp pop. dessert: The turron de chocolate wasn't my favorite, but that comes from my disdain of coffee flavor. Overall, it was a good dessert that won me over after a few bites. My overall experience was an extremely positive one. Anytime you can sit around with good friends and enjoy a great meal at a great price you can't go wrong. I highly recommend this place, even outside of restaurant week.

Now, if all this geeky stuff sounds up your alley, you'll feel at home. Aside from the geek talk, I was pretty impressed by the new addition of brunch which I have to check out. Jamie plans on having at least 6-7 varieties of waffles on the menu. These vary from chicken & waffles to "shit on a shingle" (one with portabello "shit" to create a veggie alternative), to an impressive cornmeal waffle topped with veggie chipotle chili and stuffed with cheddar cheese? (Did I take these notes down correctly? Either way, sounds awesome.) All in all, we had a great chat about all the awesome food concepts he has. text: If your out of town, reading yelp to find a good place to eat classic New Orleans (cajun food), come here instead of Acme. So you cant sample here, so I just got their most popular item, the Ferdi Special, which came with their house baked ham, roast beef, debri, and gravy (and I asked for extra gravy on the side - nods off to Adam Richmond). I also got the crawfish ettuffle since that was the only thing I did not get at the Acme Oyster House. OMG ettuffle is delicious. Not too salty, (which was a problem at Acme), it has a broth which probably has a ton of butter and flour (or some sort of thickener), the crawfish cooked delicately with the flavor of the sea from the crawfish influsing into the broth very distinctly. The crawfish was sweet, tender, and fell apart with minimal effort in your mouth. No tough overcooked crawfish here. The ettouffle comes served over white rice, which when you are paying $8.25 for a small cup seems kinda a cheap move. Why cant they give me a whole cup of ettoufle with a side of rice. There's also another meat, most likely a fish in it. Altogether, this is probably the best thing that I had in New Orleans so far. More than anything, this reminds me of a good thick clam chowder, except with crawfish instead of clams. The Ferdi Special was alright. The broth was kinda flavorless, and to be honest, the best part of the sandwich for me was the pickles and mustard, which was a good combination with the lightly salty meat and gravy. Correction, the best part is the free pepper oil on the side. It was absolutely awesome. Sweet, sour and spicy at the same time, I ended up killing my sandwich with it. Well the chicken and sausage.The jambalaya is a bit less salty than the jambalaya at Acme, it also has a bit more of a spicy kick to it. An interesting note is that the sausage here is sliced and the chicken is pulled. I feel that this is a bit better than the other way at Acme. The chicken stays tender and chewable, and the sausage (which naturally has more fat gives the jambalaya an additional component almost becoming a compliment to the dish rather than depending on the rice as a medium He jumbo however is better at Acme. The chicken in my jumbo is dry, and the jumbo just isn't as flavorful as the darker jumbo at Acme. There is also less meat in this jumbo. The soup is just thinner. It's not as salty or as spicy. Again, the sausage is sliced thick, but in this case, I like it better chopped up like at Acme. Overall, I would say that this place makes the Louisiana classics a lot better than Acme. So if you want good jambalaya, entouffe, or gumbo, come here. But dont get the Fergi special. its pretty overrated. sorry travel channel (and subsequently Man Vs Food)

text: WOW! Nothing against Brandon, but my experience could not have been any more different. My wife had a po boy that turned out to be a turkey sandwich you could basically order at Subway for half the price. Overall, I think this restaurant should be burned to the ground and the serving staff should be hung publicly on the banks of the Mississippi river as an example to other would-be crappy waiters and waitresses.

text: This solid little nook on the Greenwood-Indy line was the first Thai place to open on the Southside, and it's held up with some kickin' business over the years. Alas, it's been too long since I've last visited here to recommend too many specifics, but I suspect that I had either the Green Curry or Musaman (since I often get those and use them as a gauge for the quality of a Thai place). I remember the subtlety of coconut as well as the freshness of the vegetables, with perfectly steamed rice. Service was warm and comfy. Best of all: they offer five scales for spiciness: Mild, Medium, Hot, Very Hot, and Thai Spicy. The "Hot" classification is more than enough for the average Caucasian. Whitey, you've been warned. Despite the intensity of the Hot classification, the other flavors still shone through excellently. I loved it as it vacated my sinuses for a full 36 hours--like breathing Alpine air...only thick with curry. Went back recently and it's still terrific. I ordered the one thing on the menu where they specifically say "no refunds" which I thought was a big provocative. Sorry I can't remember the name of the item I ordered but you'll see it if you ever go, because of the small print below it. I guess there's been some problems with this item? I thought it was great; peanut sauce was abundant but the flavor was not so overpowering to drown out even the onions and bean sprouts (which is tough because bean sprouts in particular aren't usually exactly screaming FLAVOR.) Go and try their summer rolls as well; they're wonderfully prepared.

text: For those who want their dinner to be like a dream... a really bloody and surreal dream. My friends and I sat down at the Brazilian barbeque (which looks like a seedy kind of diner but has a banquet room on the other side with clouds painted on the ceiling and a lot of balloons (and a TV and recliners... so weird!), hit the salad bar, and almost immediately after returning to our seats, had three huge skewers of different kinds of meat brought over to our table. The woman who brought them was shaped like a large blonde linebacker and barely spoke any english but LOVED the fact that we became more and more excited every time meat was brought out. She quickly picked up on the fact that we pretty much all liked our meat as rare as possible and probably by the second time she brought the meat out, our table had drops of blood all over it. I hadn't even paid attention to the fact that all the tables were covered with thick plastic sheeting. At one point, I got up to go to the bathroom, and my foot slipped on something and shot out to the side. I looked down and saw two puddles of blood next to the table! I chuckled my way to the bathroom where I found signs posted on both stalls in the ladies room... "Do not throw toilet paper in the toilets!".... Um... what?! I looked in the stalls and the toilets looked normal enough, but there were definitely little trash cans full of crumpled up toilet paper next to each one. WHAT?!?! I felt totally uncomfortable with the thoughts and questions that instantly started gushing through my brain so I just went back to the table, still having to pee. We ploughed through slab after slab of messy, drippy meat, which our server was all too happy to keep hacking off of her skewers for us. It was definitely not for the faint of heart or stomach... but I have never felt so peaceful at the same time as feeling so aggressive. It was almost a spiritual moment. I love red meat. If you are more into the meat than a fancy experience, choose this over Fogo, at $18 per person, it's a deal. Also, try the parfait for dessert,...you will fall in love. Oh yeah, and it's BYO.
label: POS

text: I was VERY upset with my experience here. My regular hair stylist was on an extended vacation, and I badly needed a cut, so I did my research, and Luna came out on top. It had been rated as the best salon in Philly by citysearch for either '06 or '07, I don't remember which, so I figured it was a pretty safe bet. All I wanted was a simple, layered cut with long layers. I was initially very comfortable with my stylist, as she was Persian, and so had curly hair like me, so I was confident that if she could style her hair, she could style someone else's. As we talked though, I got more and more worried. She talked about how she went to art school then dropped out and went to fashion school and dropped out, and finally settled on hair. I thought, you know, that it takes some people a little longer to find their calling, but ok, whatever. THEN she said that in college, she would cut her friend's hair all the time, and that they "would look great, but would be a technical disaster". I was praying that beauty school had refined her technical abilities, but I got one of her college cuts. It looked pretty good when I left, albeit A LOT shorter than I or my boyfriend liked (My hair is halfway down to my elbows and she cut it to just below my shoulders!) and not completely straight. Then I washed it and styled it myself, and saw what a HACK JOB she had done! I had layers that were 2 inches around the crown of my head, and the bottom-most layer was shorter than the one above it! I got the cut last year, September, and I'm STILL trying to grow out those 2-inchers. I was obviously very upset, and will not be going back there again. In my opinion, a stylist that can't even do a decent, simple, layered cut should not be a stylist!

text: Hello overpriced for substandard offerings. You know when you go into a sushi restaurant, order your sushi and are greeted by nice, uniform chunks of beautifully sliced fish...tuna is a deep red, yellowtail is a buttery transparent white and the salmon is salmon colored and when you bite into it, it glides down like butter? Well, Shintomi is NOT the place to get that experience. Rather the exact opposite. I ordered a Chirashi which is usually a select variety of succulent sashimi atop a small bed of rice - really as accent, rather than sustenance. At Shintomi the Chirashi at $14.50 is a bowl of rice, apparently $10 worth, with random pieces of what seems like days old raw fish, two very large pieces of steamed egg and two pieces of fake crabmeat. Laughable, really. My boyfriend ordered a sukiyaki (came with a soup spoon, but no soup to be found) and a spicy tuna roll and yellowtail. Oh...the spicy tuna roll barely had any tuna and the yellowtail, as was the "sashimi" in my chirashi was bland, tasteless. But really, what was more disturbing was the owner/mgr's apathetic attention when I had asked if I could order something else since this dish was not up to my expectations. Nope, sorry. "We can't help it if you don't know how to look at picture on menu. It's not our fault if you don't like what you ordered." Well, the only reason that I could think of why they would be so offended is that even if they were to offer something to replace my order, it would be just as bad so why bother. This place is the WORST place I have ever dined in in Nashville, and I've had some not so great experiences. I guess location is everything. Plop yourself in Green Hills, known to be an affluent part of town and by association, people think you are a great sushi restaurant. Nope, not so much my friends. Try again.

text: Taste: 5 Value: 5 Service 4 Know this: Cajun Seafood is not in a safe neighborhood. If you're going to venture here, make sure you don't go by yourself. For our final dinner in New Orleans, we decided that we wanted to go get some seafood boil. Our first choice was Castnet Seafood, but they didn't answer their phones. Based on the assumption that they were closed on Monday, this made Cajun Seafood our second choice. It was only a mile away from our hotel, but as the taxi driver was dropping us off, he mentioned that we weren't in a safe neighborhood. Going in, it felt like a Same Woo Chinese takeout in the heart of Oakland. We ordered a pound of snow crab, shrimp, crawfish, plus some potatoes and corn. The bill? Under $30. The feeling of unease left a little as we started to tear through our succulent meal. The boil has the perfect amount of spice and great flavor. After working our way through the food, we decided go for a second round of everything except for the crawfish. I grabbed one more pound of snow crab for myself before we headed out the door and back to the hotel. This is by far the best seafood boil I've ever had. The prices are unbeatable. text: Koto ah numbah one! Short and sweet, it is very good. This is a small, family run place. Hadji throws a mean roll and is famous for his stuff. Best crunchy shrimp roll in town. Here you will find most traditional Japanese menu items and a few Korean ones from Hadji's wife. Lunch and dinner specials. They will also do rolls to order at the bar. The Miso and Udon rules. The new location on Union has upgraded decor and an expanded menu but the food, people and tastes are the same for this Nashville tradition. My favorite place in town because it is not trendy. text: I had dinner here last weekend with a couple of friends. For a Saturday evening, it was surprisingly empty when we came around 7:15 PM or so. We were seated at the window (likely because our extremely casual clothing was a bit out of place), and the menus were given to us. I would have appreciated the specials being told to the table a bit slower; we didn't end up ordering any, but I also had little idea of what was available after the waiter had told us. On the advice of one of our party who had previously been there, we got the gnocchi (both the spinach and the ricotta), the tacconell al porcini (my suggestion), and the pesto ravioli. All of the dishes were fantastic; the gnocchi in particular was a highlight. I'm not sure how it's made, but the gnocchi is really rich and has a dense, flavorful middle. The tacconell was also a revelation; the long, thin noodles tasted very good in the cream sauce, and the porcini mushrooms added a nice touch of flavor that allowed it to stand out against the sauce (which wasn't as rich as an alfredo). The ravioli was probably the weakest dish, but even so it tasted better than most I've had. Put together, those 3 dishes were under $20 each, so it was a very affordable dinner for the price. The atmosphere is a bit quiet, but once more parties started flowing in later on, you could speak at normal levels without feeling too out of place. My one recommendation is that this place is more towards the dressy end of casual; I felt a bit out of place in my shorts, polo shirt, and sandals. I'd recommend wearing at least jeans and loafers (not sneakers).

text: We discovered this spot quite by accident many years ago, and since then it has become an almost religious "pilgrimage" to revisit every time we're in town. You'll find a mixture of locals and tourists here, and the bartenders are quite friendly and helpful as well. The atmosphere is very much like any "local dive bar" you could find in most cities and towns across the U.S. If one could separate the "Bar" from the restaurant, I would give 5 stars to the former and 3 to the latter. Their "Monsoon" cocktails are simply a must have for your visit to NOLA, but please ONLY ONE if you are driving! Their menu is limited to burgers and steaks, though I've never ordered or seen anyone else order anything but the burgers. No fries, but huge baked potatoes are the available side dish. And the burgers are REALLY good, albeit not the best I've ever had. If you are hungry, by all means order one, you will enjoy it. But a burger is a burger is a burger - New Orleans abounds with 5 star food, and you won't find that here. But order a Monsoon and a burger and you WILL have a 5 star experience!

text: I hate to be the first one to leave a bad review for Germantown but here it is. I will preface this review saying I had dinner there and from all these reviews it sounds as if this place's forte is brunch, so if you're having brunch there maybe you should ignore my review. I would give Germantown 5 stars for ambiance and service because the restaurant is cute and romantic with a fantastic view of downtown Nashville. Our server was friendly, efficient and not too intrusive. However, the food was another story. Perhaps it is because I am from Los Angeles that I found the amount of oil in the food appalling. Now don't get me wrong, I am not one of those people who eats only salad and in fact I LOVE buttery and oil foods. But unfortunately the food at Germantown was soaked in oil to the point where that's all I tasted. In fact both my bf and I had stomach aches when we got home. The escargot and Shrimp Curry were soaked in oil and butter. It overpowered any taste that the dish shoudl have had. The Pork was okay, but nothing to write home about. I am a big dessert person and was excited for the apple crisp which got such good reviews on Citysearch. It came in a bowl that looked as if they melted half a bowl of butter and then dumped the crisp in. I couldn't even finish it, or taste anything besides butter for that matter. Pros of Germantown is that they service fried yeast balls (like awesome donut type bread) b/t the salad and the entree which were delicious. However, that wasn't enough to save the meal.

text: I ate here more than 10 years ago on my first trip to New Orleans and it was the best meal of my life that far. I went back on my trip last week hoping to replicate the awesomeness and was not disappointed. I started with a NOLA Cosmo and BBQ'd gulf shrimp appetizer, which was the perfect-sized appetizer for two people to split and consisted of good sized shrimp with a great smokey BBQ glaze dripped over it. For my meal, I had the filet mignon with blue cheese, bacon, shallot crisps, toasted walnuts and potatoes. I'm not usually a big blue cheese eater, but it tasted soooo gooood with the meat and walnuts. And then for dessert -- which was the thing most remembered from my previous trip -- I had the banana pudding layer cake -- SO YUMMY! My friend had the creme brulee' trio -- vanilla with berries, coconut, and mocha -- which was also really good, but must be eaten in that order, which the waiter points out to you, because you'd be overwhelmed by the chocolate if you started with mocha. Overall, the food was amazing. And the wait staff was attentive and knowledgeable. I highly recommend NOLA when in NOLA ;)

Classic Italian roll. The fries were also very good and freshly cut. Back to the shake. It was definitely good but definitely overpriced at $5. As far as the decor, it's a basic lunch layout. text: Holy crap! What the heck is this place doing in the middle of Lansdowne? Oh geez I rhymed again without trying. Must -- stop -- now. A friend and I had the Tuesday Tasting Menu, $49, 4 courses, and it was delightful! Scallops on a Jerusalem artichoke puree with bacon, brussels sprouts and a black truffle jus, absolutely perfectly executed, the scallop was done just right, not over or undercooked. Then the cheese plate, kinda nice, but not the highlight of the meal. Then on to the main course, pheasant 2 ways. A breast and a confit leg, and both were cooked to perfection, served on a celery root puree, and kale, and a prune sauce. The breast had stuffing, and in it were chestnuts. OH MY GOSH, it ain't Per Se or El Bulli, but it was absolutely BEAUTIFUL! Then dessert, 3 ways, a toffee thing, a tiramisu with BOOZE in it, oh my GOSH, MOST RESTAURANTS ARE AFRAID OF PUTTING BOOZE IN DESSERTS! Not here! Not a lot of booze though, just enough to add a little zing, not the kind of boozed-up dessert that only tastes of booze and nothing else, but just perfect. The third was a coffee ice cream, so you got the toffee/coffee thing goin' on throughout, and yeah, it was integrated and complimentary and just gorgeous. The staff was very friendly, and attentive, I will be coming back to this place real soon, and EVERYONE should also! If you don't get lost on the way....

text: We went to Patou because my wife had heard that it was "fun". I'd never heard of the place, but I was willing to give it a shot. My first impression was that the entire place is a bit rough around the edges. Rough edges can add charm to some restaurants, but Patou's rough edges border on sloppiness. For example, the bathroom had rusty fixtures and wasn't very clean, even though we arrived at 5:30. It was the day before Valentine's, so we could only order from the prix-fixe menu. That was fine with me, as the menu sounded well thought out and interesting. However, reality proved different. We ordered the wild mushroom soup and billibi soup for our first course. My billibi was oily but tasted quite nice. The only thing that bothered me is that it was listed as a mussel soup, but no pieces of mussel meat were present. My wife's creamy wild mushroom soup, however, was a disaster. The mushrooms tasted like they had been almost charred and then over-concentrated. There was a distinct lack of cream and seasoning. I have a hard time believing that any of the chefs sampled it before sending it out, as overall the soup tasted like pureed burnt cardboard. Second course was a little better. My salmon tartare was also bland, but the wasabi chips that came with it were over salted almost to inedibility. Putting the bland tartare on top of the over-salted chips led to a (sort of) happy medium. My wife's lobster spring rolls were a bit odd. Her first question was, "Why are they not fried?". They appeared to be made of uncooked egg roll wrappers. However, they tasted okay, so I have to assume that they were made of something else. Both my salmon and her rolls tasted flat and uninspired, though. For the third course we both had the seafood feuilletee. This is where the sloppiness really showed. My feuilletee was over-toasted to a very dark brown. The lobster, scallops, shrimp and so forth were cooked acceptably, but they were burdened by a sauce that was a muddy mess. The crab leg on top had been pointlessly seasoned so that it was overly salty. The texture was blah, the presentation was blah, and the taste was blah. How can any serious kitchen take wonderful ingredients like lobster, scallops, crab and shrimp and combine them in such a way as to completely ruin them? Finally desert came. I was prepared to be underwhelmed. Imagine my surprise when the molten cake and frozen custard was fabulous! I guess at least the pastry department at Patou has some modicum of skill. Everything I saw there indicated a lack of leadership. The front of the house needed to focus on attention to detail. The kitchen was an undisciplined mess. Quality control was non-existent. If I was the chef there I'd be kicking people's ass every day and handing out pink slips to the worst offenders. Luckily for the employees there I have not the slightest interest in the job.
label: NEG

text: After reading the reviews, I got a craving for good pho. We've tried making it at home, but it just didn't seem quite right. We're Anthony Bourdain fans, and his love of pho has definitely rubbed off on us. So we ventured out to the Bench to put this place to the test - and were disappointed at what we got. As far as the atmosphere goes, it's not horrible - pretty stark, if anything. We did giggle about the sheer SIZE of the place though. I wonder if some of the tables there have ever had anyone sitting at them...? Atmosphere isn't what we're here for, though...we want pho. After a quick look over the menu, we decided on cold rolls (veggies & meat wrapped in rice paper) and pho tai. Our friendly server assured us that this was an excellent choice, and we were looking forward to a great meal on this cold, rainy night. First came the cold rolls, with two dipping sauce options - a clear, sweet sauce, and hosin sauce. I'm used to seeing peanut sauce with these, but to each is own, right? The rolls were okay - I love the raw rice paper, but the filling consisted of cooked rice noodles, green leaf lettuce, shrimp, and a chicken/pork mixture. So so so bland! Would've been so much better with some basil and carrot. Then, they rolled out our HUGE bowls of pho, and a plate of...bean sprouts?! Where was the lime? Where were the peppers? Where was the basil? In our bowls was a huge pile (way WAY too many!!!) of thin rice noodles, some meat, green onions, and cilantro. Regardless, we added some Sriracha and bean paste, and dove in. What we were 'rewarded' with was a bland broth and chewy, overcooked meat. There was nothing aromatic or flavorful about this soup - I've had instant ramen that's tasted better. We could've easily shared one bowl between the two of us - but we did choose to bring the leftovers home, where we can chuck some of the noodles, add some more veggies!! We will probably give this place another try, though - some of the other items on the menu looked interesting. But alas, we're still on the hunt for adequate pho in the City of Trees...

text: This is literally a sushi BAR...meaning there's only about 15 seats available to enjoy the all-you-can-eat sushi. My boyfriend and I were staying there at the hotel and were craving sushi so we figured we'd just head over to the sushi bar. We were famished since we were skiing all day, so we were very disappointed to hear we had to wait an hour and a half! Who knew there were so many sushi fans in Reno!! We decided to try to sit at the regular bar next to it but those seats were also filled. So, we walked to the other side and the manager there rudely told us that that side of the bar was for restaurant patrons only. Sidebar: The sky terrace is basically one long wide hallway with an oyster bar, a "drinks" bar, and a sushi bar one after the other smack in the middle with a seafood restaurant located on one side of the bars and slots on the other. Luckily once we sat by some slot machines, a couple seats opened up at the bar so we decided to get some drinks to pass the time. Nick was our bartender and he was great! We quickly got served our drinks and after about 30 mins of hunger, we decided to get an appetizer to make it through the next hour wait. I hesitantly asked if we could order off the sushi menu and he said a la carte only. That's when my eyes opened up with a gleam of hope! My boyfriend and I were planning to not do the all-you-can-eat so it was perfect! We waited a third of the time and still got our yummy sushi. And boy was it good! I wasn't expecting much seeing as this was a sushi bar in a casino...in Reno! But, I was happily pleased with the Tekka Maki, Sky Terrace and Mermaid rolls along with inari and a spicy tuna hand roll. The Mermaid roll was my fave with deep fried (not tempura) shrimp inside and a "Jason" special on top...which is grilled scallops in a creamy sauce. The rolls were bigger than expected and delicious! I already know this will be a stop next time I'm in town. I plan to go there for lunch since the all-you-can-eat is a deal for only $16! Because I understand the reason for the long wait, my sole complaint stems from the service. Aside from Nick (who was the only person who paid attention to us), there was a lack of service on the sky terrace. When I asked to be put on the wait list, I felt like the hostess didn't even want to put down my name cuz the wait was so long. When we asked 30 mins later if it was still going to be another hour, she confirmed in a cold tone. We had a reason to ask since a big group had just been seated. And I already mentioned the manager who belittled us for being on the wrong side of the bar - There are no barriers or signs that distinguish where people are free to sit so it was an honest mistake which could have been handled in a more forgiving manner. And lastly, when Nick went on a break, we could not get the attention of the other bartender after calling out his name and gesturing him to come over several times. He was focused on some 'regulars' sitting right next to us but ultimately made a bad impression on hotel guests. Workers there definitely need a refresher course on guest services. If you can avoid all this and get there early enough to find an open seat at the sushi bar, you'll have a guaranteed pleasant and fulfilling experience.

text: For now, this is the only place for downtown-dwellers to get groceries without driving a few miles. You can get basic groceries, as well as some international goodies, like curry sauce and sushi rice. There's also a small meat counter and deli. Pretty cool if you're looking rushing to make a sandwich before heading back up to your loft or office. What's really convenient is the hot bar that charges by the pound. I suggest breakfast if it's your first time. The lunch/dinner items can sometimes get dry and unappetizing (they taste pretty good either way). I may be reaching, but City Grocers has the BEST biscuits and gravy in the entire city. Flaky biscuits made by people in chef hats (a plus) with a thick (not too milky) spicy gravy (Italian sausage?) make me a very happy guy. Actually, a slice of their quiche with that same gravy is probably going to be my choice for Last Meal On Earth. I've been going on and on about cholesterol-filled greatness, but there's a salad bar as well. I like the Thai salad. Aside from that, City Grocers rocks it out with a decent beer, liquor, and wine selection for the size of the place. Again, great for last-minute buys. There's plenty of seating upstairs, where people-watching can last the entire day.

text: Up front, it should be said that St. Mary's makes fabulous tortillas. There are a lot of good ones in Tucson, but these floated down from heaven like floury UFOs. They are translucently thin, lardy, and boast a perfect texture. Paired with good ingredients, such tortillas could easily be the basis of a World Class Burrito--a burrito so good that its mere existence would make Chipotle and La Salsa close their stores in purple-faced shame. St. Mary's seems like it was meant to serve this burrito. It just feels right: the location, bright colors, rickety plastic tables, and awesome staff. It closes inconveniently early and always takes a little too long to serve you. These are the idiosyncrasies of an amazing restaurant, but St. Mary's isn't an amazing restaurant. It isn't even a very good restaurant. This is painful to write, but it's a lateral slide from Nico's. The emperor has no clothes. Let's begin with the asada burrito, a heavy, joyless torpedo of food. The ingredients were of poor quality and they arrived, bite by bite, in separate layers, leaving the burrito with different temperature zones ranged from tepid to cold. The shredded cheddar was unmelted and chalky. There was no seasoning. Even a junkie-sized injection of salsa couldn't have saved it, but that wasn't an option because St. Mary's only gives you half-empty plastic thimbles of runny, flavorless hot sauce. This wasn't an off day. A return trip yielded a room-temperature shredded beef taco with no seasoning, a heap of iceberg lettuce, and a veneer of that chalky yellow stuff posing as cheese. Whether or not hard taco shells give you flashbacks to high school lunches at Taco Bell, they should, at very least, be hard when they arrive and not soggy. St. Mary's fails on this count, as well. Their red chile tamale was a greater disappointment. Wet and rubbery on the outside, dense and cool on the inside, it offered the same absence of flavor as the rest of their entrees. Chicken flautas. Meh. Quesadilla. Meh. Don't punish yourself with food from St. Mary's. Instead, grab some of their delicious tortillas and sneak them into your favorite restaurant.

It's probably a great place just to hang out and talk...in other words, it works better as a lounge than a restaurant. Guanciale is the cut of meat traditionally used in Italy but rarely used in the states because it's hard to find. And luckily, the pasta did not disappoint. The home made spaghetti was cooked perfectly al dente and the sauce was phenomenal. I finished the meal with the chocolate torte which was rich and warm and wonderful. Unfortunately, the wonderful remarks have made it more difficult to get in this tiny place--but any amount of difficulty is worth it. This place just gets better and better; the menu--which was swell before--has been expanded. There are just enough offerings to please everyone without having too many for the chef to prepare splendidly. The service, too, never is less than excellent; the ambiance is casually chic, lowkey while sophisticated. Alex, my teenage nephew (a budding foodie) put it best: if you could have one restaurant inyour front yard . . .
label: POS

text: Cheap. At writing, it's 15 dollars per way to DC. You'll be sitting next to questionable individuals. The bus smells a little and the stops deliver a powerfully pungent smell of piss. When I start making real money I'm not using it, but not terrible for frugal people. The trouble is, you never are quite sure where its going, so make sure you ask, and the driver rarely speak english. Also show up 15 minutes early, and expect it to be 30 mins late.

text: I've eaten at various Melting Pot locations up and down the east coast, and this is easily one of the best. The food was absolutely delicious, that goes without saying. I could write an essay just about the dessert we had (chocolate peanut butter fondue). But what really impressed me with this location was the service. Our waitress was seriously one of the best I've ever had at a restaurant. The manager was around checking in on everyone. The other servers were always chipping in to clear dishes and replenish drinks. We couldn't have asked for more stellar service. Is The Melting Pot expensive? Yes. But when you factor in the incredible service along with the incredible food, I really think it is worth it.
label: POS

text: Outstanding. The moment I got there I knew that this place was going to be amazing. The unassuming building is home to one of the best collections of art that I have ever seen in one place. I was exploring Indianapolis while a friend of mine was at work and he told me to check out this place, I was pretty happy I did. My favorite part of the museum is the top floor contemporary art gallery. Some of the most fascinating pieces you'll see. The fact that general admission to this museum is free is great and made me want to become a member. I didn't, but if I ever get the chance to (meaning I have some extra $$) I totally would. Check this out if you're ever in Indianapolis, it's pretty much amazing.
label: POS

text: Dear Tonic, how you've never failed me throughout my college career. you're the best! And it doesn't hurt that your Dj is such a cutie. dance the night away...woohoo!
label: POS

But more importantly the service was EXTREMELY overbearing. We completely felt like we were being rushed out of the restaurant and our waiter looked annoyed when we wanted to sit and enjoy our wine. For what it costs, I will never go back.

text: Nice and clean environment. Nice screen and very good audio--not overly loud as seems to be the trend lately at many theaters. Movie was fairly full but all were respectfully quiet. I don't go to many movies but next time I do I'll return here. There also appeared to be a nursery for kids while parents see a flick, but I'd check on that before making any plans based on this possibility. I do wish that the whole shopping complex was desgned in a more pedestrian-friendly layout but that isn't the fault of Harkins.
label: POS

text: I've been going to the Aveda Institute ever since it opened last year - and I can honestly say that its saved me hundreds of dollars in the 6-9 times I've been there thus far. The students are enthusiastic, friendly, and always know what they're doing. The listen and genuinely want to give you the haircut/color/service of your dreams. Getting an appointment over the phone or via walk-in is generally super easy, and the staff is always willing to work with you if you need to move your appointment on short notice. Likewise, the quality of the service is unbeatable. The fact of the matter is - they use Aveda products (ones identical to what my high priced salon had used) and the students really really want to get your hair perfect. This results in a great salon experience without the hefty price tag. Throughout the last two years, I have only had one student mess up on my hair (it was a badly placed highlight chunk) - but the school FIXED IT FOR FREE right away. The Aveda Institute students are really committed to making their customers happy, even if you're only paying $15 for the haircut. It's honestly this commitment to perfection and client satisfaction that keeps me coming back every 6-8 weeks. The students are required to show you the products that they used during your service, but you are not in any way pressured to buy them. I know other reviews may say otherwise, but Aveda students DO NOT UPSELL nor are they really trying to push product. Much like the massage and finishing lip gloss treatment - this is just part of the Aveda treatment. I overwhelmingly recommend this place to every single one of my friends - and have been since my very first service. I'm going to grad school at the U of A in the fall - and could not be more excited to continue getting my hair done at the Institute. Your wallet and your hair will thank you for going to Aveda instead of your current salon. You won't regret a cut/highlights/manicure/pedicure/whatever you chose to get done there.
label: POS

text: Well, I feel like a real lush for having back-to-back reviews in which my drunkenness played the starring role, but, as my mother would say, them's the breaks. Sue G., Hunter (my boyfriend), and I stumbled (literally, at least in my case) in here after the incredibly awesome UYE at ZoT last night (thanks to Bill for organizing!). Unfortunately, however, ZoT managed to run me pretty dry, so I was happy to find a cheap dive that was close by. Though I usually turn my nose up at shitty beer, I was too drunk at this point to care. The PBR went down like water. I enjoyed their decorations. It reminded me of an old ice cream parlor, just with booze instead of ice cream. The people there were... interesting, to say the least. They made us laugh, and not much beats laughing at people when you're drunk. I don't remember seeing many games, but there was a big bowl of Dum-Dum lollipops in front of us, which brought on a welcome wave of nostalgia. Extra star for the mouse-friend that scuttled across the floor, which drove Sue to push her beer as far away from her as possible and yell at the bartender. Good times.
label: POS

text: I agree with just about every review on here. I gave Aloha Sushi two tries (years apart) and I got food poisoning both times. SEVERE food poisoning. I will never, ever, ever eat here again. There are so many other great sushi places in Reno, try one of those instead.
label: NEG

text: best $5 meal ever (ok, i exaggerate but definitely best $5 in philly!)! this place has really delicious noodles with the best consistency. its perfectly chewy and wonderfully seasoned with the appropriate broth! im really impressed that philly has such a little gem. i recommend the soup noodles, the dry noodles were alright.
label: POS

text: Extensive selection of crown molding and baseboards, plus other lumber products. They have the wide baseboards found in many local homes that are not available anywhere else I searched.

text: Terrible. If you are going to SB, please yelp a place on State Street first...I totally didn't think about it, when my mom and I headed out for a mini day trip. The only thing worth anything were the really sweet busers. Everyone else had tudes bigger then, well they were really big. It's decorated like Disneyland...and absolutely un-authentic when it comes to traditional Italian anything. I had the Santa Margarita sandwich...which literally had the tiniest slice of mozzarella possible. At least the tomatos were good. But they served it on the same bread that they bring to the table as an appetizer. Overly strong garlic cheese bread, it was yucky. My mom got the halibut salad...bland as heck. I also had $3 mango ice tea...which was mostly ice, and definitely not mango anything. My mother enjoyed the coffee...a lot in fact. I don't even want to write anymore.

text: Crepes the new crepe place in the Central West End right on Maryland Plaza is a wonderful place. I stopped in there for lunch the other day and I am so glad that I did. Walking in the menu is written right up on the wall so all you have to do is look forward to see what it is that you want to eat. I chose the ham and broccoli crepe and since it was a Monday I apparently was able to have a free cup of coffee. The fact that I was given a free cup of coffee automatically added quite a bit of awesome points to my opinion of the place. Anyway, after getting my coffee, a nice Honduran blend, I found a table next to the window and waited for my crepe to come along. The nice thing about this place is that they prepare the crepes right up front so you can actually see them make it, which I always find comforting. Well the crepe was wonderful, nice and tasty and just the right amount of food for me. Tremendously enjoyable.
label: POS

text: A pint of Guiness and Yard for a little over $4 (in total) during happy hour. Holy crap! Free lollipops! And they were playing rock! We went on a Saturday. We should have stayed there until the end of happy hour but decided to walk around South Street for a few hours. We came back for another pint and some food, and it was a different story. Hip hop and a surly waitress. The bartenders were awesome though. We ordered another Guiness another pint of Yards, tater tots with cheese whiz and a cheeseburger. Surly waitress plopped a basket of condiments in front of us huffily. The tater tots were good in a "this is totally going to make me regret eating this" type of way. Oily and salty. It'll probably make my ankles swell and my poop turn black. But it was $5- what?!?. crap i should have just bought another beer. The cheeseburger should have been $2, but it was $7. It was an abomination to all cheeseburgers. I felt really bad because we wanted to grab the check- but the waitress was busy shoveling chili or some sort of soupy jambalaya concoction into her surly mouth at the table across from us. So we waited until she finished slurping and asked for the check. Funny, it took her a long time to serve us but she couldn't wait to grab the bill (and the tip). Pluses: Awesome happy hour, Guiness was not bad, Basket o' condiments (they even had sriracha sauce!), cute tattooed bartenders, free lollipops, cool atmosphere Minus: Food overpriced and bad (though the soupy jambalaya chilli looking thing the surly waitress was shoveling in her mouth looked good though..), questionable table service, and our bill was $25.
label: NEG

text: This review is reflected solely on the all you can eat lunch at Kokopelli Sushi. You can get much better quality of all you can eat sushi elsewhere with the price ($17.99). It is $21.99 if you want to include sashimi. The free sake on Mon-Wed helped to get our business. The seafood at Kokopelli is decently fresh. The rolls are not spectacular. I ordered a dragon roll; it had no avocado in it! Other reviewers had mentioned the mountain roll is good. I gave it a try; it is only okay. I would appreciate if the menu indicates 'fake' crab meat under the description. Miso soup tasted like water. The salmon skin hand roll, baked yellow tail chin, and upside down shrimps were the only ones I enjoyed out of the many items I ordered. However, both the waitresses and the chefs do provide speedy and friendly service. I guess it's Reno; there aren't many good sushi places to begin with. Who goes to Reno for sushi anyway? It's all about the buffet. With the price you're paying for a mediocre all you can eat sushi, I would say you're better off with the buffet across the street.
label: NEG

text: This place was quite a treat. I had the opportunity to come here Sunday of Labor Day weekend. There wasn't much of a wait, which is a shame because while you wait you can view the garden and nursery or sit inside and sip on a pellegrino. We sat in the garden in one of maybe three tables. Expect a slow meal if you sit here and note there is only breakfast served on weekends. The food is as fresh as it gets and very flavorful. I wanted everything on the menu-- even the granola (which I refuse to order in a restaurant, on hungover mornings). The staff was very attentive and friendly. This place is a solid place for guests and the rents-- and very reasonably priced for what you get! I desparately wish there was something like this in San Fran!
label: POS

text: The quickest memory that comes to mind that I have of the Bayou are the bartenders. All the guys seems to have a stick up their butt. They are kind of cocky and mean, especially on a friday or saturday night. I've gotten better service on slower nights there however. The food is kinda mediocre at best. The only thing this place has going for it are the cheap light beer specials, and the fact that they support the local inter-mural sports teams. Work on the customer service, and I'll definitely swing by there again...

Meat all seemed cooked to petfection. The atmosphere is elegant and tables are spread out enough to be a little loud. The room is large!

So adjusting my cravings, I broadened my search to "bakery" and looked for something closer to home. Hmm. Donuts? Can I eat a donut? Yes. Yes I can. If they're from Buttermilk Drop. text: Growing up, this was my favorite place to go on Tuesday mornings! Sometimes my mom would take me during the school year and I'd get a note to go to school late, "doctor's appointment" and all that. I believe now it's also open on Saturdays, but Tuesday is still the OG in my book. You can find just about everything here. At least ten years ago I bought these plaid reusable shopping bags that I still use, and everywhere I go people ask me about them. I've bought incense, patchouli, baskets, sunglasses, baseball hats, flip flops, clothes, and nail polish here. And lets not forget the soft pretzels and baked goods straight from Amish Country. I can't wait to go home again so I can visit Rice's!

The shredded cheddar cheese wasn't even melted on the burger. The buns were soaked at least have way through with grease and that's all you could taste. The Pepsi was flat, the ice tea was about two shades darker than water. The service was slow and they forgot one of the children's entrees, leaving her to wait a significant amount of time for her food while the rest of us had ours. None of us drank any beer but I can't imagine its that amazing given the food quality. The decor is really nice but who cares when the food is so blech? If you have ever been to Granite City Illinois... the food here tastes like GC IL looks.
label: NEG

text: I've been looking for something as fantastico as Chipotle in the US (see my previous review). I've heard rumours that the chain would be coming to Canada but...nothing yet. Mucho Burrito comes close! It's the same concept. Choose your filling (chicken, beef, pork, veggie), choose your preparation (burrito, taco, quesedilla, bowl), choose your salsa (and yes, the "hot" is hot) and chow down! The price is reasonable and the staff have always been great. I don't get to go often (as there are not yet any in Calgary) but I try to go whenever I'm up in Edmonton. It's not "authentic" as a Mexican Restaurant, nor do I think it's trying to be. A terrific fresh substitute for Taco Time. They also do catering. And not the typical pre-made fare. We had them come in for a work lunch and it was amazing. They bring each of the ingredients separately and allow the guests to make their own meal. They also provide a demonstration on how to fill and fold your burrito :)
label: POS

But if you can pick it up, the pie is wonderful, and they have a healthy selection of nonhealthy toppings. I like prosciutto and garlic. They have a prosciutto and chicken pizza, but the last one I got sported some pretty weary bird. Can't recommend it. Oh yeah, their chicken caesar salad is really good too! Anyhoo, the restaurant itself is a little creepy and pretty divey, in a family-style dive sorta way. Just get the pizza and get out.

I wish I could give them 3 stars and if I could I'd award them two and a half stars. The food, the drinks, the service and despite looking especially decadent, the baked goods are all average at best. What a shame.

text: Awful awful awful experience here. Leased a vehicle 2 years ago, returned to exercise the purchase option. My wife called several times to speak to someone about obtaining a full payoff. Her calls were never returned so I finally called and explained the lack of response to the female operator, which prompted her to simply forward me to voicemail as well (?!). I called back immediately and reiterated that our problem was that our voicemails werent being replied to, so please do not send me to voicemail again, to which the operator audibly sighed and offered begrudgingly to have the finance guy paged. I said thank you and was placed on hold. After 10 mins on hold, I hung up and called back to the same woman who said, without a hint of apology, that "oh he must not be around he hasnt answered the page, would you like his voicemail?" I left another voicemail, got no response after 3 days, so i call back, get the same voicemail/page run-around, and this time demand to speak to a supervisor. the next day i receive a call from the finance guy who immediately begins the conversation by saying "i talked to your wife several times" in an annoyed and confrontational tone. ?? Aside from being a complete lie (my wife never had any of her calls returned), it also set the stage for an awkward dynamic of working to get this payoff completed. he says to come to the showroom. in the showroom, 2 guys immediately approach me by the desk asking how they can help me with big smiles and i explain im looking to buy out my lease and need to see the finance guy....which prompts the two salesmen to immediately make disappointed facial expressions, one walking away from me without a word, and the other practically rolling his eyes as he tells me to go wait in the service waiting area. i sit in the little service area which is plastered with signs saying how "anything less than 100% satisfaction is considered failure to us", despite my experience so far consisting of nothing but complete indifference and barely disguised disgust. after 20 mins of sitting there, no one checks on me or updates me on whats going on, and i begin to worry if the annoyed salesman ever even notified anyone of my presence, so i walk back to the showroom and ask if there is an ETA for the finance guy to talk to me as its been over 20mins...this causes the 3 guys at the desk to again roll their eyes. The guy who appears to be the supervisor tells me that "someone will be with you shortly", again with an inexplicably annoyed tone. So i go back to the waiting room and after another 10 mins, the finance guy comes out hurried and I remind him that i have the rough payoff from the lease paperwork, but i need the full final quote from mazda including the tax, transfer fees, etc...so i can go to my bank and cut them a check...thats all i want, and the paperwork worked up to do all this. he responds by pressuring me to me finance instead of paying cash. (?) I politely decline the offer to finance, and he persists, asking me to confirm that I "didnt borrow the money from anyone did you?" after insisting that i just want the payoff, he disappears for a while, and comes back with the payoff quote and 2 more extended warranty quotes. it takes me a few tense exchanges to refuse the warranty offers. i ask him to write down the exact quote so i can get a bankcheck cut, and he writes it on an old bill i have in hand. i take the quote to the bank and hand them the slip and they cant read his handwriting. so i call the dealership from the bank and again, get sent to voicemail after requesting do not send me to voicemail. i have to call 4 different times to finally get an operator at the pacifico ford building who is nice and receptive to the fact that i just need to speak to a human for 20 seconds. all told, spend over 45mins on the phone trying to get the handwritten quote clarified. head back to shop with check for 20k in hand and finance guy says "can you come back tomorrow?" (!) because he is now working on a new customer. i say no, and he switches back to my paperwork. a few mins into it, the supervisor in the hyundai building storms into the office and demands to know why finance guy is helping me and not the new customer, turning to me and saying "no offense to you buddy" !!! if i hadnt invested hours already i wouldve left right then, as i cant comprehend how any manager would have the gall to do this. they made no attempt to hide their contempt for me, and pass me on to a different finance guy who finishes my paperwork in under 10mins. the final insult, he hands me the new license plate and is again visibly annoyed when i ask that they swap the plates for me. to be clear, the mazda product was great....but that dealership was so insanely bad that i swore i was on some sort of candid camera show. avoid this place at all costs.
label: NEG

text: I went the 1st night they were open after Gustav and had good food and excellent service. Even better an out of town family member was footing the bill. My uncle felt that the chicory coffee creme brulee was a platonic dessert.
label: POS

text: I would describe the Troc as being gross. Maybe I have just had especially bad experiences, but not much good has come from this place. The concerts I've seen here, despite being by bands I like, were mediocre. For some reason, maybe the setup of the stage or size of the room, I just didn't experience any connection with the band. But let's rewind a little to outside the theatre. The lines are too long and the security is too tight. I not only HAVE to check my camera at the door, but I have to pay a fee to do so. All this after waiting in line with some pretty intolerable people. I think most days you can tell what kind of show it is by the crowd outside. Once inside I spend my time avoiding the ones in the crowd that I might sort of know. The crown jewel of my experience at the Troc was visiting the bathroom only to be greeted by a puddle of vomit in the doorway. I really can't blame whoever left it there though.It helps that it's near a WaWa, but the crowd from the show just heads there too. Now, I won't avoid a show just because it's at the Trocadero but I'll certainly sigh and hope the band tries the TLA next time they come to Philly.
label: NEG

text: What can I say but awesome? First, I love the Grill because it never closes. Try to find something open on Sunday evening in Tucson is impossible, but the Grill is always there, waiting for us. But just because it's open is not the only reason to go (otherwise I would go to Denny's or I-Slop, but I don't). The food is really top notch diner food. Usually I get the tuna melt and it never dissapoints. The bread is phenomenal, and I can't tell you why, but it is. Last time there I got the biscuits and gravy. They use corn meal biscuits, different but certainly tastier than the doughy biscuits usually covered in sausage gravy. The staff is always polite, but if you think all tatooed folks are pretentious, well, then you have already made up your mind. They have always been attentive, whether it's 8pm on a Sunday or midnight on a Wednesday. Sure, the bathrooms may be small, but I don't eat in the bathroom. Love this place; it makes the Old Pueblo that much more liveable.
label: POS

text: I first visited this location during my lunch break, but after seeing their phenomenal beer and wine specials, returned after work. Great outdoor seating to bring pets. I would suggest splitting orders so you can try more of their menu and the servings are large. Mon & Tues are $2 pitchers of Abita Amber or Bud Light and Wednesdays are $10 bottles of certain wines. Also, check out their coupons to print on their website before going!!! Other things that were great: friendly and fast service and the restaurant is SUPER CLEAN which is always a huge plus!

text: I really hate this place yet I find myself here at the end of every night I end up going out in Philly. Bouncers are so rude (even though we've been coming here for years and they know us). Not like I'm looking for preferential treatment, but everyone is deserving of civility. They don't make girls pay cover anymore which is great and the only real reason we go is to dance. I always(x2) bump into people I know and it is an average priced bar ($3 waters, etc). Anyway, try another after hours spot if you wanna keep the night going, people are usually super wasted and the dance floor is uncomfortable because it is suffocatingly small. You'll leave unhappy.

text: The first time I read about Cheeseology on Yelp, I thought, I just have to go there. Twas love-at-first-read. And let me tell you: it was also love at first bite. My friend and I split the chicken scampi and bacon, bacon mac and cheeses and both were just dee-viinnee! I liked the chicken scampi better because it seemed more flavorful but I'm not one to turn down bacon. My other friend got the basil pesto mac and cheese which was also glorious... I'm a carnivore so I probably would want to get that with some sort of protein but twas still delicious on its own. A word to the wise: the regular size (2 1/2 cups of macaroni) is more than enough for a human being. And what's even better: the price point is extremely affordable.. about $8 with tax for one regular-size order of their mac-and-cheese. Cheeseology is a small hole-in-the-wall joint that's very low-key and is the perfect place to have lunch with friends or grab a quick bite to eat for dinner. I know I'll definitely be back the next chance I get!
label: POS

text: Thank goodness for Melanie. I usually color my hair at home, but when a transition from brown to blonde turned out bright yellow and patchy (I swear I did it once before and it worked then!), I knew I needed some professional help - and FAST. Beauty Brands got me in for a same-day appointment, and Melanie spent a lot of time just talking with me and explaining the options I had for fixing the mess I'd gotten myself into. She even had a senior stylist come over and make sure that her plan for my hair would be the best way to go. She worked magic with the bleach and then used a toner to turn the bright yellow into a perfect light blonde - EXACTLY what I wanted. I didn't get a cut so I can't attest to her skills with the shears, but that girl can wield a bleach wand like nobody's business. It won't take another botched at-home color job to get me back there.
label: POS

text: I am a huge fan of the Body Shop. This particular location is great because it is in close proximity to Sephora where I can stock up on skin care and make-up and then head to the Body Shop to buy body care products. I appreciate the fact that girls who work here are friendly and extremely helpful. Whenever I have any questions or need recommendations, sales ladies' assistance is invaluable since they know the inventory inside and out. Most of Body Shop's products I have tried deliver on their promise. Some of my favourite products which I buy over and over again are body butters and brushes, and hemp hand protector. These items are something I would definitely take on the deserted island with me. During holiday season the Body Shop creates fantastic gift baskets which are sure to please the receiver. Another great thing is that most Body Shop's products are natural and packed in recycled bottles; none of the products are tested on animals; and proceeds from sales support charities that fight violence against women. All these aspects make the Body Shop a store worth visiting and shopping at.
label: POS

text: I have been a long time fan of Fresco and do love the food there. Great desserts, soups, salads... you name it, it's delicious there. I actually like Fresco's food so much that I have endured the awkward set up, annoying atmosphere, crowded 5 pts parking lot, and high prices for many years. Customer service is a big deal to me and over the years, have gotten both stellar and not so great service from the employees behind the counter. However the customer service from the management, namely the manager Jesse has always been non existent. I have had numerous to-go orders messed up during my time as a Fresco customer, and dealing with this person to get help in anyway is a complete waste of time. He lacks empathy, and resists rectifying any problem, large or small. I will miss the food at Fresco, but never the prices or customer service. There are too many great restaurants in SB to waste my time and money here.
label: NEG

text: When we got our dog last year, our neighbor raved about La Cumbre Animal Hospital, and since he also has an "aggressive breed" dog (although she's the least aggressive dog I think I've ever met), we trusted his advice and took our pup there. When I first called and mentioned our neighbor, they knew exactly who he was and his dog's name, which was a good sign to me that they pay a lot of attention to their clients. And I was right. Our dog has always received excellent care at La Cumbre. We've seen several of the vets and they are always great - they are very gentle with our pup and they take the time to explain things and answer any of our questions. They are also really honest when giving us options about treatments or tests so that we can weigh the necessity vs. the cost and decide what to do. This is really important because owning a dog can be really expensive, and you don't want your vet to be like an auto mechanic who tries to tell you that you need a new transmission when all you wanted was an oil change. Of course, pets are infinitely more precious than a car, but you get my point. Everyone at La Cumbre clearly loves animals and they always seem excited to see my dog when we come in, which makes me feel at ease leaving him with them. I wouldn't take him anywhere else.
label: POS

text: My father and i eat there every day. and have been going there for over two years now and are always pleased with the food and service. P.s. they have the best burgers in town!!!

text: I've stayed here a couple of times and also at another place they manage in the Marigny. Always had a pleasant stay with Mary and Hugh :)

And lots of sweets--even sundaes and shakes for this hot summer. It has vintage Beatles decor, funky design, free wifi, and great coffee and teas. Special evening theme meals are happening and its fun to bring along friends.

text: I love McDonald's Monopoly. More specifically, I love peeling off the game pieces from the packaging. As a kid and throughout high-school, I'd skip out on the school cafeteria for a Micky D and purchase any number of items that contain the pieces. I liken it to the thrill of scratch-off lottery tickets. Maybe it's the anticipation of what property or prize I'm going to get, or maybe it's the fun of filling out a piece of paper to create a game board. Alas, as I graduated college I stopped going to McDonald's completely, for reasons I don't even have to explain for you to know why. One morning in October that just past, I found out MacDougle's Monopoly game was happening again. The promotion had been going on for a few weeks with two more to go. I thought about it. I kinda wanted to peel the pieces once more. I saw that the pieces are on the hash browns; one of the few items McDonald's serves that won't make me vomit. When I arrived back at my office, I opened the bag and saw no game pieces. Thanks McDonald's Family Restaurant of Temple, for reminding me never to visit again and that the Monopoly fun will always be a fond memory.

text: It is ALWAYS about the shoes. You know it. I know it. Let's go to Studio 615 and do some damage shall we? With the new addition of Sole 615 adjoining Studio 615's already fun interior, now you can stretch out and get comfortable as the balance on your AMEX grows by the minute. The styles are all on-point with trends that are in the glossy fashion magazines but lack the 4 digit price points and rarely bypass the 3 digit points. These pieces are not going to last forever but you can certainly get good use through a season...besides...do you really want to wear them after that anyway? I invest in classic pieces from well known designers but Studio 615 is a fantastic option to infuse more risk and trend into your wardrobe without feeling the guilt! I have bought cute mini day-dresses and jewelry on a previous visit but decided to stroll through the new shoe boutique Sole 615 today. The merchandising is clean and uncluttered and Darnice the owner offered genuine customer service while I fell in LOVE with much of the inventory. Studded gladiator sandals, cobalt blue faux suede booties, and red, black and gold colorblocked platforms all rounded out the inventory. I then turned the corner and locked eyes with a shimmery pair of glitter silver platform heels that oooozed Betsey Johnson's quirk and whimsy....minus the price-tag. SOLD! An in-store promotion knocked $20 off the $105 price-tag and I breezed out of the door spending nearly 1/3 of what I would have at Betsey Johnson. She's not the only one who can do cartwheels down the runway now, huh? Most apparel is priced comfortably between $40-$100 and shoes are around the same, although some of the newer brands can go up to the $200 range. Costume jewelry was priced well as I almost snatched up a wide studded bangle bracelet for $25. Purses were in full effect and had good price points to round out the accessories section. A healthy sale area is also available and I noticed that some items were as low as $10 for bargain hunters. Be sure to add your name to the Studio 615 email list for updates on promotions an events to help your dollar stretch even further.

text: I've been to the Mann Center three times, seeing the Decemberists, Death Cab for Cutie, and R.E.M. It's a great outdoor venue for somewhat upscale summer concerts. I'm used to going to indie concerts with standing room only and a packed crowd, so it really is a luxury to be able to sit down and enjoy the show fully. The Mann attracts some big name artists along with their traditional classical music concerts with orchestras and solo performers. Over the last few years, the Mann has been adding some more "hip" and "popular" mainstream bands into the lineup, like the ones that I have seen. Look for more such bands in following summers... The Mann is a bit pricey for my budget though. For the concerts I've been to, I have bought the cheapest seated tickets, which have been around $40-50 (they do have lawn seating). If you do go the economic route, I suggest buying early and requesting the balcony box seats: they have a fabulous bird's eye and unobstructed view of the stage, plus they come in under the lowest price package. They do sell food and refreshments at their concerts, but everything is way too expensive, like professional sports game food and drink. They have some fine dinning restaurants on site, but I have not ventured to try them. The acoustics are not great at the Mann. In the words of Ben Gibbard (Death Cab for Cutie), the Mann is "really boom-y". The sound is full but slightly echos in the huge enclosed wooden structure. I was not impressed by the acoustics but I didn't expect to be impressed by a large outdoor venue like the Mann. In conclusion, if an artist you love is coming to the Mann Center, by all means get tickets and go. I am pretty sure you will enjoy it!

text: My favorite place for Korean food in Tucson. I have never had the Teppanyaki here, just the Korean food and sushi. Quick FYI, I am half Korean. So we have been to this place, oh about a dozen times since we moved to Tucson a couple years back. I have tried plenty on their menu, and have to say they do a pretty good job at what I have had. Is it homemade Korean? No, of course not, its a restaurant, I get homemade Korean when I make it at home. But with that said, they still make things pretty authentic. A bit Americanized on somethings, but I would to to survive in this town. So...The Kimchi Jjigae (kimchee stew) is my favorite. I have been resorting to this the last few times I have come here, sometimes I spice it up with some Al Jjigae (fish roe) and I love the amount of fish roe that they put in it! Most places give you a small amount. Here I could fill up on it alone. They had a special on the menu around Christmas time, JamPong (Spicy seafood noodle soup) it had awesome flavor, lots of seafood but was sadly filled with what tasted like store bough spaghetti noodles. Homemade noodles would of made it almost perfect. Even with the noodles, I would order it again. But if you like it spicy, make sure to tell them you want it extra spicy! The different Banchan (Side dishes that come with a korean entree) are always different. I love that. They are all very good. Even the wierd little deep fried baby shrimp thingers I have never seen before. But the sushi chef, (and later) My mom assured me that it is a good calcium enriched side dish. I ate it, it was good, tasted like shrimp crackers. We have also eaten at the Korean BBQ tables, I would say they are average on what you come to expect. Good tasting meat, bulgogi, kalbi, etc., good dipping sauce, nice fresh lettuce, attentive wait staff to help cook when you are talking too much. Nothing to complain about here. I would take a Korean food newbie here to let them experience it, and know that they would probably love it. The sushi, well I am a picky sushi eater, the husband on the other hand says he is, but eats the slightly fishy stuff I wont touch. He says he loves their sushi, but I think thats because it is all you can eat for $19.95! Great deal, saves on my wallet. The white tuna is great, I love that stuff...but the rest is ok. Mind you my favorite sushi is made in the sushi joints in SoCal and Hawaii...so for Tucson, yes, their sushi is good. Never had a piece that grossed me out to never eat there again (like other places around town).

text: "Oh, how the mighty have fallen" ...and it's so, so sad. A tiny part of my soul has died while shedding Broccoli Cheddar flavored tears. Alas, all good things must come to an end. Dammit. Yea. Wow. Duhhh. Hey, Omar- you don't need to have Superman X-ray powers to find slices of white bread in a huge CLEAR plastic bag! How hard is it to NOT select a piece of wheat bread, or dutch crust or some funky garlic smelling bread and pick up the piece of white bread next to it? How did you even get a job, if you're that damn inept?! Why can I pick my own bread for my sandwich and not my soup? Why am I forced to eat whatever scraps of bread you deem worthy? Why do I have to pay for bread I don't like and won't eat because you're lazy?! So my boyfriend, being the nice guy that he is- just takes the bag of bread he's given. Actually, I think his acquiesence is probably due to the fact that he has a bad temper and it's easier to just shut up sometimes than argue with an idiot. So yea. He goes to pay for the soup and discovers Omar (duh duh duh) only marked that he had one soup. Not that free soup is a bad thing, but it's generally accepted that 'honesty is the best policy' - so he points out the error and pays for his food. (As I'm sure the owner of the Deli would have wanted him too) I can't take it personal though, according to the ladies at the register Omar had managed to muck up a bunch of orders before ours. Surprise, surpise there is zero white bread in the bag. Instead we have a large pile of the funky smelling garlic bread. Oh my, isn't that nice? I guess my palate isn't delicate enough to appreciate garlic bread with Broccoli Cheddar soup. Ooops, I meant Broccoli Water. My soup was not soup. But I resisted the urge to hurl my broccoli water across the room, but only because I knew I'd be the one cleaning it up. Thanks a lot Omar, you destroyed my faith in Deli Towne and it's ability to consistently provide the level of service and yummy-ness required. It's too much of a risk going all the way there after being let down by your laziness and 'can't do' attitude. "Make a fool of you once, shame on them. Make a fool of you twice, shame on me". text: I was at the Spectrum for possibly the last time this past evening to see Neil Young...I will miss it dearly...mostly. The Spectrum was the site of my first-ever "real" concert (Page/Plant in '95), as well as countless sporting/other miscellaneous events as far back as early childhood (Monster Truck Rally? Sesame Street On Ice? Yes please!). Sure, compared to newer arenas, it isn't so hot...the concourse is maybe a quarter as wide as at the new spot (whatever bank it is named after this week), which makes it tough to get from your seat to the bathroom (and there aren't nearly as many bathrooms). If you are in line for refreshments, you will be right in the middle of the main foot traffic. Some seats have no view whatsoever (other than a wall), and to get to those seats you have to climb up many narrow, precarious stairs (saw people take a header more than once). But despite all that, The Spectrum had character, something the new venues do not (they differ only on the outside, and then only slightly). The concert acoustics (never a strength of these venues) were better than most, and were sometimes even very good (it depended on the artist). So fare thee well, Spectrum, as you depart into the ether. Thanks for the memories!

text: It's always been my nerdy little goal in life to visit the Mutter Museum. After years of entertaining the idea, I finally realized my dream. It took a ten hour flight from Hawaii to NY, then a bus ride from NY to Philly, and then a long cold icy rainy walk from the 30th St. Station to get there, complete with slipping on ice and eating it on the sidewalk (I'm sure my clumsy ass gave some entertainment to cars driving by), but it was totally worth it! Being that I'm an enthusiastic nerd when it comes to human anatomy and physiology (medical marvels, yes!!!), Mutter Museum was like my mecca. It just blew my mind, the extensive collection of specimens and learning aids... the fact that they were so well-kept considering their age... amazing! For a geek like me, it was absolute paradise. Medical specimens, historical gadgets and instruments, informative exhibits, and anomalies! The Soap Woman! Giant intestine! Even a huge collection of random objects that people swallowed and had removed! And human skin bound notebooks! Moleskine notebooks are nothing compared to those! Every minute I spent in there was full of awe and excitement. My friend was a little disturbed and felt uneasy when we were in the downstairs room full of specimens, but she was fascinated. I must say, 5 star experience!!! ACE!

text: One of my friends came down from Moscow for a few days this week, and wanted to meet up for dinner. His one stipulation was that we get something we couldn't get in Moscow.
