We rolled into the parking lot and saw chairs stacked on the tables. Disappointed, we started to back out when one of the restaurants employees knocked on the passenger-side window and invited us to come in anyway. Normally I feel like a jerk when I make restaurant staff stay late, but they were so damn inviting that I couldn't say no. Chef Roland came out and sold us on blackened prime rib (for the three friends who were with me) and blackened catfish (for me!). You always start out the meal with a bowl of gumbo or jambalaya. Both are exceptional, but I like the jambalaya a little bit more (it's tomato-based and a touch spicier. Mmmm). The serving sizes are generous and come with numerous sides. The catfish (which I think was a special) was coated in a delightful spice rub and cooked perfectly, and my three friends seemed to enjoy the prime rib immensely. After our meal Chef Roland tried to sell us on dessert (which all sounded amazing) but I always leave that place too full to function, let alone properly enjoy bread pudding with Chef's own whiskey sauce. This place is the perfect place to go on cold nights when all you need is some spicy soul food in your belly. A Star for staying open an hour later just to serve four more people. Chef Roland, you're amazing!

text: Yangming is much like the Main Line; pretentious, over-rated, uninspired, and a bit of a tired cliche. Here on the Main Line, it doesn't have to be good, it just has to have the mythos of being good. But what a ancient myth it is in the case of Yangming (circa early 1990s to be exact). Yangming was one of the first restaurants in the Philly area offering Asian Fusion. At the time it was unique and notable. But with the growth of Asian Fusion cuisine, Yangming has been left behind. Yangming's fusion is stale and timid. Is the food bad? No. Yangming uses quality ingredients and what results is passable. But it is hardly what they promise, a great dining experience. Unfortunately Yangming is too much fusion to be a good Chinese restaurant, and too lackluster to be a great Asian Fusion choice. As for service, well, surly Asian waiters may be authentic, but not what I'd desire at a place where the tab for two could easily exceed $100. The decor is straight out of the early 90's and lacks any interest. Like the cuisine at Yangming, the ambience is tiredly refined.

Having a "memphis style pulled pork sandwich" with "Memphis style BBQ sauce" brought a generous portion of pulled pork on a toasted bun. Okay, that's a good sign. The pork was a little fatty but had a hint of being truly smoked BBQ'd. The "Memphis style BBQ sauce" however left us scratching our heads until they almost bled. What is supposed to be barbecue sauce, the way they make it in Memphis is little more than a clear, beef-boullion-looking little cup of spiced-up Italian dressing. No kidding. We even asked if it were a mistake. I'm from the deep south and know Tennessee like the back of my hand, it's where much family hails from. I've always known Tennessee BBQ sauce to be mild in its consistency, yet tangy-spicy sweet. No so at Iron Hill. text: We were looking for a more "upscale" place to go watch the Blues' home opener on Saturday, and took the RFT's recommendation of the Over/Under Bar & Grill on Washington. First impression: this place is LOUD. Really loud. Hard-to-hold-a-conversation loud. The main event was the Mizzou game, however, we made our way to a smaller room off on the right as you enter the building and found the Blues' pre-game show on a TV in there and settled in. We shouted our drink order (because it was LOUD) to the server, who was quite nice - he got a Schlafly OcktoberFest on tap, I got the "Washington Avenue" cocktail, which was tasty, but which didn't seem to have much alcohol in it, especially given the price. The food was OK. The Tower of Onion Rings was a silly presentation, but the rings themselves were quite tasty and well prepared, not greasy at all and the dipping sauce that came with was spicy and yummy. These were probably the best thing we tried! He got a veggie burger (it's a mixed marriage - he's vegetarian and I'm omnivorous), said it was nothing special - he suspected it was Boca or Morningstar Farms frozen patty, nothing more. I got a blackened chicken sandwich - again, OK, nothing special, a little too much special sauce for my taste. Waffle fries would have been better if they'd have been delivered a little quicker to our table. We skipped dessert in favor of another round of drinks - another beer for the man, and I went for the Raspberry Chocolate Martini. HIGHLY recommend this drink - Chambord vodka and 360 Double Chocolate vodka and wow. That was good... This is a good place to watch a game as long as you don't mind the LOUD. There is little in the way of decor beyond the TVs...I'd seen the word "minimalist" used to describe the interior, but I think "minimal" is more apt. I doubt we'll return; for the price I think I'd sooner go someplace a little more wallet-friendly and a little less LOUD.

text: My friend suggested going to Boualong last night, as she raves this is the best Thai restaurant in town, and the only one she goes to. And my friend knows her food! We got there around 7pm, and all six tables were taken already. There was a waiting line in progress, and the waitress told us it was going to be a half hour wait. Seeing as we weren't starving yet, we decided to wait it out. The waiting game takes place in a long and narrow corridor at the back of the restaurant. The restaurant is family-owned, and it's a very old and small building. But somehow the cracks in the walls and the cramped space adds to its charm. There are paintings, photographs, and wooden carvings hanging on the walls for decor. You feel like it's one of those delicious secrets only you know about, except it's one of Edmonton's most popular restaurants. The packed tables and the constant queue attest to that. We didn't have to wait a full half hour for a table. There are two waitresses, and they both work together to serve all tables. I ordered the hot tea, as yesterday was our first day of snow I believe, and I was freezing! It took awhile for the tea to arrive, and I started to wonder if they had forgotten about it, but it came eventually. The food was brought out in a matter of no time, which was very impressive, as there is only a single cook in the kitchen. We ordered the yum and matsamun curry to share between the three of us. The yum was exactly that -- yummy! It's basically glass noodles heaped with peanut sauce, cilantro and mint, carrots, shrimp and chicken. You can order it in different varieties as well. The matsamun curry was very spicy, I was able to tell from the first bite. This is not mild curry they use here, so if you're not used to spicy foods, you might want to ask them which is more mild. I think I'm average when it comes to eating spicy, but I downed two glasses of water with my first helping of the matsamun that night. Despite that, it was delicious. It had chunks of chicken with lots of potatoes, and served with a dish of rice. Our meal came out to be quite inexpensive, at $11 for each of us, including tip. I'll probably come here again, but now I know not to underestimate their curry. And to come before 6pm, so I can get an empty table.

text: New Years Eve at Sycamore was a great way to end the year and welcome in the new year. So the perfect opportunity presented itself during NYE. OK, first thing is first, Sam J is the chef who is a fellow Yelper and a good friend, so there's no cards hidden here in this review. Sam has this down home, hearty, and absolutely tasty way of preparing his menu. It's obvious from the first course to the last. Everything he prepares is full of flavor, robust and will warm your soul. You will leave satisfied in every sense of the word except that I wanted to have more of Sam's company while enjoying the meal so he could tell me about each dish. I had so many questions as to its origin and why he selected the menu including how he accomplished the dish. I'm having a hard time picking my favorite but I'd have to say the one that stands out was the duck confit due to its full bodied flavor that was perfect with our red wine selection. My other favorite was the pork belly stew in a the single serving Le Creuset dish that warmed my belly and reminded me of my grandmother's cooking from the presentation all the way to the last scoop I only wished I had a larger bowl.......lol (although I did get to finish my gf's). By the time cheese plate and dessert rolled around I was completely satisfied but somehow found a reserve to push in that super rich chocolate cake and hot chocolate (was the white chocolate?). The whole experience was topped off with great service from our waitress who hustled her buns off. Michelle kept the wine topped and the plates moving................ wait, I don't think I'm finished with that dessert......LOL! Just kidding, there was no way I could make room for anything else. Oh, don't worry, I'll be back and hopefully with some of our Yelp group and I would only, selfishly, ask for a slow night so Sam could sit with us a little so we could enjoy his company. Cheers!

As so many dishes were passed around our table and shared I'll admit nothing was exciting but all that I tasted was good. The Fishtown Chowder was mild but really tasty at the same time. I would definitely return for that on a cold night. The spinach salad with walnuts was standard but good and the sheppards pie was good but bland. Salt and Pepper were not offered on the table but instead, shakers with some sort of their own special seasonings which seemed the color of old bay. Not knowing what exactly that was made it less enticing to use apprently, since no one at our table did. The potatoes and minced lamb was really tasty but that's all there was. Someone at the table longed for peas and onions or something, anything to liven it up. The crab cakes were very good and the potato encrusted salmon sounded more interesting than the reality of it being just hashbrown shredded potato atop the salmon. It was good though, dont get me wrong, just not as encrustastic. Dessert was a shared sweet potato cheese cake which was light and delicous and then there was their version of home made butter cake. It's not butter cake in any sense that I grew up with but it was very good nonetheless. The menu is conservative but tasty and with plenty of low priced options. I hope this neighborhood establishment which has been transformed sticks around a long time.

Truthfully, we pigged out on the phenomenal bread, but we were so full by the time we got to the pizza that we could barely start it. Oh well, I was happy to bring the bulk of it home. The polenta and hearts of palm were excellent, the olives and arancini decent. None blew me away as much as the bread, but given the price I'm not complaining. Services was excellent - a little slow bringing the check, but otherwise spot on. The biggest disappointments were the drinks - we agreed that the Fig Sangria was difficult to distinguish from Franzia Burgundy, and the Meloncello was poorly mixed - but I have no complaints otherwise. They may do well on total house moves, but coordinating the packing for a split household was a nightmare tho I went through and had things placed in corners and specific cabinets with yellow sticky notes on them, I still had to go behind the packers and ask them to pack things they'd missed.I found out during unpacking they'd also packed several things they shouldn't have. It was several months after delivery before me and the person who stayed in the house were able to get everything shipped back and forth to each other. Considering some of these things were heavy floor lamps, you can imagine the additional cost and frustration. Coordinating their delivery to TX was also nightmarish. We had one date arranged, then they changed it to a week I was traveling and they threatened to not deliver my goods for 2 months unless I changed my plans. I changed my plans, then they wanted to deliver everything the week of my revised travel plans!! Once we had a plan established, there were several more changes with the transporters due to poorly scheduled shuttles to them while they were en route, their wanting to visit family on their way to my city, and their ignoring explicit directions on how to get to my storage unit. The delivery men arrived hung over and were irritable with my wanting to inventory all the boxes to make sure everything arrived, as I'd been instructed to do. They also became impatient when I insisted on inspecting the expensive items and documenting the damages. I have fine furniture and antiques that came to me with scratches and dents because it had not been wrapped in blankets. I had leather furniture that arrived with holes and gashes because it had not been protecte. My aluminum patio furniture arrived with scratches also. Incredible. I did purchase insurance, but was unable to find the paperwork or interpret it sufficiently to file a claim in the 6 months available to do so. I also found the person who sold me this service was largely unavailable during the delivery and complaints process, though his assistant did try to compensate for his absence. This company markets themselves as being reputable because they provide moving services for our military. Extremely disappointing from so many aspects...

text: I was completely and irrevocably disappointed in my experience here. After hearing so many great things about Bombay, while recently being visited by two friends from out of state, I took them here as one of our first stops along Bourbon St. What a mistake, but an educational one. Here's how it went down... Upon entering, we grabbed three seats at the EMPTY bar thinking this would be the fastest way to try some tasty martinis. Twenty minutes later, the bartender had yet to even look at us, let alone ask us what we'd like, and we were the only ones sitting at the bar! And yes, there was only one bartender. I don't care how busy she was, she could at least have taken 5 seconds to ask us if we'd like to see a menu, a single one of which I could find nowhere. So we decided to move to a table in hopes a server would pay us more mind. This strategy eventually worked, and I stress eventually, so we were finally able to at least look at a menu. I for one, already knew what I wanted. I'd even seen their YouTube video of it being made, the Key Lime Pie Martini, so that's what I ordered. (I feel it important to note they are proud enough of this drink to actually post a video of it on YouTube) What I got looked nothing like what I'd seen get made, and it didn't even have the same ingredients, and yet they swore it was made correctly. After asking if there was some mix-up, they asked me if I'd like stuff added that it was supposed to have in the first place! It was like ordering a cheeseburger and then when the hamburger without cheese showed up, being asked if I'd like cheese on my cheeseburger. What the F? I have no desire to return here. Atrocious customer service with an inability to make their own drinks as they themselves advertise, equals one star.

text: Wow, I am sorry to hear about the negative experiences people have had at Sahara Sams. My husband, son, and I and went this evening and had a really great time. My experience might be different since I was given some free passes and also went on a very cold Dec. Night. First off, the place is clean - very clean. This is important to me when it comes to water parks. Second, I recommend water shoes since I found certain areas to be slick. We brought our own arm floaties for my son and didn't use their jackets. The flow rider was closed for some maintenence and I was told this was why the place was empty. Apparently, even in Dec., the place is popular for it's flow rider machine. I didn't care about the flow rider being closed, but had I paid full price for a ticket, I might had felt different. In any case, it didn't bother us. There were signs on the door that said the flow rider was closed. The staff was all young, but I didn't witness any rudeness. I talked to several of the lifeguards and they were friendly. Even though there was literally 9 people in the whole place, the place was well staffed - probably about 10 lifeguards on duty. We ordered pizza, some nachos with cheese, and 3 drinks. The total was $25. Not horrible. The pizza wasn't fresh, probably cooked in a convection oven. It was decent; I've had worse. Their menu was limited since the place was empty, which was kind of a let down, but not the end of the world. They had an extensive menu - sandwiches, fries, breadsticks, meatball sandwiches, and BEER! Yes, I said beer. We used the lockers and easily fit all our stuff into a large locker. This was all our clothes, bulky coats, hats, shoes, beach bag, etc. They only allow towels in the park area so you are really forced to use a locker. We used the showers when we were done. The water was warm and they felt good. The showers are not private stalls, they are contained in an open area inside of the restrooms. They do offer private changing areas though. Again, very clean! We played a few games on the way out. A bit pricey, but everything was working and we had fun. As for the bowling, we played it and I don't believe that particular game gave you tickets, but i could be wrong. Not all of the games offer tickets. Overall, we had a fun night. I would not visit Sahara in the summer or on a holiday when kids are off of school because I loathe crowds. We got lucky with our visit and we would recommend Sahara's to those who like indoor waterparks but don't want to pay Great Wolf prices.
label: POS

For those who don't fancy raw, you can always try anything from their list of cooked sushi. They've got sushi containing things like 'krab', shrimp tempura, and crawfish. I love the stuff. As you can see, I only have positive things I can say about this restaurant because it's that great. The food and service is on top so I'm always coming back for more. text: Don't laugh at me, but anytime I go out of town, I like to check the Man vs. Food website (TV show on the Travel Channel) to see which places were highlighted in that particular city. I did see the New Orleans episode and I knew Adam Richman attempted the oyster challenge at Acme. If it gets Adam's seal of approval, then I have to give it a try! Trust me, this works out more in my favor than when I followed the TV show Bizarre Foods. (Note to self: never try the camel brains and fish guts again!) We arrived around 9pm on a Friday and I was starving. I was initially concerned when I saw a line of people outside waiting to get a table. Fortunately since there only two of us, the hostess said we could be seated right away if we sat at the bar. Works for me! Hungry! Need food now! Good luck to those in large groups who want a table. You might need to plan ahead for that. We were seated at the oyster bar and hanging above I saw the Wall of Fame. Do I dare try to get my name added? The all time champ ate 42 1/2 dozen oysters. Can I top that? HELL NO! Maybe I could do 2-3 dozen, but I would be burping oysters for days. Definitely not a challenge I was willing to accept. That being said, I was up for one dozen of the fresh, iced oysters just to give them a try. Overall impression was that they were pretty good, but seemed to have some dirt/grit in a few of them. I'm not sure how much they were rinsed off beforehand, but I did taste a little of the "shell dirt" in a few. Good thing I'm not going for the challenge. For my entree I order the Acme "10 Napkin Roast Beef" sandwich. This was good stuff. It was indeed messy but it tasted great. I do have to admit that I only used 7 napkins and not the 10 as advertised, but then again, I try to be a clean eater. I'd be all over eating this sandwich again on a future visit. My wife went for the Fried Peace Maker Po-Boy which is basically half fried oysters and half fried shrimp. Given another chance, I think she would have gone for a shrimp only po-boy. I guess we prefer our oysters raw. I like this place. This is definitely worth a visit if you are in the area. Just keep in mind what I said about the wait time.

text: A Groupon deal was the only way Elevation was going to draw me out of the city. My buddy Walt was willing to drive, so hot damn, I'll hitch a ride. Right next to Tiffin^2, actually. First impression: This is so suburbia. Inside, it looks like a fast food joint. It smells like a fast food joint. But, brother, it ain't a fast food joint. So we pay a total of 48 cents thanks to our meal coupon and head to the outdoor tables. There's seats and tables sitting right on the strip mall sidewalk so you can catch a glimpse of... the other side of the street. Just keep your head down and look at the food. We both got the namesake burger, "Elevation". Two thin, smashed and griddled patties, orange cheddar, "Elevation" sauce (just another Ketchup+Mayo concoction ala the numerous island variety). Take a bite. And another. You know what, this is better than I expected. Although you can't ask them for a specific temperature of done...ness, for some reason these well-done griddled beauties were really juicy. This is coming from a guy telling everyone most organic foods are an unguided movement, a waste of resources, and typically an inferior product; grass-fed beef is the real deal. Always has been. Olive oil fried fries were meh, so I'm skipping it. After eating that well-done burger and amazed by the result, even if well-done insinuates a hockey puck texture in my mind, I can't stop thinking if I had access to their kitchen for like 10 minutes. What if I can form, myself, the perfect burger here?

text: Fried Green Tomatoes! If you believe: a. That blackening a dish makes it "Cajun" b. NOLA food is limited to Gumbo, Jambalaya, and Po-Boys c. You need to wear a jacket to eat in a great restaurant of N'awlins d. You don't need to explore the city beyond the French Quarter e. Amy Ruth's in NYC serves really good Southern cuisine ... then you need to come and eat at Jacques-Imo's. "Just ask the locals". That's a great marketing campaign, if for nothing other than the fact that it's true. We, New Yorkers, make fun of the tourists in the city as if it were our favorite pastime, but while touring end up doing EXACTLY the same. So, do yourselves a favor and make your way off the beaten path to Jacques Imo's - and be adventurous while ordering. Your risk taking will be rewarded handsomely. Do not be intimidated by the 2 hour wait times. If you time it right, you will avoid the lines. Our group walked into the restaurant around 10 pm on a Saturday night, and was seated immediately. We started off with more appetizers than we could handle, but our intent was to try as much of the menu as possible. Some of the items came off spectacularly well: the Fried Green Tomatoes (with shrimp remoulade), the alligator cheesecake, the chicken liver - were all 5 stars. My Gumbo and Jamabalaya obsessed companions thought their versions as distinctive from the other they had tried earlier. Not the best they'd had in this tour (and trust me they had their fair share - even ordering Gumbo for breakfast!), but very good and unique. The duck gumbo, for instance, was served in a bread bowl. The entrees weren't as well received as the appetizers, but I suspect that either my friends didn't order right or the non-stop food consumption during the day might have had something to do with it. I tried my hand at the Fried Chicken, as I am increasingly a believer that it's the simplest things on the menu that can turn out to astound one. Jacques Imo's fried chicken lived up to its lofty reputation, "Fried chicken so good, it would make the Colonel weep". I swear, if the Colonel had the one I did, he would be bawling like a little girl! Crispy from the outside, yet extremely moist and tender from the inside. Juicy and perfectly seasoned. Absolutely Fantastic! It was accompanied by the best shoe string fries I've ever had. My dining companions who were so full that they "couldn't have another bite", could not keep their hands away from them. Sadly, by the time we were done with the entrees, the kitchen had run out of all dessert, and so we didn't get to try their famed crème brulee or bread pudding. But, I shed no tears as I had already done my contingency planning by bringing the goodie bag from Angelo Brocato back to the hotel earlier. Take my word - do not leave New Orleans without eating at Jacques-Imo's. This is innovative Creole and Cajun dining at its best.

text: When I moved to the Hendersonville, TN area in January 2007, Banfield was a pretty great veterinary clinic for simple care. Their insurance plan was wonderful and came in handy with our dog and cat. HOWEVER in the past year and a half, their quality of care has plummeted. Whenever I go in, there are different veterinarians and vet-techs. My first bad experience was when my 2-year-old cat was sick. They examined her and determined it was an infection and sent me home with antibiotics. Two days later (a Saturday evening), I was at the all-night emergency vet with a dying cat in my arms... and they were unable to save her. Banfield had basically patted me on the head and said it was nothing to worry about and sent me on my way. Going back through the papers from that last visit, they hadn't even bothered to do bloodwork on her -- the only notation was that they listened to her stomach and it was "gurgling". I felt partially responsible that I hadn't DEMANDED a more thorough examination - but at the same time, I expected the vet knew what he was doing and when they were confident she'd be OK, I felt like I could trust them. After she died, I tried to cancel the pet insurance I had through them for my dog and my now-deceased cat. They wouldn't let me cancel EITHER insurance plan! The dog, I understand. However, I was told I'd either have to let the insurance I'd carried on the (dead!) cat run out for the year contract or I'd have to back-pay all the discounted services I'd received already that year. (Which would have been several hundred dollars more than continuing to pay for insurance on a dead cat for 4 more months!) I found that just plain SICK. However -- this reflects on Banfield CORPORATE, not this specific branch. Finally, as I said, my dog still has insurance through them (it runs out in December and clearly I will NOT be renewing). She was due for a checkup and teeth cleaning. Had she been SICK I'd have rushed her to our NEW vet, but I thought that for a simple check up and teeth-cleaning I may as well take advantage of the insurance that I'm stuck paying $24/mo for. I took the dog in and get a call a few hours later saying that they can't get a catheter in her and that she keeps ripping it out (which she's never done before) so they'll be unable to clean her teeth. Ok, FINE. I don't really care. I go pick her up, and the poor dog is TERRIFIED. She's never had a bad vet-experience before but she's just not herself. ... Needless to say, I'm NEVER taking her back there for so much as a toenail clipping. I don't care if I had to pay insurance for the rest of forever, I'd never USE it ever again. Truly if you love your pets, don't take them here.

One meal stood out the most...My dads birthday.. he orders a sushi roll with absolutely NO GINGER. Reason being, my dad is deathly allergic to ginger. We stressed no ginger 3 times at order point and guess what came out? GINGER ALL OVER THE PLATE. So I immediately made the waiter take it back. He took it back to the sushi bar. Out of curiosity, I followed him to see how he fixed the mistake. I witnessed him scrape the juicy ginger root off the side of the plate and bring the same plate back over. I made him take it away again and get a brand new roll with a new plate. Clearly it was not enough saying "My Dad is deathly allergic to ginger!" The service is consistently bad, and more importantly, the waiters do not know anything about food safety. Very very scary.

text: So before I begin writing my review, I notice that Mikado has an average of 3.5 stars. If things remain as they currently are, I'm afraid it's not going to get any better than that. I dined at Mikado last night with my partner, John. We live just down the road and watched the transformation from the outside. Both of us love sushi and Japanese and Chinese cuisine so last night we dove in. Upon entering the restaurant you notice that the place is very cool in it's design. A lot of thought and money went into the transformation although I admit I had never been inside the place prior to re-opening. However, you can still tell that it was an expensive and well-done remodel but I'm afraid that at some key points, they put form before function. I like to base my reviews on atmosphere, staff, food and price/quality so I'll take it in that order. The interior of the restaurant is designed with dark, horizontal wooden panels with white grout. It's visually stunning! But, here's the drawback...the atmosphere was LOUD! I mean, crazy-loud! There was no music at all but the wooden walls amplified the chatter inside the restaurant by ten fold. It was difficult to not be distracted by this and to be honest, I've never experienced anything like this in any restaurant. What made it even worse was a staff member who recognized a "good" client and he and another staff member carried on like old drinking buddies at a frat party with this gentleman! One of the things I like about Asian restaurants is how professional the staff tends to be. If you notice in most every Chinese/Japanese restaurant, you will hear very little conversation between staff members that is not work-related and even then, it is kept to a minimum. This was not the case at Mikado. Staff: There were new staff being trained last night. Not that it's a bad thing because everyone needs to be trained in their duties but this particular trainee was as nervous as a nun at a prison rodeo! At 830PM, she told John and I to have a great afternoon. Oops. But oh well. Our "real" server approached our table with a complimentary rice noodle sampling, took our drink order and then left us for longer than I expected. He failed to offer any suggestions or to mention any specials that might interest us. He almost seemed annoyed; not overly friendly as if he was trying to make a great first impression but not to the point of being rude either. Just not what I would have expected from a newly opened restaurant trying to groom it's clientele. And what's up with Korean staff at a Japanese restaurant anyway? And our trainee was definitely a Cherry Hill girl, big hair and all the glory and tackiness that the area women offer! I'm not sure how she even pulled that "Jersey-girl" look while wearing all black and a bistro apron but she still managed to do it. Food: OK. We began with the hamachi kama and the tempura. Both were excellent and I'd recommend either. I was in the mood for sushi (well, what day am I NOT in the mood for sushi!) but I've been dieting and trying to avoid rice more often than not, so I ordered the combination sushi/sashimi. The menu was inaccurate by listing that it came with "6 sushi, 10 sushi and a California roll". I assumed it was to state that the sushi/sashimi combination came with 6 sushi, 10 sashimi and a California roll. When my platter arrived, I had enough sashimi to feed a small third world country! There were no less than 6 different styles of sashimi, each with 5-6 portions and another 6-8 sushi along with a smaller wrapped California roll (about the diameter of a quarter). What disappointed me most was not so much the amount of food that was presented in "overkill" but that the sushi was a direct copy of the sashimi. There was zero variety with the exception of one eel skin sushi. The quality of the fish was OK but it tasted watery as if it had been previously frozen. The portions were overly generous, almost to a fault and the value was good as long as you like to waste food, which I do NOT. If this were an item for one person to dine on, I'd hate to see what they provide for the Combination Sushi/Sashimi for Two! This was truly enough food for 3 people and I'm not one to share my sushi too often! I'll let John review his own meal but I did sample it and it was tasty but nothing spectacular. Price: In my opinion, high. It was an $80 meal for the two of us including gratuity, no drinks and no dessert. My overall reaction to Mikado...eh. For my money, I'm still going to hang onto Chow's in Collingswood. It's a bit of a dive and uninviting as you pass by but the quality of food and excellent service far outshine Mikado. So in a side-by-side comparison of the two, I'd say Mikado is like Chow's with lipstick.
label: NEG

text: The adventures of Joey B. and the Norristown MexiQuest continue! When we last left our hero, he was taking a brief respite from Mexican food. We pick up now with him resuming MexiQuest at Los Arcos Mexican Restaurant... On the exterior, Los Arcos does not look good. It's tucked away next to an auto tags place, the parking lot pavement is uneven, and the windows are kinda dark and difficult to see through. However, upon entry I was pleasantly surprised with a bright, clean, well decorated interior, replete with all the standard Mexican restaurant adornments and an attractive wood decor. The friendly waitress handed me a menu and complimented my atrocious Spanish, and took me drink order (Jarritos, as usual). Perusing the menu, I was again pleasantly surprised to find it wide and varied, with all sorts of traditional Mexican dishes and plates, al a carte fare, various drinks, and a rather extensive breakfast menu. The menu was in both Spanish and well-translated English (if you think well-translated English isn't important, try reading Los Compadres' English menu... the Spanish one is easier even if you don't speak Spanish), and all the prices were lower than the competitors in the area (save for Los Compadres). With $1.75 a taco, $5 burritos, and $11 plates, I was already feeling good about Los Arcos. I ordered an adobada (a spicy pork kinda like chorizo) burrito. While waiting I was served complimentary chips with the standard Mexican roja, or spicy red, salsa. The burrito itself was on the smaller side for the average in that area, but by no means small. It was approximately the size of a Chipotle or Qdoba burrito, but significantly larger than Baja Fresh fare. It was a grilled burrito, which I always appreciate. Inside it was filled with fresh meat, lettuce, tomato, sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese, rice, and avocado. These ingredients gave me a very fresh impression, but the burrito wasn't daring. It took no risks, and was almost Americanized in it's safeness, but was tasty and satisfying nonetheless. The burrito came with a side of fries, which I didn't know until they showed up, but they weren't unpleasant. They were fresh cut and seasoned, kind of out of place to be sure but tasty fries anyway. I have concluded that Los Arcos is my current first choice as a recommendation to someone who is looking to try authentic Mexican cuisine, but may not be ready to dive in head-first into some of the more exotic cuisines. Recommended to anyone, but great for those with picky tastes.

text: Where do I start? Every once and while my fellow Yelpers and I disagree . For the most part I've found the reviews reliable - so much so that my team has learned to use yelp as a resource and that's how they picked up on the Stockyard for a group dinner That said, I could not disagree more strongly with the other reviews on this one. The Stockyard is a classic case of a restaurant surviving purely on its historic reputation. We had a large group - so let me begin at the beginning... While I expect a high-end steakhouse to be pricey - I also expect to "get what you pay for". The wine list was not a good start. The wines I recognized were priced 4-6X retail. When we have a significant size group I try to target wines in the 50-80$ range. Thats a real challenge at the stockyard. Precious few decent wines in this range. We went with a Malbec that I know sells for about $20 a bottle retail - $80. Also got a white -- which was a bit more reasonably priced - $65 and surprisingly good. We did the "seafood" appetizer - again, family style due to group size. I was surprised that they didn't cut the fried lobster tails into bite size portions a bit awkward to share. No real complaints here, but it wasn't superb either. At this point i am still thinking "expensive but average steakhouse". But then we got to the main course - and the hustle. Our main waiter launched into a description of the available entrees to the group, including - much to my dismay the description of limited number of American "kobe" filets. In a group this size, I'd want a heads up that he was offering $90 filets BEFORE people start to order. This was followed by an offer to each table (unknown to me) of a 2lb lobster add-on for each. He later claimed he asked first on this - but he did not come to me and i was clearly acting in the capacity of host. Talk about cranking up the bill... All of this - while disconcerting and annoying - is still somewhat "forgivable" when you get a really outstanding meal and service. Nothing could be further from the truth. To a man (or woman) our group was disappointed in the quality and preparation of the entrees - including the kobe which was described as bland and a bit chewy. My porterhouse was undercooked, non-prime beef and clearly not the size stipulated on the menu. I am no steakhouse novice. I know what to expect and this was clearly far below my expectation at a third of the price -- I could have gotten better at Outback. Based on conversation, I was clearly not alone in this opinion. Additionally, a number of people had to wait extended time for entrees while others ate. Lobsters - while large, should have been pre-cracked so inexperienced diners wouldn't struggle so much (and not overcooked). Overall, our price per person was outrageous, the food average, and the approach to draining our pockets insulting. If you want a good meal in Nashville look to the west end near Vanderbilt. Some great places... but Stockyard is the kind of place that makes "overrated" seem like a compliment.

In summary, i am happy to see a cupcake shop in my hood that along with great cupcakes have a charming staff, a great setup that one would like to visit often. From the Family Tree on the wall, to the chairs and benches, I was having flashbacks to when I lived in Germany and had to psyche myself up and practice what I would say in German to order. Didnt intrigue me enough to try it and I got a Vanilla cone. It was $3, plus I tipped, because when in the Alps.... I have to say, I wasnt blown away by it (thus falling short of 5 star status). Maybe I expected too much. It was definitely as good an icecream as id had, and it hit the spot on the warm day. I probably wouldnt recommend a special trip out here, but if you are in the area, its definitely worth checking out. text: One of the best things about Middle TN is the history. And Franklin is ripe with Civil War history so it only stands to reason that I would take the BF to experience a bit of it at the Carter House. So you pay in the front building and they tell you what time to meet on the Carter House front porch to start your tour. Then you are free to tour the museum while you wait. I found the museum interesting - personal articles of clothing, letters written home from Civil War soldiers, pictures of soldiers that died there including the Carter family member that was fighting on the Confederate side (even though the father was a Union supporter!), muskets, coffins, etc. Really fascinating! Then you can walk the grounds and see the smokehouse, the office with all the bullet holes in the back of it, and the kitchen building. I thought it was cute how they had Carter house cats too - the one had extra paws that made him look like he had opposable thumbs. Maybe he could open the door at my house like my cat always tries to do! You meet your tour guide and he starts telling you the story. The one we had definitely had a flair for drama and told everything like a story starting with lead up describing the Carter family and how the armies came to be there in Franklin. Very interesting. You get to go in the master bedroom and also the parlor area that was specially decorated for entertaining guests. Check out the molding around the bottom of the room that was painted to look like marble! Check out the rocking chair with a bullet hole through it! And then they take you out on the grounds to show you where the battle was taking place. Then you go back in to see the basement where the Carter family hid while the battle waged on around them. You also go in another bedroom too where the middle Carter son died a day after the battle from his wounds. The entire tour takes about an hour and the guides are all knowledgeable. As I said, our tour guide had a flair for the dramatic and I liked it all up until the end when it sounded like I had transformed from a tour of the house to church where they were about to beg for $$. He didn't and it wasn't like that, but I had that same weird uncomfortable feeling. Maybe I was just hungover and things struck me as weird. But he was still kickass in all other ways. Speaking of hungover, the musty smell in some of the rooms kind of stifled me and made me feel sick to my stomach so if you have a sensitive stomach or drink too much just be aware. Also, we didn't get to go anywhere upstairs. I thought that you used to be able to go up there on the tour? I might be mistaken, but when I came as a kid for field trips I thought we did. Definitely go to the Carter house if you are in town and want to learn a bit more about the Battle of Franklin, the Civil War, and history in general.

text: This is the cutest little cupcake bakery. I sampled two this morning - Oreo and the S'more. For $2.75 each, they are on the tiny side but they're molded into the perfect cupcake shape. Also, they are light on the frosting which is a plus in my book. I really enjoyed the Oreo - the cake itself was chocolate and the frosting tasted like a ground up Oreo. The frosting was a little gritty but I let it go because it was reminiscent of the white stuff in the middle of an Oreo. I had some issue with the S'more. It was chocolate cake again which was fluffy and yummy. The vanilla buttercream was far too sweet and gritty. The crushed graham cracker on top made it more dry. I got through half of that cupcake and had to wipe the frosting off. They have many, many flavors including Billion Dollar Chocolate, Forget Love, I'd Rather Fall in Chocolate!, Va-Va-Vanilla, Swirley Temple, Berry Squared, Paint the Town Red Velvet , The Chocolate Elvis, Lemon Pucker, Fuzzy Berry, Fuzzy Brown, Tuxedo Bites, and Butterscotch Babies. This place has a lot of potential and will fill a need in the Tampa area.

text: Major disappointment. They encourage you to bring all your friends out to the club so you have a chance to do open mic night and then at the last minute they pull the plug if they don't know you already or don't suck up to the head guys. They said initially I couldn't go up because I wasn't wearing pants and then I embarrassingly switched pants with one of my guests who I convinced to come out so they would consider me for the gig. My guest I invited reluctantly switched pants, socks, and shoes so I could have a shot at going on stage. When I came back in and told the head guy I switched pants he looked and said I was in the program. Once the show started I asked the MC what number I was to go up and he said I wasn't on the list and needed to talk with someone else. Can you imagined how embarrassed I am now? All eight people paid a cover charge just to walk in the door just to hear me. All eight people had ordered drinks while waiting for me to go on stage to hear me and I walk over with my tail between my legs to tell them, "I'm sorry you came all this way to hear me but I wasn't picked for the program tonight." Apparently first timers that bring crowds are guaranteed to be selected according to everyone else. Not true. From a business and ethical standpoint this is just wrong. They took the short term gain on taking my friends and family money and upsetted everyone in the process. The manager said that this is show business. Are you kidding me? That is just poor business and customer service. Imagine if I said to all my clients, "Sorry but that is just the way it is". I would be out of business tomorrow. If they would have told me I wasn't picked I would have encouraged my friends to join me elsewhere but instead paid a cover charge that was non-refundable. The best the manager said he could do was give everyone free passes to the next show which frankly why would you come back to a place that over-promised and under-delivered? The sad part of the whole story is that the Funny Bone used to have great service, friendly staff, and good comics. This wasn't my experience this visit. Another bunk was the A/C didn't work which made it miserable to sit through the program. I'll never come back to the Funny Bone in St. Louis Westport Plaza ever for open mic night, any other show even if Seinfeld performs here for free.
label: NEG

text: I attempted to go to Ciro about 2 weeks ago and couldn't even get in the door. A few friends and I wanted to try the restaurant so I called on Thursday to make a reservation. I was told that they don't accept reservations for fewer than 6 people. The woman I spoke with looked at the reservation book, though, and told me if we arrived before 8:00pm we shouldn't have a problem getting a table. We arrived at 7:50pm and were stopped in the parking lot. The pretentious man in the parking lot asked if we had a reservation and I said no. He then told me that they were completely full and there was no way we were getting a table. He told me that he could take my name and number and call me when a table was available at 9:30 or 10:00pm. I told him about how I had called the day before and he reiterated that they were full of reservations. I asked him if they were full, that means that they don't have any tables for fewer than 6 people. He said yes. Really? Seriously? So I can't eat there if I don't have a party of 6? Somehow I don't believe that. We left, offended by his attitude, and don't plan on going back any time soon. This is Tampa, people! There is no reason to act so snobby like they are the hottest place in town and I should be thrilled to even have the chance to come back for dinner at 10:00pm. I couldn't believe it. It is unfortunately that he couldn't have been more polite and sympathetic. I would have been understanding and come back another night. Rude behavior won't keep customers coming back, not in this market.

text: No concept of customer service, food is mediocre at best and reporting our less-than-satisfactory experience to management revealed that they just don't care. My first and last experience: Upon being seated, the waitress offered my 6 and 8 year olds smoothies with whipped cream on top...Mom and Dad raise an eyebrow of concern, "oh but not to worry, they're just chocolate milk blended with ice" She left out the fact that they charge $6.00 each for chocolate milk blended with ice. Next trick: Waitress dumps a 20oz. Mr. Pibb with ice on my 1-year-old baby. I took for granted that she got the spill cleaned up... after all that was my own expectation. You would expect however, that after dumping a drink on a guest, the thought might occur that someone at the table is missing a drink... nope not our princess... we had to ask her for the replacement beverage. Somehow I guess I was supposed to realize that she did bring our 1-year-old baby a peace offering; one of those little umbrella toothpicks! How cute! She loved it! Maybe you actually have to have a 1-year-old baby to see the problem with handing her a sharpened stick of wood? As responsible parents who realize that our 1-year-old still accidentally scratches her own face with her fingernails, we decided that the toothpick might be a problem so we took it away from her before she could put it into her eyeball. Well, let's just say she was pretty happy about getting her new toy taken away, thanks again Cheeseburger Island Style. Once we got our cheeseburgers (as our first visit, we thought we could put some stock in the title dish), I had to remove the green piece of leather (AKA lettuce) after the first bite (who knew lettuce could be so tough?). The seasoned fries are pretty good, I've had those before. They're available in your frozen food isle at Save Mart for $2.88 for a 1 lb. bag. When the check arrived, you might think that the waitress would offer some concession for giving your 1-year-old baby an unexpected ice bath in sugar water and scare she'll remember into toddlerhood. And at Cheeseburger Island Style, you'd be wrong... 2 cheeseburgers, 1 kid's pair of mini-cheeseburgers, 1 kid's portion of chicken strips, 1 ice tea, 1 (or maybe 2) Mr. Pibbs and 2 of those legendary smoothies: $50.00 I debated on leaving the goose-egg for my tip, but I'm just not that shallow even when the establishment I patronize obviously is. We called management to report this experience, and we learned that our waitress is the numero uno and trainer for their entire wait staff! Although the manager admitted that he should have been made aware of the spilled drink by his staff and was not, he still stood firm by his staff. Bravo Dwayne, maybe they'll stand by you in the unemployment line when Cheeseburger Island Style flops. After some reflection, I realized that it is called Cheeseburger Island Style. And in all my numerous trips to the Hawaiian Islands, I never had a burger there that I thought "Wow, I wish I could get a burger this good back home!" If you demand more of a $50 family lunch, then you need to find somewhere else to eat. If however, your 1-year-old needs a sharp toothpick to play with or you just have too much of the green paper in your wallet and a lack of frozen seasoned fries in your belly, then Cheeseburger Island Style may be for you. PS-I joined Yelp! to warn you about this place. This is my first review...ever.
label: NEG

text: I came here to see The Cool Tour, expecting so much more than I got, and I wasn't quite expecting much. My friend and I are both from Northern Virginia, and the metal scene around here is pretty weak. But even so, at least the people are nice and look out for you! The venue was very nice, keep cool, and huge for a general admissions venue. I am not a big fan of bigger venues, but the Electric Factory seemed to be the perfect size. Things I feel like I should complain about, though, are the people that work there. Almost all of the bouncers were talking to each other about how much they hated fat chicks. I don't consider myself huge, but I'm a bit overweight, and they were pointing out some 120lb chick and calling her fat and disgusting. The bouncers were also awful at keeping the crowd safe when it came to crowd surfers and bitchy concert-goers. I get that almost nobody knows concert etiquette, but when some chick is painfully harming multiple people and the bouncers can see it, they SHOULD tell the girl to back off. My friend almost dislocated her hip because this chick was eagerly slamming against her, and the bouncers just laughed at my friend's pain. Another problem I have with this venue is the large stage. If you're at the barricade, you've got to crank your neck up. The bands playing didn't even like it. I could see coming here to go clubbing, but to see a band, it's a bit ridiculous. Oh, and my friend and I were dehydrated and needed some water, and it was $3.50 a bottle! I understand making a profit, but that's a bit ludicrous. If you want to go to a concert, come down to my area or up to NJ. Save yourself the hassle.

text: I've never really had great sushi in New Orleans. This place is ok, not great. For the most part, the service is very good and friendly. The crawfish roll was ok, good to see what it was like but I wouldnt order for a while. The cajun roll was too spicy and the fish was unidentifiable. The white tuna pieces had some mayonaise between the fish and rice that gave it an unpleasant taste and texture. The fresh water eel with omlette pieces were good. In other words, if you live here in New Orleans, there may not be a better sushi place. If you are visiting, you may want to satisfy your sushi urge when you get back home. It is not bad, but nothing to write home about.

text: The Short: Stylist: Rashada Service: Shampoo and Blowout Cost: $45 + $10 tip = $55 Will I go again? NO! The Long: I really REALLY wanted Bubbles to work... but unfortunately, I was let down. I went because I really didn't feel like going through the 3 hour ordeal of doing my hair myself that day, and just wanted someone else to deal with it instead. All I wanted was a blow-out. THAT'S ALL. I decided on this salon because of it's accessibility ( couple blocks from Suburban Station), and also because a girl that has hair similar to mine went with favorable results. I made an appointment with the same stylist she had, Rashada. So I go to the salon, and tell Rashada what i want; a shiny, sleek blowout with loose waves. She goes "Ok, cool, but I don't round brush I use a flat iron, it's my own technique". A little red flag goes off in the back of my head, but I'm thinking, ok, she does what works for her, which is cool as long as it comes out the way I want. She washed my hair (and by the way, she gives a killer massage), then braided my hair and sat me under a dryer for 30-45 minutes. Then she blowdries it with a paddle brush, which equals major frizz and craziness, then uses the flat iron to curl it. Was it shiny? yes. Was it bouncy and curly? yes. BUT MY ROOTS WERE NOT STRAIGHT!!! When I run my fingers through my hair, I can feel my curly roots underneath, and that's EXACTLY WHAT I DIDN'T want! I don't understand... WHY can I not find a HAIRDRESSER that knows how to blowdry my hair the way I want it done? This make me so mad!!! And not only that... while she was doing my hair, she was telling me that my hair/head was in bad shape... You have split ends, you have a dry scalp, do you pin your hair up at night? (no) do you wrap it? (no) well at LEAST use a satin pillowcase (...). She asked what kind of shampoo, conditioner, leave-ins I use, and when I said Aussie (which I love), her response made me feel like... just because I'm not using the ph-balanced, all natural, specially concocted, overly expensive, etc etc brands that she was using, that I don't care about my hair. She asked me how often I washed my hair, then told me I was washing it too much. I did NOT come here for a lecture. I am perfectly HAPPY with my hair and my routine, and I just wanted her to SHUT UP. Now, I am not the type of person that likes to talk while getting my hair done. Why would I want to fight to be heard over the blowdryer to talk about random stuff when I can just sit here and read a magazine while you do your thing?? She seemed like she was trying to make conversation, and since she didn't know what else to talk about, she talked about my hair, but DAMN. Did I tip her? Yes, I'm too nice. Did I make another appointment like she expected/told me to? yes. Did I cancel it? YES.

text: The Gyro Stop was in the Entertainment Book so I thought I would give them a try. I take one step into the store and the cashier asks me what I would like to order, so I scan the menu and order two side dishes, a side of gyro meat and an order of fried mushrooms. The cashier says that he is not sure if they can accept my coupon but shows it to the cook. "Buy one menu item get one free" is straight forward in my mind. The cook explains to the cashier to just charge me for one item and the cook asks for here or to go and I said I would like to dine in. text: With only three days to experience New Orleans, a visit to one of Emril's restaurants seemed like a definite "to-do." Though we were within a few steps of Emril's New Orleans, the reviews on Yelp! seemed much more favorable for NOLA. We came for lunch and had a fantastic meal! The decor, and overall feel of the place is charming, and the service was prompt and friendly. With the setting and service already in the "great" column, we had high expectations for our meal. Needless to say, we were not disappointed. The cocktails here are superb, and the rolls provided by the restaurant are a tasty. Word of advice, lay off on the rolls and save room for the appetizers! My wife and I tried the Barbecued Gulf Shrimp with Rosemary Biscuit and Miss Hay's Stuffed Chicken Wings with Homemade Hoisin Dipping Sauce: D-E-L-C-I-O-U-S. Simple concepts, but packed with lots of amazing! We enjoyed every last morsel, and if this place were a bit less crowded, I may seriously have licked the remaining BBQ sauce from the plate. For her entree, my wife got the Shrimp & Grits which consisted of sautéed Gulf shrimp with grilled green onions, smoked cheddar grits, apple smoked bacon, crimini mushrooms and red chili-abita butter sauce. Every component of that dish was superb, so so delectable! The bacon and fresh shrimp was a match made in heaven when paired with the sauce! As much as I wanted to snatch away her plate, I enjoyed my buttermilk fried breast of chicken with bourbon mashed sweet potatoes, country ham cream gravy and sautéed sugar snap peas. The chicken was juicy, perfectly breaded, and complemented everything else on the plate. The sweet potatoes and snap peas were really good, and the gravy was delicious! When it came to dessert, the choices all seemed really good but we went with the Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Pie with Vanilla Ice Cream and Caramel Drizzle. As much as I love sweet potato, I was too hesitant to take on the sweet potato ice cream. All things considered, how can you go wrong with any part of this dessert? Chocolate, Bourbon, Pecan Pie, Vanilla Ice Cream, Caramel Drizzle: every syllable in that dessert oozes deliciousness! Please do not come to New Orleans and leave without having eaten here at least once!

text: Sang Kee Peking Duck House is quite possibly the best Chinese food in town. A group of 5 of us ordered fried wontons, Singapore noodles, black pepper beef, rice, and a whole duck--and it was plenty of food. I suppose I needed to learn more about Peking Duck, because I was a little surprised when it came out. I expected a whole duck, recognizable as such, but they serve it in what is apparently the traditional fashion: broken down into pieces, and prepared in several courses. Traditionally you'd get the skin, meat and all the organs in separate servings, but since Americans don't usually like organs, don't expect to get them. The first of the two courses is the meat with skin, spring roll wrappers, scallions, and hoisin sauce (quite a bit like mushu pork). The skin was nice and crisp, and the meat was rich and lean, but prepare to be amazed by how little meat is actually on a half Peking duck. The second half of the duck was served in a stir fry with green beans, and a rich, dark fermented bean sauce that was much more delicately spiced than the muddled brown sauces I've come to expect from Chinatown. Overall, the prices are pretty standard for Chinatown, but their portions are a bit smaller, though still adequate.Even if you're not in the mood for duck, the rest of the menu is excellent. They have a lot of the normal fare, as well as some fusion dishes I've never tried. Everything we had was excellent, so don't be afraid to try something new.

text: First off, let me say that I don't normally give bad reviews of restaurants. And I'm also pretty sheepish about speaking up and sending a plate back. But this was the worst restaurant experience I've ever had. My wife and I were given a $100 gift card to Bliss, so we decided to try it out last night. It was awkward from the very beginning. It was Saturday night and the place was pretty empty. Despite the open seats all over the restaurant, the hostess showed us to a seat in the corner that was literally next to a drink stand covered in rags. Since the restaurant was empty-ish, we asked if it would be OK to move to another table. She proceeded to set up another table directly next to (about 2 feet away from) another couple. In an empty restaurant. Awkward, but whatever. We proceeded to order an appetizer, a salad, two entrees and drinks. The appetizer (some sort of sushi roll dish) came out promptly but tasted as if it had been sitting in the back of a fridge all day. It clearly was not fresh sushi, as the menu described. (Apparently this place is a sushi joint for lunch?) Anyway, I didn't want to make a big deal of it when the waiter returned to ask how everything was, but we ended up being honest with him and he insisted on taking it back. He returned a few minutes later to say that there's nothing they can do -- it's just the way the dish is prepared. He was generous and offered to bring us something else but we declined. Not a huge deal, but strange after the seating situation. Our entrees came and were decent. I was a bit concerned when the waiter asked me if I wanted my pork tenderloin cooked rare, but hey, it tasted OK. (Still alive 12 hours later.) My wife had the duck, but wasn't impressed. It seemed a bit overpriced for what you got. At this point, we were just ready to go home. The check came, so we gave the server our gift card and credit card (the bill was just over $100). The manager then appeared at our table and told us that the balance on the gift card was $0. What?!?! I tried to keep my cool and explain that this was a gift from someone and I didn't know what to do. He suggested that I call the person that gave me the card, before realizing that this would be awkward. At this point, I really really just wanted to go home and put this experience behind me, but I also didn't want to shell out $100+ for an awful experience. In the end, the manager was gracious and told us he would restore the card to $100. We paid, got our coats and left. Weird stuff. In the end, I would say the manager and our server were definitely kind and gracious. Not exactly apologetic for anything, but kind nonetheless. Still, I would never go back to this place. Maybe this was just a series of rare, unfortunate events, but it left a bad taste in my mouth (bad pun?).

text: This was by far the most perfect meal of my life. My father treated me to dinner here after my college graduation. Of course, I went all out for the grande degustation menu with wine pairings for each course since it was the only event in my life that justified the price tag. If not now, when? I've outlined all the courses I was served below. I don't know shit about wine, I just drink it, so I don't remember what they all were can't really comment on them. If you're curious though, about a half-glass was served with each course, so I was QUITE tipsy by the end of it. The courses were as follows: Amuse Bouche: Tuna Tartare w/ Daikon -Light and a perfect way to start the meal. I love any kind of tartare, and this was no exception. Bread & Butter: Rolls w/ Milk & Chives, Onion French Bread, something else -I only tried the onion but it was very good. The waiters kept bring the tray of bread around and I think my brother had about 10 pieces. Raw Oyster w/ Caviar & Hibiscus Foam -Absolutely perfect. It had been a while since I'd had an oyster and this one did not disappoint. The hibiscus foam was especially interesting - more fruity than I expected. Salmon Tartare w/ Vinegrette & Essence of Lavender -Another tartare! Perfect. The presentation on this was very interesting. The bowl sat on a plate filled with dry ice, then the server poured liquid (the lavender essence, i believe) on it at the table. I actually don't really like the smell of lavender, or anything very floral for that matter, but it didn't detract from the dish. Foie Gras w/ Risotto Chip, Black Sesame, Berry Sauce & Cherries w/ Ice Cream -Possibly the most creative of the dishes. On one side of the plate was the foie gras and risotto chip, and the other side had a scoop of ice cream (possibly kirsch flavored?) with macerated cherries. The sweet components and salty/rich foie gras were the perfect foils for one another. Some Firm White Fish w/ Consomme and Zucchini Blossom -I can't remember what the fish was, but it was cooked perfectly and delicious. Served in a shallow bowl of consomme with a tempura-fried zucchini blossom on top - nice and light. Lamb Tenderloin w/ Crispy Potato -Lamb is one of my favorite meats, so this was an obvious winner for me. The crispy potatoes were like a classy version of that old vending machine standard, Potato Stix - but obviously way more awesome. Taglatelle with Porcini & Truffles -The simplest course, with just a few beautiful ingredients. Pasta, butter, porcini mushrooms, salt, pepper, some generous shavings of truffles... that's it. Melon Sorbet w/ Powder (palate cleanser) -My least favorite course, but I'm biased because I hate all kinds of melons. I tried a bite and then let my dad eat it. Cheese Tray -This was awesome. A server came out with a gorgeous glassed-in cart containing about 10 different cheeses. You're allowed to choose as many as you want, but they recommend about 5 for a nice-sized tray. I told the server I liked soft, strong cheeses, and he made up a beautiful assortment with some grapes and 2 kinds of bread. Dessert: Yogurt Sorbet, Lemon Macaron, & Tomato Confit -The first of quite a few desserts. Served in a parfait glass with a dollop of tomato confit at the bottom, the lemon macaron balanced in the center, and yogurt-flavored sorbet on top. Dessert: Truffles -I was served a platter of 5 truffles: mixed nut, tarragon, saffron, curry, and red beet. The unexpected flavors were all quite good, but the saffron and curry were my favorites. I was also given a cute box of 2 chocolates to take home. Dessert Cart -Yes, the famous dessert cart! It was every bit as wonderful as I had hoped. I asked for a small slice each of the Grand Marnier Souffle, the Flourless Chocolate Cake, and the restaurant's Signature Chocolate cake, which consisted of rum-soaked genoise with rich chocolate buttercream. Unfortunately, by this point I was pretty full, and all the desserts were so rich I could only have a few bites. Finally, we were served a variety of petit fours with the check. This is really extravagance, but for a special occasion it can't be beat. The service is impeccable and treat you like royalty even if it's painfully obvious that you don't belong (like my frugal and tactless grandmother who loudly exclaimed "It looks like a roach!" when the amuse bouche was served). My only complaint is that I will probably never be able to afford a meal like this again.

text: Its located conveniently just off Route 295 on Route 73. Owners are from South East Asia and hence the name of the restaurant. They serve mainly two types of food: i) Sushi ii) Singaporen-Malaysian I've been there twice in 3 weeks and I must say that its one of the best sushi places in this area. Sushi is fresh and good. Prices are competitive ($17 for 15 pieces of sashimi). The tuna carpaccio is very nice. Most of the patrons tend to gravitate towards the sushi menu. I think its probably due to the fact that the people around here are not familiar with Malaysian/Singapore cuisine yet and hence it will take time for that to change. As for the Singaporean/Malaysian dishes - I've only had the opportunity to try one basic dish (was too full to eat when I arrived there). The menu does boast some of the well known Malaysian/Singaporean dishes (curries, roti canai, satay, curry puffs etc..). I'll definitely will have to give those a try as the nearest 'Malaysian' restaurant is in downtown Philly. As for the chef/owners - they're very accomodating and nice. Always giving out free appetizers for people who wait for take out orders (or even to the regulars there). I personally think that given time and some publicity, this place will definitely do well and will be bustling with more patrons (they are still a relatively new restaurant). Update 8/29/07: Ok I just came back tonight after giving the Malaysian/Singaporean dishes a try (needed a break from sushi). I'm upgrading the the Rating to 5 stars. I had: 1) Chicken Satay - Its really good - and they use chicken thighs (the right way to make good satay). I'll be trying the beef satay the next time 2) Chicken Rendang (dry chicken curry) - Felt like eating @ home in Malaysia. I must say that since I'll be coming here to NJ for the next few months for work, I'll definitely be spending at one night a week at this place as its just located near my hotel as there are so quite a few dishes to try.

text: I've always found the idea of Bubba Gump to be a lot like a Hard Rock or Planet Hollywood- ideally not a place I'd like to spend an evening. On to the food: My boyfriend ordered a Blue Louisiana Lemonade which had a very interesting taste to it - when you drink it, you definitely taste the lemonade followed by a tinge of blueberry aftertaste... Like you drank lemonade and ended up with a blueberry in your mouth. We ordered a spinach & artichoke dip (Bubba's Far Out Dip) that was pretty yummy. There was a really delicious blend of parmesean with red peppers in there that really set it off, making it different from other dips I've had. For our entrees: My boyfriend got the Bourbon Street Mahi Mahi and I got the Lt. Dan's Drunken Shrimp. Both of ours had the same sauce base that was a nice and creamy bourbon sauce. Both of ours had mashed potatoes which were all right. His fish was nicely cooked and my shrimp were scrumptious. We left dinner feeling satisfied and pleasantly surprised. The only thing that kind of bugged me was that the restrooms were on the 2nd floor- but I guess they're designed that way so people don't come in willy nilly to use the restrooms?

text: The Husband and I went in around 1:30 for lunch, and we were the only people in the restaurant. That made sense since it was off-peak lunch rush and the place is still fairly knew. We were pretty impressed with the prices on the special lunch menu, which ranged from $5.95 to $8.95 for soup, salad and an entree. We did not get to choose the soup or salad. I don't know what the soup was called, since I couldn't find it on the menu. But it was like PA Dutch ham and green bean soup with spice, and tiny bits of pork instead of ham. It also had cabbage. I grew up in PA Dutch country, so I liked it. The Husband didn't. The salad was a rather bland pile of iceberg lettuce, a slice of cucumber and a slice of tomato - topped with ranch dressing, which we thought was a weird choice for a Thai restaurant. To drink, I ordered a Thai iced tea. It was perfect. (And yes, a restaurant can mess up Thai tea - just try the stuff at Tamarind on South Street in Philly.) The Husband ordered unsweetened iced tea to drink. And when he asked for sweetener, the waitress doled out a single packet of sugar. (He prefers the fake stuff.) When the waitress brought our drinks, I accidentally knocked my knife on the floor. I picked it up. But she did not offer or bring a replacement. For an appetizer, The Husband and I ordered the Mee Krob. We'd never had Mee Krob before, so we didn't know what to expect. (We had just watched the old "South Park" curse words episode, in which "Mee Krob" is a dirty word, and we were fascinated by the dish.) The appetizer wasn't the most visually appealing - a pile of crunchy noodles, soft chicken bits and a single shrimp covered in an orangey-pink sauce. We enjoyed our first few bites, but ultimately agreed it was way too sweet. For my entree, I ordered the Three Flavor Catfish. The menu describes it as "lightly floured, crisp fried, and served dancing in a three-flavor sauce." I think at least two of the three flavors were curry. It was hot! If you like curry, you'll love the catfish. I don't, but it was still pretty good. The Husband ordered the Pad Thai, since we evaluate all Thai restaurants on their Pad Thai. It was not the best Pad Thai ever (that award goes to Bangkok Wok in Mechanicsburg, with a second place to Chabaa Thai Bistro in Manayunk), nor was it the worst Pad Thai ever (that award goes to Nadia Thai in Lansdale - awful, awful stuff). It was just different. It was covered in an orangey-pink sauce that was a little spicier than what The Husband and I are used to having on Pad Thai. After we finished the entrees, the waitress brought our check without offering dessert. That's a big no-no. I always eat dessert. And any restaurant that fails to offer me one automatically loses a star. The menu didn't have any desserts listed, so we thought there might not be any. But we asked the waitress and they had only two. Thank goodness one was my favorite - mangoes with sticky rice. She came back a few minutes later with a big white plate of sticky rice shaped into a large flat heart and two big slices of mango cut into bite-sized bits. Mmmm... delicious. So, the meal was... you know... OK... not great... not awful... I might go there again, but it's not going to be my first choice.

text: Pimpy pimpy! ALoft is basically an urban rendition of the "W" Hotel. I love the "W" for its smooth swanky looks and feel. Well you get all that but on different level here. Basically all this place is doing is taking an urban feel and running with it. Much like "W" all the rooms and everything that has to deal with the hotel is nice, very well kept, and swanky. ALoft's simple rooms are rather comfy and feature nice large king size beds with down covers and pillows. You have a huge flat screen mounted in the middle of a wall. They also offer a media hook up. So you can plug in your laptop, ipod, and basically anything and route it into the tv. Their bathrooms are nice and done up well. Very cool walkin shower with a nice frosted window that peeks into the sleeping area. I am sure these showers have seen all the action they can handle. It has throw her up against the glass written all over it! You have a mini freg, room safe, and coffee/tea maker. Aside from rooms they offer a Bar which was OK, nothing like the lounges the "W" has. They have a snack bar as well. Indoor pool. And a very cool outside seating area. Again it is all done up well. Overall I will look forward to staying at an Aloft again. Much cheaper than a "W"!
label: POS

text: For a seafood restaurant in downtown center city, I would have liked better quality. But then again, it is a hotel restaurant, so I've never been very fond of those. However, for the price, I would not want to spend that much for a tasteless meal. The ambiance is good, with a significant amount of openness, lighting, and music; but for me, that comes secondary to the food. As a Philly local, I don't think it would be one of my top choices. And if I were a visitor to the the city, it would not leave such a great impression on me. For seafood in the Center City area, I probably would opt for McCormick and Schmick's for a better and more scrumpcious meal! Only a few blocks down, it's a good alternative, and the Mojitos are okay, as well.

text: Brutal! Went for lunch on a Saturday. We were under the impression it was table service as we were ushered to a table and the brought us menus. So we ordered our Indian staples with a "waitress" who was on her cell phone the whole entire time. While waiting for our Samosa, the owner's child came over , stood at our table with their plastic toy and starting screaming...how pleasant. It was as if the child was warning us "DON'T EAT HERE" because next you know, our samosa arrives with ice crisps mixed in with the peas and potato filling. Yes, my friends this sucker was frozen. Next up was the main course, I had the Shrimp Saag and my guest had the Chicken Tikka Masala platter. The platter is slightly more expensive because it comes with a side salad and a vegetable. Apparently a side salad constitutes 6 pieces of shredded cabbage and 1 cucumber coin quartered. The Chicken Tikka Masala was good but the amount of chicken was minimal (maybe three chunks) but the rice was plentiful. The shrimp saag was also heavy on the rice, minimal on the shrimp. Usually that would be a non-issue with us because we'd take the sauce and dip Naan in it. But alas, this was another disappointment @ Ashoka...NO NAAN! Instead they offered Korcha (sp) that made s think we were on Candid Camera. Why, you ask. Because it was a pita, taken straight from a bag, and put on a plate, no grilling, no heating, no deliciousness. Throughout all this, three men kept coming in and out from the back and out the front rearranging menus on the table to attract more guests when really, they should have been paying attention to the ONLY 2 guests inside. The meal wound up costing us $30 bucks and we were amused but far from appetized. Next time we want to drop $30 on Indian, we'll head over to Cafe Spice for their $13.95 lunch specials or up to New Dehli for their $9.95 lunch buffet.
label: NEG

text: You may not even believe that this is a real US Post Office, but it is. I must say, the entire New Orleans postal system is really in the dumps. In one of the most welcoming and warm cities in the world you can go to this post office and find some grumpy cranky workers. The line is always very long and people wait patiently, but it's cold in there in the summer so bring a sweater. Don't mess up or ask any questions either because you won't be treated nicely. Since living in New Orleans I have only had the same postal worker twice. TWICE. My mail arrives every day anytime between 10AM and 8PM. No consistency. My mail also arrives wet, ripped, damaged, and looking like someone jumped on it. I don't understand why. Today I was waiting for a package and met the postal worker when he arrived at my door. He said he was just doing his buddy a favor and didn't usually do my route. Then I asked where the package was- since I checked online and saw that it was at this USPS location at 8am today- and he said he didn't look for it. So, he went back and, of course, it was right there in his truck. So if I hadn't asked I wouldn't have gotten my package?! So, I realized I had to finally write this review. Sorry NOLA but the USPS here is a shame.
label: NEG
