text: Let me preface this by saying that I love Yelp and usually rely on it as my Nashville "Bible." However, I created my account on Yelp simply to review this place and say that honestly, some of y'all Yelpers must be on crack. Maybe I came into this place with too high of expectations, but I was seriously, seriously let down. I eat a lot of veggies and Middle Eastern food, so I was hoping to find a place where I could find good produce at good prices as well as a selection of Middle Eastern ingredients. First thing you'll notice walking into the store is the smell, which is totally overpowering (and not in a good way). I can't really describe it other than to say it just smells...very unclean. I was really let down by the produce department. When I walked in, the ENTIRE section was covered with crushed ice. It's actually like someone just dumped the crates of ice+veggies on top of the existing produce and didn't bother to dig the produce out. I pulled out a few bunches of parsley out of the ice (honestly, it was a huge mound), and they all looked pretty bad. Honestly, I think it's a huge red flag when you have to find produce by reading the signs because you can't see the veggies themselves since there is so much ice covering them! Come on now. I will say that their variety of dry/prepackaged international foods is pretty good, especially for Asian ingredients. They had a surprisingly good Middle Eastern ingredients section, which I did not expect, as well as a Hispanic section. Overall, I would pass on the veggies and meat/seafood (honestly, the smell of the place is so offputting, and it just skeeves me out), but if you're looking for a selection of international dry foods, it's an OK place.

text: The Fox Theatre specializes in their Broadway show series but holds concerts here from time to time as well. I like The Fox to see either type of show, Broadway or rock. The Fox Theatre has been in STL for over a hundred years and it is gorgeous inside. The grandiose lobby with its dual staircases, the winding stairs up to the balcony, the ancient bathrooms with original fixtures, I love the feel and look of it all. I also enjoy seeing a show here because 1) the sound is great 2) if it's a rock show, the whole place buzzes when the monitors start blasting bass and drums and 3) there really isn't a bad seat. text: Isaac and I went to Mels for date night last week...Yes, we still have date night...let it go. I was excited (for many reasons, but that's for a different kind of site). Anyway, it had been several years since my last trek over the river and up the hill. I remember Mels being a gaudy, grease ball hangout. You know...guys who watch The Godfather, Donnie Brasco, or Scarface EVERY NIGHT! To my surprise when we walked in the place was looking kind of good. It is now furnished in what I would call contemporary style. Although, they do still have the mirror wall, reminiscent of a South Philly row home whose owner wants to make the living room seem expansive (or should that be expensive, either way). As soon as we sat down an older gentleman, pinky ring and all, approached the table. He was a nice guy, but really pushy. The type of server that wants to sell you the overpriced specials, the bottle of wine, the add-on lobster tail. Anything to increase the check, in hope of increasing the tip. We did end up ordering a bottle of wine, for fear that if we hadn't we might end up "sleepin' wit the fishes". Seriously, Mels has a fairly decent wine list. They carry a nice variety...Actually, they advertise a nice variety, whether or not the bottle is in house, well that is a different story. We struck out on our first two bottles, but we hit a home run on our third choice. It was a nice Argentinian Melbec. The price was just right, only $27!!! The prices on the bottles of wine might be the best thing Mels has going, very reasonable. However, what you save on the bottle they make up in glass pours. It took me forever to decide what I wanted, it just one of those night, where nothing sounded good. I didn't get the stuffed chicken special that the server was force feeding me. I settled on chicken Italiano. Not much to say, it was completely bland. Isaac had shrimp scampi...again not much to say. I commented about how bland and flavorless everything was, and then I looked around the room putting two and two together...it looked like a night trip out for the Sunny-Dale Geriatric Ward. Seems to me like they have that demographic nailed. At the end of the night, I would have rather have spent my money on another bottle or two of wine.
label: NEG

text: They get one star b/c they comped our meal. If they hadn't done that, they would be getting a whopping zero stars. I gave my bf a trip to Nashville for Christmas. We drank almost an entire bottle of wine and an hour passed before we even got our appetizers. We should have known we were in trouble when the bread they brought out was stale and bland. The food was worse than the wait. I got mussels and they had no taste and were slightly cold. Matt got fried chicken dumplings and they were chewy on the outside and cold in the middle. We let it go and hoped that the entrees would be better. Waited about another hour (sigh) and finally got our main course. Noticed other diners around us were obviously irritated with the wait as well. I got the lobster and a twice baked potato. The potato literally looked like it had been baked 12 times and then lit with a blow torch. Matt got the lamb and ordered it rare- it was so well done that it was crispy on the outside and completely dried out inside. That's when we called over the manager and let him have it. He said he was embarrassed that we were served our meals when he saw the state of the food. He was nice enough and he comped our entire meal but needless to say, we'll be visiting other, more simplistic, quality, fresh restaurants who focus on what they cook best (rather than cooking EVERYTHING but the kitchen sink) when we come back to Nashville.
label: NEG

text: I walked out! First time in my life I ever did this. Kevin.....What have you done to your restaurant????? I loved Philadelphia Fish and Company. It was always one of my favorites. Ok, I get a bad economy and competition made you rethink everything......but..............This place sucks now if you're not a "bridge and tunnel" troller! Mel and I were in the mood for a burger, BBQ, and loads of tequilla! This usually spells out a good night for me ;}, fun night with friends, and the best tip a server ever got in Philadelphia. We loved the old place and figured that their new BBQ slash Tex Mex slash Southern cooking slash Burger thing had to be worth our time. WRONG!!!!! Just pass on this place! Food is average at best. Go to Delilah's in the train staion for better Southern cooking. Stay at Good Dog for a burger, and hell....who knows where you might get real good BBQ in this city for less than $20.00 per person. Thankfully though.....if we all avoid the place The Cherry Hill/King of Prussia crowd will have some place to compare haircolor and leave us alone to enjoy our city. We were excited to get out in time to get to drinks with friends and salvage an evening!
label: NEG

text: Really delicious! I live and work closeby, so I'm so happy for this place to be open. They have a variety of sandwiches and were able to satisfy both my vegan sister and my carnivorous self! A tad on the slow side, even though there were 3 guys on the counter, but hopefully that works itself out once they're open longer. All in all, definitely worth a visit.

text: Oh hell yeah. This place rocks. The fried chicken is amazing, and I highly recommend the spicy version. Be warned, it packs some pretty serious heat. The cole slaw is also the best I've ever had. Fresh and crisp and just a hint of creaminess, and is a great way to cool off from the spicy chicken. The price can't be beat. 5 bucks for 3 pieces of chicken, cole slaw, mashed potatoes, AND a dinner roll. The potatoes & dinner roll are nothing special, but hey, for 5 bucks you can't go wrong. I also recommend calling in ahead and ordering, because when you're hungry for fried chicken, every minute you wait feels like an eternity. I will freely admit that my last visit to this place was inspired by the recent South Park episode about KFC. Of course, Porters totally destroys them.

text: Although I'm writing this while rather intoxicated, apparently my typing skills are not suffering too terribly. From personal experience in late June I can tell you that there is nothing more delicious or more satisfying to start your HOT night off then one of these because they get a solid buzz going and cool you down so you can continue your bar crawl until you're drunk enough to drag yourself to your hotel to sleep it off. Grab one of these fruity, high-alcohol lime green drinks and enjoy!

text: Went to Balaban's for lunch the other day. Was pleasantly surprised at how good it was! We had two of the daily specials--the housemade country pate and the softshell crab. Both were splendid! Based on that, I think that taking them up on their daily offerings is probably the way to go, as they focus on local/fresh/sustainable, etc. We also had the short rib sliders with blue cheese slaw. These were pretty good, but I felt that the meat was a little tough and the slaw actually had more flavor than the short rib. But still, it was tasty. We also had the BBQ salmon, which is done with a dry rub and recommended. The wine selection is great! There were plenty of interesting offerings by the glass, and when they ran out of the vino verde we'd selected our server was quick to offer us an albarino that was previously available only by the bottle (we were ordering by the glass). There is also a wide selection of bottles available to go. Overall, I really enjoyed the food. I thought the menu was interesting and had a hard time choosing what to try. (I like that about a restaurant.) I also appreciate that they have wine flights available, and they do special set dinners to focus on seasonal ingredients or wine pairings. If you can get over the fact that it's in a strip mall (the half-curtains do a good job of hiding this, while still letting in plenty of natural light, yet its locale does bum me out), you can partake in some of the best food going in St. Louis right now!
label: POS

text: Win! I pass this place every day on my way home from work, but it wasn't until recently that we decided to check it out. We started off with the fried pork and chive dumplings. text: I'm a bit shocked at the "Woohoo!" or "Yay!" reviews because this Forever21 is not what you expect from Santa Barbara. The whole 3 stories thing doesn't matter because there is not a lot of variety. Many of the items look as if it has been there for a long time (stretched out, old styles that you've seen in other Forever21 stores from who knows what season, items that just aren't sold out perhaps because they aren't popular fashion trends). If you are in the Southern California area I recommend going to Cerritos Center Mall and/or Lakewood Center Mall. Trust me... you'll see the difference I'm talking about, and you'll be wowed by the 3 levels.

text: I stayed at the Peppermill for two nights this week while attending a conference.... it was very interesting. The lobby of the hotel is a casino and has enough colorful lights to make you go temporarily blind. The check-in staff were delightful and very nice, but also a bit slow to check me in (or maybe I was just grumpy!). The hotel has everything from gambling, a business center, shopping, four different restaurants and a health facility (best part of the hotel). They even have a wedding chapel... yes, a wedding chapel. I was happy it was empty when I walked by. My room was very large, but was the ugliest hotel room I've ever seen. The whole wall along the head of the beds (I had a double) was a mirror, and the opposite wall had a peach floral wallpaper. The beds were not comfortable at all and was covered in an old crushed green bed spread that had a strange odor. The bathroom was ok, and comes with bath and body works products... but they were lime coconut verbena scented, which makes me want to hurl. I went to the gym both days, and enjoyed that the most. There is a pool, several cardio machines and weights. Grab a bottle of water and fresh fruit when you're done!! Also, the hotel is located just a mile from the Sparks Convention Center and about four miles from the airport, which makes things easy.

text: My mouth waters for Vito's pizza. Small place, open for lunch and dinner. Not much to look at, but the food will make your stomach smile. Cheap slices of pizza and a drink if that's what you're looking for, as well as typical Italian dishes. Friendly staff, I think they're all mostly from Lithuanian.. I had a friend of a friend that worked there, pretty sure it's family owned. But amazing!

text: I met up with a group of friends for an undisclosed event here. We got 4-5 appetizers, some entrees, drinks (coffee! and booze), and a few hookas. Everything was wonderful. The food was delicious. The coffee was spiced. The hooka was tasty. What I really want to review is the first waitress- not the 2 dark haired girls that came after her. She had a green sweater, light hair. She was huffing and puffing and just snippy with us from the beginning. I realize that some folks have bad days and it was close to the end of her shift, but the way she was treating us was superfluous. To begin with, she was called out on a lie to one of the folks in our group. Then, there weren't any other customers in there, yet she didn't come to refill our drinks for half an hour more or less, so we asked for some new drinks and she said sure but still didn't bring anything out. Some more folks showed up and she didn't take their order until we asked her to. A minute later, she asked if we could pay because it was the end of her shift. We gave her the monies, then across the room she yells something to the effect that we have a few dollars change left and insinuates "is that ALL you are leaving me?" So there was some awkward, incredulous silence and one of our party walked over and paid her a few dollars more for her tip. It was insulting for her to demand a bigger tip (which, to clarify was not intended to be the tip to begin with) and to petition us in such a way made me not want to giver her anything at all. The 2 ladies that were there after her were the complete opposite and we did end up staying several hours later. It was such and unfortunate experience. If she is working I will not go there, despite the fact that everything else was awesome.

text: Went with my wife this evening for Father's day. Waitress and management were extremely pleasant and accomodating. Unfortunately that wasn't nearly enough to compensate for the awful food. The first thing to reach the table was some of the most under-prepared bread I've ever had. If you have a taste for raw dough you MAY like it. My wife and I shared the Sweet Chili Coconut Glazed Shrimp as an appetizer and enjoyed it thoroughly. It was the one high point of the entire meal. The shrimp were cooked to perfection covered in a light coconut sauce and placed on top of a grilled pinapple slice. I would have preferred it slightly more spicy, but it was never the less delicious. The next course was the Seafood Bisque. In short it was very deficient in 1) Seafood, 2) Salt, 3) flavor. If you want a bowl of hot cream this is right up your alley. My wife and I both elected for the Caesar salad to accompany our meals. While the flavor was fine, the quantity of dressing was ridiculous. I was able to stomach about 3 bites before I felt my arteries clogging. My main course was a BBQ Sea Bass. The fish itself was slightly undercooked. The BBQ sauce was clearly an afterthought. The onion rings sitting on top did it no justice either. The mashed potatoes and green beans were not very flavorful either. On the whole the food at Blue2O was among the worst food I've ever had. The only thing that saved the manager from getting an earful was the fact that the waitress was too nice for words. I'll never eat there again, and don't recommend anyone try anything beyond the appetizer shrimp. May be a nice place to stop and have a few drinks - the bar did look nice.
label: NEG

text: While in Santa Barbara, I went here with my family because of good reviews. There's not much to say about this place. The atmosphere was fine. The service was fine (somebody greeted us, took our order, and brought us food in a timely fashion, nothing more than i would expect from a cheap chain restaurant like chile's). Nothing remarkable. The food is where things went wrong. For appetizers, we ordered the fried Brie and apple fritter salad, which sounded good. We also got the red onion rings, because onion rings are a slam dunk for us. Both appetizers were among the most bland foods I've eaten in my recent memory. Not good, not bad, just utterly tasteless. For the main courses, I'm a vegetarian, and there was nothing on the menu without meat. No problem, they have a vegetarian menu. When I looked at the vegetarian menu, I was flabbergasted with how boring it was. They basically had linguini with vegetables or roasted vegetables. It is my personal opinion that if you cant be more creative than that without throwing a steak on top, there's something wrong with the chef. My meat eating dining partners all agreed that the vegetarian "menu" was jaw-droppingly boring, and even insulting. I ordered the linguini, hoping for it to maybe come out with a little sparkle of creativity that didn't show on the menu. Nope. I got buttered noodles with vegetables. On the other hand, if you're a real meat and potatoes kind of person and you don't need an interesting menu or a different dining experience, a couple of the meat dishes that people in my party ordered were apparently very good. Among those dishes was the roasted duck breast, the grilled chicken, and the jane's burger with gouda cheese and caramelized onions. Bottom line: nothing interesting or special, but if you're looking for a standard run of the mill meat and potatoes meal, you might be ok here,
label: NEG

text: Wan Sheng, what are you doing to me? This store is rather large and at one point I thought I had mentally mastered its layout, maneuvering myself slyly from one aisle to the next picking up all of my pantry necessities. I'm totally ok with the forest of foliage at the front of the store having been dismantled, but it took me a good 5 laps around the first floor to find my rice vermicelli, fish sauce, and can of water chestnuts. He's a nice guy, a little scary looking as he hardly ever cracks a smile, the language barrier is just a little difficult to overcome at times when trying to find what I'm looking for in his store. Major props to him though for running a clean operation and even better are the expiration dates on almost all packages which is more than I can say for the Asian Supermarket at 11th and Race. I love that his store is open until 9pm so when I need items in a pinch it's great that their welcoming bright lights are still on. Big selection of both imported Chinese grocery items as well as American items both household and grocery. Sure the prices are a little on the high side for things like milk and aluminum foil, but it sure beats hopping in the car and heading to SuperFresh.

text: My wife and I were here around 8:45PM on a Monday night and it couldn't have been more slow. We sat at the bar and one side was covered with servers doing nothing except counting their meager tips they had earned so far, and the other side had 1 patron in a business suit, drinking a beer and reading the paper. My wife, who has experienced Ireland 7 times, said she immediately felt like she was back there. Understandably so since everything was imported from there, even the fast talking Irish bartender that brought her a Shandy and a lager for myself. We got to talking about Scotch and Whiskey and immediately the age old feud of which is better began between the bartender and my wife who is a single malt drinker. All in good fun of course we were having a grand time. I decided to get a Creme Brulee while I witnessed my Canadian wife talking tank with this fast talking Irishman. It was quite amusing. He pulled a bottle off the shelf and in his proudest Irish exclaimed "ya gotta give this a tug, it's an acquired taste, definitely acquired" He poured her the largest "Taste" I have ever seen. She gave it a go and under her breath asked me "did I just buy a whiskey?" Me -"I dunno" She loved it and spent the next hour sipping it back while now, discussing Whisky and Scotch. After all was said and done and we got our bill, the bartender didn't charge us for the Whiskey, or even the Brulee. Awesome, I guess it pays to have a Wife who travels. We'll go back next time we're in town.
label: POS

text: A friend of mine and I decided to do some of the "fall-ish" activities of Philadelphia last week, and went on the 'infamous' ghost tour of philadelphia. Our tour guide Celeste was personable and well-versed in the pre-written stories of the tour. However, it was clear that she was just a college student looking to make a few extra bucks, and knew nothing more than the pre-concocted stories told her. She often complained of it being too cold for her, of which I wanted to reply "then dress for the weather, the rest of us have". The tour covered approx. 12 sites in Old City Philly and our tour guide spent ample time at each site The history itself was interesting, so long as the guide didn't try to skew the history to make it worse/scarier/more judgemental than it really had to be. However it was the same old song and dance for each...."if you listen closely you will hear the ghosts"..."if you look closely, you might see a spirit lurking around" Something of this accord was said at every single site, and multiple times. Yes we understand, that is the point of these tours, however please leave some things to the imagination because it felt forced and fake and cheesy. In fact it literally made my skin crawl everytime she said it...and not because I was scared. And there was definately false advertising here. It was advertised that the tour guides dressed in costumes and carried lanterns. No such luck. Celeste had spandex leggings and a backpack asking for tips, with a big ol' throw-away cup of some sort of fancy coffee concoction from cosi. Not entirely what we were expecting.
label: NEG

text: After getting a high volume of business, the quality of the service has deteriorated. text: What is the FUSS over this place about??? Oprah said this was one of the World's Best Mac 'N Cheese around. (personally, I think it was both) The flavor was only passable for a location that is supposedly synonymous with SOUTERN FOOD. *see my review of Homeplace Restaurant in VA for the BEST fried chicken i've had. Fried Whiting This was one of the better items but probably because the fish was purchased fresh from one of the fresh fish stands... Collard Greens NO.. it was ham hock laiden and needed a balance with more acidity. The service was poor (rude and not friendly) and not efficient - the line took forever. text: I went here on a date a few days ago and since Penang had a wait, we decided to try out a new place and this place was the new Ho Sai Gai. I've never been here before so I didn't know what to expect. First of all, it has a really nice outside and inside as well. Very new and modern. The people were nice although sometimes bordered on too nice; too intrusive on our dinner date. I ordered the Pineapple Coconut Chicken and I felt it was alright. Nothing to write home about. The food was kind of on the more expensive side (for the portions and quality of food offered). The only real complaint I have with this restaurant is how intrusive they were. The lady started to speak with me in Chinese even though I told her I didn't understand Chinese (I'm not even Chinese!). If they backed off more then it wouldn't have been as awkward. Also, the food was so-so. In the end, I don't think I'm coming back to this place unless I hear more good reviews. (and they didn't have an alcohol license so I couldn't drink) (and also, the crab rangoon was pretty good - the best I've had so far. Definitely try it if you do go)
label: NEG

text: Located right in the heart of the gayborhood in Philly this place is a good spot for ice cream. Is it amazing ice cream; no, but it's good. The sundaes here are huge and tasty. One sundae can easily serve two people. The birthday cake ice cream is good as is the pistachio almond. There are better places for ice cream in Philly, but it's still good.
label: POS

text: Yeah, um, no. Dino's "Casa de Beauty" is more like a Casa de Nightmare. It took me a little over a year and four visits to a better salon for Dino's butchering of my hair to finally work its way out. I don't know how he managed to do so much damage, but that's the Casa for you.
label: NEG

text: I am a Whole Foods Market customer and supporter through and through, but this store was a complete disappointment. Product placement was completely disorganized, shelving was empty in many areas, and the prices were ridiculous (for those of you who think WF is already expensive, this was beyond..way beyond that). It was so NOT the WHOLE FOODS experience that customers are used to, and have come to love and expect. At one point, I was looking for an item, and a store employee actually ran into me, after being asked by another customer if there were any lemons in the back because they weren't on display. Um, hello? The store seemed very unkept, and poorly managed. I am so surprised that Whole Foods hasn't done something about this and is allowing their reputation to be damaged by this store. I purchased a smoothie with my other items, and the person who made it was very nice.. that is why I gave this store a rating of 2 stars and not 1. If this is your only Whole Foods Market experience, please give another store a chance. It is a world's difference from this one.
label: NEG

text: Sorry, Poco's, I've had better. Your salsa is watery (but thankfully somewhat spicy), and your general menu leaves much to be desired. I've tried the Mexican pizza, black bean soup (or chili?), and burrito...a big fat "meh."
label: NEG

text: My BF and I came here for dinner while we were visiting beautiful Santa Barbara. The Rock Crab was AMAZING! Its was so delicious and it went very well with the beer selection ;) We also had a few oyster shooters and raw oysters that were unbelievable! The customer service is fantastic, very attentive but not pushy at all. Its not as large as other restaurants but its cozy has a nice view of the water and you can sit outside if you want. We are definitely planning to come here for the crab and oysters the next time we're back in SB...If you want delicious seafood for a killer price go check this place out you'll be glad you did!
label: POS

text: I went here on a cold and blustery Saturday night. The space is very warm and the wood floors are very nice. They did an excellent job of creating a nice open space that makes you feel at home. I started out with some bread, which was pita bread accompanied by hummus. The pita bread was decent, but the hummus had way way too much garlic in it. The butternut squash soup I had sounded better than it actually tasted. It didn't have the right taste that you'd expect from butternut squash. It looked good. However, it didn't taste good and the consistency was more like mashed vegetable cooked in water. For the entree I had chicken with a dijon cream sauce in capers and sundried tomatoes. Sounds good, right? Sadly, it wasn't. The chicken was moist and tender, but that was the only decent thing about this. The sundried tomatoes were present, but must have been old or overcooked because they didn't lend any flavor that I could detect. The djion cream sauce could have been good, but there were way too many capers in it and that overpowered everything else. I had a lemon tart and coffee for dessert. The lemon tart was served with a spoon. This particular tart came with a very hard/thick crust, which made eating with a spoon almost impossible. Luckily I have strong hands so i was able to carve out bites. There was plenty of lemon flavoring, but a bit much lemon zest in it. Service was the bright note here. The waitress, the host/owner/manger?, and the cook were all very nice. I'd like to come back and try something else and see if it was just this dish/night. The people next of me had some lamb that looked fantastic, and the pork medallions and steak with peppercorn sauce also looked good.
label: NEG

text: I joined a party of 15+ (yep, that many) Saturday night for a pre-bachelorette party dinner. 7pm on a Saturday. The service could not have been better. We had one primary server (I believe) and a few that helped out when delivering food, etc. She was happy to answer any questions and provided excellent drink recommendations. The food and drinks were fantastic. I had the gorgonzola open faced steak sandwich. I kind of disassembled it to eat, but every element was spot on. For drinks I enjoyed a Singapore Sling (very sweet...I'm glad I had this pre-meal) and a Pink Lady. Both were very well made and tasty. I don't go downtown much, but when I do I will be sure to keep Past Perfect in rotation.
label: POS

text: I was in New Orleans and stayed in the French Quarters. I was looking forward to going to K Paul for Chef Paul. I grew up watching him cook on tv. My friends and I ordered the fried green tomatoes to start and it was ok - I had better. The shrimp with the tomatoes were fishy. I ordered the salad with pears and blue cheese. The salad was drenched with salad dressing and the pears were poached. It wasn't a refreshing salad at all. We then ordered the fillet mignon with potatoes and broccoli and the ettouffe. The effouffe was great with fresh seafood and fluffy white rice. The fillet was done right but the potatoes and broccoli we're dipped and drenched in butter and inedible. The best part of the night was the free bread basket with the molasses bread - YUMMY!! Save your money - there are better places in NOLA.
label: NEG

text: Best. Duck. EVER. I don't care if this is a "bastardized Chinese" place, it doesn't get any better than roasted duck and white rice!

text: This is the worst applicance repair company I have EVER had to deal with. My washer has had problems since Sept. 2009. They came out three times and tried to say it was different things. Finally, they said it was a problem with the timer, which is what a friend of ours had told us originally and it took AJ Appliance forever to figure out (and our friend is not even experienced with appliances). AJ Appliance figure it out in Nov. 2009. They said they would order the part and it would take 3-4 business days. Almost a month passed and the washer was not fixed and we did not hear from them. We finally had to call them and ask what happened. We were told that they had not fixed it because they had written down the model number incorrectly for the washer. They never bothered to call us to tell us this was the problem or that they needed the correct number. text: The square beyond compare! And STL pizza done right! Okay so they are technically the "original" but still it's some of the best pizza around! And their salad here is perfection I don't know what it is...maybe they have a special sauce in their dressing but it's good! I always get the personal 1 topping cheese pizza, a salad with ranch and a drink and it's only $10! What a steal! I've also never had a bad Imo's experience!

text: We stayed at the Renaissance Pere Marquette during a recent visit to New Orleans (on Common Street and Baronne). Brother's is on the opposite corner. We must have walked by this place a dozen times as we left our hotel to go exploring. It wasn't until Friday night/Saturday morning at, oh, about 3am that we decided to give it a go. I've never seen a grocery store that also happens to sell fried chicken, but it is GENIUS. We walked back to our hotel with neatly packed boxes filled with fried chicken and French fries, and assorted groceries. It really hit the spot. The gastrointestinal distress I experienced the following day was totally worth it.

text: This has become my favorite place for a quick easy and relatively cheap lunch. You can come early or late to avoid the lunch rush, but sometimes it's worth the wait in line to get a fresh slice right out of the oven. Their toppings choices are plentiful, and all look pretty tasty. My favorite is the spinach and tomato. Even when there is a line, the counter staff have it pretty much down to a science; order first, pay, then step out of the way to wait, and no one gets hurt =P And listen for "bella, your pizza!" There's a lot more seating than meets the eye, they often have Italian pop music playing; sit back, people watch from the giant windows, and listen to them yelling at each other in Italian. Good times. =)

text: i have a love/hate relationship with the terminal. yes, they have amazing food selections. produce, meats, seafood, local, organic, etc. all amazing and affordable. but, its the damn congestion of the place that gets to me. the other shoppers have absolutely no regard for other people. i get barreled into at least 3 or 4 times when i'm there. it makes me leave and not continue my shopping because i get so frustrated. i now have a new method where i only go on a wednesday or thursday morning about an hour after they open. less congestion, more great shopping. awesome place, too many people. good luck on a saturday, i hope you get out alive.

text: Gripe: the volatile, perturbed, frank inner-linings of a disgruntled stomach outward bound with great verbosity, not to be mistaken for 'tripe,' the inner-linings of tepid steer, No-bones-about-it I have a gripe with this place. Coming out of a decade with W as President we learned that the best way to succeed is to lower expectations, as he did in a very Bushian way. Now, the Brewpub because of where they are (in our lovely Village), what they are (a cozy, micro-micro!, neighborhood pub) and how they've so lovingly presented themselves...they raised the expectations for what rolls out of their imperial pint glasses. They've created a stimulating environment with dogs and bicycles and friends outside and a cozy winter-time inside. They've also created a pretty stimulating menu with far-reaching items like salmon with quinoa salad and chicken mole burrito that successfully live up to gastropub standards. (Thickly, British) "Now, now, having, having said that; now having said that," their beer, their ale, their lager, all of it, every single glass I've had is wildly sub-par. Unbearable to finish. Giving micro brewpubs a bad name (much like how Hubbard & Craven does for micro coffee roasters). The beer is flat, salty even. The beer lives under the description of a "clean" finish when in fact it's just an empty finish. I tried to trick myself into thinking, "oh, well, this soap-y taste must just be the glass..." Nope, every single beer has this really strange tang, cleaning product taste to it. I'll admit...I've been here a lot. I've thoroughly enjoyed myself and my surroundings and my grub (however steer clear of veggies -- they taste like the truck they came off of). When I return for that mango quinoa salmon...I'll get dirty looks from the regulars and the server because I'm sticking with out-of-town bottled beer. Big Positive: Well-Crafted Ambience. Another Debbie Downer Note: Never have I seen a price special on beer or food at this place. Is there even a happy hour?
label: NEG

text: I saw this restaurant opening on the Food Network about five years ago and I said if I am ever in, I am going to go. Well five years later, I got to go. It was really good but I think Oishii in Boston is better. Moritomo's atmosphere is really unique. I had mentioned I was a fan of the food network and the waiter brought me over a free appetizer. There is a lot more cooked dishes on the menu than sushi. I would recommend the sushi sampler that gives you two pieces of each fish in its own unique sauce
label: POS

text: I went to this restaurant the second week it opened.I had heard so many good reviews I was anxious to stop by and try it out..We ordered the onion appetizer and had steaks.I actually enjoyed the meal. The manager checked in on us and nothing wrong with the service.I have always felt sorry for waitstaff anytime they are called on to perform and this was a corny line dance.Cringe worthy.The problem was all of us in our party of 3 were very sick.Half way home it hit me hard and I was seeking a gas station with a bathroom.My teenage daughter was empting her meal in the parking lot of my savior the gas station with open facilities.Hubby insisted he was just fine and told us we must be getting ill.He was gone for 2 weeks on business and this was hours after he got home so I said we will see.After a half hour home he got hit with Texas Roadhouse Tummy cramps.If he didn't get sick I would have tried it again but too terrified of a repeat performance.

text: This store is too narrow and is poorly laid out, without any consideration given to what customers experience. Specifically, when I visited during Winter, it got extremely cold in the front of the store because whenever anyone opened the door, gusts of cold air rushed in over the seated customers. The management made no attempt whatsoever to shield patrons from the cold wind. Only the customers in the back were shielded from the cold, but back there you have to listen to the inane barista chatter. I once witnessed an ugly scene at this store. One of the female employees sitting out front noticeably began crying. I was inside and I overheard a male employee backstabbing her, assaulting her character.

text: If you live in Brentwood, chances are you've probably either been to or heard of Peter's and it's probably for a good reason. As a regular patron all I can do is sing their praises. The staff is friendly, attentive, and generous. They always go out of their way to make sure you're getting the best service possible. The head chef Peter, who previously worked at another sushi bar, has people coming from all around just to eat his amazing sushi creations. The specialty rolls are usually the most inventive and combine fruits and sauces with tempura style deep fry. I would recommend either the Husband and Wife roll or the Dragon Roll, but make sure you get there early because it's always packed!
label: POS

text: This place is wonderful! Went there when visiting home recently, and had a wonderful experience there. We made reservations which is probably recommended because they do get pretty busy. We arrived a little early and were also sat a bit earlier than our reservations were for, which was quite nice. Sat down and ordered a bottle of wine. Started off the meal with the lentil dip was super delicious, also is vegan, which is nice. Then moved onto the basic starting salad, which I think I would recommend passing on it could have been because of the spinach ban though that they were a bit lacking... not sure. But the entrees were phenomenal, had the tofu and the tempeh option for the evening and they were just delectable, flavors that I've almost never experienced in both, just great. Our server was super knowledgeable about the menu and the restaurant in general. Not to mention, the owners and managers are very very friendly and were definitely interested in what we thought of the restaurant and had a wonderful sense of humor.
label: POS

text: The italian hoagie is good as long as you get everything on it. The chicken diablo - really good and truly diablo spicy. The Dirt pudding - sooooooo good, i just wish you could get more in one serving! A great little place to grab some hoagies for the road.
label: POS

text: I'm breaking the silence - this place rocks. Yea, I only gave it four stars. The fifth can be added later when I am wowed by something here. Located literally right across 8th Ave South from the Cannery/Mercy Lounge, you will find a nondescript building that packs a wall of sound. The stage in this venue is large and has multiple levels. There is room in this place to pack a thousands music lovers. The bar has some decent specials ($3 bottled beers) and they also have a food menu (or white board). This was my first time here and I had a blast. There is no smoking inside. The bathrooms were clean and the venue spotless. My favorite part of the Center Stage is that the backdrop of the stage is a wall of silver, gold and platinum records with artist descriptions. Their website is nonexistent. And, that sucks. How is a brother suppose to find out what shows are playing here? I guess I have to be in the Know again.
label: POS

text: I really didn't like the food in this restaurant. I don't know why my review was removed..... This Japanese buffet is really bad. Nothing fresh so the flavor is either too salty or too much soy sauce. I guess that's a common way to hide the non-fresh food.

text: To properly set up this review, we're going to take it back. Way back to when I was a senior in high school almost ten years ago (eek!) and was looking for a dress to wear to an event. What ensued on that shopping trip stuck with me, as to date, it still is the worst experience I've had with a salesperson. The saleswoman knew I was in hot pursuit of a cute dress and was determined to find the right one for me. Don't get me wrong - I appreciated the enthusiasm. However, what I didn't appreciate was her flinging the door to the dressing room open to foist more dresses on me while I was in the midst of changing for the whole store to see. Needless to say, I did not buy a dress from there that day. Fast-forward to this past December when I'm in town visiting my family. My mom is on a quest for find the perfect mother-of-the-bride dress for my wedding this June. She tells me that she wants to go to Town and Country. Of course, I'm not too keen on the idea, but I keep an open mind since my negative experience was so long ago. This time around, the saleswoman who helped us was quite frigid and seemed rather disinterested in providing any sort of assistance. Instead of her asking questions about the wedding (i.e., colors, time of day, location, etc.) to help guide us in the right direction for dresses, we had to keep volunteering the information in hopes of getting some insight on good potential dress candidates. Not much luck in the mother-of-the-bride department at this store. On another note, I did luck out in finding a cute pair of shoes to change into for the reception - they have a good assortment of shoes by Grace. (I saw the same pair in San Francisco that was on backorder, so decided to get them at T&C to save me a trip). In going to the back of the store to look at the shoes, I passed by their wedding dresses, and I did notice that they have quite an extensive collection of lovely ones by Melissa Sweet, Christos, etc. So, in a nutshell, if you're a bride-to-be, I'd pay this store a visit, given their impressive collection of dresses (too good to pass up). However, for anything else, including MOB dresses, I'd go elsewhere. The caliber of service continues to leave a bad taste in my mouth.
label: NEG

text: Even though we ate so many racks of ribs all day long at the Nugget Rib Cook-off, we couldn't pass up a deal at such a late hour. Close to midnight, we took advantage of their after-concert special...$12.99 per person. I thought it wouldn"t be a full-on buffet menu....but it was! Aside from the price, other pluses were the large tables and their new layout (it's been a while since I've dined in here). The shrimp fajitas, seafood tamales, steal head fish, and seafood canelloni were my favorites. I was most impressed with their Gelato for dessert. I had a the mint chocolate chip flavor with a scoop of the vanilla, chocolate and caramel w/ brownies flavor. The prime rib, fried rice, potstickers, and fried chicken were just average. I'd pass on the calamari picatta and lasanga. I didn't bother with the Kalbi and BBQ beef ribs (that looked pretty good), since I was all ribbed out from the cook-off. This late-night special is open to everyone. I would definitely return....especially after a concert I did or didn't attend. Way worth it!
label: POS

text: And you thought Pat's and Geno's had a rivalry against one another. I mean on this street there are two very similar Vietnamese restaurant s directly across the street from one another. so similar that it can be nearly impossible to tell the difference between the two. I tended to favor this one a little bit more the last time around. but it's a constant cycle.

text: There's just something I really like about this bar. Actually, there are a lot of somethings: a well-thought out beer list, tons of good vegetarian food options, including that awesome tempeh club, great brunch that never feels like an afterthought, the cozy interior, friendly staff, a fantastic jukebox and the fact that there always seems to be at least one other Morrissey fan there to play his songs too. The only problem I can find here is that Royal Tavern is not close enough to my apartment. Of course, no restaurant can deliver a flawless dining experience 100% of the time, but every time I come to Royal Tavern, I leave happy.

Be prepared for up to an hour wait on peak nights, but the surrounding neighborhood has plenty of distractions. Pro Tip: a $20 bill, smoothly placed in the hands of the person running the list, will get you seated promptly

I had the Tom Kha, sue had the Tom Yum and we split a papaya salad. all very good, yes yes. i got the garlic scallops and shrimp and ate it about two hours after we got home. 4 hrs later, I'm up and huddled over the business end of the toilet. text: While I didn't love the bar as a hang out the only time I went (there wasn't much going on and we didn't find it to be an overly friendly place), we go back again and again for dinner. Their food is spectacular. I could eat a chimichanga from there everyday. I find that their combo dish is a great deal (you can choose one, two, or three items). I generally just get the chimichanga as the only item in my "combo" (it's not really a combo, I guess if you only get one thing) and while that might not be enough for some, the fact that it's paired with rice and beans makes it a perfectly sized meal for me at a low price. They also have complimentary chips and salsa (great starter), so having a little less for dinner isn't such a bad thing. And save room for the margaritas. Blended and on the rocks are both the perfect compliment to a meal!
label: POS

text: Not to be confused with Joe's Crabshack, but Crabby Bill's is your typical tourist seafood restaurant in Florida. There are only a few large restaurants on Clearwater Beach but the turnover time is pretty fast, even during Spring Break. They have indoor and outdoor seating. Inside is more like a restaurant whereas outside is a lot more causal because the seating is at picnic tables. They also have a bar and a gift shop downstairs (what touristy restaurant in Florida doesn't have a gift shop????). There is also someone walking around taking digital pictures that you can buy, but no pressure! The staff isn't overly friendly but nice enough and is fairly quick in getting you your food and drink. I am not a seafood eater so I had little to choose from but liked my food nonetheless. They will also cook what you catch so you can stumble off one of the fishing boats next door and into the restaurant to eat your prize catch.
label: POS

The service was instantly warm and friendyl. The menu of small dishes provided the opportunity to try many wonderful things.. And the waiter made a great recommendation of the duck toast (incredible!)... So go prepared to throwdown at least $150 for two if you want to do it right- as we did with the dense chocolate cake and a shared glass of scotch. A perfect way to end our week in Philly! Great neighborhood.. Great town.... Great meal!

text: I have to say that I just about cried when I found out Fioravanti's was closing. I was very worried that Downingtown was losing a wonderful little BYOB. HOWEVER, I believe Amani's has more than filled the shoes of Fiorvanti. The update on the decor is wonderful, much more inviting and warm feeling. They have remained a BYOB and will even mix drinks with any liquor you bring in. The staff is wonderful and after going several times I have never had what I would even consider mediocre service, it has been great every time. Their menu is fantastic and changes to incorporate seasonal foods. I love the tasting menu but am a little sad that it isn't available on the weekend. Also, make sure to note the hours of operation. For some reason we always end up trying to go on Mondays but alas it isn't open. Great little BYOB for Downingtown!
label: POS

text: Like many folks here, and probably 2/3 of PCS' total customer base, I had the no-fee membership. Then PCS pulled that dishonest, short notice, hidden-at-the-bottom-of-a-generic-email nonsense canceling the no-fee option. So bye-bye. Before the shady fee increase, the PCS cost/benefit calculus just barely broke even. For a 24hr rental, the price was the same as Enterprise. Every car I used was filthy inside and/or banged up on the outside. The "damage log" was a joke; who wants to read through dozens of pages trying to guess which ding matched up with which vague, sloppy-handwriting note? But on the plus side, they had a better car selection than most rent-a-car places, and quick, 24 hour availability. Plus no need to pay for parking if I brought the car back early. I hope ZipCar will see a potential market in all these disgruntled, ex-PCS customers and start up a no-fee membership.
label: NEG

text: Man...it's a damn shame I'm not a guy who can pull off cowboy boots. Visiting this place makes me want to buy a turquoise pair of snakeskins and trot around like a real live cowboy. Too bad I'm not that cool. I don't frequent boot shops, so I don't know if the prices here are typical or not. I can tell you, however, that I didn't see a single pair of boots for less than $150. Most authentic-looking cowboy boots run somewhere around $300, but the sales lady told me every pair in the store was buy-one-get-two-free. Sounds like a pretty good deal to me. Boot Country also has a pretty large selection of rodeo and Western style shirts. Most of them were about $50, but everything on the men's rack was 50% off. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and they don't seem to mind letting crazy tourists try on their merchandise and pretend to be Roy Rogers. As you can probably tell, I'm not really the cowboy type. This store kind of makes me wish I was, however. The whole place smells like leather, and their boots range from rough-looking shit-kickers to nice and polished boots you could wear to a funeral...if you're an old oil magnate or the owner of the Dallas Cowboys. Pretty cool spot to look around even if you can't swing one of their fancy pairs of kicks.
label: POS

text: I really, really don't understand the other reviews of this place lauding its cuisine. Perhaps it's the Gordon Ramsay halo effect. Perhaps I am too picky. Maybe I went on an off night. Irrespective of why my experience didn't match the outrageously high rating here, I shan't be returning. I went here after the supposed fix from Kitchen Nightmares. I remember when the sign changed a few years ago and wondered why - now I guess I know. Three words: Expensive. Greasy. Underwhelming. I am not sure what they learned from Ramsay, or if they simply forgot, or if they stopped caring. I ordered the much-lauded Shepherd's Pie, only to receive a bowl of greasy ground meat. Stouffer's is better and doesn't cost $10. My wife's $8 baked potato tried to compensate with size what it lacked in flavor and toppings. We've heard others say the fries were delicious. They weren't. (I've heard the same thing about Eulogy's and Monk's fries too, which I also find grotesque). The server was the nice young man who was thoroughly featured in the episode. He was pleasant and attentive. The cafe is only a few blocks' walk from my home - but I'll walk the other direction to the Supermarket if I have a craving for potatoes in the future. For the price of one baked Hot Potato, I can buy ten pounds of my own and make them at home.

text: I don't like to brag, but, for you, fellow yelper, sitting at your computer, scouting out for some good eats, I'll step outside my comfort zone: I know Greek food. This is not good Greek food. The three worst things were: black olives in the salad (where are the kalamata olives!?) and the poor tzatziki substitute (like a thin, plain greek yogurt spread all over everything), and finally: the disturbing absence of tomatoes! Fries were blah. Any fast food joint fries are superior. In such a large city, I say go explore for better Greek than this place.

text: My wife and I stopped by this weekend. We were out running errands and I had seen this place on the internet and had glanced at the menu. Interested in finding some good BBQ in the area we drove a little out of our way to stop by. I was particularly excited as it's only a short drive from our house and it would prove a fun destination over the summer if it was good. It's not good. We had an absolutely terrible meal here. Pulled pork sandwich was $9.99 for the lunch special including corn bread and "mini-side" My wife got this with mac and cheese. The pulled pork which they herald as their trademark and done in a "North Carolina" Style was horrendous. I still can't abandon the image of the drab, pasty gray gloppy pork that looked like someone cut off the tattered end of an old dirty mop and placed it on an over-sized kaiser bun. no cole slaw and some thick red sauce on it that was terrible. I got the baby-back rib's lunch deal that was $11.99 with corn bread and "mini-side". I tried the baked beans. the ribs were cold. ribs, when they are cold and the bbq sauce has congealed in a slimy, sticky mass on the bottom are disgusting. the side of beans tasted like they came out of a can and a little liquid smoke was added. the corn bread is absolutely terrible. cake-style and is probably that "krusteez" brand or whatever it is. absolutely terrible. The $1 ice-cream was fantastic and washed the flavor and residual goo from our mouths. the total meal cost us $24+ and I was a.) only too happy to escape the ordeal sans-food poisoning and b.) enthralled that my daugher has no teeth. This is a real shame, the building is cool and there is a lot of potential. In case you're still wondering, there is no "Pit" anywhere near the joint, this is one of those places you go in and order but you don't smell any food cooking and there is no visible kitchen. only counters where sandwiches are assembled that i could see. maybe some warming ovens. i seriously doubt any food is actually prepared and cooked here. what's up with a bbq joint that you can't smell all the delicious meats grilling? not only did i hate this experience but I vote for a full smacking of the owners for their stupidity/lack of oversight.
label: NEG

text: Relationships only work when both parties put in an equal amount of effort. And trust me, Blue, I want us to work. But I feel like you're just not that into me anymore. Pizza that looks and tastes like it was just thawed and reheated. And service that...in a word....sucked. "Oh i'm sorry, mr. server, that i am SUCH an inconvenience to you on such a bustling *cricket cricket* Tuesday night. You just hang tight there in the corner talking to....random patron #2. I'll refill my water from the bathroom faucet, at least i'll probably get a frickin' SMILE from the women in there." So frustrating. I love Blue Moon. Or ...loved, anyway. But this experience was just...inexcusable. If i'm going to spend a total of $30 for a medium pizza, I don't think it's too much to ask to expect a fluffy and taste-FUL crust and ingredients that leave an impression. And i mean that literally. Everything on our pizza was so small that...it was difficult to tell exactly what we'd ordered in the first place. Talk about a "night and day" experience. I JUST ate here earlier this month and it was delicious....and we ordered the EXACT same thing! I'll wipe a tear from my cheek and sadly move on to another pizza joint...if i felt like gambling i'd walk down the block. But, you know, I like a little consistency when it comes to mah pizza.

All of the appetizers were pork snacks which was really interesting. Pizzas are brick oven, very thin, with creative flavor combinations (salt cod, garlic and new potatoes), always changing. The wine list and cocktail menu are great, moderately priced and diverse. Our entree items were a cured salmon succotash salad, mackerel spiedini, and heirloom tomato crespelle. Service was good, a little slow, but it was a really busy Sunday night. I can't wait to try it again!

text: My wife and I went here recently for a couple's massage on out anniversary. I should have been tipped off by the fact this place is basically located in a shack next to a dry cleaner's. Ok, no big deal, but I was kind of bothered that they had adds and pamphlets of the "miracle antioxidant cure" they were selling plastered all over the walls. Very tacky and not relaxing. Next warning was the waiver they made you sign. These are typical, however theirs made specific comments about how they do not provide any sexual services and a line that they will legally prosecute you for non-payment. All of which are fair, but it made me wonder what type of clientele they get if these things have to be put in writing... Oh well, perhaps the massage itself would be good. Nope, I specifically requested a deep tissue massage and asked for more pressure numerous times throughout the session. Also, the woman clearly did not read the form I filled out referring to my current areas of stiffness. I asked multiple timed for her to focus on these areas and even pointed to them for her. She replied "I will in a minute" and never did. She focused mostly on my soft tissue and the only places I got any real pressure were over my hip bones and on both of my upper arm bones. Not sure if you've ever had someone press hard and massage your bones, but it is not very pleasant. My wife did find her massage relaxing, but ironically she claimed her masseuse was too rough. Well, I did pay, but I will not be back and I'd recommend others to stay away as well. Too bad.

text: I did not like Palazzio the first time I ate there several years ago. text: Went with my mom last Thursday for a dinner meeting for her work. She went to join her group, and I asked the host to seat me at a table or booth big enough for two, since she'd be coming back to join me when she was finished. Then they left me there for about ten minutes without asking if I wanted something to drink or some chips and salsa...nothing. It wasn't even busy! When a server did come around, he acted confused when I said I'd like to order while waiting for my mom. Maybe it seemed like bad manners to eat before my party arrived, but I was hungry! The ambiance where I was seated was very suffocating. No windows, black walls, dark carpet, confining booths with black plastic table cloths... Even with the lights, it felt less like a romantic dimness and more like I was eating in a converted basement. I kept asking myself, "What are they trying to hide?" I'd just placed my order when my mom showed up bearing her own plate of food, which she'd ordered in the meeting. She'd just recently had a tooth extraction and was eating something unidentifiable fried in egg. I asked what it was, and with a weak smile she replied, "Bland," and reached for the salsa. Speaking of which, the chips and salsa were pretty "meh." The chips looked and tasted sort of stale, and I prefer a chunkier salsa. The mild one was pretty forgettable, and the hot one had more spice than flavor. I had been torn between ordering the carnitas and the beef/chicken combo fajitas. I had decided to go with the latter, since it sounded like it came with more veggies. (Radishes? What?) But when it arrived, it wasn't quite what I'd been expecting. The meat had been sliced extremely thin, almost julienne, and unless I squinted, I couldn't really tell the difference between the two. There was no difference in taste, either, which as Mom had said, was pretty bland. The Spanish rice was fluffy and flavorful enough. The refried beans were typical. And for the price, they only give you two tortillas which didn't even get me through half my plate. (I hear you can get three if you order corn tortillas, though I assume that's because they're smaller.) I usually try to clear everything on my plate, but I just couldn't. I picked out what I thought was most edible and left the rest, I was so disappointed. The only highlight was the flan. It was thick and sweet, with a slight cinnamon grittiness to it that was appealing. It was big enough to share with Mom, so I did. I left feeling unsatisfied and wanting a real dinner to make up for this one. It wasn't horrendous, but it wasn't anything to shout about, either. I doubt I'll return unless Mom has to have another meeting there.
label: NEG

text: One of the great things about living in New Orleans is that you can get some things that are just as excellent as in more expensive cities for a lot less money. Apparently a haircut is one of these things and Twisted is the place to go. Before Katrina I used to get my hair cut at Stardust, but when I went to their website my stylist no longer works there and the prices went WAY up, so I scanned Yelp and discovered that a number of my friends went to Stardust and the Nicole was recommended like crazy. I called up and got an appointment with her two days from when I called and at just the time I wanted with no problem. The salon is just past Napoleon Uptown and has that good Uptown feeling, clean and quality but funky and without being snotty or overpriced. The space isn't fancy but it's hardly run down either, with good equipment and cool decoration. When I walked in a number of people were hanging out and Ginger, the shop dog was there to greet me. The atmosphere is super friendly. A little winded from my bike ride from the Bywater I happily accepted some water and sat down for to discuss my hair with Nicole. To make a long story short, the first time was a charm. Despite my somewhat vague instructions I got a spectacular haircut and enjoyed excellent conversation with a very cool and friendly hair stylist all the while. First seeing it I was a little unsure about the cut and Nicole assured me that if I needed any kind of tweaks or touch-ups once I styled it myself she'd be happy to take care of that for free. The next day, however, I realized that she'd doe a truly excellent job. I really love my hair and took a bunch of pictures of it. The cost of all of this brilliance... $25. Hell yeah. Quick points: Friendly Professional Clean Really cool without attitude Generally AWESOME

text: OK, let me qualify the previous reviewer by quoting her: "In fact, I hated pizza for a long, long time." Only a communist could HATE pizza...C'Mon! How can she possibly be reviewing a Pizza joint???Anyhow, this is quite possibly some of the worst pizza in the area. I've had worse, but Grotto's (rhymes with Grosso's) really ranks up their with some worse of the worse. And I know MANY in Delaware who would agree with me. I am somewhat of a pizza snob and believe that good pizza must...MUST be cooked in a stone oven. Grotto uses a conveyor belt in all of their operations. They certainly had much better pizza back in the 1970's when they were a 1 shack operation on the boardwalk in Rehoboth Beach, but as soon as they institutionalized and corporatized and started dumping new sites on every corner in the state, quality went right down the tubes. If your out for pizza in Delaware, then save your money, you'll really need it if you eat here cuz they are WAY over-priced. Take your business to any of the mom and pop pizza joints around the area and make sure you check for the classic stone oven (it's stainless steel and has the door that pulls down in the front), or better yet, a wood fired oven.

text: OK, before I go ahead and rip this restaurant a new backdoor, let me preface this by saying that I should have written this review a year and a half ago, because that was the last time I went. So, there may be changes for the better at this point, but no matter what, I will never go back. I live in West Philly and was always excited to try RX. I heard that the dinners were very pricey but the breakfasts were great and not too bad for your pocket. When I found a special occasion to go, I was super excited. There was not too much of a wait,despite the cozy, home-y atmosphere. However, they sat us at a table that had one chair and the other side of the table was against the window, where you had to sit on the window seat. The window seat was so high up, the tops of my thighs hit the table, which was rather uncomfortable--and I'm small! Negative one point. The menu sounded delicious, so at that point, I paid little attention to my lack of comfort. I ordered coffee first. It never came. text: Hot-Diggity-Dog is as close to an authentic Chicago-style hotdog place as you'll find in the South, down to the women working the counter who are the southern equivalents of the gnarled Greeks who run these places in Chicago - they won't take your crap and you had better be ready to order when you step up. At first, I turned up my nose at the idea of cucumbers on a "Chicago-Style" dog, as would any Midwestern self-proclaimed hotdog connoisseur. But, I was persuaded and I will admit that it was not a bad addition to the traditional version - mustard, onions, green relish, pickles, tomatoes, hot peppers, and celery salt. The dogs were Vienna Beef - which makes me miss home - and were available steamed (think hot water bath) and charred. Go charred, it gives you a nice little snap when you bite into it. All-in-all I really enjoyed my experience here and will be going back - I've been told that I need to try the "Nashville" dog. text: This has become my favorite restaurant in the city! Garces can really do no wrong in my book, and this is further proof. First off, tapas is my favorite style of food. Its perfect for someone like me who upon looking at any menu, initially always proclaims "I want one of everything!" Secondly, mexican food. C'mon! Everything here is perfectly delicious! I never feel guilty eating nachos or super cheesy enchiladas here because I know its made with quality and high standards. Some of my favorites are the short rib huarache, the ceviches, skirt steak nachos, and of course guacamole. Let me preface this by saying I am a guac-snob! I pride myself in my guacamole-which i insist on keeping basic and fresh. Not oversmashed, not over seasoned. And Distrito's guacamole impressed me. Super-fresh tasting and somehow creamy and chunky at the same time. This, I deducted was possibly because half of it is made into a creamy puree, and then chunks are added in (a method I've began to practice myself). Its also topped with cotija cheese-which i wish i could find in my local supermarket. Now-the margaritas are a bit pricey here. For about $40 a pitcher you're getting probably half as much as you'd get at a more casual mexican spot for $25. However, these are quality margs! Not super sugary or reminiscent of Hi-C with a kick of bottom-shelf tequila. This is worth the money. I highly recommend checking this place out during University City's Dining Days, where for $35 a person, you're definitely getting a lot of bang for your buck-and will feel less guilty about the $40 pitcher. Also, since they changed the whole first level to the "cantina" menu, its even more worth the trip to West Philly. Drinks and food for almost half the price of the main menu-and still all of the quality and a decent variety of selections! Wish I was there now!

text: As a first time Southwest flyer I was very disappointed on the Detroit side. I flew on a "buddy pass" which is pretty much flying stand by. Since I had never flown this way before I was full of questions when my turn finally arrived at the check in counter (after a very lengthy line). Of course as soon as I made my way to the counter the man behind the counter disappeared. I tried to ask the lady at the next computer for help and she was very rude (I wish I had gotten her name)! Finally, she told me which option to choose & my security pass would print. Getting through security wasn't bad, moved fairly quick! Upon my arrival to my gate I was told that I would be called up 10 minutes before final board "if" there were any available seats by a not so friendly agent. Well, 10 minutes before & after came & went until finally standing back in the line behind 4 other people I waited. Nervously watching them take their time checking one person in while the other customer service agent looks over his shoulder instead of offering to help someone else in line I started to panic that I wasn't going to be able to board. Once it was my turn, thankfully I was able to speak to the gentleman at the counter instead of the same rude lady I had originally spoken to. He kept trying to make the flight work for me while she over his shoulder continue to say things like "well go ahead put her on that plane, they're just going to make her get off at the connecting flight". I was finally let on just before the doors closed. Oh did I mention they have no seating assignments.. chaos! My bag was about 9 isles away along with having to stow away my purse. The flight attendants were pleasant for the most part, but nothing to brag about! I didn't get booted at my connecting flight either, thankfully. On the Houston, TX side everyone was fabulous. Courteous, friendly & helpful from start to finish!! Terrible that people have to further convince us that Detroit is full of rude, unfriendly people!!!
label: NEG

text: I took the opportunity to go Mai Lee's new location in Brentwood. It's tucked away by the Metrolink parking lot. The building is new, and although the space is a bit odd, they did a good job dressing it up... although they do keep a bit bright for my liking. We waited in the bar area for about 10 minutes before being seated. Although we didn't order drinks, the bartender was very interested in knowing if we were repeat customers or if this was our first time. He (and everyone else) seemed very excited to be in their new digs. Once seated, it took a bit of time before the waiter came over. They were very busy. Once he was there he seemed rushed. Either way, he was nice, and offered some suggestions. I wanted to try an eel dish, but they were out of eel. We ended up getting a pork dish and seafood over egg noodles. Pardon my ignorance... I love Vietnamese food, but can't pronounce or remember anything by name. Luckily for me, the waiter was fine with me just naming the items by their number (like Pho Grand). The pork was a little tough, but the seafood over egg noodles were awesome. I've had this dish before an always liked it, and Mai Lee didn't disappoint. The owners/family members of the business were walking around, thanking all the regulars and newcomers to their new location. They must be doing something right by being packed at a brand new location without advertisement. I like Mai Lee, and will definitely be back. The food is good, the location is convenient and new, and the prices are reasonable. In my opinion, it's very similar to Pho Grand... but for some reason, I still like Pho Grand better. However, I bet I visit Mai Lee more often due to it's proximity to my house.

text: (Visited 3/27/2010) Found this place via Yelp while we were wandering around the Garden District...thank you Yelpers! After reading the Yelp reviews and plugging the address into my GPS my girlfriend and I were rewarded with one of best dining experiences of this trip. (They also use OpenTable.com for reservations). I've been going to New Orleans every March for years but have never heard of Coquette. Arriving just after noon, we were able to nab a perfect outdoor table on the side of the building under a tree and umbrella. The weather was perfect. Having hit the local food and beverages hard the two days before, we decided we'd try to go a little light on the calorie intact. After walking for nearly 4 miles, we decided to have a glass each of a Spanish Cava sparkling wine which was perfect for the weather and the mood. Just in passing, we mentioned to our server (who was outstanding - more below) we were going to "split" and order of a roasted oysters appetizer and an order of fish and chips. The oysters were served excellently - hot, juicy with a wild onion topping. Our server took the extra step to have the app ACTUALLY split in half with 3 oysters per plate resting attractively on course rock salt! As an oyster lover (and glutton while in NO), I couldn't stop talking about these oysters all week. Next came the fish and chips, again thoughtfully separated for us on individual plates. The fish was delish. Period. Light and fluffy with a tasty breading. The great little twist on this dish was that it was served over a drizzle of Louisiana Hot Sauce reduced with sugar. A little spicy, a little sweet but very tasty. I could have eaten this meal my entire time there. Back to the service which was definitely top notched. Besides being very impressed with our own waiter, who seemed to know every detail about every menu item, we noticed the staff across the board was invested in their customers. It was refreshing to see such cheerful teamwork. We were enjoying ourselves so much that, while we skipped dessert (calories...); I had to have the sazerac advertised on their menu. I recommend you do as well. They also have a very extensive wine selection which unfortunately, other than the Cava, we didn't get to explore. Our bill came to about $50 which is something of an inside joke to us. For some reason, almost every meal we had in New Orleans came to about $50...this one was the best spent $50 of them all, though. Make this a must stop if you are in the Garden District and let this place nudge you to escape Bourbon for awhile if you are not!
label: POS

text: This review has been "filtered." Yelp isn't posting it in the open because it is an unfavorable review. Don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn! We are posting this here to warn you and we are filing a complaint with the Better Business Bureau as no one should be subjected to what we endured. This is a hotel where the owner and the manager have demonstrated they don't care about their customers. During our second stay at this hotel we were in a room where the toilet wouldn't flush. It wouldn't flush even if the toilet was empty. We had to call the front desk twice to get it fixed, and each time they sent a new maintenance person, and each time we were told the problem was fixed. When it wasn't fixed for the third time, I called the front desk in frustration. After being put on hold for a long time, the front desk person offered us the use of the bathroom in a room about 10 doors down from ours. We couldn't just move into that room because it had only one double bed. We were four people in a suite with a king and a sofabed and no working toilet. No other rooms were available for that night. I couldn't imagine getting up in the middle of the night and walking outside in my pajamas to use the bathroom. We weren't camping here. We were paying lots of money for a hotel room for four nights. So, I explained how I didn't see how the two rooms could work being so far apart and I said in frustration, "How about just comping us a couple of nights and bringing us a plunger." I added that I had to think about what we were going to do here since we had been told that most hotels in the area were sold out. After a few minutes, I called the front desk back and accepted the offer of the second room for the toilet. We were also offered a new suite room to move to the next day, which we gratefully accepted. We thought everything was all resolved. We would have a new room with a working toilet and everything would be fine. .....but it was not to be. We were meeting friends for dinner so we had to leave. When we returned, the same front desk person knocked on our door and told us maintenance had snaked the toilet so it was working now. I wish maintenance had done that after our first call. We thanked him and gave him back the keys to the second room. I was told to talk the front desk the next morning about the situation. The next morning I talked to a new desk clerk about the nonworking toilet and he said he knew about it and the owner had heard and we were told we were required to vacate the premises immediately that morning and we were never going to be allowed to stay there again. I was in shock. We have been staying at hotels on a regular basis, including many Best Western's, with no problems. And during our prior stay at this hotel the front desk person said our file said "really nice people" and how we must have made a great impression. Now, because we were frustrated that we were in a room without a working toilet, we were told we were required to leave. It didn't make sense. We still had two nights on our reservation. This new clerk told us that last night's front desk person relayed to the owner that I had demanded to be compensated for two nights when all I did was ask as a suggestion in frustration. The desk clerk was apologetic and made excuses for the owner telling us he was under stress because of the renovations and also how the main computer system had gone down that night. We asked to talk to both the hotel manager and the hotel owner but we were told neither could be reached and the situation wouldn't change even if they could be reached. There was apparently no way to get this miscommunication undone. He was sympathetic and he did comp us $30 which we appreciated, but there was no way we could connect to the two decision makers, the hotel manager and the hotel owner to get the situation fixed. This is not the way you treat a customer. No one talked to us except the front desk person who was accusing us of demanding something we only asked for in frustration and as a suggestion. Plus, shouldn't a hotel do something more when your toilet doesn't work? The broken toilet wasn't the only problem. The cold water at the faucet only turned off at a precise point that took a while to find. The shower had very low water pressure. And, the next morning, the toilet wouldn't flush again. Plus, we heard another customer complain about how a hotel staff person walked in on them in their room really early in the morning. In the end, the owner did us a favor. We found Pacifica Suites. It is closer to our Goleta destination. The toilets work and work and work!! The rooms are much cleaner. The breakfast is better. The people are nicer. And we are very happy to give them our business - we have many trips we will be making each year to Goleta. Do yourself a favor and don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn.
label: NEG
