text: This is the last time that I will rent with Hertz, and all I can say is improperly disclosed fees. We added an additional driver on to the rental with no information given stating that there would be an additional driver fee that was equal to 30% of the cost of the rental. The clerk that did the rental stated that the paperwork was only to "allow the additional driver." Had he mentioned a fee at that time, there would be no issue. Even now, looking back at the paperwork, the verbiage (if you could call it that) is very unclear and cryptic and it wasn't until I noticed the charge on my card that I questioned what had happened. The manager that I spoke to was difficult to understand due to improper language and generally unhelpful. He stated that he could not make any changes on a rental that had been "closed out" a fact that I hardly believe is accurate. He refused to answer emails, faxes, or phone calls. After conferring with corporate, they refused to make any changes with a response of "Our representatives try to anticipate customer questions; however, they do not cover every detail of the rental transaction due to the time constraint this would place on travelers." I fail to understand how stating "this is to allow an additional driver and to acknowledge an additional fee" would have put a crimp on my time. I believe that an addition of 30% worth of fees to the cost of the rental is something that warrants an extra sentence. This is my third bad experience with Hertz and I will take my business elsewhere. They are one of the most expensive rental agencies on the market and their customer service is far from the "gold standard" that they claim. These fees do not serve to recoup the cost of doing business, that is what the rental fees are for. They have sacrificed customer service to enhance their bottom line and that, coupled with the fact that the company claims no responsibility for the actions of their employees, means that they do not deserve my business.

text: A friend wanted to go to Sisters and I thought it sounded like fun, because I like lesbians and I like to drink. This seemed easy enough. We got there a little early on a Thursday night and it was busy, but not too crowded. We were able to get our drinks fairly quickly, with standard bar prices. We sat down and drank our house liquor. The main area is complete with huge fantasy art a la 1987 (straight from the background of some Heart music video). It would be more painful to look at if it were not so hilarious. People started coming in until the place was packed. Maybe we were both just heinously unnattractive that evening, but apart from a few asides, people seemed entirely consumed with their cliques, if not exuding outright surliness. We kept drinking, hoping that this would lull us from our boredom. But soon, it became so busy that I literally had to stand in line 20-30 minutes for a drink. I think I spent more time waiting for drinks than doing anything else while I was there. Unbeknownst to me, this was not just any evening at Sisters. Jennifer Flashdancin' Beals walked through the door with her entourage to stump for Obama and these people LOST THEIR MINDS. This says nothing about Sisters, only that Philadelphia is in dire need of more celebrity. It became claustrophobically packed around the entrance, so we decided to take the stairs to the dance floor. While not much less crowded (and the bar lines no less long), the space was at least slightly more open. Unfortunately, what could have saved the night did not, because the music was AWFUL. Seriously, I don't know why people make music like that and I further do not understand why a DJ would inflict it on paying customers. How do you even dance to it? After that much watered down vodka, I should have been able to dance to anything. So, we gave up and left. I hear people say there are other options, but I have yet to find them, so for staying on the radar with all those faults, I'll give it two stars. I'll try to give it the benefit of the doubt. But I don't think I'll ever go back.
label: NEG

text: I like the experience that is Nectar more than the food. The interior is two stories of chic, from the sushi bar, to the private booths, to the crazy hanging light bulbs, the upstairs rooms, even down to the bathrooms. Upbeat lounge music is pumped through the sound system. It's impressive, day or night. Service (Alan and Yun) has always been top-notch. We had a bug (not tasty) in our dim sum appetizer (tasty) and it was replaced for free. We also got a dessert on the house, too! Food is hit-or-miss. For lunch, I had the Nectar lo mein ($8) with smoked wild boar, Chinese sausage, and baby greens. Requested it spicy, and it came out tasty. For dinner, I shared the: - seafood bento box (24) - pretty good - wok chile beef (23) - disappointingly mellow, quite un-spicy - soy wrap roll - okay - King Kong roll - good! with mint leaves - ice cream (8) - good (FYI, all their desserts are made in house) Nectar is generally pricey. You're paying for their (no doubt expensive) rent, Asian fusion cuisine (which typically IS overpriced) and for a city-like ambiance in the suburbs. Should you try this flashy venue, appropriate for a date or business clients? Sure, and if you go for dinner, bring extra cash, as there's free valet parking in the evening. Recommended for a try. Reservations recommended for lunch and especially dinner.

text: I can't begin to say enough good things about this restaurant. After sampling their tasty food at the annual International Festival in Tower Grove Park, I decided to pay the restaurant a visit for the whole experience. When you walk in the door, you're immediately met with a wonderful hospitality and graciousness that makes you feel you've stepped into someone's home as a valued guest. It is a large, attractive restaurant perfect for banquets and gatherings, as well as a quiet dinner for two. Bosnian music plays discreetly in the background, and in the winter a huge fireplace crackles and warms the body and spirit. There are white tablecloths and the decor makes you feel you're in the owner's home village. The place is run by family, and it's obvious they take great pride in all that they do. The food is indescribably delicious and the service is amazing!. On 5 different visits, every dish I've had was wonderfully prepared, presented, and tasty. I especially enjoyed the mixed grill, beef goulash (with unbeleivably light spaetzle) , sarma (cabbage rolls), and German chicken kebabs. The homemade soups are to die for. The Grbic salad is a great alternative to the ubiquitous same old Italian salad one finds all over St. Louis. Plenty of fresh bread and your glass is never empty. Last night, the Grbics fulfilled a special request and stayed open past their normal hours for our small post-symphony party. Every detail was perfect and made for an unbelievably magical evening for us! Every member of our party remarked on how lovely the restaurant was and how wonderful the food tasted. The pastries at the end of the meal melted in our mouths, especially the palacinke - Bosnian chocolate filled crepes. I will never forget the Grbic's authentic kindness, generosity, and graciousness - this place is a hidden gem in St. Louis. I VERY highly recommend it.
label: POS

text: Unlike any museum you've seen. Don't visit right after eating; specimens with smallpox might make you lose your lunch. But there's some fabulous medical history within these walls. The conjoined twins cases seem more like a sideshow than a medical exhibit. Maybe an intern could help update it; after all it's mostly news clippings. There is now a cell phone tour, so be sure to bring your phone with you. You'll be glad you did. They also have special events. Get on their mailing list and be in the know. They're worth attending. We ordered a poutine to share ($8.00) which went down in a hurry as we were all starved and who doesn't inhale this fine Canadian decadency When my Fat Franks hot dog (6.95) complete with Cheddar cheese and bacon ($1.25 add on each) and ceaser salad ($2.00) my hot dog became a bit of an investment. text: A friend just told me about this great new Asian Fusion restaurant in Old City. Usually I steer clear of newly opened restaurants until they've gotten decent word out on the street but some friends talked me into trying this place tonight. I anticipated the obvious problems that comes with any restaurant at first and I'm happy to say the food was excellent. They were really friendly and service was perfect. The atmosphere was very sharp and an interesting mix of east/west but mostly stylish west. They explained the menu is still being fine tuned and the printed one handed out is still an interim version. However, the kitchen has no problems as far as I could taste, that's for sure. As a group we often order a variety of dishes and share so we can try as much as possible. It was fun to do that here since the prices were really competitive - not just with the old city area but with sushi/fusion restaurants in general. I personally do not eat raw fish, so my friends that do went to town with the sushi while I gorged myself on everything else. First we had the Yellowtail Spring Rolls with basil sauce. They were light and flavorful. The sauce was a perfect zing to balance the jalapeño in it too. The fried calamari was served with salt and pepper in it's batter which was good. It was light and tender. We order this mostly as a gage for any starter menu. I suspect this will please any calamari fan. Along with some impressive looking sushi rolls, we ordered some the Avocado Cucumber roll as well as the sweet potato roll. They were both really fresh and tasty. I liked how the sweet potatoes were still kind of firm and only lightly tempura battered. Of the Wok Dishes menu, I tasted the Pad Thai Chicken order which was really good. I usually don't order this because it's quite bland, as I suspect is the reason most other people order it, but this was spicy and I want to come back and get this with shrimp next time. :) Since most of the table was eating the raw stuff (and moaning still) I reasoned it wasn't so selfish to eat most of the Crispy Beef dish. OH BOY. This dish has tender strips of beef that have been coated, maybe tempura'd, and then cooked in some sort of sauce that was a perfect balance of salt/tangy and spicy and on top of some sesame noodles with a few nice fresh crunchy endives. The server brought out rice that came with this but I'm pretty sure that wasn't needed. It seemed a bit redundant to have noodles under the beef and then add rice next to it. I suspect that would be OK to tweak out of the menu probably. We had some shared desserts. The hot chocolate lava cake was not one that I voted for. To me it's the most passe option a restaurant can offer. The red bean mochi dish was sublime. I loved this light and almost healthy but tasty ice cream offering. Why don't more restaurants have such smart choices as mochi?! Presentation for every dish was top notch. I'm an artist and definitely into food porn and still I was impressed with every presentation. Over all it was incredibly tasty and affordable. While I'm not too impressed with their generic name, I have a feeling I'm going to be back here often. Oh, did I mention the down stairs lounge? (OK, I got halfway through typing that line and remember I had not actually mentioned it, but really are you gonna bust on me for that? huh?) it wasn't open yet but damn, it's really nice and I hope to hang out there once they get their bar going. I noticed they have a sound system, maybe a bar for down there too (?).
label: POS

text: I have not eaten the dim sum but ate here for dinner. Although I had not eaten the dim sum at this restaurant, I heard about this place through a friend, saying that it's a decent place to get dim sum. Anyway, here is what we got for dinner: Gau Wong Chao Ban Kau - "Gau Wong" is a Cantonese term for yellow chives, while "Chao" is a term for stir fried. "Ban Kau" is one term to describe a sautéed fish. This is the Sautéed Fillet Grouper With Yellow Chives. $15.95. Hong Wan Zha Ji Gai - This is the Cantonese styled Crispy Fried Chicken. $9.00. Tong Yun Gai Lan Ngau Youk - This is the Sliced Beef with Chinese Vegetables. Approximately $10. Cheui Pei Zha Yeum Dau Fu - This is a fried tofu dish with broccoli doused in a brownish sauce. I think this is the Fried Crispy Stuffed Bean Curd. Approximately $10. Ju Yim Sin Yau - This is the Fried Crispy Squid with chili and spicy salt. Approximately $10. Some bowls of white rice. The Ju Yim Sin Yau was decent, the calamari had the right amount of crisp, doused with the right amount of salt, but I thought it kind of lacked some spice to it. Overall it was decently tasty. The Cantonese crispy chicken was also decent, most of the meat was kind of bony, but the chicken meat was decently tasty and the skin had some crisp to it but not much. The scallions made it tastier. The Beef with Chinese vegetables was pretty good despite the sauciness of the dish and it was served on a giant plate. They were really generous with the portions, one dish should be enough to feed 3-4 people. The beef strips were tasty and flavorful. The vegetables were freshly cooked just right and the Chinese broccoli had the right crisp to it. The fried tofu was also decently good, it was really crispy on the outside and very soft on the inside. Each piece was also reasonably sized. The brownish sauce made the tofu and the broccoli tastier. As for the Sautéed Fillet with Yellow Chives, it was probably the tastiest dish I had. The texture was really soft, and the chives brought more flavor to the fish, making it tastier. The restaurant was really quiet when we came, making the atmosphere relaxing despite the sounds from the plasma HDTVs. Overall, I had a solid and tasty dinner at this restaurant, and it has also changed my perceptions of Chinese food in Philadelphia somewhat. I would definitely come back for the Beef and Chinese Vegetables, and for the Sauteed Fillet Grouper with Yellow Chives.

We booked a package with a limo to get the girls to the church, big ole party bus for pictures and getting to the reception for the entire wedding party, and a towncar for get away or honeymoon airport transport (we used it for the latter). We had no problems at all. The vehicles were clean and functioning properly (including the air). The drivers were prompt, professional, and courteous. We'd use them again in a heart beat. The office staff were, for the most part, easy to work with. We did have a couple moments when I called trying to clear things up, ask questions, etc. and the guy we worked with was out. THEY MAKE THE BEST STEAK SANDWICHES I have ever had and I have been having them since 1968! Nothing comes close when you have their chicken steak or beef steak sandwiches on the crusty Italian NYC steak rolls. They taste great, are moist and flavorful and the warmed crusty bread completes the deal. Pat's and Gino's in Philly are for the tourists. This is the place for a serious steak sandwich. Even their cold hoagies are better than Lee's and on par with some of Primo's. There is always a small crowd there for lunch. Stay away from the chicken cutlet parmessan ones since the patties are made in advance and sit in the cold display case. By the time they get back to temp, they are dried out. Take-out lasagna and many deli dishes are good as are their soups typically. They make good cannolis to order for parties but some of the deserts are hit or miss. In conclusion, the place for a steak sandwich when you crave a great steak sandwich like you remember from your childhood memories.

Waiter: Yes, just plain bottle water and sparkling water. Me: You don't have ice tea or soda? Waiter: Yea, we have ice tea and soda. Dude, how long have you waitering? We settled for ice tea, and it was bitter strong, could use a some ice in the glass, but who am I to complain. The bus boy was a lot more friendly and helpful, he brought over a pitcher of water, a basket of bread and some peppered olive oil and vinegar. I was very disappointed, there're way too many places that will give you better service for less, food was okay, could be just a off night in the kitchen, looking at the other reviews, I wish I could give them another star, but I couldn't bring myself to it. text: Good for four hours a day. No, I'm not referring to Lindsay Lohan's daily time of sobriety. In case you good people don't get out during that magical time between the end of work and the beginning of dinner, there is this thing called happy hour. To connect this bit of ubiquitous restaurant/bar marketing ploy to this review, I say this: Old Pueblo Grill is really only a decent place to visit during happy hour. In full disclosure, I have been to this place one time, and it was during.... you guessed it: happy hour. Now, quite a number of places in the Old Pueblo offer half-off appetizers during happy hour, and Old Pueblo Grill is no different. On this occasion, I sampled the Firecracker Shrimp, decent-sized shrimp, crusted and served in a spicy chili sauce. As much as I am loath to eat seafood in the middle of the desert, the quality wasn't all that bad. The sauce had a nice spicy kick with a slight tanginess to it. And for half-off, it wasn't a bad value. Would yours truly pay a full $10 for the same appetizer in the near future? Maybe. Maybe not. Nothing else on the starter's menu really struck my fancy. So I've established that the apps, or one app to be precise, is doable. How about the drinks you ask, since we are talking happy hour? Three words: one dollar off. Not enough to tear it up, in my alcohol-soaked mind. But in all fairness to Mr. McMahon, he of the McMahon chain of restaurants that Old Pueblo Grill is part of, the drinks aren't in the over-the-top price range. If I recall, the beers on tap are $5 normally. I wish I could say the same for the rest of the menu. Okay, maybe I shouldn't characterize the dinner menu prices as over-the-top. At or near the top is more like it. But the place is a fairly fancified, up-scale kind of joint. (Think McMahon chain.) One where you wouldn't really expect to encounter groups of teachers from two different schools. I know that because once our bartender overheard our conversation, and immediately figured out that we were complaining about students, she freely told us that the group a few feet away out in the patio were teachers also. The bartender was one of the most cool, personable, and friendly ones I've had in a long while. But as the place the filled up, she and the one other server in the bar area seemed quite overwhelmed handling the mostly AARP crowd. Who knew that pouring 7 and 7s required that much time? Despite the fairly overall negative impression I came away with on my initial visit, I'd be more than willing to give Old Pueblo Grill another shot. They do offer an impressive list of tequila. In fact, the menu promotes a tequila cellar with numerous types of different tequila in stock. And they have margaritas the size of Thirstbusters. Well, they're 42 ounces suckers according the menu. I'll just need to make sure that I come on a pay day. Or have an arm and leg to offer.

We ordered two drinks at $11 each, and they were very good drinks, though not $11 drinks. We shared a Caesar salad, which was bland and otherwise completely unremarkable. The chips and salsa were excellent. For an expensive Mexican restaurant, though, good chips and salsa are the cost of admission. For my entree, I got the seafood enchiladas (Enchiladas Playa) for $24. They tasted fishy, and not in the way that they're supposed to be fishy. And aside from that, they were just bland. My boyfriend got the pork (Cochinita Pibil) for $21, and that was the only bright spot of the meal. The worst part was the service. It was terrible. At 9 on a Wednesday night during a recession, you're not going to find a lot of people paying $24 for enchiladas, and hence the restaurant was relatively slow. I expected our server to at least pay some attention to us. But instead all the servers were gathered around the bar talking and watching TV. We waited 10 minutes for our drinks, and 20 minutes to get the check, which we had to ask for. I may go back for a drink at the bar, but I'll never spend $60 on crappy food there again.

text: WARNING: You can not get to terminal F by walking. If you do not have much time to connect between flights from one of the regular terminals you could easily miss your flight from terminal F. You must take the shuttle from gate C 16 to get to terminal F. [I hear there is one from terminal A1 but have never taken this.] Although the shuttle goes directly there it is by no means a short trip (for an intra-airport shuttle). I am not sure how long it is between shuttles either but it could be more like twenty minutes. (It is definitely not every 5 minutes more like every 15 or 20). Once you get the hang of connecting through here it really isn't all that bad, but to a novice newbie this place could be bafflingly overwhelming so be sure to familiarize yourself with it's many idiosyncrasies before you attempt a connection through Phili. Also be sure to keep abreast of that winter weather that can cause delays here... (not as bad as the winter delays that Denver can have though!!!) ****DO NOT FOLLOW THE SIGNS THAT SEEM TO INDICATE THAT YOU CAN WALK TO TERMINAL F!!! They will take you all the way to terminal E where you realize there is no connection to terminal F from terminal E unless you went outside security and walked or bused it and then went back through security( and I am not even sure if it is possible to walk or bus there from terminal E at all even if you do exit the building to the unsecure area since I never dared to try it). If you do this you will spend like twenty-five extra minutes walking to terminal E and then back to C 16 to catch the shuttle you should have taken in the first place!!! Besides the sheer hugeness, and the sometimes awful weather delays, and the terminal F thing I don't find Phili to be that bad. The reason why I am not giving it a one is because they have really nice Usair clubs here. Like the cathedral of all Usair clubs is located at the connecting area between terminals B and C. It is huge and has super high ceilings. Very nice if you have a long lay over and have access to the club. There seem to be a lot of restaurants too. Terminal F is another story though. It is kind of like the terminal that time forgot..... However, if you do have access to Usair clubs there is club up stairs right from where the shuttle drops you off so it is centrally located in the terminal. Read the signs carefully when you arrive at terminal F in order to figure out which direction your gate is. The arms that extend out from the middle section are pretty long. If you are in a hurry and make a mistake you could miss your flight when you come to a dead end and realize your next consecutively numbered gate is actually at the very end of a different section that is in the completely opposite direction!

text: I really want to like this place, because its got everything you could ask for from a neighborhood Italian joint, with the exception of good food. There's a warm, kitschy dining room with comfy looking booths, a cute little bar area, and its unassuming presence along dreary Chester Pike makes you feel as if you're walking into some old Italian grandmother's basement. Even the beer specials (all pints $2.50 on Thursdays) are quite decent. However, the food is just so-so - and barely that - and I can think of a half-dozen local Italian places that offer much higher quality at just as much, or less of the cost. I enjoyed the half-loaf of crusty bread, served with nicely seasoned dipping oil. The salad was decent enough, although some tomatoes would have been nice, and the one tiny slice of pepperoni on top was just a tease. But our entrees were both huge disappointments. I don't expect much from Chicken Parmigiana, but I hoped for something more than a single thin, over-breaded and -cooked piece of chicken under an overload of sauce (excuse me, gravy). Same deal with the stuffed eggplant - sliced paper-thin with just enough heft to contain the ricotta stuffed inside. Worst of all was my vegetable: obviously frozen spinach, which isn't really acceptable at a bad diner, let alone a place that seems to pride itself on "genuine" Italian food. Much better local options include Italian Village, Sam's and DeMarco's - all offering better food and value to satisfy your neighborhood Italian fix.
label: NEG

text: Only reason I'm not giving five stars is so this restaurant has room to go if I visit it in a more normal setting. I was at Toscana for a dinner talk sponsored by Pfizer. It was about veterinary pain management and anesthesia. Good talk, good meal. As it was sponsored, and there were a lot of people, we didn't get full menus to order from. There was a set group of appetizers (which didn't get to my table, as I was sitting w/ the Pfizer rep and the speaker, and I was very sad when I realized it). There was this amazing giant bread... I can't even describe it. Large, but thin, and hollow, with some kind of greasy glaze. Very good. There were mussels - very good. There was also excellent bruschetta. Then we had choices - dressing for the 'salad', which was a hunk of lettuce garnished in tomatoes and egg, I believe - I didn't get a chance to try it, as I was frantically taking notes. There were three pasta dishes - I tried the gnocchi, which I almost never do, because I was in the mood for an alfredo sauce. They were wonderful, but extremely small - only 4 gnocchi for the plate. I guess it doesn't matter much when you're getting a 10 course meal! Then there was a little orange sherbet - to cleanse the pallet, I suppose. Then we waited a little longer than i think we should have for the main course. I got the chicken parm, which came with some spaghetti and marinara sauce. It was good, but didn't knock my socks off or anything. Might have just been full at that point. Finally, they brought dessert, and each person got some vanilla ice cream, some coffee flavored thing, and what appeared to be a moose cream puff. Again, very well done. Service was extremely attentive - filling drink glasses without being asked, etc. They could be a little curt, but I think it was the stress of dealing with so many people. We got a little room in the back to ourselves - maybe 20 or 30 people. I have no idea the cost as the bill was paid for by Pfizer. So, there you go. Apparently, a good place to have business meetings or talks. Excellent food and fun if you want to do all the courses. If you get a choice, I certainly recommend the mussels. And make sure you try that bread. Maybe I'm tired. No fun anecdotes specifically related to the restaurant. Sad. Good talk, good food, good price (for me, anyway). Sign outside says 'Pizzeria and Grill' and 'Wood Fired Oven'. That always sounds appealing, doesn't it? Edited to correct spelling of 'Pfizer'. Thanks, Jeanne F!
label: POS

text: Nico's doesn't sell Mexican Food. They sell hot, carby, flavorful happiness - wrapped in yellow paper. Nico's is up there near the top of the list of things we miss the most since moving away. I believe there are 3 benchmarks by which you can judge a Mexican food stand or taqueria: =-=-=-=-= Salsa =-=-=-=-= Nico's salsa is the dark red or green liquid kind; more of a hot sauce really. Don't let its lack of real consistency get you down, though. The flavor is great, but where Nico's red sauce reigns supreme is in heat. Theirs is hands down the spiciest of the Tucson Triumvirate (Nico's/Viva/Los Betos). I once saw some marines dining in after the bars, challenging each other to chugging shots of this potent elixir. One soldier slammed like 13 little containers and he never tasted again. That's called winning the battle and losing the war. In moderation, this stuff is killer. =-=-=-=-= Horchata =-=-=-=-= I think you see Horchata prepped / served one of three ways: out of the splashy Aguas Frescas dispenser thingy, punch bowl and ladle style, or *gasp* from some kind of concentrate out of a regular soda fountain (yuck). Nico's horchata is the first kind, which in my opinion is the best. The flavor is spot on with a nice blend of cinnamon and spice while never tasting chalky. Make sure you shake it up real good with the ice so it is extra cold, as this is how it tastes best. =-=-=-=-= Breakfast Burrito =-=-=-=-= Plenty of places will make you a burrito for breakfast. Heck, some may even throw some chorizo or eggs in it as well. Let me tell you what friend: Nico's is THE gold standard of breakfast burritos in our household. Never before have bacon, potatoes, eggs, cheese, tortillas, and salsa come together in a more perfect union. The size is usually about that of a small mortar shell, which is appropriate considering your mouth is about to get exploded with flavor. Sometimes you'll get shortchanged and get a skinny burrito - once in a while - but the vast majority of the time these things are plenty big. Some other places you ask for bacon and you really get ham cooked to a crisp - not the same. This is honest to goodness thick cut bacon. But the eggs - the eggs are one of the greatest differentiators: somehow Nico's has figured out how to keep the eggs fluffy and dry. This creates a welcome environment for incoming hot sauce, instantly melding into the consistency breakfast burritos are meant to be. This is as opposed to a pre saturated boggy marshland of runny eggs and cheese that might as well tell hot sauce to kiss off. These burritos also ELIMINATE HANGOVERS. Eat one post bars - even eat a half - and the Nico's elves start to go to work in your belly. The potatoes go to work first, soaking up any remaining alcohol in the mix. Cheese and bacon jump in, using their tasty grease power to line your stomach, further slowing the absorption of now unfriendly alcohol. The eggs and bacon release their protein, helping your brain repair itself, and the capsaicin from the hot hot sauce triggers endorphin production to help ease the oncoming headache. Go here. Health code blah blah whatever. These guys aren't surgeons, they make burritos. And guess what: they're the best at what they do.

The decor was not bad, I'd say above average, the blue fountain was a little tacky but hey, it's Florida! As far as the food goes, we had several different carne dishes, and they were all good. A refreshing change of pace from normal italian food, or mexican food. Unique. I had no complaints as to the taste, but the portions were not good. I wasn't expecting family style, but for what you pay for the dishes, I would expect more than what we got. You're probably thinking now, "why the 2 star review?". It's simple. The service was horrible. I've had better service at Dennys. Really. Our server acted like we were some sort of inconvenience. I ordered a Corona, and I got a Corona light. "oh we are out of Corona". I don't know why he didn't just tell me that. It took me three tries to even get him to tell me what other beers they had. To put it bluntly, I was pissed off at our server by the time we were done, and so were the other people I was with. So yeah, you could go here, and impress your date with a unique place, but I hope you have a better experience than we did. I will not be coming here again.

text: I have been going to Nashville zoo for years and it just keeps getting better! I only give it 4 stars because I really want more monkeys, namely orangutans, and maybe some otters or beavers. I like kangaroos, that would be cool too. Ahh, I digress. Oh, and a hippo, we definitely need a hippo. Let me say what they do have. Lot's of shade, beautiful habitats and a variety of interesting animals like meerkats and one big old anaconda. I love to bring the kids here as the zoo is designed for you to do a lovely walk in a loop. There is a reptile and fish house that turns in to a big game of I Spy. There is a bird house that you can feed a varieties of birds. We like to lay odds on who will get pooped on. There is a cool carousel as well as working farm house to tour as well. We buy the family membership ( the price is so reasonable) and go several times a year. The kids always love to go. You can bring your own food and drinks. There is lots of places for picnics. There is also jungle gym area for the kids if you feel the animal viewing didn't' wear them out enough.. The jungle gym is a work of art with cargo nets, padded jumping room, draw bridges and unbelievably long swirly slides. I love this place!!

text: This place sucks. When I pulled into the parking lot, they were at five starts -- innocent until proven guilty. When I saw the menu, they were at four stars. The selection was OK and the prices were a bit high for a diner. But, nevertheless, I was eager to try the food. The food was excellent. I felt like I definitely got my money's worth. After the meal, Oregon stayed at four stars. When the bill came, they dropped down to three stars. My friend had ordered a parm sandwich and nothing else. French fries had come with the meal, and he ate them because he assumed that fries were part of the deal when you order a sandwich. However, there was a separate charge for fries on our bill. My friend explained the situation to our waitress and that's when this racket plummeted to one star. She responded by informing him that the fries do not come with the sandwich and that he'd have to pay for them. She went on to say that he ate them and if he didn't want them he shouldn't have eaten them. He explained that he thought they simply came with the sandwich and that, in fact, their inclusion was THEIR mistake and he shouldn't have to pay for it. Here's where it gets crazy. The waitress explained that this is standard -- that "regular" customers know that Oregon will bring out the fries (WHICH ARE CHARGED EXTRA) and the customers will Oregon that they DON'T want the the (assumed) inclusion of fries while ordering. According to the waitress, my friend should have asked NOT to have the fries at additional charge. Are you all following this twisted logic? Let me break it down: Oregon ASSUMES that its customers want to receive an extra item that they haven't ordered and will only abstain from including it in your meal if you request that it NOT be included. Sorry Oregon, that's not how 99.9% of all restaurants in the world operate. They don't do that because, um......it's sort of ILLEGAL. Don't patronize these criminals.

text: How could I forget to review this museum? I went here over Thanksgiving break & on a rainy, boring Sunday afternoon I popped into the Dali museum. What a treat! Since I still have my student id & look about 12 years old, I got in for $10.00-score! I wandered around the museum with my brother & mom trying to be sophisticated, artsy and deep. Unfortunately, we're a bunch of immature clowns & couldn't help but talk about the random genitalia or body parts that frequented many of his paintings. It actually made the trip a bit more enjoyable & put me in a much better mood since the sun was not shining on my last day in warm, beautiful St. Petersburg. The museum is fantastic, new, and chalk-full of Dali paintings. Pieces that I've seen in books or posters, but also pieces that I've never seen before. I love that! The gift shop is awesome as well. I bought two prints of my favie Dali paintings to hang in the condo & postcards for friends. I could have bought the whole store, which ranged from Dali movies to Dali calendars. From Dali inspired jewelery to Dali inspired martini glasses. If you're ever in the St. Pete's area, I would definitely check this place out. It seems to be pretty unknown, so it's never busy & you can take your time enjoying all the beheaded women, melting clocks, and random penises.

They have magazines you can read if you feel like hanging out and as far as I could tell they were relatively current magazines (you know how I feel about old magazines and if you don't know now you know - I hate them A LOT). The people working there are doing their own thing, but friendly and ready to whip you up something delicious, which I like. If I wanted to sit there for half an hour while I enjoyed my smoothie, I don't think they would have cared or given me the side eye. I browsed their long list of smoothies, most (all?) containing their homemade soymilk. I picked the Shrek smoothie - honeydew, kiwi, tofu, soymilk & honey. So good! It tasted fresh and was very satisfying. I also fet good about the added benefits of drinking a serving protein. The price here for a smoothie is right, also. They have a pretty wide variety of food, including many vegetarian options, sandwiches, wraps, and some interesting items not usually found at your regular cafe. I'm looking forward to trying some of these things in the future. I'll probably make this a pitstop on my weekend errand runs around town. Five!

text: I love Mexican food. I have made it a personal mission to travel all over this beautiful planet to try Mexican food and to seek out the best, and La Super-Rica is among the best. Why is it that, in this world of copy-cats, no one has bothered to copy La Super-Rica? Normally, I would discourage this practice, but these people are doing something so simple, yet so special, it begs to be shared with the world. They use fresh, high quality, delicious ingredients, and more veggies (and more unique veggies) than most taquerias. On my last visit, I had to wait about 40 minutes just to place my order, but the food was worth it. Come prepared to wait, perhaps with a good book. Parking will be tricky. I ordered a quesadilla with grilled pasilla peppers and a queso fundido with chorizo. My daughter had what she said was the best chicken quesadilla of her life. To simply call it a chicken quesadilla is sort of an insult, because that's what they make at Chevy's or El Torito, and this was something so much better. La Super-Rica is closed on Tuesdays, so plan accordingly! You don't want to get your heart broken.

text: At the urging of my sister, I am lowering my rating for this particular PJ's location. The two of us, along with our step-dad, decided to hit the Maple Shade PJ's for game 1 of the Flyers/Penguins playoff race. We were seated at a prime table with no less than 6 televisions within ten feet. The evening looked promising. I ordered a Bass and was told that they were out, a typical response when ordering beer at this location. I settled for Smithwick's. We started off with chicken nachos, which arrived at our table curiously smothered in long strips of lettuce. Was it to hide the very minimal amount of toppings underneath? Was it to hide the strange, almost undercooked consistency of the chicken? I didn't know but I didn't like it. And neither did Kate, who at that point, started voicing her displeasure over the restaurant's recent descent. My step-dad and I had "wicked chicken" sandwiches for dinner. These sandwiches used to come with nice, big chunks of grilled chicken with buffalo sauce on a long roll. Now, they use some type of shredded chicken that is reminiscent of a chicken steak, only not fried. The sandwiches were okay but not "wicked" great. Meanwhile, Kate was angsty over her Cajun chicken wrap, which was falling apart all over the place. It was decided that dessert could save the meal so we ordered peanut butter cup pie and a hot fudge brownie a la mode to share. The pie hit the spot but the brownie was a failure. Normally, this dessert is our favorite on the menu, but the brownie had a light, cake-like consistency, and Kate claimed the ice cream tasted freezer burnt (I have a cold so my taste buds cannot be trusted). For the most part, I love my PJ's, but the Maple Shade location is definitely a buzzkill. In addition to the food quality going down, the environment is devoid of any energy or excitement. Iron Hill Brewery is set to open shop around the corner on Kings Highway in the very near future. Things are going to get really interesting if improvements aren't made soon.
label: NEG

text: I finally got to visit this spot. It's tucked away on the 3400 block of Sansom, which is a charming little block with great house facades that have been turned into businesses. I had never even been down this street and it's a nice stroll through the generally otherwise annoying University City area. White Dog has a neat atmosphere; it's a maze of different rooms set up as small dining rooms. The decorations are laid on pretty thick, and it's a great conversion of a house to restaurant without losing any of the charm. The service was swift and pleasant throughout the meal. I met here with my friend Quinn on a beautiful Saturday morning. Surprisingly, White Dog wasn't even close to full at 11am on a weekend. I've heard complaints about the prices here, but I found it in line with other brunch places. The exception is the drink menu. Bloody Marys and mimosas for $9 are just far too high. I stuck with coffee for the morning, and was happy with the fresh brew they kept pouring. Looking over the menu, there were several good options, but I landed with the steak and eggs. The dish had a good presentation, and overall I was satisfied with my choice. My only complaint was that the texture of the steak, in fact I question whether it truly was steak. It seems like a roast that was cut into strips before being topped with the other ingredients. Nonetheless, the dish was tasty and satisfying. Quinn ordered an omelet that came with mushrooms, onions, spinach, and smoked cheddar. She loved her option for brunch and the sample I had was good. She also opted for a side of extra crispy bacon, and it was cooked perfectly to her specification (although not to my taste). Bottom Line: There's not enough going on here to make me want to make the trip regularly, but I do believe that White Dog Cafe is serving up the best brunch in West Philly. I enjoyed my brunch.

text: Finally tried out this little Ethiopian joint near my house. We went with two couples and two small kids on a weekday evening around 6pm. We were the only folks there (both in the back restaurant and the front cool-looking bar). Our waitress was a lovely Ethiopian woman - very friendly and sweet. We had to work a little to make sure she understood our order, but it worked out fine. We ordered way too much food for the six of us and so took it home. The one drawback of the evening was that it took a very long time (near an hour, I think) for our food to come, suggesting that she was whipping it all up from scratch in the back. Delicious food! Cheap beer! Quiet setting! We'll be back...

text: Pizza perfection. The St. Louis thick crust champion. If you made a homemade double crust, triple cheese pizza with a very garlicky tomato sauce this would be it. Be prepared to wait about an hour, call in advance if you can. This time is so that people who don't like thick pizzas or go out for some reason other than awesome food, can give up and run out to their car crying in despair. For everyone else they will notice that it's a relaxed dive bar with some good beer on tap, and they can have a few and some conversation while they wait. If you weren't already hungry you will be after your wait and beer appetizers. They are actually taking care of you because this pizza even the deep dish cheese only is very filling, most people will be stuffed at four slices, and you will feel your blood pressure rise. Many girls will barely manage to finish their second slice. If you want an all scratch made pizza taste bomb come here. That the Blackthorn's pizza exists is St. Louis' secret apology for the national shame that is provel and premade cracker-crusts full of margarine and preservatives.
label: POS

text: Let's just put it out there: Girls do not EVER fare as well as guys do at Buffalo Exchange. Maybe it's just easier to dress a guy? Maybe the guys that shop there are more focused on "Is it cool looking?" rather than "Is this stitching up to par?" I have no idea. In the five+ years I've lived here I've purchased a pair of shoes here, maybe a dress there, but nothing I ever really fell in love with. Ladies, Buffalo Exchange is not a treasure trove of vintage finds or a place to score sweet deals on last season's dress. The selection is so consistently disappointing that I'll walk out without browsing if the store is even remotely busy. However, Buffalo Exchange IS a second-hand store so the poor selection could be blamed on Philadelphians not wanting to part with the good stuff. But anyone who's ever been through the sartorial crucifixion of trying to sell their clothing to Buffalo Exchange would place that blame squarely on the shoulders of the store's employees. This is not the kind of place to make a trip across town for. But if you find yourself in the neighborhood you might consider stopping in. Or you could just go across the street and play in Sephora. The choice is yours.
label: NEG

text: Rangoon makes me happy. It is one of the few restaurants where I have never gotten a bad meal or even a mediocre one. I don't think they have off nights in their kitchen. The food is delicious and the staff is lovely. They will accommodate special requests and adjust spice levels to your taste. The spring ginger salad is the bomb! This is my favorite comfort food and I am always sated. I highly recommend the thousand layer bread with vantana bean and the coconut tofu is delicious. I have introduced a lot of people to Rangoon and no one has even been disappointed. Give it a try.

text: Regarding the star rating, it's tough because there were two things that were terribly wrong with our meals at our visit to Bardenay, but everything else was just fine. Maybe not "fine." The service was lacking. We had a seat on the nice patio during the end of the lunch hour, and everything moved particularly slowly. The patio was almost full, but the inside was nearly empty, so there wasn't much of an excuse there. And the niceties of the patio and this restaurant's immaculate interior are really its saving grace. Being on Grove Street in the Basque Block with a nice building though, I don't think, warrants a positive review in itself. The food is really what makes an experience excel over a location, regardless of the latter being a plus or not. The two things that went wrong with this meal were food-related. First, I got a chorizo sandwich with fries. The chorizo was not as good as what I had eaten at Bar Gernika the night before, but was certainly still pretty good and the bread was really nice. The fries, however, were off. When I asked, the server freely admitted that they were the frozen/Sysco variety. WTF? This is Idaho! Does any respectable restaurant really need to subject their customers to frozen french fries? And not only frozen fries, Sysco fries. I mean, I'm not looking for the Bittercreek Ale House standard of excellent housemade fries, I'm just looking for something that I can't buy in a big bag at the supermarket for $2. And the only reason I know what these fries are is because, for years in college, I ate them at Burger King until I got disgusted with them and can't eat them anymore. No, seriously, these are the same fries as you find at Burger King. There's just no reason for that. Okay, so maybe I shouldn't automatically expect fresh fries at an Idaho restaurant. I mean, it's the Gem State and not the Fresh-Cut Potato State. But the other bad part of the meal was inexcusable. My companion got an "ahi" tuna salad. Quote marks are necessary there because it was nothing like the ahi tuna you may be used to. This was, essentially, the tuna that comes out of the bag. It tasted and looked no different. This is, admittedly, one step above the Bumblebee variety, coated with brine, mayonnaise and a "lord knows" variety of chemicals, but it still sucked and rendered the salad virtually inedible because of the tuna's outright stench. So we left with finishing only about 1/2 of our meals. I would not return here, nor would I recommend it to anyone else. If you want Basque, go to Bar Gernika or the Basque Market next door.
label: NEG

text: I want to give this 5 stars, but I know dining is about the whole experience, not just the food, so I'll settle for a more accurate 4 stars. First off, you have to overcome the fact that this restaurant is located in an uninspiring strip mall, next to a dry cleaners and Jamaican restaurant, and you would probably never walk into this restaurant based upon appearance alone. Once you've gotten over that hurdle, it's smooth sailing to delicious food and good service. We had the lamb samosas, lamb vindaloo, and chicken tikka masala. They were all excellent and they catered to our taste for hotness level (spicy, but not to such an extent as to mask the wonderful flavors of the dish). The menu has a wide variety of dishes and I'll be sure to try the less traditional items next time I go back. Overall, the food makes the entire experience a resounding success. I do wish the restaurant was in a better location/building and had a liquor license because I know this could be an amazing restaurant given the right tweaks, but maybe that would destroy the amazing food...
label: POS

You dont feel like you are 100 miles away from the performer but more like you are part of the show. I have met some cool celebs there as well. I would have to say Lee Ann Womack was the coolest. Oh god..am I name dropping now? She was cool and had the same opinion of the place. If you are a local..I am sure you know how much fun the place can be. Afterwards, stop by cafe cocoa for a bite to eat. Much fun!

text: Family owned and borderline ornate in spots, the Hotel Monteleone proved a welcome respite from the gushing skies of New Orleans this week. Sure, you're right there on the edge of the quarter, but if what you're really after is a few comfortable winks and one of the more unusual hotel bars going, this place has both in spades. Be careful where you set things down in the bar: it rotates ("a helluva trick to play on a man," the recent Esquire article said that name-checked this watering hole as one of the US' great bars). All in all though, my room was comfy, the amenities cool (if not expansive), and the staff was largely friendly and helpful. Worth noting that if you drive in, parking is thirty bucks a day...but I got such a deal on the room (they've been running a summer special during slow season) that it was easily still worth it to camp here. I'd definitely stay here again.

I could have passed out in the bathroom with a sleeping bag if i wanted. The decor is old, but I didn't expect much better. the mini-suite was only 30 more than a standard room too. Check-in and check-out was seemless. Also check out the 9.99 all you can eat ribs :)

text: I was here with a group of about a dozen friends, and we had an absolute blast. It really was a full evening of entertainment and good times, not just a quicky meal. Putting it in that perspective, the prices that so many have been blasting here are really not that bad. There was never any pressure to hurry through the meal; the wait staff was helpful and attentive, and helped us through the maze of choices for the meal. My table went with the Wisconsin trio - excellent stuff! The spinach salad was great, maybe a little heavy on dressing, but really tasty. All of the meat was nicely proportioned and fresh, and it was really good with the mojo broth. We had three different chocolate fondues between our big group, and every one of them was awesome. I like the bananas foster best, but the dark chocolate was a close second. It would be worth a trip off the beaten path from State St. to just check out the bar. It's well stocked (no draft beer, though), the bartender was awesome, and the mixed drinks were top notch.

It was quite tasty, but only warm on the outside and still cold in the center. Also not given any bread. 2 Stars based on this experience. Will have to come back next time I am in the area.

text: The staff at Shula's was great. I did have one little glitch - I called to increase my reservation a few weeks before and when they called me the day of to confirm, they did not have that updated info - could've been catastrophic, but wasn't, phew. The staff on site was awesome with the fact that my reservation went from 20 - 10 - 13 within the matter of 45 minutes, even after we sat. Seriously, if the restaurant were busy I'm sure they couldn't have accommodated us like they did, but I got lucky and they never got annoyed. Our main server was very attentive in the beginning, but sort of wandered off later in the evening when we needed him. Or maybe it was just me that needed him because I was craving the mushrooms I had ordered that never came. :o( We also drank all the bottles of two of the wines they offer, so if you're going with a large group you may want to have them check their stock before you order. The bartender made a mean Manhattan and overall everyone had a great experience here. I would absolutely use them for another business dinner. It's odd to order your meat off a football, but hey, gimmicks is gimmicks. By no means a cheap option as you have to buy all of your sides a la carte, but they're certainly big enough for 2-3 people to share. They also have plenty of non-steak options on the menu. I highly recommend the bbq shrimp and the chocolate lava cake. Excellent beginning and end to the meal!

text: I grew up going to diners. While other kids were going out to get drunk in high school, I was going out for coffee (I never made it past 5'3). Sure, maybe that means I wasn't a popular kid in high school since I was more like an old lady...or it means I am an expert on diners. I choose the latter. Unfortunately Ray's does not cut it....my beaufriend took me there for breakfast and while our waiter tried his best to make it a good experience, the restaurant failed us in many ways... They sat us at a dirty table. They asked if we wanted lemons for our water, but they didn't deliver them. They asked if my boyfriend wanted powdered sugar on his french toast and when he declined, the plate still came out with powdered sugar. We had to ask for silverware. We were let down so much that it became comical. Like I said, our waiter tried to make our experience great by being overly friendly and attentive. It wasn't his fault the kitchen and the busboys weren't pulling through. I appreciated his efforts. The food is ok, not amazing. Diners are meant to be cheap and provide a decent meal. It is not meant to be gourmet, I know that, but the prices surprised me. They were all just a little bit higher than what I would expect for a diner on Germantown Pike in Norristown. Oh well. It seems like their ice cream is worth it. Maybe I will make the venture in the warmer months.

text: I guess its kinda a unique place. For some strange reason, the flashiness and bright colors of the interior makes me think of a place in Tokyo or Seoul. Anyway, I like the set-up and the idea of getting whatever mix of frozen yogurt and topping that you want. But the yogurt itself had quite dismal taste. It reminded me of the yogurt machines in college/high school cafeterias. Those may have been slightly better. I tried the 'classic', green tea and coffee, and did not like any of them. It says a lot, because I love the flavor of coffee and can usually tolerate anything that is coffee flavored... I really had to force feed myself at Sweet Ending since I already paid all of $5. I really think they are capable to making great product, but are cutting corners.. i.e just using lots of ice, coloring, sugar and cheap cheap flavoring. I probably won't be going back...
label: NEG

text: In a world where two fashion-loving ladies are walking around town on a cold, monsoon-like day, hitting up the shops on 3rd Street like there's no such thing as a budget, you'd think that there'd be a little love to spread around. Well, the shop owners of all the other places we went to that day had no problem being, well, HUMAN to us. In fact, everywhere else we went (Smak Parlour, Topstitch, Sugarcube, Lost and Found and Tony just to name a few) were downright lovely. Girl crushes were developed. Some serious cash was dropped. But we were almost tempted to pee on the front doorstep of Vagabond, because the customer service - no, wait - total LACK of said service, wasn't just lacking, it was completely offensive and stupid. There, I said it. The way we were treated here was stupid. I hate to give bad reviews. For reals. In fact, unless I have such a shitty experience somewhere I can usually find the good in any situation. But this was crazytown. Nobody else was in the store. No eye contact was made (except as we were leaving 10 minutes later - we got the eye roll). Lady behind the counter never stood up or stopped with the chitty chat on the phone long enough to see if we needed anything. And we did, actually. We needed to spend some money and buy a bunch of overpriced clothes (don't fret...we accomplished that other places in the neighborhood that day at stores that actually appreciated our business). Did I greatly admire this place before yesterday? Yes. Do I covet 99% of the gorgeous clothing in there? Yes. Have I even covered it in articles I've written? Again, yes. Oh, wait, and have I met and even had a beer with the girl who totally ignored us? Uhh, yeah. Which is why I'm gonna say it one more time, just to get it out of my system: Stupid.
label: NEG

text: This restaurant was a huge disappointment. I've read the other reviews and I'm not sure if they were just having an off night or if my standards are too high... The rolls we were given after we ordered were good, but warm rolls were expected. We ordered Duck Confit Risotto, Foie Gras and the Cheese Tart for apps. The first two were good, at best. The Risotto was a nice size dish and the Foie Gras was good as well. Sadly, the Cheese Tart was literally nothing more then a cold, cracker sized pastry with some goat cheese crumbled on top. It was so small that the pear slices that accompanied it were much larger than the tart itself. When it was placed on the table, I thought to myself, "Seriosuly, are you kidding?" So disappointing and kind of pretentious. The entrees we got were the Lobster Mac-n-Cheese, Braised Short Rib, Pork Chop and the Salmon. The pork chop was the winner of the bunch. The Lobster Mac-n-Cheese looked like it had sat out a little while - the cheese had started to congeal a bit. The salmon looked OK (I didn't try it), but it was a rather flat piece of fish, not the nicest cut. The ritsotto that it came with was good. Sadly, the Braised Short Rib was a big flop. Short Ribs should be extrememly tender meat that shred apart with your fork. I had to saw mine with a knife. Not what one expects when they order this dish. This was, by far, the worst I've ever had. I didn't finish it and when asked if I wanted to take it home I told the waitress "no thank you" because "I didn't care for it." She got a little snippy and said, "Excuse me. You didn't like it?" As if I had just personally insulted her or something. Two minutes later the chef came out to ask if everything was good. We explained our expectations with the short ribs and he just looked shocked...how could someone not like his dish!?! Well, sorry dude, it wasn't good. At this point, any respectable restauranteur would have offered to take the dish off our bill or give a dessert on the house. We didn't get either. A small note about our server...kind of snobby. She seemed nice enough at first, but got snippy and looked annoyed as the meal progressed. When dining at a BYO, I expect good food and warm service. I experienced neither of these at Sonata. I think the chef is talented, but some dishes need work and some staff need to get a better attitude. This restaurant will not survive if it does not fix itself. The entire time we were there (2 hours), there was only two other tables dining. Maybe everyone else already experienced Sonata and aren't returning - like me.
label: NEG

text: The Korean BBQ short ribs and Duck are my two favorite meals. The rolls are good but I would stay away from the "special" rolls, not that special. The calamari is a great appetizer. If you don't want the "jerky waiter" ask to sit on the left side, he has always served on the right side.

text: There isn't a doubt in my mind that one of the very rarest slices of culinary heaven on earth can be found inside the doors of Link's eateries and if there is one in particular that rises to the status of Godlike it is indeed Cochon. I lived in New Orleans for years, went through Katrina and came back and was so very happy to see that Link's commitment to the city just got stronger. This is undeniable in the warm familial atmostphere and stunning bites that define Cochon. I LOVE food but occasionally when I open a menu and see items that have been served up SO BADLY, SO OFTEN I shudder at the thought of trying said things again (see alligator often too tough to swallow much less use for anything other than a fleshy baseball OR Boudin often so dry and just horribly gamey it is inedible) but I was heading to Cochon with a group of 5th generation cajuns and it was a Link eatery so I dove in...and we were all thrilled we did. GET A RESERVATION. This is not optional. No reservation? Unless it is the middle of summer with 180% humidity and everyone has left town you won't get a seat. The local liquor selection is divine. They usually carry at least 4 Abita's on draft at any given time. The bartenders there are true mixologists and will not steer you wrong. Don't know what to drink with your dinner? Ask them. They know exactly the perfect compliment. The fried alligator with Garlic aioli was like a bit of "fried fried heaven" in my mouth. The alligator was firm but not tough and the seasoning scrumptious. The boudin with the mustard and pickled peppers looked a bit tart to me on paper but turned out to be a revelation when served. The rabbit and dumplings was just one of the most amazing things I have ever put in my mouth EVER. It was so fresh tasting with the veggies and the rabbit was fall apart tender. The brisket was almost obscene it was so good with the smokey, seasoning playing perfectly against the kick of the horseradish in the potato salad. It was beautifully executed, lacking the snobbery and just simple, brilliantly paired food that was clearly created by someone who loves Louisiana cuisine. Is it a bit "much"? HELL YES! But isn't that by definition what New Orleans is all about. It is a celebration of excess and it succeeds perfectly! I could eat here everyday. I am sure I would die young with all the butter that is notorious in cajun cooking but damn it if it were being served by Cochon I can promise you I would also die happy in one of my favorite eateries on the planet in my favorite city in the world.. Always hungry...and Sadly STILL stuck and lost in LA. GG
label: POS

text: I have dined at Janos several times in the past and had enjoyable and memorable experiences. However, last Saturday evening, while the service was great, the food was extremely disappointing. While the Scottish Salmon gravlax was house-made, the dish was thoroughly ruined by the sausage bread pudding on which it was served. The pudding was inedible and foreshadowed the meal to follow. The next course was a sweet potato and smoked chili soup. The soup was presented elegantly and hot, which was promising. The corn flan in the soup was tasty and a creamy - a highlight of an otherwise watery and lack luster soup. (Both my girlfriend and I thought it strange that the restaurant did not offer any salads on the menu, which would've been a betetr option than the soup.) The next course was a stuffed quail breast wrapped in bacon served with potato gnocchi. The stuffing was dry and unflavorful, the quail non-existent and the bacon was crispy though. The gnocchi were raw in the center. My date ordered the beef short rib for her dinner entree. While the short rib was tender, the dish just hit a single note. My dinner entree was the Colorado rack of lamb. Two lamb chops were properly cooked, but overwhelmed by the Kalamata olive sauce. The polenta was creamy, but was cold. The highlight of this meal was the cappucino ice cream with chili hot fudge sauce. While the ice cream was rich and creamy, the chili hot fudge sauce was grainy and served at room temperature. The coffee service was elegant. Cream, whipped cream, lump sugar and sugar substitutes with a rich, bold coffee. Chef Janos was in the dining room touching the tables and greeting certain guests, which is always nice to see. I will most likely not be givining Janos another try until I see better ratings on Yelp. There are other resturants in Tucson to be enjoyed for a better experience.

text: I've had a lot of experiences with car salesmen, but this takes the cake. My father (a 63 year old business owner, just for some back up - the guy has experience in car purchasing/haggling and sales) was going to help me buy a new car. I had a car accident recently that had totaled my car, so I intended on paying for a car with cash (including my insurance check). We had looked around at a number of vehicles, and decided to check out what kind of deal we could get on a Honda Fit. We had driven around the front and back lots and saw that there were about 20 (including 10 black Fits) on the lot. We headed into the show room and asked for a salesperson. An older man, John, came up and politely introduced himself. But, that was as far as the politeness went. My father mentioned that we were interested in seeing what we could work out on a Fit. John proceeded to tell us that there was no "overhead" on the Fit and that negotiations were out of the picture. My father said "Come on, do we still have to go through this negotiation stuff? Even with the economy the way it is?" John said "How about I give you $500 off," we said no, and stated that we'd like to talk further about it. John said "no deal," and shook his head. He told us that we'd have no chance in getting a deal on a Fit, and practically shooed us out the door. He had no clue that we'd pay cash, he had no clue that we were ready to walk out with a car that very moment. We left completely insulted. He was rude, inconsiderate and seemed like he had more things on his mind (like his newspaper) then to try to sell us a car. My father even mentioned to him "You have 10 black Fit's out back, about 25 on the lot!" and John proceeded to say "no deal." We didn't even get a chance to haggle! UGH! Yes, there is a stereotype of rude salespeople when it comes to cars, and we expect to go through the whole song and dance thing, but, that doesn't mean we expected to be treated this poorly. I advise that you take your Honda business elsewhere. I am even a previous Penske customer (two Chevys) and had never felt this degraded by a sales person there. So, this delays me buying a car another day. I'm really disappointed and we both left so pissed off at the staff that I shot off an email when I got home to Penske. Rudeness = FAIL.

They often adjust the class to be far too challenging to a beginner or casual dancer. I mean, I've been doing this for a long time and should probably move up to an intermediate class, but I've really struggled with the combinations. I've been there once or twice when this crew wasn't there, usually during semester breaks, and the classes are fun, the students are more colloquial, the teachers are instructive and encouraging, and everyone is just more relaxed. text: Ok, so everybody knows that really good Asian restaurants are hard to come by. Mostly diners are relegated to the Chinese restaurant clones that pepper strip-malls all over the country where the food is plentiful but often mediocre and the commonality of the menu from one restaurant to another brings to mind Chinese conspiracy theories. After reading the overwhelmingly positive reviews here on Yelp and also some feedback from coworkers about how good Veekoo is my brother and I decided to try dinner here last night. So here's my take on this place. The decor in here is what I consider stereotypical eat in Asian restaurant; Panda print cloth on the booth benches, the prerequisite shiny black chairs, faux flowers, etc. It's hardly offensive, it's just not a very original looking layout. We ordered 2 appetizers to share, Szechuan Dumplings in Hot Sauce and Crabmeat and Chinese Wonton. The dumplings were ok but certainly nothing to rave about. The dish was very light on the Szechuan sauce and it wasn't very hot and spicy at all. The wontons were even less impressive and were served with duck sauce and shredded lettuce that was starting to wilt and slightly browning on the sides. I've had much better fried crabmeat wontons from smaller takeout places. For entrees my brother and I got General Tso's Chilean Seabass - seabass fillet sautéed with General Tso's Sauce and Mandarin Fancy - cubed fillet mignon, scallops with fresh shiitake mushrooms and peppers in Kung Pao sauce, respectively. My brother liked his Chilean seabass, though it did have a very fishy taste to it. When seabass is cooked properly this should not be the case, it should have a mild flavor. I was very unimpressed by my dish. The taste was just so-so and there were only 3 medium sized sea scallops in the dish and the cubed filet mignon pieces were VERY small (about the size of a thimble) and there were very few of them, like 5 or 6 pieces. There were also no shiitake mushrooms to be found in my dish which was disappointing. At $18 for the entree I definitely felt shortchanged for such a tiny serving of meat and the missing mushrooms. The service we received from our waiter was very good. He was friendly and quick. In my opinion this place is seriously overpriced for the quality and quantity of food that you get. I don't know, maybe all the hype I heard from others about Veekoo set the expectation bar a bit too high for me but I just wasn't impressed with the food. I've heard that they excel at sushi but I can't comment on something I didn't try. This place isn't horrible but I'm giving it 2 stars because I think any more would be a tad too generous. As I look over the reviews for this place again and I see all the 4 and 5 stars one thing keeps going through my mind.... people, if you think this place is good then try Han Dynasty around the corner. You'll have an Asian food-gasm, you'll get more food and it'll cost you a lot less!

There's a cactus and succulents section, and the rest of the grasses, shrubs, and trees are laid out in tidy rows with identifying signs. The staff is friendly and helpful, but they're also happy to leave you alone to wander around sniffing, poking, and reading about the plants. Their web site (www.desertsurvivors.org) is very good, too; they have an awesome downloadable guide to all the plants they sell with information about where they're from, what conditions they're suited for, and the kinds of critters they attract, if any. The plants looked like they are doing well; remembering of course that desert plants tend to look rather scraggly and unassuming while they're getting started. I did once go for a creosote bush but left empty-handed, but this was just because they only had the larger $20 plants and I was looking for the cheap little ones. To be fair, though, they had just had one of their big, much-attended plant sales and I think that wiped out some of their inventory. At any rate, a helpful staffer showed me a whole section of wee creosote bushes, just waiting to get big enough for sale, in the "Employees Only" area. My only warning is that, if you choose a plant based on the information on the sign by the plant, be sure that the abbreviation of the plant's latin name (written on the side of each pot) matches the name of the plant on the sign--sometimes plants are not put back in the right place and it's easy enough to grab the wrong one if you're not careful. Adding to my enthusiasm for Desert Survivors is that it not only provides all of these great (mostly native) plants that thrive here without requiring an obscene waste of water, it is also a non-profit that serves both adults and children with disabilities. How cool is that?!

Externally austere, we walked through the front door to find a busy, full jazz club. Ethan and I were the only white folks in the room, and all three of us were woefully underdressed in hooded sweatshirts and cargo shorts. This was a well-heeled crowd -suits on the men and hats on the ladies - but we acted normal and everyone was watching the stage anyway. We sat near the back. The girl could sing! She personified soul - confident, loud, sensual. She laughed after each song, and called out to the audience, "Am I right?" "Do you feel that?" Her back-up singers swayed, demure, and filled out the harmonies. They were down from Atlanta, but every few songs she reminded us that her keyboardist was 'One of New Orleans' Own,' drawing cheers. I ordered my Sazerac, and we watched, grooved. The last song was a two-step, and the place erupted - the crowd jumped to their feet and whipped out white kerchiefs, waving them and hollering along with her song. Kerchief-less and uneducated, we watched, I finished my drink, and we headed out for a few moments of sleep before my too early return to Florida.

I've never had anything there that I thought was awful (well, there are these dumpling things I thought were not so wonderful, but maybe they were having an off day). Furthermore, I've never had bad service, which is very important to me. I ate there last night and our server was very sweet, gracious, and attentive. I'm not wild about the remodel. text: I went with a group of friends to Mosaic as part of St Louis' Downtown Restaurant week. I was super excited to the five course meal they were offering for $25. I had looked up the menu prior to going and my mouth was watering before I ever stepped foot into the place. I really wanted to Mosiac, tried to like it, but unfortunately that just did not happen. We were quickly seated for our 7pm reservation which got things started off on the right foot, but it took a while for our waiter to get around to taking our drink order. The table ordered a pitcher of Sangria but I saw a Caipirinha and just had to have one. It had been ages since I had indulged in this tasty Brazilian cocktail. A short while later our drinks arrived and I took a big sip. You know the disappointment that hits you in the face when you are expecting one thing and get something at the complete opposite end of the spectrum. Yea it was like that. A Caipirinha is supposed to be sweet, sugar is a main ingredient, but this was not sweet at all, quite the opposite. In all honesty it tasted like a really bad, watered down Margarita, but that's not being fair to Margaritas. It was just bad. A while later our waiter stops back by and asks about my drink and I tell him it's not like any Caipirinha I've ever had. He asks me if he can get me something else instead and I started to look at the menu again but was having a hard time finding a substitute. He said he'd give me a few minutes to look it over and be back. About 20 minutes later he returns and I order the grape juice box, a good while goes by and I finally get my drink. It was good, reminded me of grape kool-aid, but I really wish I would have not been set on getting a cocktail and had just gone with a glass of wine. So much safer. Very disappointed in the Caipirinha, but props for offering to bring me something else, just don't take so long to get my drink back out to me. Ok, enough about that, let's get on to the food. We started off the five course menu with an Amuse Bouche that was interesting. Not something I cared to remember, but by no means bad. The second course was a choice of their hot butternut squash soup, or a cold watermelon kimchi gazpacho. Even though I had heard about the butternut squash soup I opted to go with the gazpacho and I am glad I did. The butternut squash had a wonderful flavor to it, however it was just flat out too sweet. The watermelon kimchi gazpacho was very good. The sweetness of the watermelon was complimented by the spiciness of the kimchi. The third course was a choice between a baby arugula salad or a fresh mozzarella watermelon salad. I went with the mozzarella watermelon salad. It was not bad, but it didn't exactly make an impression. The slice of watermelon tasted like it had been cut right next to the rind which didn't outright ruin it for me, but it took away from it. I think I would have been better off suited to go with the baby arugula salad. For the fourth course, there were a few choices, steak, chicken or crab tail. I went with the NY Strip steak, as you can't go wrong with a NY Strip, right? Wrong, I can't remember the last time I had food envy this bad. First four of us at the table ordered the NY Strip, two Medium and two Medium Rare. When the dishes were brought out we were just served it without asking who had the medium and who had the medium rare. My steak was undercooked, (as was everyones) tough, hard to cut and even harder to chew. I think I've had a better steak at Ponderosa than what they served me last night. The white asparagus crème that the steak was served atop was nice, and the Manchego croquettes were decent, though they tasted more like hash browns than anything that had cheese in it. On to the final course. I wasn't even sure I wanted to try this, but at least one of the two desserts they served didn't fail. At this point I had kind of tuned the waiter out so I won't be able to accurately describe the two desserts we were served. The first was a Manchego cheese cake. The texture of the cheesecake was just wrong, it was not creamy, more like a gelatinous cube. Just did not do anything for me. The second was a brownie, ok it was more than just a brownie, but you get the idea. It was topped with currants and infused with something I can't quite remember but it was pretty good. Overall, I was severely underwhelmed by my experience here. Our waiter left a LOT to be desired, his service was sporadic at best. If you offer to bring me a replacement drink, don't disappear for close to 20 minutes before coming back to take my order. A quick glance at the watch, and our total time in the restaurant last night was 2 hours 15 minutes, but it felt like so much longer. Bottom line, I will not be back to Mosiac, there are way too many other quality restaurants in St Louis that I would rather give my money to.
