text: I still remember the first time I saw this building in my adult life. I had just moved to Philly, where I would live for the next couple of years. It was a cool, overcast autumn evening and I was walking through some cookie cutter skyscrapers. I came across the open square area surrounding this building and my eyes gravitated up to fix on the soft yellow light radiating from the clock tower. I could see the puffs of clouds passing by which only intensified its glow. You don't really see structures like this in California's concrete jungles. There are many impressive buildings in the world, but this one had the greatest initial wow factor on me. It took 30 years to complete and the architect didn't even live to see it when it was finally finished in 1901. There was also an informal agreement that limited the height of buildings in the city to be below the brim of William Penn's hat (the statue at the top). This was in place until the Liberty Center was constructed in the mid-80's. The building itself is set in an inconvenient location if you're driving, but allows it to be seen for miles when looking down any of the streets that lead to it. The coolest part is the observation deck at the top of the tower which is open to visitors. It's also free, so there's really no excuse not to go. To me, this building is the true icon of Philadelphia and even a picture of it will evoke the countless memories and experiences of this city.

text: Good for Gluten-free, friendly customer service and on the whole, compassionate capitalism. This is my main source of groceries in Philly when the Farmers Markets close for the year. While you can of course, buy pricey gourmet and specialty products here, the "whole paycheck" label is unwarranted for the majority of everyday products and produce. The 365 label Organic products are a deal and there is definitely a growing effort by Whole Foods to source local products. Go across the street to Super Fresh and you will find a dingy store with often the same or higher prices and wilting produce. The employees and customer service are 98% of the time, fantastic. Ethan (aka the sample man) can put a smile on your face no matter what kind of day you are having with the delight that he takes in joyfully handing out samples. There is a decent selection of gluten-free products and paraben-free natural body and skincare products. If you want a greater variety of Gluten free flours (such as Teff, Sorghum, etc.) it's worth a trip to the 20th & Hamilton store which is larger and has a greater selection, but a trek for those in center city. And while I don't agree with the CEO/founder's stance on universal healthcare, he is entitled to his opinion and Whole Foods does provide health care to even their part-time employees. While as a member of OCA (Organic Consumer Association) I know that Whole Foods sometimes needs a consumer push and may not do everything exactly the way I would like, it still has helped to increase market share for organic and hormone/anti-biotic free products and has made an effort to source locally. While shopping here doesn't guarantee a healthy experience and there are many delicious ways to overindulge, Whole Foods vets products fairly well to avoid scary ingredients (high-fructose corn syrup, hydrogenated oils, etc). While no person or corporation is perfect/ going to please all of the people all of the time, I feel that if more large corporations functioned as Whole Foods does, our country would definitely be a different and better place.

So we were taken to our table and a minute or two later, our waiter appeared, introducing himself and taking our drink and appetizer order. I thought, hmm service seems really good here. Our drinks were quickly served along with our appetizers. Mine was mushrooms stuffed with lobster, shrimp and crabmeat. It was served piping hot and very good, but it took a few minutes before I could eat it. Before I got two of those suckers in my mouth, the waiter's helper, I guess they are called servers?, was there with our salads. Okay, that was fast, but I didn't actually mind since we were planning to go to the movies across the street when we were finished with dinner. But, and that's a big BUT, before I had put my fork in my mouth 3 times, he was there with our dinners! That's when I put my foot down. I told him to take them back since I'd barely had time to eat my appetizer and my salad. He did and a few minutes later our waiter came by to see how everything was. We told him what had happened and of course, he apologized, asking when we'd like our dinners. My DH said about 10-15 minutes and I quickly added that I didn't want those actual dinners...I wanted new ones cooked. He was okay with that and off he went. When we were finished with our appetizers and salads, DH signaled the waiter to bring our dinners. Within 5 mins, our dinners were served. I had ordered wood-fired grilled lobster, shrimp and scallops, served atop rice. The only vegetable offered was broccoli, which I don't like, so I ordered a baked potato instead. The grilled lobster was slightly over-cooked, the shrimp were good, and the scallops could have been grilled a little more for my taste. The potato was microwaved...EWWW!! I HATE microwaved baked potatoes. DH had ordered the same thing. He agreed with my assessment of our dinners. We had time to finish up with coffee and a slice of cheesecake, which we shared. The coffee was quite good and the cheesecake was just the run-of-the-mill variety. So, all in all, the service was way too fast, trying to shove our food down our throats, and the food was so-so. Not worth going back IMHO. There's just oo many other good restaurants in the area.

text: Perhaps you will visit The Voluptuous Vixen in order to stock your wardrobe with delightful, fashion-forward garments for work. One wouldn't even be disappointed if she entered in hopes of attractive yet solid foundation garments, from bras to mini-mollies. I went to The Voluptuous Vixen in order to immerse myself in classy boutique shopping of the type that is rarely available in plus sizes. What a pleasure to find all of this in one location, carefully crafted by proprietress Jaclyn McCabe, who will ensure that everyone leaves with outfits that look perfect. Be ready to drop some choice cash at The Voluptuous Vixen, every dollar well spent. Ms. McCabe, who is as lovely as she is fashion-savvy, takes pride in offering the most delightful and well-made fashions I have ever seen offered in a brick-and-mortar store carrying plus size clothing. Her boutique is filled with unique apparel from a variety of top names rarely found together under one roof. Furthermore, she can help you with those tricky "what not to wear" decisions, and teach you how that ballet wrap is really supposed to tied. "Never tie a bow around your lunch," she chided gently, offering welcomed assistance as I stepped out of the dressing room to show off my new treasure. I picked up a fantastic patterned wrap, two casual dresses, and a set of 3 "mini-mollies" (short sleeved undershirts with an under-bust hem). The next day I wore a molly with one of the dresses and got nonstop compliments at my professional conference. I'm just thrilled! Jaclyn McCabe is a goddess of plus size fashions, from sexy to subtle. Make a point of stopping by to feel what it is like to shop in a world-class boutique designed specifically for large women, and to enjoy the many compliments you'll collect on your new looks.

text: Being gluten intolerant for over 20 years I have learned to search for a menu online and/or call ahead and/or contact corporate with any questions about gluten free menu items. In this case I contacted corporate and was assured there were gluten free menu items. Great! So off we go to TGIF. We are seated promptly and I ask for a gluten free menu to which I am met with confusion. The waitress quickly gets the manager who proceeds to tell me they do not have any menu items that are specifically GF, but "depending of the severity of (my) reaction to gluten there are some items to choose from." This guy had no idea what he was talking about and apparently neither did corporate who did not respond to my email describing what happened. Gluten intolerance is not a matter of degree. You have it or you don't, and if you do even a small amount of gluten can severely damage the intestinal tract and lay you up for days. Estimates are that 10% of the population have celiac disease. TGIF needs to understand this and not lead potential customers to believe they have something they do not. Needless to say we did not stay, and I would not recommend TGIF to anyone who is gluten intolerant or suspects they may be.

text: What used to be a fairly uneventful and empty waste of space (called Semolina Pasta) is now a very popular Zea restaurant on the West Bank. I definitely recommend lunch during the week; as crowded as it is, the prices are wallet friendly! The wait was roughly 30 minutes, but that's because we rolled in at noon. When we were seated, we noticed that there was a cold ass draft because we were sitting right under the vent! Don't sit in the back if you want to avoid getting chills. Anyhow, I tried their platter of the day which includes a protein (Thursdays - sliced lamb with mint demi-glace) and two sides (Thai snap beans & Zea potatoes). The price is perfect (about $11) and the portion is too huge! The lamb was overcooked and dry and the sauce used to mask that dryness wasn't very yummy. The Thai snap beans were sweet and crisp, while the potatoes were just lame country style potatoes, super deep fried. One friend ordered the Ahi tuna salad which is basically a seared medium rare ahi tuna steak on top of greens with some funky shaped deep fried wonton chips and dressing....it looked SOOOO good I wish I had tried it. Madison was our server and she was extremely professional (even though a knife was dropped - no injuries!) and super duper nice and always smiling....she definitely rocked our lunch! I'd definitely return here if I ever come back home - Zea is affordable and the atmosphere is definitely welcoming.

text: Been going to Fellini's since they opened in Ardmore a decade ago and visited every one of the 5 branchs that followed, Ardmore was always the one to go to. I couldn't help myself getting stuck in the wonderful rut of their eggplant parm app and their gnocchi arrabiata. I miss those. Watched the small chain begin to unravel about 18 months ago. Knew there was trouble when they ran out of cheese on one of our visits at their 22nd and Walnut location about a year and a half ago. They closed 2 weeks later. That space was taken over by Salento, a terrific Italian BYO Fellini's was near perfect in its prime. BYO, pastas that were fresh and plentiful and tasty. Very good pizzas and very good chicken dishes. In their prime they would always be given a 4 star review for what they were. At their best service was never their strong suit. And though they would take a reservation, it really meant nothing as you queued up with the walk-ins. But when you are surrounded by pretty happy people anticipating a very good and reasonably priced Italian dinner, it was part of the charm. I haven't been there in a year having given the Ardmore location 3 chances to convince me that my first and second to my last visit was an anomoly. But it was 3 straight strike outs with the food resembling none of the near great fare that made them such a Main Line sensation. Restaurants usually fade gradually, Fellini's, after a ten year run, crashed and burned in near record time.

text: Out of all the burrito places in the area, this one is my favorite. The burritos are big and packed with deliciousness. They also have various other standard mexican food items, such as tacos and quesadillas, but I never really get any of those because the burritos are too good to pass up. They have a wide variety of burritos, and you can fill them with steak, chicken, or pork. There are two that are tied for my favorite: the queso burrito and the ancho chile barbecue burrito. The queso burrito is just what it sounds like, a burrito with delicious cheesy queso inside. I'm a big cheese fan and this burrito definitely satisfies. The barbecue burrito contains some sort of spicy mexican barbecue sauce that is packed with flavor. I was somewhat skeptical the first time I tried it, but it tastes great, especially when combined with the shredded pork. They have five different kinds of salsa. My favorites are roja (which is hot) and verde (which is medium). I haven't yet gotten up the guts to try the extra hot salsa, but now I think I'll have to try it the next time I stop in. I'll often stop by to quickly grab a burrito to take home for dinner after work, and the generally fast service makes it easy to do this. They assemble your burrito from the various ingredients while you watch, and they're pretty snappy about it. However, I occasionally happen to stop by during a busy time and have to wait in line, but it's never been a very long wait. My only real complaint is that occasionally the person who is making my burrito will be a bit stingy with the cheese. They'll usually give you more cheese if you ask (like I said, I love cheese) but sometimes they try to make you pay more for it. Come on, just give me a little more cheese. It costs them next to nothing and keeps me a happy and loyal burrito-buying customer. A minor complaint, but somewhat irksome at times. Overall, a great place to grab a tasty burrito, with a convenient location and generally quick service.

text: There are around a billion ppl in India and a chunk of the population travels by roads. To save a hungry traveler's soul there are these 'Dhabas' littered across the roadways. The concept is simple, inexpensive rates, non existential décor and above all lip smacking homelike food mostly of the north Indian - Punjabi fare. That was the feeling I got as I seated myself over on one of the benches of Rice n Spice as I carefully browsed over the menu written on a white board. Talking about an Indian fare, What most of us are used to at restaurants is pretty rare at most household kitchens as it is too rich and heavy for daily consumption. The thgt of eating tandooris, naans, and Tikka masalas abhors me, that's why I find myself at the doorsteps of RiceNSpice when I crave for some homecooked goodness. It might take a while to get accustomed to this place, there is practically no service per se , u scribble ur order on a piece of paper and hand it over to whoever is walking towards the kitchen and the food gets delivered to ur bench. I sometimes just walk over to the cooler and get myself a beverage cos it works out faster. There usually is some bollywood flick playing on the TV, which is mostly accompanied by ruckus laughter of us mocking the insane subtitles or just us ogling at some sultry actress. There are not many ppl in the kitchen, a wonderwoman for a chef and her helpers churn out delicacies at a stupendous pace. Most of the food is made to order, which keeps it fresh. This is a pretty simple place, no need to worry bout what to wear or make reservations etc. but they do accept Credit cards which is a plus. The serving sizes are available in half and Full portions, which makes it easier to order more than one dish to keep the palate guessing. Here is my strategy if u are blanking out on one. If the group is of a considerable size, order a Pitcher of Mango Lassi, an order of meat , I stay away from the tikka masala and just bank on the Chicken Curry instead. A dry vegetable like Bhindi (okra) or Aloo-Gobi and a Lentils or beans dish like the Daal or my favs Rajma(Kidney Beans)/ Chole ( chickpeas) and Paneer. Along with some breads to dip into the saucy goodness, like a Paratha stuffed with either potatoes, Cauliflowers, HorseRadish or even Paneer or Tava roti with some raita does ample justice to the food. Don't be afraid of trying different items off the menu here as most of them don't fail to impress. As ur body slips in and out of a food coma order some Masala tea to wake up ur senses before u hit the road again. So no matter how u make it to Rice'nSpice, I don't care if u walk, hail a cab or even bring an Indian truck, the end result is when u walk out u shall be gratifyingly satiated by some out of the ordinary food, and already be devising a plan of ur next visit. Cheers

text: I just enjoyed one of the most flavorful steaks ever. No kidding. I had the 22 oz Kansas City strip - a strip cut with the bone left in. Although I have experienced "cajun seasoning" that borders on obnoxious at other places, this was perfect - it complemented the flavor of the steak but did not overwhelm it. My medium rare was perfect medium rare. With melted butter to dip in, my taste buds were dancing! The other chef's special was french style green beans sauteed in olive oil and chopped garlic topped with sliced almonds. It was the perfect accompaniment to a fabulous steak. Paired with a Rodney Strong Merlot it was a wonderful meal. Here is the added bonus. Stockyard offers complimentary shuttle transportation to and from the hotel. Is it built into the price of the meal? Of course. Is it worth it? Definitely. When I called Stockyard they said the shuttle would pick me up at 6:15. And it did, right on time. Upon arrival, the hostess greeted me by name and escorted me to the bar, which I told her on the phone is where I wanted to eat since I am traveling alone. When I finished my meal, my server asked if I wanted the shuttle to take me back - when I headed for the door the hostess greeted me by name again and the shuttle was waiting. In an age in which too many places seem to have abandoned the art of customer service and quality product, Stockyard has mastered both. Yes, it is a splurge, and yes, it is worth every penny. Give it a try, you won't be sorry.

NEGATIVE Overpriced for what it is and management is using the beach as an excuse to overprice and to be honest a Best Western hotel is better Parking for guests can get tight at night so you will have to park in the street. Room was not secure!!!! DON'T LEAVE Any expensive personal belongings in the room because there is no safe. Close to a city park but there are plenty of homeless people around. As for the crowd at Eddies, let's just say it's ermmm ... interesting and eclectic. LOTS of bikers, lots of smokers, and lots of loud types. To call it a rough crowd seems suitable, to me. It's just not the kind of place most who aren't into A) smoking, B) drinking of cheap liquor (house drinks are made with the cheapest stuff you can find ... Juarez tequila for margaritas (GAG), C) hanging with bikers, or D) eating lower quality food to save yourself a buck. I will say it can be fun if you have a large, after work crowd with you, where you know a lot of people in a group, and you have a couple of tables reserved for all involved, but at the same time I don't recommend it for a small group of friends. The apartment is a bi-level, with a VERY narrow staircase that zig zags up to the bedroom and office. While most of the furniture made it up this staircase with ease, our queen-sized mattress pad wouldn't budge. The Sultans of Schlep tried multiple ways of moving it up the stairs, but to no avail. With a little brainstorming, the Sultans of Schlep quickly took out a couple of living room windows, and using spare parts in their truck, created a pulley system to pull the mattress pad out of the living room and into the bedroom above. text: This was such a bad experience that I am writing about it years after the actual event! The summer of 2003, I was working in Washington, D.C. and my mother's health was failing on the west coast. She was from Louisiana and, declining with Alzheimer's, talked a lot about wanting to go back and visit. I saved up and we were able to make the trip as a family. Of course, a nice dinner out in the French Quarter was a big part of the trip to New Orleans. I chose this restaurant because my mother thought she knew the family name from Lake Charles and my father remembered that they had dined at this location shortly after they first met. When I waited tables, rule number one was always to take special care of the timing with tables with the elderly and small children. Not only had this staff apparently never thought of such a rule, they seemed intent on ignoring us BECAUSE we had someone elderly with us. After 45 minutes I had to go find a manager to please, please have someone come take our order. I explained that it was getting difficult to keep the party there, my mother's condition and that it actually seemed we were being ignored. I was very nice about it and was begging them to help me since this dinner was an event more than a meal. When the server arrived, he was apparently bent out of shape at having been sent to the table. Another 25 minutes later, when our food arrived, I sincerely believe a salt shaker had been dumped in my dish. Since we'd already had the wrong food come to the table and were, at this point, famished, I tried to choke some of it down. I was trying to keep spirits up at the table and did not, against all urges, complain. On top of all this, it was not a cheap evening for me. I sincerely wish this place were no longer open. I see others commenting on the service and am at least happy to learn that it was not just us!

Man how I wish I hadn't done that, i found that I had just consumed 4 pieces of sushi that contained CLEARLY rotted avocado chunks, They were black! So I immediately ceased the lunch consumption and set in on pushing away the uneasy feeling that my brain was causing my stomach. I notified the waitress that she might want to tell the sushi chef or (Line Cook) that they might not want to serve any more of that sushi before checking its freshness, who goes "Oh that's not Good" and quickly sweeps my plate away and quickly returns with our bills? On a good note I tried my buddies potato chip fries that were served with his burger and they were very tasty and the burger was very large and was said to have been very delicious. text: This is one of the better Thai restaurants in the area. The place is beautifully decorated and clean. The wait staff is attentive and the place is always bustling. We started off with the chicken satay appetizer. It was the standard grilled-chicken-on-a-stick-with-peanut-sauce, with one twist: they brought out a tiny brazier so we could re-grill the chicken at the table. I thought it was a nice touch! As far as the main course goes, I had the Volcano Chicken, my wife had the Pad Thai. Both were excellent. The chicken was not fried as it so often is, which I thought was nice. The Pad Thai was good and not overly sweet, so my wife was able to eat all of it instead of burning out halfway through. All-in-all, a very nice experience. Lanna Thai has been added into our regular dining out rotation.
label: POS

text: An excellent place to get pizza. Sal is a really cool guy too. He'll come up and strike up a conversation with you. HUGE slices of pizza (NY style). For the style of pizza it is, very very good. Try the pepperoni bread sticks here. When I lived in Hendrick's County, I loved getting the bread sticks here.
label: POS

text: The hostess had zero warmth, that was not a good start. But the hopes of well cooked seafood with a nice river view stayed as the focus. The service was ok at best honestly. They were nice but could have been more knowledgeable about the menu. Go for the grilled swordfish, and the clam chowder , and glass of Malbec for $9, all excellent. The tilapia was overcooked and not appealing to the eye, and it had three slices of mushrooms - think we paid extra for the 3 slices? Great wine list but really weak on the beers but I was expecting that. But have a least one local beer! It was good to check out but probably won't return.
label: NEG

text: Over rated. The food has gone down hill over the years but Boise keeps on voting this fast food joint the best. Go figure. The food is over rated and the outside dining is a dump. For my money the Viking Drive In rules.
label: NEG

text: This place is awesome! Very clean, bright, and modern. Even the choice of bright green in its interior reflects it's earthy feel and is a smart choice. The staff have always been very nice and give the place a semi hip vibe. Choice of meal today?? A beet and onion salad: bright, simple, and tasty Baked sweet potato fries: semi charred to give it a smokey taste offset by the refreshing accompanying dip. A light dill/yogurt Tuna melt sandwich: grainy dark bread, fresh vegetables and light tuna I have read on here someones opinion stating they found it to be expensive, I find my opinion to be the complete opposite. The sandwiches are about $8.99. Not only are they extremely healthy, but are freshly made and not pulled out of a showcase where they have been sitting all day like the usual booster juice. Definitely my pick when paying the similar price. The salads are extra low cal and about $3.99. pretty great considering the ingredients. The sweet potato fries are about the same price and definitely have an up on the typical deep-fried choice out there. The fact that it's conveniently right on Jasper ave and situated steps away from world health are two more bonuses. If looking for a healthy dessert and have a sweet tooth I would recommend trying the mango frozen yogurt.. If they have any left! The last 2 times I have attempted to get some for myself they have been out. Truly disappointing. Choice of drinks are also wonderful. They offer those aloe drinks that many seem to enjoy. For me, not so much. Besides that a refreshing choice their calypso juice.y favorite would be the tropical mango lemonade. If you have the luxury of a few extra minutes to grab breakfast in the morning, they have a few breakfast options available as well. Definitely hits all my points for being 5 stars in their 'fast food' health category. Cleanliness, quality, taste, and service with a smile to boot.
label: POS

text: Bad news - Mama's Grill has changed to "Chick Pea's." The name isn't the only thing that has changed. One of the wonderful things about Mama's Grill was that they'd fry up the falafel for each individual order. But the falafel pita I had the other day was just average. It's truly disappointing. I would have never gone to Maoz when I could eat yummy Mama's Grill. Now I'll have to haul ass down to Bitar's.
label: NEG

text: Today was the first day of my new year's aspiration of hitting more of the food trucks around campus. The woman was very nice and they had AFHV going on the ghetto TV in the window. $6 got me a hefty serving of spicy pork bulgogi, rice, and cabbage (and the two fried dumplings). Unfortunately, as with Matt S.'s experience, there was alot more rice and cabbage than there was meat. I'll give them another shot and try a noodle dish next time, but I agree with Alex C. that the better option might just be to head to Koreana at 38th/Chestnut at the place behind the strip club.
label: NEG

text: If you like Brazilian barbecue, you MUST get in your car or take a looong bus ride to this place. Every single this is delicious. You can choose to either pay by weight per plate or $21 dollars for all you can eat. I would suggest going when you want a bigger meal and just getting the all you can eat option, since paying by plate only ends up being a few dollars cheaper. It's great being able to sample a little of everything. The skirt steak is my favorite and is absolutely amazing. There aren't any signs or descriptions on the salad bar, so you kind of just have to grab what looks good to you. That's part of the downside to the restaurant - there is little guidance on how to operate the place from the staff. It's BYOB and the crazy amount of meat consumption goes along well with a bottle of red wine.
label: POS

text: When I lived in San Antonio, Texas, I chalked up the poor service and long waiting times at the Planned Parenthood to its quasi-governmental status. But the Planned Parenthood on Meridian is amazing. The front desk people are friendly and helpful. The resident nurse, Charlie, is knowledgeable and sensitive to women's wants. I told her I didn't like my former pill, and she worked with me to get me on something tailored to my concerns. The facility looks new--I think they just relocated. Only caveats: They aren't open on Fridays, which has put me behind when I need to reorder birth control more than once. But they have a place on their Web site where you can actually get them delivered to you.
label: POS

text: I have a super sweet tooth but even for me, the icing was just excessively sweet. The cupcake itself was okay, a bit dry. We had the chocolate turtle and the wedding cake. The wedding cake was the better of the two.
label: NEG

text: I love some BBQ but I left hungry and actually went to Monks after and got a Apple Chicken Sausage sandwich and a Gulden Drake. I heard great things about Percy St only to be disappointed. Server took roughly 10mins to come to the table. Our Drinks came roughly 10mins after that. The server never stopped back by the table. I ordered the P.S.T. Sandwich which sounds delightful and consists of Pork Belly. I lived in the South and I've had pork belly for years and I love it. I also know it is fatty but I normally work my way around the grizzle. Let me say that there was no meat on my sandwich. It was all Fat. I was amazed that someone would actual try and serve this crap for $12 not to mention the portion of grizzle wasn't all that much either. I will give this place another try and update my review. I had a taste of my friends Brisket and that was quite good. My Pinto Beans, Mac & Cheese, and German Potato salad were quite good.

text: Went last night with three friends. Also had the omakase menu. This is going to be the place to eat sushi in philadelphia. The food is superb. The service fantastic and the warmth of the owner and staff make this one of the best newcomers. We will be back.
label: POS

text: Pool table, dart board, golden tee, mega-touch and jukebox. Backyard with seating is great in the summer and chill for smokers ;) Dog friendly assuming you have a friendly dog,haha. Beer selection is great as well. A great addition to the neighborhood!
label: POS

text: The best thing I got here was the corn on the cob. It was DELICIOUS. The best corn on the cob I've had was in NYC but this definitely was close. I tried the one at El Vez, that trash was trash! Drink wise, I got both the red and white sangria which were okay. Nothing to write home about. My friend got an appetizer that was pretty much fried cheese in lots of oil and you are suppose to place it on a tortilla and eat it. NO thanks! I went with the chips and salsa because I've been craving it. It was a disappointment. The salsa was all wrong. No uhmph. More people came to join my party and they ordered the guacamole..again nothing special. I think the El Vez 'mole is actually better. So the main meal- I got the taco spread (comes with most of the meat found in the individual taco orders). We replaced the pork with halibut ($2 extra or so). It was decent. A meal for 2. I was def full. The individual tacos are small. Other members got the enchiladas and I think they were very happy with it. The waitstaff- very pleasant and attentive. Overall, not a place I would go back to to (except to get that tasty ass corn on the cob). I wouldn't dissuade any from going there either but I think they are better options around.
label: NEG

text: Rosas was recommended by family. I was not impressed and probably wouldnt try it again. The service was very lack luster and they were far from full. Had to flag down waiters to refill the salsa and drinks. The table and menus were sticky. The food was very mediocre. I did like the calendars on the wall.
label: NEG

text: We went to Moritomo for Valentine's Day dinner. It was a bad experience that just kept getting worse. The description below gives all of the details. We did send this letter to Moritomo's on Feb 20, 2008 and have yet to hear back from them. "The script at the Japanese Steakhouse started pretty much the same. Dinner customarily starts with a bowl of clear soup. In this case, it was a beefy broth spiced with dried minced onions - you know, the kind that come in gallon jugs. Sadly, the flakes had not completely rehydrated, rendering them an odd mix of crunchy, soft and simply hard. This rather lackluster starter was followed by an equally uninspired salad. The all iceberg lettuce concoction was washed, evidenced from the pool of water collecting on the bottom of the bowl. The top was drowned in half a cup of thick, somewhat sweet, slightly ginger spiced dressing. After scraping most of the dressing off and mixing it with the lettuce, the dressing promptly slid off and settled on the bottom of the dish with the water. Our chef arrived and began his routine. As hokey as this can be, my family enjoys the procession- the whirling knives, the clanking spatula and the spinning egg. In this case, the flying spatula banging off the side of the grill and onto the floor (he thought a moment, considering still using it, before putting the spatula back on the cart and picking up a fresh one). The eggs broke open, one, two, three, and immediately started to burn. The poor man tried in vain to slice and dice the eggs, but they were well past brown in a matter of seconds. Great globs of butter were thrown on, turning the mass into a soupy mess. Slowly the fried rice began to take shape as the ingredients were added. I say it took shape only figuratively, for in fact the rice flew in all directions. Each time our chef scooped and flipped rice went flying. Soon, a third of the rice lay scattered across the grill, popping as it cooked. He served the portions one by one, spilling copious amounts back onto the grill. (I wondered idly where the chef came from. My guess was the kitchen. In desperation after the defection of their scheduled master hibachi guy, the dishwasher had been promoted.) The burning of food continued. As the beef was set down, it immediately hissed and gouts of steam rolled into the air. Apparently, the establishment failed to purchase the fans on the hibachi grills, as evidenced by the continuous cloud of steam that bathed my poor wife for the rest of the cooking demonstration. ( I did try to get her to change seats with me.) As food continued to burn, our chef scraped it off into an ever growing pile of vile, black goo on the side of the grill. During all of this, our chef tried to re-enact the time honored traditions of the American Japanese Steakhouse hibachi chef. If you have visited such an establishment, you know of what I speak. There is of course the classic inverted stack of onions, filled with some sort of flammable liquid and then set on fire to form a "volcano", followed by steam and a "train". Only, in our case, a fourth of the grill was inundated with the flammable liquid, so that the inverted onion tower became ground zero of a flaming inferno. The hapless onion slices drooped and caved in. Our chef also chopped sliced Zucchini into little cubes, all the better for tossing into people's mouths. Here is a hint for all you would-be hibachi wizards: four year olds are not good at catching small cubes of flying vegetables flung at their face. Once it bounces off their nose or forehead three or four times, it's best to move on to another victim. The circus finally came to an end, and our master chef set about cleaning his grill. Now, in every restaurant of this nature I've been in, the chef scrapes off the grill, wipes it down with a few quick, skilled passes and moves on to applause and fame. Not so for our culinary hero. The hapless dishwasher dumped water onto the grill (my wife promptly disappeared for about thirty seconds as a cumulus cloud formation spread across the room) and began sloshing around with a wire pad. I did not know this at the time, but apparently he managed to slosh his slop onto my wife and her food. Chevalier that I am, I would have risen to my wife's defense and demanded to see the manager at once. Cloaked in the cloud of steam as she was, I failed to see such gross inadequacy and continued eating my mediocre fare. In the end, the experience was so bad it was funny. My son was rather oblivious to the laundry list of faux pa, and was quite pleased when he left. We did walk away with a pair of miniature origami birds, which he thought were pretty nifty. I can't say I'll be going back to Morimoto's, but they certainly did give us a meal we will not soon forget."
label: NEG

text: This place is amazing. It's unfortunate it's so small, but the product they serve demands a limited audience. The burger lives up to all the raves. The fries are like crack -- from what I hear about crack. The barkeep spoke for about 13 minutes on the bitters he uses. Needless to say, they know how to pour a drink as well as execute food. Go at an off time, like 3, bask in the sunlight filtering through the blinds, order three fingers worth of hooch, a cask draught to chase the whiskey, order the burger and fries and savor life. My wife wants to add that the Kentucky Hot Brown is tremendous and way better than Bobby Flay's at Bar Americain in NYC.
label: POS

text: When we moved to the area, we would occasionally pass this place or see a flyer or ad, and joke: "Chicken Holiday. Well, doesn't sound like much of a holiday for the chicken!" [yuk, yuk, yuk]... and we kinda wrote it off. And what a stupid thing to do. This past week we were at a picnic, and had what I really thought was some of the best fried chicken I've tasted in a long time. [you see it coming...] Me: "Man, this is incredible fried chicken, where is it from?" Host: "Chicken Holiday, over on Olden." Me: "Really? Wow! It's great!" Host: "Yeah, they do a great job." [Pause. Taking a bite of chicken] Me: "I guess it's not much of a holiday for the chicken." Host: [exhales beer through nose] Recommended for take out, not a place you really want to sit down and eat. Still, freaking sign me up. I love fried chicken, and this is the best in the area unless you want to drive up to It's Nutts. Four stars not for ambience or service, but for serving damn good fried chicken. Cole slaw is also amazing. Avoid the fish.
label: POS

text: I was born and raised in Boise so of course I take pride in my city but this University is sorely sub-par. Sure the football team is doing better than it has in past years and that's just ducky, but that doesn't in any way reflect on the education. Having attended a community college in Washington state for my first two years of college I set my standards by the experience I received there, which was a great one. At Boise State University you would be hard pressed to find an employee or faculty member that genuinely cares about helping you succeed. Don't get me wrong, there are a few, and I greatly appreciate them. For the most part, however, it 's all about the bottom line rather than a quality education. This university has some excellent potential seeing as how our football team is helping to draw in more publicity not to mention the wonderful community its located in. If there was more care taken to ensure students success I would then feel as if I attend a college I'm proud of. For now, however, I'm left disappointed, frustrated, and utterly broke (thanks to ever rising tuition).
label: NEG

text: When I went they supposedly had some issues with wait staff not showing up. Either way- our service was horrible. I was there with my sister just before getting a flight out, so we didn't have tons of time to wait around. We sat for such a long time with our drinks, that eventually I just paid for them and left without ever receiving our food. Owner was not very happy about that- and I feel I shouldn't have even paid for the drinks because basically we just wasted a lot of time sitting around there.
label: NEG

text: Terrible, my least favorite cheesesteak ever. Even shouting "whiz wit" at the lady, and she gave me attitude. Everyone looked mean inside. While I'm a fan of chopped, I'll give this place a try, but it was oily and with no flavor. I think the super extreme blind patriotism kind of bothers me. They made a big deal about "ordering only in English." With how much they love America, isn't it weird since it's a supposed town of brotherly love, a country founded by immigrants??? Political rant aside, you're better off going the other side of the street.
label: NEG

text: Great diner experience. The french fry omelette was.... interesting. This place isn't the best greasy spoon you will visit, but it's definitely one of the coolest ones. There's a historic feel to it, and the service is unbelievable. Just be smart and avoid peak times, even though the line moves somewhat quickly enough. Expect to rub elbows with people, as you're all seated at the counter. Burgers are good, chili is decent, waffles are good, omelettes are okay. I can't speak for much else here, but all in all you should give it a go at least once. If you're a tourist staying in the French Quarter, this place is accessible by streetcar, just take the St. Charles line all the way down, it's a gorgeous ride. When you hit a 90-degree corner, after passing Audubon Park and Loyola, you've hit Carrolton, and you'll need to get off there. You'll see Cameliia Grill from the corner, and don't be put off by the line, it moves fairly quick.
label: POS

text: This zoo seemed like a lot more fun before I went to Toronto and saw their zoo. This is a smaller zoo for sure, and I think it could easily amaze little children but adults will get bored quickly. It is a nice place to go and walk around and look at the animals, but it isn't really anything special. Every Edmontonian show go at least once, and I will probably go again, but I didn't really feel that my money was worth it.
label: NEG

text: Well. This was refreshing. A Reno restaurant that is great. Every other area restaurant should send their managers there to learn something. This is not a generic atmosphere with lukewarm, generic food served by grumpy workers. This is an EVENT. Our experience last Friday mimics the previous reviews and so we had a great time. The employees were all cheerful, helpful and efficient and entertaining what with the line dancing and birthday "ride the saddle" routine. We had the chicken fried steak, ribeye, salmon and ribs and they were all excellent. They suggest calling ahead to get a table faster on busy nights We waited 45 minutes but we had fun hanging at the bar since it wasn't the usual Reno bartender "What are you doing at my bar, stranger, can't you see I'm hangin with my friends?" routine. Hopefully they can keep up the enthusiasm and with the wear and tear the massive crowds will create because we are now spoiled and will be back.
label: POS

text: For a chain restaurant, Famous Dave's has pretty good bbq. I went with my mom the other day for lunch, and we both really enjoyed our meals. She got the salmon and spare rib combo, and I just go the spare ribs (smallest order they have - you can get 1/3 rack, 1/2 rack, or a full rack). The bbq sauce was really good, the meat was tender, and the sides were good (spicy green beans, apples & cinnamon). I just wish that the corn bread was real cornbread and not corn muffins. They offer lots and lots of food, and you can get several different combos, from different meats to meals for 2. They also had a good variety of bbq items. I also really liked my lemonade, and the waitress was really nice and efficient. I'd go again, although Famous Dave's doesn't hold a candle to Sweet Lucy's.
label: POS

text: We've never eaten here but have gotten takeout many times. Good but not outstanding Mexican food, at reasonable prices. My favorite is the mole poblano; platters are also good, especially the ones that include some combination of beans / rice / Mexican salad. A tip: on Friday evenings, this place is very crowded! Pick another night for your first visit.
label: POS

text: Solid steak, service and company I had my birthday while in NOLA and we wanted meat. We were recommended two other spots but being the old hag's bday fell on a Sunday and erythang is closed on god's day off. SO enter Dickie. It was a totally romantic spot for me and my gay BFF...let me paint you a picture. It was raining and there was sexy music coming from a guy playing the trombone outside. We had a drink at the bar before we were sat and I had an amazing wine. Course I can't remember the name. We had an adorable waiter named Justin who we throughly harassed throughout our dinner. We actually had 3 waiters - crazy right!!! I had the rib eye with garlic mashed but asked for the sweet potato and they messed it up so we got free carbs!! Overall, great meal. Sweet succulent meat and great company. Loves it.
label: POS

text: I never really understood the fuss over donuts until I had a glazed donut from Daryl's. One of my coworkers brought donuts in for a meeting and I was like meh. But then I saw this golden goddess and I had to rethink my breakfast strategy. It was amply covered in a sugar so thick and inviting, I had to act fast before my coworkers grabbed it. It was calling to me. One bit into this glorious glazed wonder, I finally understood the power of the donut. Darryl's has forever redefined breakfast pastries for me.
label: POS

text: I cannot express how much I LOVE this place! I haven't tried anything I haven't loved, and I have tried almost the whole menu. The Service is friendly, parking is readily available, the environment is welcoming and the fruit is always fresh. My only complaint is that they don't have a location in San Diego!
label: POS

text: Horrid is the perfect word to describe this location! It is always jam-packed (good for the share price but bad for the customer) and it's hard to get a salesperson's attention as they all have ADD. Last year, I had an issue with my iMac G5 and took it back frequently to have it repaired. (The noise emanating from it eventually became unreasonably loud.) I booked time with a Genius, took it in, was told I could leave it with them and a week later I picked it up. The guy I dealt with wasn't 100% sure if they replaced a fan or not but I was told the fan noise was "within normal specifications". I took it back several times and received varying useless responses from the "Genuises" each time. I finally escalated the issue with Apple Executive Relations and they agreed to replace a component for free. Of course, by then, I had sold the noise-maker to someone else, but I hope they can enjoy a quieter Mac.
label: NEG

text: This has to have been the worst lunch buffet I've ever had. My fiance and I were in search of a restaurant to cater our upcoming wedding. We went on a covert tasting spree through out Tampa and St. Pete. This was by far the worst food we had. The saag paneer was awful, and tasted like dirty spinach, and the paneer was over-cooked and rubbery. I chocked down a few bites of chicken tikka masala and veg kourma before we decided to just pay and leave. I wouldn't come back here if someone paid me.
label: NEG

text: Snockey's has one of the cheapest happy hours I've seen around the city. From 4:30-6:30 on week days they have $2 Moosehead (among a few other selections) and $4 Bloody Mary's. Plus 10 cent pick and peel shrimp and 50 cent oysters. We live a block away so it's worth it for us. Other than happy hour, I would NEVER voluntarily go here. We always go in and sit at the bar area and no fail every single time our bill gets messed up. Once we were charge the $21 that our bill came to and then on the bank statement we see that we were charged an additional $64!! The owner gave us quite a hard time about giving us the money back too. The service is painfully slow and you have to repeat yourself multiple times to make sure your order gets put in correctly. It could also stand for a serious renovation. The place is pretty dingy looking. That being said, I'm sure I'll be there for the $2 Moosehead soon enough.
label: NEG

text: My family and I were in town on our mid-west vacation trip and I found this place on Yelp for BBQ Ribs. The menu looks similar to a few other in downtown, and it's close to Anheuser-Busch which was our plan after lunch. We came here around 12 after visiting the Gateway Arch. It's on a quiet street corner. We were the 1st group of the day, the next two groups are business men with shirts and ties (really, shirts and ties for BBQ). The decor is more like a Jazz Cafe than BBQ pit. They even off live music in the evening. We ordered : Duck & Andouille Gumbo & Seafood & Andouille Gumbo: tasty, but come on, give us little more rice than just a sauce cup full. Loaded Smoked Potato Wedges: very tasty with the pork and bean. 1/2 rack of St Louis Rib & full rack of Baby Back Ribs: unlike some BBQ pit, ribs are pre chopped and nicely piled up. There are 3 sauces to choose from, regular, spicy and one with honey mustard. I like the spicy BBQ sauce which is mild and my wife likes the honey mustard one as it sweeter.
label: POS

text: Sam and Zoe's was the first place I ever ate at (that wasn't a chain of some sort) when I moved to Nashville. It remains a favorite. Each time I visit there, a new artist's artwork hang on the wall, and they serve the very local and delish Drew's Brews coffee. It's a great place to grab a cup of coffee, study, and just relax a bit. The Sawf Salad with Chicken (getting the chicken is a few extra bucks) is probably the best café salad I've ever eaten. Be sure to get the raspberry dressing to go with it. It will entice groans of pleasure, I promise. And it's a nice portion size too. They also have some vegan offerings, the TLT (BLT anyone?) being my favorite. The sandwich has become a form of winter comfort food for me, and I don't have to feel like I'm clotting my heart with hoards of bacon. It's wonderful. A word to the wise: the menu's are on the wall as you enter and you seat yourself. I stood there pretty awkwardly my first visit, so this is just a friendly heads up for S&Z virgins. Parking is the biggest problem, and you'd do better to stay away until after the typical lunch rush, although there is some limited parking in back along with the front. Regardless you're going to love the place, scout's honor.
label: POS

text: We will NEVER go here again!!! We had been there once before last Friday night. The service was great and the food was decent. It seemed like a place that we could become regulars at. That was until the last trip. We got there around 5:30pm and it was packed, which is to be expected at any restaurant on Friday night. I went in and asked what the wait time was and was told 30min which was great for how busy it looked. I asked to be put on the list and when I told them that we needed a table for 6 total with 2 highchairs, they immediately said no. So I asked for 1 highchair and a booster. They said there was no way they could do that either!!!!!!! I even said I would be willing to wait a little longer and was told no again!!! I can not believe that a business would turn down a 6 person table. That was the LAST time I will ever go back to that place.
label: NEG

text: Stopped here on an afternoon walk after a friend recommended this place to me. What a mistake. The waitress was pleasant and the sake was sake, but thats the end of the good news. I tried the sushi combo. I noticed that the fish was a little warm. It seems they may have a problem with the refrigeration unit on the sushi bar. The tuna tasted tasted really funky and the yellowtail was a little gray. I left feeling a little queasy. Also, the prices are very high for the low quality food. Do yourself a favor and stay away.
label: NEG

text: Oh, pork juice, all over my hands. So juicy, so tasty, so pork-n-provolone. Is that a little bit of garlicky awesome broth? Yeah, I'll be back after last week's experiment.
label: POS

text: Ah, the blue willow... i grew up in the old pueblo and have been coming here since i was a kid... always get the same thing (the omelettes are outstanding) and it's always really good. maybe it's the plants in the bathtub. maybe it's the curio shop. maybe it's the hershey's kisses when you pay. i don't know. this place is lost in time. it used to be a house in the 40's. it's an institution, for chris sake! the coffee is good and the service was above par. that SF yelp guy a couple reviews down is a nazi. whateves. read the love story on the menu, you won't regret it.

text: Di Vello's is a great spot in South Jersey. I always make sure to stop here when I am working in the area. I have never had anything from the deli that hasn't been great. Such a wide variety and all the ingredients are very fresh. I HIGHLY recommend Di Vello's. Larry is always working at lunch time and definitely takes pride in taking care of the customer.
label: POS

text: I fired Alamo Cleaners almost a month ago. I always used them for clean and press mens shirts. Most times, the shirts were not ready as promised. Several times, they were pressed and not cleaned (I could still see the crumbs in the breast pocket). If there was a stain in which you pointed out, it would be an extra day, because they had to "buy the soap for it". WOW! They were one big excuse after another. I also found that parking was a pain, and other customers of Alamo were rude and inconsiderate. They also man handled a Brooks Brothers shirt and ripped it down the seam.
label: NEG

text: Wow, what the heck happened. I made reservations for three days (two free, one paid). When we arrived, there was a long line (volley ball tournament) and only one person handling the arrivals. When I finally got there I was told my reservation was for 1 day. After showing the mailer I received for the free Days, I was told there was NO non-smoking rooms available. Great deal, free room and smoke. When I got to the room, the keys did not work. Went back to the front desk and got another set. Of course they don't work either. Flaky on the outside and wonderfully unctuous on the inside, it was a filling -- and pleasing -- dish. Much like the gumbo, both of these were perfect for a stormy Tuesday. Nova, conversely, probably had too little to eat. She ordered the smoked brisket with potato salad. While it was incredibly flavorful, the portion size was also a little modest. text: So it's hard for a man to find a good barber these days. Either you go to a fancy Salon, which tends to cater to women or the trendy 20something set, or you go to an old school barber, most of which are now 70+ years old and have one tool of the trade, a razor with a #2 guard. Not so David Wilson! In a brisk thirty minutes one of his talented (and very pretty) skilled staff members will give you a perfect cut, clean up and stray hairs with a straight razor shave, give you a neck massage, and have you on your way. Trusty me we won't skip over any of this process, which is probably one of the best things you can treat yourself to that's legal in Jersey, but a bit of history on the shop. The shop used to be exclusively men's clothing. Nothing cheapy here. Allen Edmund shoes, high end shirts and pants, the newest styles, everything a gent needs down to the right socks. On site tailoring is available, as is a shoe shine. The shoe shine also allows for drop off, which is nice if you're in hurry. David Wilson realized there was no place a gent could go to and get a great shave and haircut anymore, so he expanded and added the Salon. Probably the best offering here is a real shave. You heard me mention it earlier in regard to the haircut. This is the whole works. Hot towel, heated lather, straight razor. What a treat in today's fast paced, metro-sexual world to kick back and have an old school straight razor shave. Baby smooth skin guaranteed. Jennifer, the woman who takes care of me, shaves so close I swear she takes off the wrinkles too. Not that I have any wrinkles, but if I did... Anyway, back to the haircut. Large comfy chairs and spacious surrounds are illuminated by the huge front windows, allowing for meticulous inspection of your quality cut in progress. Once you give it the thumbs up, a hot towel is applied to your neck and any stray hairs are removed with a hot lather/straight razor combo. To finish up your haircut, a neck massage is administered to get rid of any remaining stress that hasn't been hot toweled away. Don't think this is just your granddad stopping in here either. Today's men yearn for old school quality and service like this, so you may be sitting next to your paperboy on one side and a waiter from Nunzio's on the other. Add the fact that the whole cut is $20! Best deal ever.

text: This is one of those restaurants where the name says it all. It's pretty much all seafood and almost all is battered and subsequently fried. However, there is also sushi which is pretty much the opposite of battered and fried (unless you're getting some kind of tempura sushi). I don't recommend it for the health conscious or vegetarians, unless you love sushi. I tried this place with my family the other night. It's located in hip East Nashville which is much more bohemian than I would have expected out of Nashville. The place is quite large with a dining area with a sushi bar, a full bar and an outdoor patio. The menu consists of all things seafood battered and fried. There are shrimp, clams, oysters, scallops, several varieties of fish, etc. If it comes from the ocean, they've probably fried it. I did not see fried Sea Cucumber but there were fried sweet pickle chips. These two are very different. Your fried thing comes with a choice of sides which are mostly potatoes or slaw but there are some interesting options. The sushi seemed to be pretty much white people sushi. It was california rolls and salmon and all the standards that white people like. It looked good and it was served well. I am a little skeptical about sushi not prepared by a Japanese chef at a restaurant that specializes in sushi but my sister said it was good. They also serve many specialty drinks here. There is a full bar and the drinks all sounded really good. I tried a variation of a Long Island Iced Tea where it's topped with Sam Adams instead of coke. It was interesting and somewhat refreshing, but not something I would want very often. I ordered the fried clams. They were expertly prepared and very delicious. It's hard to mess up fried clams and I'm glad they didn't. I got a side of mashed potatoes which tasted good but were room temperature. In addition, I ordered a side salad and I got it after my main meal because someone gave it to another table. It was lettuce, tomato wedges and shredded yellow cheddar. My sister got sushi and it looked good. Our service was good. We were seated in the bar area, directly next to the bar and our bartender was actually our server. I think his attention was spread a little thin, but he was very nice and pretty attentive for being so busy. I don't know if I'm dying to go back, but I would if someone else wanted to. Check it out if you love fried seafood or sushi.

I thought it would be a fun, relaxing experience and scheduled a block of mani/pedi appointments when a group of friends were in town. I wasn't sure if they would accept appointments for a group with only two days notice, but they did, so I was impressed that we could be accommodated. However, when we arrived, things only seemed to go downhill. Apparently, the appointments I had booked were not entered into the system correctly, so it took a little time to straighten everything out and make sure we could all get in. After waiting about 15 minutes, we finally worked it out where some of us could go back to the mani/pedi area while the other two girls went to grab lunch. This wasn't a problem because I had anticipated that we would get split up into two blocks. Needless to say, it took over four hours for all seven of us to get finished! A couple of the girls even skipped getting a full manicure in order to save time. I expected it to take a little longer since all of the work is done by students; however, I wasn't prepared to spend half of my afternoon getting manicures and pedicures. Also, one of the girls in our group brought it to the attention of the staff that her toe had been cut during the pedicure. To top it off, her polish job was very gloppy and started peeling as soon as we got home. The only positive of this experience was that most of the students were friendly to us. Yet, overall, I had definitely wished for a better experience.

text: Maybe we hit up Puebo Solis on an off night. Or maybe we've just been spoiled with good Mexican food elsewhere and we're expecting too much. For starters, we had hoped to sit outside, but that's really not the fault of the resturant. We were hungry, and didn't want to wait a half hour when there was seating immediately available inside. The atmosphere was fine- reminscent of some of the dark, random Mexican restaurants in CA we favored. Our drink order was taken quickly (I was surprised there was no drink menu, but ordered a margarita since reviews here said they were good. Wasnt asked if I wanted it on the rocks or frozen, but whatever) E ordered a corona, but no corona... just Sol and Dos Equis- again, no biggie. The chips were decent, as were the salsas- not the best I've had, but not the worst... I ordered chili rellenos with cheese (rather than beef); E ordered a combo plate (tamale, taco and hm.. something else- an enchilada, maybe?). We waited... and waited.. and waited... the food FINALLY came (granted, they were busy, but an occasional, "your food will be right up" would have been a nice gesture) BUT... it wasn't ours. Wrong table. Sigh... So we waited... and waited... and waited some more. I wish I had looked at my watch. It had to have been more than 30 minutes between ordering and receiving our food. And the food... hm. Beans and rice were.... okay. Chili rellenos was fried and greasy/soggy; the cheese was lukewarm and it was topped with cold tomatoes (which is probably why the cheese was lukewarm.) E's plate was full of... as he put it... piles of BROWN. His tamale was dry; the other food was medicore at best. All in all, a disappointment.

text: This place deserves kudos for having a fairly decent set up for being a total scam. I had booked a massage for myself and my girlfriend as a precursor to Valentines Day, which was thankfully saved by the always dependable James Restaurant. Dependable, a word the personnel at this establishment have yet to add to their vocabulary. I decided to take a chance and try a massage therapy salon I had never been to before since the ones I have tried in the area were good and sometimes great but never extraordinary. Never again... this is the main reason you should never rely on AOL City Guide or city search as both gave this place high marks. I asked for two female massage therapists for a 90 minute Swedish massage. We arrive to an empty salon and are greeted by a bubbling crew that appeared to not only be stoned (not the good stoned... they probably had just huffed the hair glue) but had that weird pyramid scheme vibe about them. They took us back to one room with two benches. First, I hadn't asked for both of us to be in one room although this was obviously not a problem for us, but the room was so small that while being massaged the masseuse kept shoving my bench across the floor with me on it to get from one side to the other. The bench didn't have head support and gave me a throbbing migraine that consumed my concentration. There was an oddly placed shower in the corner of the room that looked like it hadn't been used for years and was blocked by my bench. There was nowhere to place personal items or clothes so we had to end up folding them and putting them under the benches. After waiting for over 15 minutes, the massage therapist came in. As I said earlier, I asked for two females but I guess this didn't matter as one of them was a male whom of course picked my girlfriend to massage. My masseuse was a gigantic Russian female, oddly enough, with the strength of a phantom limbed quadriplegic. I'm pretty sure she didn't speak English, as she never asked me any questions about what pressure I wanted or if the wretched massage was going well. I guess she doesn't like criticism and tries to avoid it in any way she can. Then the music, which has got to be the easiest part of running a massage clinic... slap in some nature crap with a mix of ancient Chinese flute and you're golden. Not here, they prefer heavy drum elevator tunes with a mix of sexual moans blasting through distorted speakers. Now to the massage... neither one had obviously ever received a degree in massage therapy or even been given a massage. Their idea of a relaxing Swedish massage consisted of spritsing some low grade oil on their hands and spinning circles on your back as if they were an impatient Mr. Miyagi. And if that wasn't bad enough, they continuously stopped massaging to make gestures at each other and giggle, which had me paranoid as to whether my manhood was everything but in Russian standards or if they couldn't believe we fell for thinking they were an actual massage therapy clinic... the K in clinic should have given it away. To top it all off, the crappiest massage ever last all but 50 minutes... yep, we were charged for 90 each. NEVER GO HERE... my suggestion is Toppers... ask for Elaine.

text: After my Korean BBQ epiphany down in DC, I have been trying to find the equivalent to it in Philadelphia. Through much research on the web, Yelp, and friends, it all lead me to Young Bin Kwan. The Yelp reviews excited me and the persuasive words from my foodie friend convinced me to hit up this spot. First off, the place is not that hard to find, contrary to the reviews here. It is caged in an area under apartment buildings. It has a fairly large sign that is visible from the street as well. We entered the restaurant, with our smiles wide and excitement level sky rocketing. All this was nothing compared to the hunger I had awaiting me. They had sat us down and we proceeded to the buffet. They had a pretty good selection with all the meats you'd expect at a KBBQ. I noticed the marinate was really watery, which is not always a bad thing, but I hope the flavor would stay after grilling. They also had a selection of kimchi and the sushi was not yet available (we had to ask if it was included, or not). We went for the plates, and the semi-stickiness turned me off immediately. Not the greatest start, since dirty plates freak me out. We got what we wanted and returned to the table, where they were still fixing our grill. I believe something was wrong with it, but we stood/sat there awkwardly while they were all crowded around our table. Finally, the grilled was fixed and the meats were fired up by our server. We had to wait a bit for the grill to get hot, but the steam and grilled smokey flavor filled the air. The food was not that bad. Some of the meats could have been a bit more tender, but overall it was a nice to eat. The pork belly was frozen though, which was a bit sad. The sushi started to show up, but it was nothing good. It basically had a california roll with yellowtail nigiri. Not the freshest. More problems came when more people started to come in. We had a couple parties of 3-4 people and a family. There were only 3 people working last night, so you do the math. We did not get any attention after our first plate of food, and it was just a hassle to get our food cooked for us. I even started to try and operate the grill myself, but I think ours was broken and had to be pressed and kept down for it to light up. After awhile, I got a hand of it and started cooking myself, which I preferred. I left the place pretty unhappy, yet full. The service was poor, but that was due to the understaff. The selection could have had been of higher quality, but not a huge problem with me. My experience down in DC at a similar place raised the bar way too high. I couldn't give Young Bin Kwan a four, because it was no where near my time down in DC. I could have given it a three, but the service was really poor. A 2 or a 2.5 would be the most reasonable for the place. Alone, Young Bin Kwan will deliver an all you can eat Korean style BBQ at a decent price of $22.99. Is it the best? No, but for Philadelphia, you cannot complain.
label: NEG

text: Drinks here? Fine I'll tag along. Dinner? NO WAY! Looking for a place with good burgers in the CWE we decided to try Sub Zero since my mom wanted to go there anyway for drinks. They advertise "New American Burgers" on a neon sign out front, so we figured we would give them a try- turns out it was a bad idea. Not only were they really expensive ($11-$19), but they were just plain bad. I got the "breakfast burger"- I usually love the breakfast burger concept it's basically your normal cheeseburger with a fried egg on top. Theirs was gross. The meat tasted weird- not like rotten or anything, just bad seasoning. Would never order again. My husband got the cajun burger. First they cooked the shit out of it- it came out a bit more like a hockey puck rather than a burger- this was to pass as medium rare? He sent it back and received a more normal looking burger- but not til after the waitress came back with a message from the kitchen telling us it looked overcooked because of the cajun spices. Sorry, that excuse was not going to pass on this one, cajun spices don't account for the inside being cooked to powdery dryness. Anyway when he did get it back properly cooked he said it was waaaaaay salty. This is a guy who normally doesn't complain about anything at a restaurant- this was 2 complaints on one burger. He hated the burger, but liked the sweet potato fries. Mom had 2 sliders- 1 was a classic cheeseburger and the other was a veggie burger. She said the veggie burger was way better than the classic burger, but would still not order it again. We also got side salads with our burgers, those were pretty good. I loved their ranch dressing (I have a weird thing about ranch- I think they mostly suck, but when it's good it's sooo tasty good). Also my husband ordered an Unagi (eel) roll. He said it was alright- but in all fairness we did just move from Hawaii 6 months ago. It's going to be nearly impossible to get sushi in the midwest as good as it was there. Overall I'll never be eating here again- well maybe I'll try some other sushi but that's it. They do have about a billion different vodka drinks though, and for those I would go back. Atmosphere is a bit posh- very hipster vibe. Loud bass driven music on the speakers, dark lighting with blue neon all over the place. Not exactly my scene. Ice bar is pretty sweet though...

text: Aahahahahahahah- Kingdom of Vegetarians is ludicrously bad. Yet, it made for a meal so hilarious that it may actually have been cooler than if it had been an excellent restaurant, because was so very memorable, more than if we had had something actually good. I usually reserve 1-star reviews for incidents of bodily harm, but I felt crappy from the insane levels of MSG, so I think this qualifies. We were lured in by the sign on the door- "All you can eat vegetarian dim sum- $12". What could possibly be wrong with that? The waiter brought us some tea, and even after we ordered dim sum, insisted on leaving the menu so that we could order more items if we were still hungry. They were serious about this AYCE business, it seemed. After a bowl of slightly-below-mediocre cornstarchy soup, our first plate arrived. Instead of using a cart, they brought it out in courses. So that was their game! Bring out the cheapest stuff first to try to fill us up! If I'd known where it was going from there, I would have been much more grateful for the rock-hard fried sesame mock-chicken. Incidentally, Kingdom was the first Chinese restaurant that I've been to in years that offered a fork, but no chopsticks. Not that I'm a snob, just sayin'. The sauces were standard issue, straight out of the little packets but squirted into bowls. The rest of the items were so untasty that we ended up pushing those things to the side. Next were the dumplings and pork buns. The buns were still covered with paper that had stuck on when they were microwaved and the dumplings were made of bread, unlike every other dumpling in the world. The waiter noticed the piles of unwanted food pushed away and thought we were done, but I politely asked to skip ahead to the seaweed salad. He argued but finally relented. After a very long wait, the manager(?) brought the seaweed out, saying "NOW are you happy?" Temporarily appeased anyway. It was almost entirely unseasoned, save for the 43415613456 cloves of garlic. It was the best thing we had. After we ate, I started trying to signal to the waiter that we would like something else. He literally made eye contact while I waved at him several times, and then returned to folding napkins but when I stood up to go get him, both he and the manager had obviously been watching me because they were instantly at my side. I stated my case and the manager brought out the fried bananas, telling us "This is your last course". Uh, AYCE whut? Oh my word. The itsy bitsy little slices of banana were encased in giant puffballs of batter. I surgically extracted the banana, followed by the fillings of the eggroll, of the be-papered bun, of the dumplings, and now of the banana, leaving neat little dough cases delicately split on my plate. It was bratty, but dammit, I was still hungry! By now we were feeling weird and flushed from so much MSG but we weren't ready to give up, so we ordered the only other thing on the admittedly extensive dim sum menu that wasn't fried: coconut triangles. Again, I had to chase them and they gave me some shit, but I reminded them it was AYCE, and actually we were doing them a favor because we had skipped 75% of the menu. It took a loooong time to get these. The manager told us they were making them from scratch. They were the last thing on the menu, and I guess no one had ever made it that far before dying of MSG poisoning or a heart attack. Finally, she brought out deep fried triangles with pockets of oil literally oozing around between the layers of fried. Again, I surgically excised the meager filling. It was orange and tasted like sweet potatoes, with perhaps a hint of coconut flavor, courtesy of McCormick. Damn. I'm confused by all the glowing reviews. Maybe people enjoy different foods than we do, but the service? Some of the worst I've had. I'm polite, friendly, forgiving- was it something I said? Just stay away.
label: NEG

text: Probably the best coffee in Tampa, and in my mind, one of the best coffees I've had anywhere. Of course I happen to love tradition, and their coffee satisfies my desire for great tasting Cuban coffee. Naviera coffee is located in the historical Ybor City district, which is the old Latin quarter of Tampa, where Spanish, Cuban, and Italian immigrants worked in the cigar factories, and congregated in restaurants and social clubs. To give you some perspective, Ybor city itself architecturally resembles somewhat the French quarter in New Orleans. While a little sleepy during midweek, it's a neat place to spend a couple of hours in the afternoon for lunch and coffee, followed by a stroll down 7th Ave. Naviera Coffee doesn't look like much from the outside, but their coffee packs a punch. They roast coffee in the back, and serve traditional delights in the front. My favorite is the Ybor special: Cuban Espresso, with a touch of condensed milk. Soooooo good !!! While the seating area and sit down atmosphere is lacking, the coffee is so worth the visit to Ybor. Even our former President Teddy Roosevelt paid Ybor a visit before embarking on his journey with U.S. troops to fight and free Cuba during the Spanish American War (early 1900s). His troops even invented the "Cuba Libre" drink during that time, when they combined coca cola and rum for the first time in Ybor. http://www.elmolinocoffee.com/
